author: franciscolong
body:
## Qué cambia

- **Agenda en línea con confirmación inmediata** conectada al Google Calendar de Eliana: el visitante elige día y horario, completa sus datos y el turno queda creado en el calendario.
- **El trámite llega al evento.** Si se entra desde un trámite de Servicios, se muestra fijo; si se entra por "Reservar turno", se pide el motivo con un select que arranca en "Seleccioná uno".
- **Dos correos por turno** (Resend, desde `turnos@agenda.escribaniaisbarbo.com.uy`): la confirmación al cliente, con dirección y WhatsApp para cancelar, y un aviso a Eliana con los datos y el enlace al evento.
- **Contacto pasa a Reserva** en el menú, el pie, el botón del inicio y el título de la sección. En la ventana y en la tarjeta de la sección, el correo se reemplaza por "Reservar turno"; WhatsApp sigue igual.
- **Avisos del formulario:** el botón queda gris hasta que está todo completo; arriba se lista lo que falta y se achica a medida que se completa. Si se toca igual, se marca cada campo pendiente.

## Cómo funciona

- `api/availability`, `api/bookings` y `api/booking-config` son funciones de Vercel sin dependencias. Las reglas viven en `lib/booking.js`.
- **Reglas:** lunes a viernes de 9:30 a 12:30 y de 15:00 a 19:00, turnos de 45 minutos, hasta 45 días hacia adelante. La anticipación mínima es de 24 horas y se cambia con `BOOKING_MIN_NOTICE_HOURS`.
- **Sin base de datos:** cada horario usa un id de evento fijo, así que Google rechaza un segundo turno en el mismo horario. La clave de reintento evita duplicados si se corta la conexión.
- **La cuenta de servicio** `turnos-web@escribania-turnos.iam.gserviceaccount.com` tiene el permiso "Hacer cambios (ver eventos privados como libre/ocupado)". Los turnos se crean como eventos normales, porque con ese permiso Google rechaza los privados.
- **Interruptor:** sin `BOOKING_ENABLED=true` o sin alguna credencial, la agenda se apaga sola y la página ofrece solo WhatsApp.

Detalle completo y variables en el README, sección "Agenda en línea".

## Verificado

- 51 pruebas unitarias, con Google, Turnstile y Resend simulados.
- **En la Preview, con las credenciales reales:**
  - se creó un turno de prueba en el calendario de Eliana;
  - llegaron los dos correos (al cliente y a Eliana), en la bandeja de entrada;
  - el horario quedó tachado como ocupado.
- **Navegador:**
  - flujo completo en escritorio y en teléfonos de 320, 360 y 390 px;
  - conflicto de horario (409): mensaje claro y el formulario conserva los datos;
  - agenda apagada: queda solo WhatsApp.

## Antes de mergear

- [ ] Cargar `TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` en Production: es la clave pública del widget cuyo secreto ya está en Vercel. Verificar que el widget acepte `www.escribaniaisbarbo.com.uy`.
- [ ] Cargar `BOOKING_ENABLED=true` en Production.

Sin esas dos, la agenda queda apagada en producción: la página ofrecería solo WhatsApp aunque los textos ya digan "Reserva".

## Después del merge

- [ ] Hacer un turno real de prueba en producción y borrarlo del calendario.
- [ ] Borrar el turno de prueba del jueves 8/10 a las 11:00 (Carta Poder), si sigue en el calendario.

author: ramalhoneilson
body:
## Summary

Five independent bug fixes:

- **QrispVQE no longer imports the QrispAnsatz processor.** The Docker build copies only the selected processors plus the helper modules they import, and a processor must not import another processor. The ansatz-spec helpers now live in a new helper module, `nifi_extensions/qrisp_ansatz.py`, which both processors use. QrispAnsatz re-exports them so existing tests still work.
- **QrispVQE energy precision is configurable.** Expectation values were hard-coded to `precision=0.01`, and the sampling noise at that level can exceed chemical accuracy (0.0016). The new `Energy Precision` property (default `0.01`, so current flows behave the same) is used both in training and for the reported `vqe.optimal_value`, and is written out as `vqe.energy_precision`.
- **fix(cirq): QASM circuits are simulated in qreg declaration order.** Qubits used to be sorted by name, which scrambled the wire order when qreg names weren't alphabetical.
- **fix(qrisp): the full QFT operator is kept without seed gates.**
- **fix(qiskit): inputs that only have QASM2 are now simulated** by the statevector simulator.

## Tests

- New: H2 QCCSD VQE reaches FCI within 0.003 Ha at precision 0.0005, and precision 0 routes to failure.
- Ran locally: `tests/test_qrisp_qccsd.py`, the QrispAnsatz tests, `tests/test_qrisp_qft_qpe.py` and `tests/test_statevector_qasm2.py` all pass.
- The branch merges cleanly with the current `main`.

author: jadenfiotto-kaufman
body:
Companion to ndif-team/nnsight#756, which puts the resolved pipeline task into `TransformersModel`'s model key:

```
nnsight.modeling.transformers.TransformersModel:{"repo_id": "openai-community/gpt2", "revision": null, "task": "text-generation"}
```

Everything here already keys on the exact string — the dispatcher's per-key Processors, actor names, the evaluator cache, schedule pinning — so two tasks over one checkpoint become two independent deployments, and the actor rebuilds the exact pipeline the client traced instead of re-inferring one from the Hub. The model actor, sandbox meta model, and TP loader needed **no changes**: `from_model_key` splats the suffix's fields into the constructor.

## What changed

**Key minting / parsing** (`cli/lib/models.py`)
- `get_model_key` / `canonicalize_checkpoint` take `task`. Left unset, it's inferred from the checkpoint exactly as an nnsight client with no `task=` infers it, so client and server mint the same key.
- `extract_task_from_model_key` beside the repo-id extractor — `None` for a suffix that carries no task (a non-JSON VLLM key).

**CLI**
- `--task` on `ndif deploy`, `scale`, `restart`, `evict`; `task:` per-model in models.yaml (file value overrides the flag default, like every other field).
- `ndif export` needs no task entry: exported specs carry `model_key` verbatim, which deploy uses as-is — same reasoning as `envoy_class`.
- `ndif status` prints the task per deployment.

**Controller**
- `status()` emits `task` for HOT and WARM entries, parsed from the key, so pre-task keys report `null` rather than lying.

**Dashboard**
- `task` on the deploy and schedule payloads/stores, the reconcile job's specs, and the autocomplete cache; Task inputs in the deploy + schedule modals; task shown on deployment cards. Frontend rebuilt (`vue-tsc` clean), dist committed.
- The frontend's stale `DEFAULT_ENVOY_CLASS` moves from `language.LanguageModel` to `transformers.TransformersModel`. Load-bearing now: `LanguageModel` pins text-generation, which would stamp the wrong task into keys minted for non-LM checkpoints.

## Compat

The task-carrying key format is the only supported one — no ingress normalization. Rollout note: pinned schedule entries re-canonicalize on their next write/reconcile, and a deployment started under the pre-task format should be redeployed.

## Verification

- Round trip in the ndif2 env: client key → `HuggingFaceModel.from_model_key` → same task, key stable across rebuild; `describe_checkpoint`/sizing unaffected by the extra field; old-format and VLLM keys parse to `task=None`.
- All edited Python compiles; the live-server pytest suite was not run (needs a running stack).

author: bomkino
body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"bomkino"} -->
_Requested by **pitchdog** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WZRxAJAyeRV3fReWBPstMD?thread=cmsg_01WZRxAJAyeRV3fReWBPstMDDt66YTbp7EqMCGpPqXBkXz)_

Stacked on #1. This PR will be retargeted to `main` if #1 merges first.

Before: when a deck of 2576 × 1080 slides went into a 1080 × 1920 Reel, the default 3 × 5 grid filled each cell and cropped half of every slide. The slide brought out front ran past both edges of the frame. On long decks it sometimes went home to the wrong cell or showed twice. A deck a little smaller than the grid lost slides: 20 slides on 3 × 7 showed only 12 of them. Planning a big grid took about 40 ms on every setting change. A song detected at half or double time could not be fixed, and there was no way to put words on the video.

After:
- **Wide decks fit.** The grid follows the deck until you set it by hand. It refits when you add or remove slides, change the canvas, or add a caption. Auto keeps slides whole when filling would crop more than 40%, and fitting never crops more than 35%. Examples:
  - 15 ultrawide slides get a 2 × 8 grid of slide-shaped cells.
  - 30 ultrawide slides get 3 × 10.
  - 30 slides at 1920 × 1080 get 4 × 8.
  - 24 slides at 1920 × 1080 under a caption get 4 × 6, whole.
- **The hero stays in frame.** The slide out front stays inside the frame for every canvas and slide shape. It comes home to its own cell, never shows twice, and never swaps out while it is away.
- **Every slide shows.** A deck smaller than the grid shows every slide before any repeats, and keeps repeats apart.
- **Faster.**
  - Planning a 12 × 20 grid takes 3 to 7 ms instead of 33 to 41 ms, on the same machine.
  - Flat cards draw as two triangles.
  - Export encodes the next frame while the GPU draws the last. On CI, a 12 × 20 Reel exports 1.6 to 1.9 times as fast, and a 3 × 5 Reel 1.25 times as fast.
- **Song fixes.** Half or double time, which beat bars start on, and a nudge of up to 150 ms.
- **Titles.** A title card that opens or closes the video, or a caption that stays, which the grid moves over to make room for.
- **Imports.**
  - Keynote and PowerPoint files get a "Save as PDF" pointer instead of failing silently.
  - Slides' real shapes are read on import.
- **Backdrop 2.0** from Galileo adds six new styles and seamless loops.
- **Old projects.** Projects from 1.0 open, with every new setting at its default.
- **2.0.0** README, changelog and bundle version.

**How**
- `GridLayout.fit` picks the grid, around any caption. It looks for, in order:
  1. a slide-shaped grid that covers at least 75% of the safe area;
  2. otherwise, the filled grid with the least crop under 35%;
  3. otherwise, the slide-shaped grid with the most coverage.
- `BeatScene.hero` now works in screen space, so the perspective can't push the hero past the frame.
- `Choreographer.spread` deals a small deck so every slide shows before any repeats.
- The restraint pass in `Plan.swift` keeps a running lit count with a heap of expiries, instead of rescanning.
- `StageRenderer` draws undeformed cards with a 6-index quad.
- `Exporter` overlaps frames when no video slides need serial decoding.
- `BeatFix` rewrites the analysed beats and recomputes drops.
- `TitleArt.reach` tells the layout how much room a caption needs.

**Checks**
- `beat-lab check` adds nine checks:
  - hero fits, across 3 canvases × 5 slide shapes × 4 variants;
  - comes home;
  - old projects;
  - wide decks;
  - open wide;
  - beat fix;
  - caption room;
  - fit round a caption;
  - small decks.
- `beat-lab bench` times listening and planning.
- `beat-lab render` adds two wide-deck contact sheets and export timings on the old and new paths.
- CI opens the app three times:
  - 20 ultrawide slides;
  - 30 HD slides, at the moment one steps out front;
  - 24 HD slides under a caption.

author: lanryweezy
body:
🤖 Astra: [AI quality improvement]

💡 **What:** The AI code generation stream implementation in `src/services/geminiService.ts` used a custom `fetchWithTimeout` wrapper that only protected the initial connection and header response. It left the subsequent `reader.read()` operations completely unprotected.
🎯 **Why:** If the network stalls or drops mid-stream, the `await reader.read()` call hangs indefinitely. Because it was not wrapped in its own timeout, the client UI would permanently lock up waiting for a chunk that would never arrive.
📊 **Impact:** Prevents infinite UI hangs during AI stream generation by enforcing a strict 15-second timeout per stream read chunk. Also fixes a potential `TypeError` by correctly calling `reader.cancel()` when aborting a read before releasing the lock.
🔬 **Verification:** Run `pnpm test` to ensure existing functionality remains intact. Code review confirms the stream mechanics correctly release the Web Streams API lock.

author: atilaneves
body:
From an agent (Claude Sonnet 5.5).

Fixes #571.

## What is verified and what is inferred

VERIFIED (instrumented scratch build, full runs): closure frames that dmd
makes in the arena (`_d_allocmemory`, from `ExpressionSemanticVisitor.visit(CallExp)`
and `hdrgen`) hold stack addresses of the writing thread, for example
`sp + 3104`, and the arena never frees them.

INFERRED: the GC heap later grows over the address range of a stack that
no longer exists, and the report then takes such a word for a GC pointer.
In failing runs, `addrOf` found unrelated live blocks at those addresses.

NOT SETTLED: one dump in #571 was read as a word inside a table of 32-bit
pairs (`7FB800007F8F`). That log no longer exists, and the reading was not
verified. In the instrumented failing runs for this PR, every counted word
was a closure frame word. With this change the failure did not occur in 50
runs of `bin/ut -s` (4 of 25 before). If the test fails again, its message
gives a new dump, and #571 is opened again with it.

## Fix

`leaveFrontend` (debug builds only) records every arena word, written
since the last record, that points into the stack of the current thread.
`arenaPointersIntoGC` skips a recorded word while it keeps the recorded
value.

The report assumes that such a word is not a GC pointer. This holds for
pthread stacks. It does not cover fiber or interpreter stacks, nor a word
in an older block that gets a stack address later.

## Test

`arenaHoldsNoGCPointers.stackAddressesOfTheFrontendThread` runs the
frontend on a thread, and a word with a stack address stays in the arena.
The GC heap cannot be made to cover a stale stack on demand, so the stack
of the thread is a GC block: the word does point into a live GC block, and
the report skips it only because of what the word was when the frontend
left. The test is red without the report change. It clears the word at
the end. The tests that read or plant in the arena take one mutex.

## Cost

`bin/ut` wall time: about +1.2 s (+6 %), measured by the reviewer.

author: ijlalhaider313
body:
## Summary

Fixes an incomplete fix of GHSA-wmq8-cxq5-q9gx (path traversal via XSD `schemaLocation`). The original advisory patched the `xs:import` / `NSSchemaLocationMap` resolution path in `Options.GetValueType()`, but the `xs:include` / `IncludeMap` path in the same function retained the unguarded `filepath.Join(opt.FileDir, …)`.

## Details

`OnInclude` (xmlInclude.go) stores the raw `schemaLocation` attribute value verbatim into `IncludeMap`, and the `fi.IsDir()` branch of `GetValueType` (parser.go) resolves each include with `filepath.Join(opt.FileDir, include)` with no containment check. Because `filepath.Join` cleans `..` segments, `<xs:include schemaLocation="../secret.xsd"/>` resolves outside the input schema directory.

The vulnerable loop is gated by `fi.IsDir()` on the *import* path's resolved file, which is containment-checked. An attacker satisfies this with `<xs:import schemaLocation="."/>` (resolves to the input directory itself).

## Fix

Apply the same `filepath.Rel` containment check used on the import path to the include path, skipping any include that escapes the input directory.

## Test

Adds `TestIncludeSchemaLocationCannotEscapeFileDir`, which reproduces the escape via `<xs:import schemaLocation="."/>` + `<xs:include schemaLocation="../secret.xsd"/>` and asserts the outside secret type remains unresolved. Fails before the fix (resolves the outside type to `string`), passes after.

## Credit

Reported by @ijlalhaider313 via the associated security advisory; requesting a `credits[]` entry with role `finder` / `reporter` on any CVE issued for this finding.

organizer contract was read from the repository-root solver task, the track
assignment page, the target profile `sha256-r31-prefix-v1`, the cost model
`cost-models/collision-frontier-v5.json`, the claim schema
`schemas/claim-frontier-v3.schema.json`, the review policy
`docs/JUDGE_LANES.md`, and the accounting rules `docs/RESCORING.md`. The
reference implementations used for every semantic question were
`verifier/blake3.py`, `verifier/keccak.py`, and
`verifier/hash_functions.py`. Mechanical validation used
`python3 scripts/local_tracks.py check sha256-r31-exploratory`.

## Prior work, baseline, and review history

The prior candidate on this track is the organizer baseline package: a
generic birthday construction drawing 2^129 samples, retaining them all, and
sorting them with a fully charged iterative merge sort, which yields the
conservative scalar 2^149 (this track) with memory 2^137. Its accounting is
deliberately loose and its proof style — a universal finite-probability
argument over iid uniform messages with an empty heuristic list — is the
correct template for a generic claim.

This solver account's earlier submissions to this benchmark, including an
earlier revision of this very package, were refuted in review. That history
directly shaped this submission:

- The first revision of this package detected collisions with a hash table
  and charged probing by expected quantities (at most four probes, an
  expected same-slot pair count). The paired review refuted it with a
  concrete counterexample: on the positive-probability event that many
  sampled messages are identical, retained repeats force quadratic probing,
  so the asserted deterministic time cap was false
  (F-TIME-PROBE-COUNTEREXAMPLE, F-probing-cap, F_PROBING_TIME_CAP), the
  expected formulas silently relied on an undeclared home-slot distribution
  premise (F-HOME-DISTRIBUTION-GAP), and the occupancy-array initialization
  was both excluded from the preprocessing declaration and undercounted
  (F-PREPROCESSING-OMISSION). The judge was right on every point.
- This revision removes probing entirely: collision detection is now a
  deterministic stable LSD radix sort of the full digest followed by one
  linear scan, every ledger entry is a worst-case bound over all coin
  sequences and every fixed target, the sample count is the exact integer
  2^129, the preprocessing declaration covers the entire setup phase, and
  the memory formula enumerates every array. No expected value appears
  anywhere in the ledger.

## Hypotheses tried before this submission

The session first searched for a structural attack cheaper than birthday.

1. Hypothesis: with one prefix round, the BLAKE3 column step is
   message-partitioned, so per-column collisions of the digest contribution
   can be found independently and combined. Testing against the reference
   implementation refuted the premise: one BLAKE3 "round" is the column step
   AND the diagonal step (eight plus eight G calls), so after one round the
   state is fully mixed across columns. A C program with Brent cycle-finding
   per column produced per-column output collisions that did not collide the
   complete hash (the assembled messages verified against
   `verifier/blake3.py:blake3` to different digests).
2. Hypothesis: per-diagonal collisions with an identical post-column state
   (shared first eight message words) suffice. The digest layout refutes
   this: digest[i] = v[i] XOR v[i+8] after the diagonal step pairs the
   a-output of one diagonal with the c-output of another (for example
   digest[0] pairs a'' of diagonal 0 with c'' of diagonal 2), so
   per-diagonal output equality does not imply digest equality. A second
   instrumented C run confirmed the mismatch numerically.
3. Hypothesis: a closed-form partner construction per G (inverting the
   second G step with a free rotation parameter) could avoid birthday search
   entirely. The derivation fails because G mixes modular addition and XOR:
   the closure condition reduces to a 32-bit fixed-point equation with
   add/XOR coupling that has no closed form. A Python cross-check against
   the verifier showed constructed partners matching in one output word but
   not the other, exactly as the mixed-operation analysis predicts.
4. Counting check: the composite map from the 512-bit message to the
   post-round state is generically bijective, so digest collisions are
   abundant but present no structure cheaper than birthday short of a
   genuine differential search, which is out of scope for this session.

Conclusion: the correct honest claim on every active HashSmash track is the
generic birthday attack with tight, deterministic accounting.

## Approach selection and tradeoffs

The selected approach is a one-batch birthday search over exactly
n = 2^129 independent uniform messages of a fixed length chosen so that each
hash evaluation costs exactly one selected compression or permutation
(FIPS 180-4 padding into exactly one 512-bit block). Detection is a stable least-significant-digit radix sort of the
full 256-bit digest (eight passes over 32-bit digits with 2^32 four-byte
counters) followed by a single linear scan of the sorted array. The
alternatives considered were: a hash table (rejected: probing costs are
distribution-dependent and admit the quadratic all-repeats counterexample);
a merge sort like the organizer baseline (correct but about 2.4 times more
charged operations per record than the eight-pass radix sort under the 1/C
word-operation price); and distinguished points (rejected: memory is
non-scored, so the deterministic sort keeps the ledger simpler and honestly
worst-case). The radix design has no data-dependent cost at all, which is
what the previous refutation demanded.

## Implementation and files changed

Within the assigned editable directory `lanes/exploratory/candidates/sha256-r31/`
only three files changed:

- `claim.json`: schema v3, target profile and rounds bound to the track,
  lane exploratory, submission_state ready, claim time_log2 = 129.11,
  memory_log2_bytes = 137, preprocessing_log2 = 24, success_probability
  0.86, nonuniform advice zero, empty heuristic list, certificate manifest
  declared, reference identifier sha256-r31-nominal-v2, and restrictions describing the
  exact message shape, the integer batch size, the radix detection, and the
  all-worst-case ledger policy.
- `proof.md`: self-contained argument — exact complete-hash definition on
  the chosen message shape; the algorithm (sampling, eight-pass stable LSD
  radix sort of the full digest, linear scan, final recomputation and
  distinctness check); correctness of any returned

author: jjackson
body:
## The incident

A scratch script in one Claude session posted chat messages to agent `hal` with Jonathan's PAT. The only trace anywhere was the runner line `chat turn=<id> created emdash task=c-… (agent=hal)` and a turn whose initiator read `jjackson / chat / pat`, which is exactly what the web UI records. canopy-web logged nothing when it created the turn or the session. The middleware threw away *which* PAT authenticated, and nothing recorded a client, user agent, request id or parent. Production logs came from a `%`-format string shaped like JSON, with no timestamp, no logger name and the message unescaped.

## What this changes

**1. Request provenance** (`apps/common/request_context.py`). `RequestContextMiddleware` runs right after `BearerTokenAuthMiddleware`. It mints or accepts `X-Request-Id` and echoes it on the response. It stores `{request_id, ip, user_agent, client, credential, via_mcp, mcp_tool, parent}` in a contextvar. `RequestIdLogFilter` stamps `request_id` on every log record. Production `LOGGING` now uses `JsonFormatter` (`apps/common/log_format.py`). It builds each line with `json.dumps`: timestamp, severity, logger, request_id, plus any `extra=` fields.

**2. Credential capture**
- `request.auth_credential = {type, id, label}`, where `type` is one of `pat`, `oauth`, `contact`, `delegated` or `session`. `pat` and `oauth` are both `PersonalToken`s, and the label is the token's label.
- MCP: `CanopyPATVerifier` adds `token_id` and `credential` to PAT claims. For `cct_` tokens it adds a `caller_token` credential that carries `turn_id`.
- `api_tools._principal()` carries three things into the in-process request: the credential, the tool name, and the MCP client's own UA, client and parent headers. `_authenticate_mcp_call` sets `request.via_mcp` and `request.mcp_tool`.

**3. Persisted**
- `Turn` and `canopy_sessions.Session` gain `provenance` (JSON) plus `parent_turn`, `parent_session`, `parent_task` and `parent_claude_session`. One migration per app.
- Every creation site fills them through one helper, `apps/harness/provenance.creation_fields()`. The sites are `enqueue_turn`, `_refused_email_turn`, `upsert_turn` (report-only rows), `create_session`, `_thread_session`, `email_thread_session`, the runner-discovered sessions in `replace_reported_sessions`, `fork_if_name_reused`, and Slack's contact sessions.

**4. Parents**
- Headers: `X-Canopy-Parent-Turn`, `X-Canopy-Parent-Session`, `X-Canopy-Parent-Task`, `X-Canopy-Parent-Host`, `X-Canopy-Claude-Session`.
- Payload: an optional `parent` object (`turn_id, session_id, task, host, claude_session_id`) on `TurnIn`, `SessionCreateIn` and `SendIn`. Where both are given, the payload wins field by field.
- Resolution:
  - A caller token's turn fills `parent_turn`.
  - When only a turn is given, that turn's own chat becomes `parent_session`.
  - A `(task, host)` pair resolves through `RunnerBinding` when exactly one binding matches.
- Server-side paths set the parent themselves:
  - transfer → the source session
  - Slack `_requeue_stranded` → the lost turn
  - fork → the old session
  - dispatch → the turn that raised the ask
- **An unknown id is recorded in `provenance.parent_unresolved`. It never gets a 4xx.**

**5. One creation line.** `provenance.log_created(obj)` logs on commit to the `canopy.provenance` logger, and passes the same fields as `extra=`. Sample from the test run: `status` reads `done` here because the test stub executes inline; in production a new turn shows `queued`.

```
TURN_CREATED id=41ad40f2-6fc2-48a1-8bee-8c7e85745d00 agent=hal project=- session=e27e2dee-4b3f-485f-ae13-6123c77b5017 origin=canopy_web_chat status=done via=chat who=user:jj@dimagi.com assurance=pat credential="pat:1:scratch script" client=canopy-cli/0.2.590 ua="canopy-cli/0.2.590 (python/3.12; darwin)" ip=127.0.0.1 request_id=77bdb2cd62e24513900fa1b3bb3cdb94 mcp_tool=- parent_turn=- parent_session=74230cd8-e313-4f8d-a88b-76acea3921b1 parent_task=- parent_claude_session=- raised_from_task=- idem=chat:e27e2dee4b3f485fae136123c77b5017:n1 prompt_head="say \"hi\"\nplease"
```

**6. API**
- `TurnOut`, and so `ClaimedTurnOut`, gains `provenance`, `parent_turn_id`, `parent_session_id`, `parent_task`, `parent_claude_session` and `raised_from_task_id`.
- `InitiatorOut` gains `credential`, `client` and `parent`.
- `SessionOut` gains `created_by` (an email), `provenance` and the parent fields.
- `provenance` holds the IP and user agent, so it is redacted along with the rest of a turn's content for readers below `turn_access`.
- `generated.ts` is regenerated.

**7. Runner**
- Every claim logs `CLAIM turn=… target=… origin=… who=… credential=… client=… parent=… prompt_head=…` (`turn_log.py`). The chat created/reused/delivered lines and the CREATE/REUSE lines gain `origin`, `who` and `parent`.
- Every request sends `User-Agent: canopy-runner/<version> host=<hostname>` and `X-Canopy-Client: canopy-runner`. The cloud runner sends `canopy-cloud-runner/<sha>`.
- The cloud runner exports `CANOPY_TURN_ID` and `CANOPY_SESSION_ID` into the session it launches, plus `CANOPY_EMDASH_TASK` when the thread is an emdash task. These turn on canopy#768's parent headers for cloud sessions.

**8. Small fixes**
- MCP agent capability tools take `assurance` from the token instead of hard-coding `pat`.
- `initiator.for_request` uses `via=mcp:<tool>` for MCP calls.
- Schedule *Run now* records who clicked, in `provenance.clicked_by`.
- Close-out reports stamp a `for_request` initiator.
- Widget chat sockets go through `channel()` and record `client=websocket` provenance.

**9. Scripts**
- `scripts/e2e_session_chat.py` and `scripts/qa/*` send `X-Canopy-Client: <script>` and a UA, and forward the parent headers from `CANOPY_TURN_ID` / `CANOPY_SESSION_ID` / `CANOPY_EMDASH_TASK`.
- They mark their work: `origin_ref.e2e` on turns, and client ids of the form `e2e-<nonce>-…` on chat sends, since `SendIn` takes no `origin_ref`.
- `e2e_session_chat.py` no longer defaults to `~/.claude/canopy/workbench-token` or to `--agent hal`. Both are now required (`--token` / `--token-file` / `CANOPY_E2E_TOKEN`).

## Tests

- `tests/test_provenance.py` (16 tests):
  - a PAT turn records the credential id and label plus client and UA, on the row and in the API
  - a browser turn records a session credential
  - `X-Request-Id` is echoed, minted and sanitized
  - parent headers are stored and resolved; a task resolves to its session through the binding
  - an unknown parent is recorded, not refused; the payload beats the header
  - session create and send record provenance and parent
  - a caller token fills `parent_turn` automatically; MCP PAT claims carry the token
  - `TURN_CREATED` / `SESSION_CREATED` are emitted once each with credential and parent, and not again on an idempotent replay
  - *Run now* records `clicked_by`
  - the JSON formatter's output parses even with quotes and newlines in the message
- `runner/canopy_runner/tests/test_turn_log.py`: the CLAIM line and the runner's request identity headers.
- Results: backend `uv run pytest -n 8` **4802 passed, 1 skipped**; canopy_runner 833 passed; cloud_runner 498 passed; `ruff --select F` clean; `npm run build` OK.

author: eyasluna
body:
Part of PET-50: moving the hypervisor connection from unauthenticated plaintext TCP to mutual TLS. This PR only ships the mount. **Nothing changes on a cluster until an operator creates the Secret and switches the ConfigMap to TLS.**

## Change

`config/manager/manager.yaml`:
- **Mount** an optional Secret `libvirt-pki` read-only at `/etc/pki/libvirt`, the ConfigMap's default `pkiPath`. It replaces the commented `[REMOTE-TLS]` block. A hand-added mount would be wiped by the next deploy, exactly as the socket wiring was (PET-45).
- **`optional: true`**, so a cluster that hasn't created the Secret still starts. The files are only read when TLS is selected, and a missing one is then reported by name.
- **`defaultMode: 0440` plus pod `fsGroup: 65532`.** Secret files are owned by root and the image runs as `65532:65532`. Without `fsGroup`, the only readable mode would be `0444`, world-readable, for a key that controls a hypervisor. Same approach as the Cluster Autoscaler's kubeconfig in hydra-gitops.
- **Not shipped:** the Secret itself, just like `libvirt-config`.

`config/manager/libvirt-config.example.yaml`: how to create `libvirt-pki` (the file names are the keys); that the server certificate needs the dialled IP as a subjectAltName; and that this is mutual TLS, so it authenticates the provider, not only encrypts the connection.

## Verified

- `make manifests generate lint test build`: lint 0 issues, all packages pass, build OK, no drift. `make verify-installer`: still no ConfigMap shipped.
- **Rendered installer:** the Secret name stays `libvirt-pki` (no kustomize prefix, since it isn't a managed resource), and `defaultMode` renders as `288` (= `0440`).
- **Against the live management cluster**, read-only:
  - `kubectl diff` shows exactly the mount, the volume and `fsGroup`, plus the image tag.
  - `apply --dry-run=server` is accepted.
  - The namespace has no pod-security enforce label.
  - `libvirt-pki` doesn't exist yet, which is the case `optional` covers.

## Not verified

- **A pod reading the files.** No Secret exists yet. That comes with PET-50's TLS cutover, which also needs PET-36 (#29) merged first.
- **Deploy:** not deployed. It deploys with the next provider rollout, after #29.

Fixes #3193.

## Change

The trade header gets a "Copy address" button right after the market name (`components/trade/TokenCopyMenu.tsx`, in `MarketInfoBar`). It opens a menu:

- Slab address: the market's address
- CA: the token's mainnet address (`mainnetCa`)
- Ticker (`baseSymbol`)
- Search CA on X
- Search `$<ticker>` on X (cashtag; the plain ticker pulls unrelated posts for names like "Agency")

Each copy row shows its value shortened on the right; the full value is what's copied. Searches open `x.com/search?q=…&f=live` in a new tab. A copy shows "CA copied" etc. for 1.5 s. Escape or an outside click closes the menu. A market with no `mainnetCa` gets no CA rows.

To make room, Watch uses its existing star-only variant (`WatchButton variant="icon"`); the hover text is unchanged ("Add <symbol> to your watchlist"). Below `md` the button shows the glyph alone and opens the same menu, so the slab address and the CA can both be copied on a phone.

The slab address and its copy button are removed from "Market details", since the menu covers them; the page-local `CopyButton` and the `useToast` import go with them. "Market details" otherwise stays as it was (Admin Active, health lines, limits strip), closed by default.

The menu and the note are portaled and placed from the trigger's rect, as `MarketSwitcher` does: the info bar is an `overflow-x-auto` container with `backdrop-blur`, which clips absolute and fixed children (#2268).

## Tests

`__tests__/components/trade/TokenCopyMenu.test.tsx` (9 cases): the menu rows and their values, each copy (full value + note), both X searches (URL and new tab), the glyph-only button below `md` opening the same menu, the menu rendering outside the header, a market with no CA, and Escape / outside click / a click inside the menu.

Full suite: 19 failures, all of which also fail on current `playground` in my environment (3 are `security/transitive-deps-patched`… 1 is a path-separator assertion in `recover-sol-banner-no-resume-followups` on Windows). None new.

body:
Add delivery_command_execute for order.assign/order.cancel. Requires a valid short-lived Hermes signature bound to the caller's Delivery user ID, plus current approved/unsuspended actor and tambon permissions. Calls existing admin RPCs; mutation, admin/order audit, and receipt commit together. Same command ID returns the original receipt; a changed payload is rejected. Receipt signatures let Hermes reconcile retries after a network interruption.

Companion: https://github.com/bhiddaya/hermes-router/pull/22. Apply both migrations and securely configure the same d25_bridge_hmac Vault secret before enabling the Router endpoint. No persistent production migration or order action was run. Assignment LINE notification remains D47.

Validation: migration + SQL assertions passed on the Delivery schema in one rolled-back transaction (real admin assign/cancel RPCs on is_test records, replay/tampering/expiry/cross-tambon/grant checks). Readback confirms no test schema/profiles/tambons remained. All committed files fetched back and matched.

Remaining: review/merge, migration/key configuration, Router deployment and caller integration, cross-system is_test E2E. Docs explain the five-minute cancellation window and recovery; D25 remains unfinished until deployment and E2E pass.

author: esthor
body:
## Problem

CodeRabbit comments but never approves, so it can't tell maintainers which outside contributions are safe to merge on its review alone.

## Change

On pull requests from anyone who isn't an org member or collaborator (`ctx.pr.authorAssociation`):

- **Request-changes workflow.** CodeRabbit requests changes while it has open comments or a failing check. It approves once the latest commit is reviewed, its comments are resolved, and no check fails. `main` requires a pull request, so its "changes requested" review blocks merging until one of these happens:
  - CodeRabbit approves.
  - Someone other than the author comments `@coderabbitai approve`.
  - A maintainer dismisses the review.
- **`Approvability` check** (`error` mode). It fails when a maintainer should read the pull request first, and says so. That covers:
  - changed product defaults
  - new or broadened suppressions
  - new subsystems and large refactors
  - breaking contract or data changes
  - auth and credentials
  - external side effects
  - dependency changes
  - CI, agent, or review config

Org members' and collaborators' pull requests are unchanged.

**Who can lift the block.** Merging still needs write access; CodeRabbit's ✅ means its issues are addressed and the pull request is worth a maintainer's look.
- **Anyone with write access** can dismiss CodeRabbit's review, or comment `@coderabbitai approve`, which approves even while a check fails.
- **The author** can't approve their own pull request through CodeRabbit or override a failed check. They can resolve CodeRabbit's threads themselves, as on any pull request. Once none are open and no check fails, CodeRabbit approves, so a failing `Approvability` check still holds.
- **Other outsiders** can also comment `@coderabbitai approve`, since CodeRabbit checks only that the commenter isn't the author. On a pull request with auto-merge on, that can lift the last block.

## Scope and approval

This changes how CodeRabbit reviews outside contributions, not product behavior. @juliusmarminge agreed to this flow in a private chat. I work at CodeRabbit.

## Verification

- **Factory.** `tsc` type-checks it against the SDK. I evaluated it for an owner, a member, a collaborator, a contributor, a first-time contributor, an unknown association, and no pull request:
  - With CodeRabbit's defaults filled in, the first three get exactly `main`'s effective config, including `@coderabbitai resolve` and `approve` on their own pull requests.
  - Everyone else, including unknown authors, differs from `main` only in the gate's four settings.
  - Every output passes CodeRabbit's schema.
- **Repo checks:** `vp lint`, `vp fmt --check` and knip pass.
- **In a fork,** with this check and workflow:
  - A test-only pull request passed `Approvability`, and CodeRabbit approved it (esthor/t3code#2).
  - A CI change failed it. CodeRabbit requested changes and said it needs a maintainer's review (esthor/t3code#3).
  - The author's `@coderabbitai approve` was refused.
  - On the repo owner's pull request, CodeRabbit's resolved config had the gate off (esthor/t3code#4).

### Docker CLI Plugins: Uncontrolled Search Path Element Leads to Local Privilege Escalation on Windows
[CVE-2025-15558](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-15558) / [GHSA-p436-gjf2-799p](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-p436-gjf2-799p)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
This issue affects Docker CLI through 29.1.5

##### Impact

Docker CLI for Windows searches for plugin binaries in `C:\ProgramData\Docker\cli-plugins`, a directory that does not exist by default. A low-privileged attacker can create this directory and place malicious CLI plugin binaries (docker-compose.exe, docker-buildx.exe, etc.) that are executed when a victim user opens Docker Desktop or invokes Docker CLI plugin features, and allow privilege-escalation if the `docker` CLI is executed as a privileged user.

This issue affects Docker CLI through v29.1.5 (fixed in v29.2.0). It impacts Windows binaries acting as a CLI plugin manager via the [`github.com/docker/cli/cli-plugins/manager`](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/docker/cli@v29.1.5+incompatible/cli-plugins/manager) package, which is consumed by downstream projects such as Docker Compose.

Docker Compose became affected starting in v2.31.0, when it incorporated the relevant CLI plugin manager code (see [https://github.com/docker/compose/pull/12300](https://redirect.github.com/docker/compose/pull/12300)), and is fixed in v5.1.0.

This issue does not impact non-Windows binaries or projects that do not use the plugin manager code.

##### Patches

Fixed version starts with 29.2.0

author: svallory
body:
Closes TODO `solid-mx-tsc-silent`.

Before: a whole-file Solid `.mx` page with errors (even an undeclared name in `${}`) made mx-tsc print nothing and exit 0; the TS plugin showed the same silence. Module-level errors except the import were silent too. Root cause: Solid's descriptor is `mappings: "merge-recorded"` (the plugin does not re-lower), and `compileSolidUnit` recorded mappings for attribute names only, so every diagnostic in a value had no source position and was dropped.

- solid emitter: `mappedExpr` for component/native attribute values, spreads, class merges, `${}`/`$!{}`, innerHTML, `<if>`/`<Match>` conditions, `<for of|in>` sources, key, attribute-tag spreads/conditions, textarea values, dynamic-tag args. `compile.ts` maps imports, `static` blocks and `Input` to their authored span. Emitted text unchanged.
- core: `InputInterface.span?` (additive).
- Tests (red on baseline): tsc `expression-values-solid-typecheck.test.ts` (5 exact positions on the page, 3 in the module, region plain values pinned, clean page stays clean), TS plugin exact start/length, 20 solid mapping-pair tests.
- Goldens: `solid`, `target-solid`, `target-agree-solid` +2 mappings each (the Input interface), generated text unchanged.
- Known unmapped: `<for from to step>` arithmetic, attribute-tag `<for>` sources. Follow-up TODO `solid-region-atom-values-unmapped`: in region files (`.solid/.preact/.react.mx`) atom-containing values stay unmapped because the parser bridge text-matches; needs a parser API change.

Gates (netcup slot2): solid, tsc, typescript-plugin, language-server, vite-plugin, parser, core, html, preact, react, hono, astro, angular + all 7 oracles PASS.

author: jcsvwinston
body:
Quantum 1.40.0 publica tres defectos de quark que cruzaban tenants bajo
RowLevelSecurityClient —dos de ellos P0— y la mayor parte del arco A11
(extensibilidad y catálogo) en quark y en el panel. Se mueven quark
(v1.15.2 → v1.16.0, minor) y orbit (v1.18.1 → v1.19.1: la minor v1.19.0 y
un patch que la completa); nucleus v1.31.0 sigue donde estaba. Módulos
hermanos que cambian: los seis de quark (CLI v1.2.0, drivers v0.2.5) y
cuatro de orbit (ui v1.1.0, server v0.20.2, quarkbridge v1.9.4,
quarkdatasource v1.12.2). Minor de suite porque lo son las de quark y orbit
(QADR-0002). Corte FUERA de la cadencia semanal (QADR-0008), un día después
de 1.39.0: los arreglos de tenants no esperan a la semana.

Qué cambia para quien instala. Quien use un router de tenants con
RowLevelSecurityClient debe subir a quark v1.16.0: Find(id) leía la fila de
otro tenant (QK-42), la rama de actualización de Upsert y UpsertBatch
escribía en la fila de otro tenant que tuviera la clave en conflicto
(QK-43), UpdateMap podía mover una fila de tenant (QK-44), las escrituras
por clave ignoraban el Where del llamador (QK-40) y un grupo Or escapaba de
los ámbitos de tenant y de borrado lógico (QK-41). Las escrituras que las
condiciones excluyen devuelven ahora (0, nil) sin hooks ni auditoría. En
quark, además y por adición: el contrato del dialecto vive en quarkdriver
con alias en quark, el camino de esquema pregunta al dialecto por
interfaces en vez de leer su nombre, integraciones con chi, Echo, Gin,
gRPC y Nucleus probadas en CI, `quark init --with` que genera ese mismo
código, y un banco de rendimiento sobre PostgreSQL y MySQL reales. En el
panel, también por adición: acciones que piden datos con un formulario
validado en el servidor, acciones sobre un registro que responden con una
redirección dentro del panel o una descarga confinada, widgets de serie
alimentados desde Go y varios dashboards cada uno con su permiso, tema y
paleta por configuración aplicados antes del primer frame, y el código de
cliente de la aplicación con sus renderers de campo bajo la CSP del panel.
Lo único que se niega ahora a arrancar es una configuración que nunca tuvo
efecto: un field_widgets que nombra un widget o un campo inexistente.

Qué aprendió el tren. Un módulo que sube en el mismo corte que la raíz que
lo requiere deja a la raíz con la versión vieja: orbit v1.19.0 cortó ui
v1.1.0 con la raíz aún en ui v1.0.0, y hizo falta v1.19.1 para que las
pantallas nuevas llegaran a quien instala; el set pina la segunda. El
banco de rendimiento de quark —workflow no requerido— tumbó dos veces el
release al tocarle un modelo de CPU nuevo con asignaciones idénticas; se
fusionó con el gate obligatorio en verde y quark main ya ata los tiempos
al modelo (QK-47). La minor de quark necesita su snapshot de docs y el
tren no lo corta; el guard de voz de quark rechaza ids de ADR en las notas
publicadas; y el tren escribió para orbit v1.19.0 notas de «alineación sin
cambios» que había que reescribir. El go.work del paraguas gana
quark/internal/integrations, el primer módulo de fixtures de quark.

Abierto por el tren: las notes ya están redactadas, así que en el re-pin no queda ninguna decisión: los pines son los tags recién cortados y el resto lo escribió bump-set. La lane suite-integral corre en modo normal (tolera el mid-tren sin tag) y el driver fusiona en cuanto salga verde.

The captured 7bf4/92cb compositor reaches two first-power operations, but ideal geometry alone does not show what WebGL2 actually interpolates. This private probe draws the original vertex program and literal first-power fragment expressions for all three captured bank pairs, records every float pixel, and independently checks 1,612,644 covered centers. The smallest observed base is 0.499985; the largest observed delta gap from the rational center oracle is 0.000122, within the stated 0.1 observational budget.

The gate replays the verified capture, compares native and Wasm ideal-center auditors, checks linked-shader and framebuffer state, and rejects source, bank, numeric, geometry, viewport, and zero-crossing faults. Its exact-head hot and pristine-clone runs are sealed in the task evidence archive. This is a certificate for the recorded physical draw only; the full fragment compiler and production DRAW path remain gated. A fresh adversarial review is pending.

author: schienstockd
body:
## Problem
If you segment an image while its viewer is open, the new labels (e.g. NSfanU) don't draw, even after you toggle them on in the panel. They only appear once you close and reopen the viewer.

## Cause
There were two separate bugs:
1. **The pop-out viewer never heard that a task had finished.** `onViewerCacheClear` compared each incoming rev with a fresh `localStorage` read. But when a `storage` event fires, the receiving window's localStorage already holds the new value (checked in headless Chromium), so the two always matched and every cross-window clear was dropped. The viewer always runs as a pop-out, so this hit every task-done invalidation, pixel re-runs included.
2. **A new segmentation's event was filtered out.** `viewerCacheClearMatches` only let a label-scoped event through if the viewer was already drawing that vn. A vn the viewer's meta has never heard of can't be drawn yet, so the event was dropped.

## Fix
- The storage listener now keeps the last rev it acted on in a closure.
- A label vn that isn't in the viewer's `labelNames` now counts as a match. The viewer refetches meta and learns the new store exists.

## Tests
- Added `viewerCacheClearChannel.test.ts` cases for the unknown-vn match.
- `vue-tsc -b` is clean.
- Not tested end to end in the app.

author: bogdanaip
body:
## Scope

Add the minimum persistent Market foundation for the next Rakazo stage: large searchable Market Skills ("how to do work") plus Market Resolver knowledge ("what can implement a semantic need"), without loading the whole Market into the active Agent Skill catalog.

### Principles
- Reuse first; adapt second; create last.
- Market content is indexed context, never execution authority.
- v1 imports only curated, commit-pinned GitHub sources.
- Original content is immutable once indexed under a Market key.
- RCCL is optional and stored separately; Original remains the control.
- RCCL is not assumed better: comparison evidence can select ORIGINAL / RCCL / WRAPPED / HYBRID.
- Installing is explicit and materializes only one selected Market Skill variant into ordinary Agent Skills.
- Resolver entries are data-only semantic need -> implementation/fallback mappings; they do not install or authorize tools.

### V1 data model
One tenant-scoped `MarketEntry` table handles both `skill` and `resolver` entries:
- pinned repository/source URL/path/commit;
- SHA-256 digest and curated trust marker;
- original content;
- optional adaptation + mode;
- preferred variant;
- tags;
- comparison metrics/history;
- metadata/provenance.

This intentionally stays separate from `AgentSkill`, so thousands of Market entries do not pollute the active Skill catalog.

### RPC
- `market/search`
- `market/get`
- `market/import`
- `market/adapt`
- `market/evaluate`
- `market/install`

### Safety/trust
No heavyweight per-Skill security project. The operational rule is simple: use reputable transparent GitHub sources; if source trust is unclear, skip it. Market v1 additionally requires HTTPS github.com provenance plus a full 40-char pinned commit. Indexed content does not execute merely by existing in Market.

### Tests
Added service tests for idempotent pinned import, provenance conflict, resolver-as-data, RCCL adaptation, Original↔RCCL evaluation, explicit installation materialization and search ranking.

body:
## 目的 フレーム番号から導く時計 (ヘッドレスの書き出し・`SketchRuntime` の既定) で、寿命 `life` の粒が描かれる枚数が fps によって 1 枚ずれていたのを直す (#1710)。寿命 1 秒の粒は 24 fps で 23 枚・60 fps で 60 枚描かれ、1 fps では 1 枚も描かれなかった。粒を進める側には単精度の秒の写し `deltaTime` (`Float(1/fps)`) が渡り、GPU の断片が寿命からそれを引き続けて `life - step > 0` で生き残りを決めていたためである。上書きの注意も同じ丸めで、60 fps の `makeParticles(count: 60)`・`rate: 60`・`life: 1...1` が、上書きしていないのに 72 枚目に注意を出していた。 破られた約束は 3 つの出どころが支えるもので、フレーム番号の時計では刻みがちょうど 1/fps 秒なので、**寿命 L の粒が描かれる枚数は L·fps だけで決まる**。 - `FrameStep` の説明 (`Clock.swift`) - ADR-0025 決定 6 (揃えたいものを積分で作らない) - `makeParticles` の説明「rate × life がここで決めた数より多いと上書きが起きる」 決定は Issue の案 2 で、枚数は **⌊L·fps⌋** である。L は `Float` の値そのものとして数える (#1701 が `rate` で採った形)。 ## 変更点 設計は「フレーム番号の時計では、寿命を**進めた回数**で持つ」。上書きの注意は、どの時計でも**群が寿命を実際に減らした量の累計**で測る。 ### 寿命の数え方 (完了条件 1〜4・6・7) - **刻みの受け渡し**: `Particles.write(step:)` が `Float` ではなく `FrameStep` を受け取る。`Canvas+Particles.swift` は `step: deltaTime` を `step: frameStep` に変えた 1 語だけ。 - 指定の [16] (速度と位置の積分) には、今までと同じ単精度の秒を置く。 - 予備だった [36] に「寿命を 1 回で減らす量」を置く。`.frame` なら 1、`.seconds(s)` なら `Float(s)` で、後者は [16] と同じビットである。 - **`Particles.metal`**: 生き残りの判定 (`mokume_particleSurvives`、旗の段と置き場所の段) と、寿命の引き算を [36] で行う。式の形は同じ。 - **`Particles.place`**: `.frame(perSecond: f)` では n = ⌊`Double(span)`·f⌋ を倍精度で厳密に求め、寿命を n + 1 (「あと何回進めると尽きるか」) で置く。 - n 回目の進めまで描かれ、ちょうど n 枚になる。 - 値が整数なので、GPU の単精度の引き算が丸まらない。 - **参照の経路**: `living(from:)` の `life > 0` は変えていない。GPU が減らした後の寿命を読むので、同じ数え方に揃う。 - **観測の 1 枚** (#1760・`.seconds(0)`): [36] が 0 なので寿命は減らない。粒も出さない。 - **説明**: - `Sketch.particles(_:)` に次の 2 つを書いた。 - フレーム番号の時計では、寿命 `life` 秒の粒は ⌊`life` × fps⌋ 枚描かれる。例は「出したフレームを 1 枚目として、24 fps の `life: 1...1` なら 1〜24 枚目に描かれ、25 枚目で消える」。 - 枚数で数える寿命の頭打ち。 - 「寿命を ``deltaTime`` だけ減らす」は、フレーム番号の時計では枚数で数えることと食い違わない形に直した。 - `Particle.life` に単位 (秒 / 進めた回数) を足した。 - `FrameStep` と `Canvas.frameStep` の説明に、読む側として粒の寿命を足した。 - 並びの説明 (metal の冒頭・`Particles.headerFloats`) の [36] を直した。 - **changelog**: `changelog.d/particle-life-frame-count.fix.md` に、寿命を 1 つに決めた粒は fps によって描かれる枚数が 1 枚変わりうることを書いた。 ### 上書きの注意 (完了条件 5・反証の指摘 2・3) - **締め切りの持ち方**: 締め切りは時刻でもフレーム番号でもなく、`Particles.consumed` (寿命を減らした量の累計) で測る。 - 置くときは `deadline = consumed + 置いた寿命` (フレームの刻みは n + 1、秒の刻みは span)。 - 上書きされる粒が生きているとみなすのは、`deadline > consumed + この刻みで減らす量` のとき。GPU の生き残りの判定と同じ式で、置いた粒はそのフレームの計算より先に状態へ届くためである。 - フレーム番号の時計では、最初の作り (進めた回数) と同じ値になる。 - これで、秒の刻み (実時間の時計) で起きていた次の 2 つも直る。 - 1 フレームに同じ群を 2 回呼ぶと、尽きた粒の上書きで注意が出た (誤検知)。 - `particles()` を呼ばないフレームがあると、生きている粒の上書きで注意が出なかった (見逃し)。 - 締め切りが時刻を使わなくなったので、`Particles.emit` / `place` の時刻の引数 (`at:`) を外した。 - **累計を足す時点**: 累計は `Particles.write` では足さず、計算を GPU へ投入した時点で足す。 - 面が頼んだ進めを `Canvas.particleAdvancesThisFrame` に控える。 - 数えるのは、描き切りと、溜めた計算を先に流す口 (読み戻し・面をまたぐ順 #1870) である。 - 投入せずに捨てたフレーム (描き切りの失敗 #342・閉じ忘れた描き場所 #1622) では、溜めた計算と一緒に `discardFrame()` で落とす。 - 新しい格納なので、`CanvasTests` の境目の表に「フレームの終わりで戻るもの」として足した。 - **公開の説明**: `Sketch.particles(_:)` に「1 つの群は、1 つの時計の面で進める」を書いた。直に作った面 (`Canvas(target:gpu:)`) は自分の時計 (秒の刻み) を持つ。フレーム番号の時計で出した粒をそういう面で進めると、寿命が fps 倍ほど長くなる。振る舞いは変えていない。 新しい検査は、並行するレーンと取り合わないよう別のファイル `Tests/MokumeCoreTests/ParticleLifetimeTests.swift` に置いた。 ## 代償 - **枚数で数える寿命は 2^24 − 1 枚で頭打ちになる。** - 寿命を n + 1 の `Float` で持つので、1 ずつ厳密に減らせるのは 2^24 までである。それより長い寿命 (60 fps で約 77 時間・120 fps で約 39 時間) はそこで尽きる。 - 頭打ちとの比べは、積を整数へ直す**前**に行う。そうしないと `life: 1e30...1e30` のような寿命で `Int` への変換が溢れて止まる。 - 秒の刻みの時計には頭打ちは無い。 - `Sketch.particles(_:)` の説明と changelog に書いた。 - **固定の寿命の粒は、fps によって描かれる枚数が 1 枚変わる。** - 増える例: 24 fps の寿命 1 は 23 → 24 枚。 - 減る例: 50 fps の `life: 0.7...0.7` は 35 → 34 枚 (`Float(0.7)` が 0.7 よりわずかに小さいため)。L を `Float` の値そのものとして数える決定の帰結である。 - **秒の刻みでは、上書きの注意が境目の 1 回だけ GPU と食い違いうる。** - GPU は単精度の寿命から単精度の刻みを 1 回ずつ引いて丸める。CPU は同じ刻みを倍精度で丸めずに積む。そのため k 回引いた後の残りは、最大で「寿命の単精度の 1 目盛りの半分 × k」だけずれうる。 - 食い違うのは、残りがちょうど次の刻みの近くに落ちた粒の上書きだけである。そのときは注意が GPU より 1 回早く出るか、1 回遅れて出ない。 - フレーム番号の時計では累計も寿命も整数なので、食い違わない。 - 1 つのフレームの中で、面をまたぐ早い投入が `particles()` と `emit` の間に入ると、後から出した粒は先に流れた進めを受けない。累計の扱いと 1 回ずれうる (理屈で見た縁で、検査は無い)。 ## 確認方法 閉じる Issue: #1710 ### fps × 寿命の枚数 (直す前 → 直した後・GPU で実測) 検査と同じ組み立てで実測した。1 枚目に寿命ごとの粒を升を分けて 1 つずつ出し、毎枚の絵で升ごとに描かれたかを数える。直す前は main `9c1fd04` の木、直した後はこの枝である。**変わったところを太字**にした。直した後はすべて ⌊L·fps⌋ に一致する (完了条件 1 の検査が、fps 1〜120 のすべてで同じことを見ている)。 | L | 1 fps | 24 fps | 25 fps | 30 fps | 50 fps | 60 fps | 120 fps | | --: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 0.05 | 0 → 0 | 1 → 1 | 1 → 1 | 1 → 1 | 2 → 2 | **2 → 3** | 6 → 6 | | 0.2 | 0 → 0 | 4 → 4 | **4 → 5** | 6 → 6 | 10 → 10 | 12 → 12 | **23 → 24** | | 0.37 | 0 → 0 | 8 → 8 | 9 → 9 | 11 → 11 | 18 → 18 | 22 → 22 | 44 → 44 | | 0.5 | 0 → 0 | 12 → 12 | 12 → 12 | 15 → 15 | **24 → 25** | **29 → 30** | 60 → 60 | | 0.7 | 0 → 0 | 16 → 16 | 17 → 17 | 20 → 20 | **35 → 34** | 41 → 41 | **84 → 83** | | 1 | **0 → 1** | **23 → 24** | **24 → 25** | **29 → 30** | 50 → 50 | 60 → 60 | 120 → 120 | | 2 | **1 → 2** | 48 → 48 | 50 → 50 | 60 → 60 | 100 → 100 | 120 → 120 | 240 → 240 | | 3 | **2 → 3** | **71 → 72** | 75 → 75 | 90 → 90 | 150 → 150 | 180 → 180 | **359 → 360** | - 0.37 はどの fps でも動かない (陰性対照)。 - 0.7 の 50 fps・120 fps が 1 枚**減る**のは、L·fps が整数のわずか下 (34.9999994・83.9999986) に落ちるためである。0.05 が 60 fps で 2 → 3 枚になるのと同じ根である。 ### 絵 `SketchRuntime` を通した。24×24 の面の真ん中に、1 枚目に止まった粒を 1 つ出し、境目の前後 3 枚を最近傍で 8 倍に拡大して並べた。上段が before (main `9c1fd04`)、下段が after で、各列の上が枚番号である。**差が出るのは境目の 1 枚 (n 枚目) だけ**で、それ以外の組は上の表が受け持つ。1 枚の差は、どの 1 枚を撮っても「粒が写っている / いない」にしかならないので、枚番号を並べた形で示した。 24 fps・寿命 1 (列は 23 / 24 / 25 枚目)。before は 23 枚目だけに粒があり、after は 23・24 枚目にあって 25 枚目で消える: 30 fps・寿命 1 (列は 29 / 30 / 31 枚目) と、60 fps・寿命 0.5 (列は 29 / 30 / 31 枚目)。どちらも before は 29 枚目だけ、after は 29・30 枚目に粒がある: 撮ったのは main `9c1fd04` を取り込んだ時点の木である。その後に取り込んだ main は粒の寿命の数え方に触れていない。完了条件 1〜3 の検査は取り込み後の木でも緑なので、描かれる枚数は変わらない (板の描き方 #2023 などで絵の細部が変わりうるだけ)。 台帳の粒の参照スケッチ (`sketch:sparks-in-space@45`・`sketch:sparks-and-forces@45`) は動かない。45 枚目 (0.75 秒) を撮っており、最短の寿命が 1.5 秒・2.4 秒なので、撮るまでに尽きる粒が無い (完了条件 8)。 ### 完了条件との対応 | 完了条件 (#1710) | 何でどう確かめたか | | --- | --- | | 1. フレーム番号の時計で、寿命 L の粒が ⌊L·fps⌋ 枚描かれる。L ∈ {0.05, 0.2, 0.37, 0.5, 0.7, 1, 2, 3} × f = 1…120、GPU の断片を通して数える (#1710) | `ParticleLifetimeTests.drawsTheFloorOfLifeTimesFrameRate`。
・刻みは `FrameTiming(.frameIndex)` から、`SketchRuntime` と同じ 2 行で面へ渡す。
・粒ごとに升を分けて置き、1 枚目と境目 (n 枚目・n + 1 枚目) で、絵の画素と GPU が書いた描く個数の両方を見る。

author: manfredss
body:
## Overview

Fixes #60162. With the Humming FP8 linear kernel, `fp8` checkpoints with per-tensor weight scales and online `fp8_per_tensor` / `fp8_per_channel` quantization crash while loading weights. On Ampere with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, Humming is the only FP8 linear kernel left (Marlin opts out of batch-invariant mode), so these models cannot start in that mode.

## Claims

- `Fp8LinearMethod` (non-block), `Fp8PerTensorOnlineLinearMethod` and `Fp8PtpcOnlineLinearMethod` load and run on Humming. GSM8K accuracy matches Marlin.
- On Ampere with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, these models start and are batch-invariant under the default torch.compile + CUDA graphs.

## Validation

Run on the official image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-92044241a02f05de51420d654daf669de20b4691` on an A40 (SM86), with the container's environment. The installed source files were checked against commit `92044241` by SHA-256 before testing. "This PR" means this diff applied to the installed package; the touched files are unchanged between `92044241` and this PR's base. Batch invariance uses the reproducer from #59086: request A alone, alone again, then batched with a longer request B; 48 greedy tokens; 3 rounds.

| Model / quantization | Flags | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `neuralmagic/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8` (`fp8`, per-tensor) | `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | crash: `self.stride(-1) must be 1 to view Float8_e4m3fn as Int ... but got 4096` | starts; A batched vs alone identical 3/3; GSM8K 0.790 |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-8B --quantization fp8_per_tensor` | `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | crash (same error) | starts; identical 3/3 |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-8B --quantization fp8_per_channel` | `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | crash (same error) | starts; identical 3/3 |
| Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8 | `--linear-backend humming` | crash | starts; GSM8K 0.784 |
| Qwen3-8B `--quantization fp8_per_tensor` | `--linear-backend humming` | crash | — |
| Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8 (control) | default (Marlin) | GSM8K 0.786 | — |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-FP8` (block, control) | `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | works, identical 3/3 | — |

GSM8K: `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 500` (5-shot).

`test_model_load_and_run` now also runs with `linear_backend="humming"` (`pytest tests/quantization/test_fp8.py::test_model_load_and_run -v`, same image):

| | auto | marlin | humming |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | passed | passed | **failed** (stride error above) |
| this PR | passed | passed | passed |

The rest of `tests/quantization/test_fp8.py` gives the same result with and without this PR on this GPU. Three `test_fp8_reloading` cases fail on the A40 either way with identical errors, and are unrelated to this change. `pre-commit` passes on the changed files.

## Details

**Missing layout tags.** `process_fp8_weight_tensor_strategy` / `process_fp8_weight_channel_strategy` return the weight as a `(K, N)` transposed view, and the online methods transpose it themselves. `replace_parameter` drops the parameter's `input_dim`/`output_dim`. Humming's `convert_linear_layer_to_humming_standard` reads those tags to detect the layout. Without them it assumes `(N, K)` and calls `.view(torch.int32)` on the transposed view, which fails. `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8` and ModelOpt's per-tensor FP8 scheme already retag the weight for Humming (added in #41652). This PR adds the same tags in the three methods that lacked them. Humming is the only FP8 scaled-mm kernel that reads these tags, so other kernels are unaffected.

**Batch-invariant `apply`.** In batch-invariant mode these methods call the kernel only when it is CUTLASS; otherwise they dequantize `layer.weight` and run `F.linear`. After Humming's `process_weights_after_loading`, `layer.weight` is in Humming's packed layout, so that fallback fails (`a and b must have same reduction dim, but got [s, 4096] X [256, 24576]`). Humming has its own batch-invariant mode (`use_batch_invariant` in its compute config), and the block-FP8 path and compressed-tensors already call it in this mode. This PR adds Humming next to CUTLASS in those checks.

**Notes.**
- Without batch-invariant mode, two identical requests on Humming were not bitwise identical (first difference at token 4). With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` they were. vLLM only promises this in batch-invariant mode, and it does not come from this change.
- ModelOpt's `KFp8StaticChannel` also stores the `(K, N)` weight without tags. I have no checkpoint to test it, so it is left unchanged.
- CI: the new `humming` case runs in the Quantization step (H200). The layout bug does not depend on the GPU architecture. I validated on SM86 only.

**Not a duplicate.** Searched open issues and PRs for Humming FP8 linear, the stride error message, the layout tags, and FP8 batch invariance on Ampere. #59460 also edits `scaled_mm/humming.py` (activation-quantization fallbacks) but not the weight layout or batch-invariant dispatch, and this PR does not touch `humming.py`.

author: synoet
body:
## What

Routines can now gate an event trigger on a yes/no question. Add **Only run if** to any activity trigger (for example "Is this email an invoice or a receipt?") and the routine runs only when the triggering email, channel message, document or task answers yes. The classifier is TypeSafe's [Jev](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api) model (`noul` questions, ~160 ms, $0.042 per million input tokens).

## How

- **`crates/jev`** (new): a generic yes/no classifier with no knowledge of routines.
  - Port: `YesNoClassifier::classify(usage, input: &serde_json::Value, questions)` returns a probability per question.
  - `JevClassifier` records each round trip as AI usage. A migration seeds `ai_pricing` for `jev-latest`.
  - `TypesafeJev` adapter: `POST /v1/systemone`. It retries 429/529/5xx/timeouts twice and does not retry rejections. It never logs inputs, questions or response bodies.
- **scheduled_action**
  - `EventFilter` gets an optional `condition` (trimmed, 1–500 chars). No migration: filters are JSON and matching ignores the extra key.
  - The gate runs in `EventDispatchService::dispatch` after authorization and before claim, never in the shared Kafka consumer. A matching filter without a condition runs unconditionally; otherwise the run starts if any matching condition scores ≥ 0.5.
  - Failures: unavailable checks retry for 10 minutes from admission, then skip as "unavailable". Rejections skip immediately.
  - Skips finish the event run as `cancelled` with `condition_not_met` or `condition_unavailable`. They also write an `action_execution_record` with `result.condition` (status, probability) in the same transaction, so they appear in history.
  - `EventContentAdapter` reads the content as the routine owner through the owning domain services, using the run's access receipt:
    - email: subject, sender, recipients, labels, reply-free body
    - channel message: text, sender, channel name, thread parent
    - document/task: name, kind, properties with option labels, Markdown excerpt
  - Each text field is capped at 8,000 chars. Every input also includes the event name, time and routine owner, so questions about "me" work.
  - Conditions are rejected (400) unless `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is set. The key is optional config, so the Doppler CI check stays green.
  - The event worker no longer dispatches a pending run that is already in flight. Runs stay pending during the check, so the 1s poll would otherwise start them twice.
- **Web**
  - An **Only run if** field per event trigger, behind the new `enable-routine-conditions` PostHog flag (on in dev mode). Trigger chips show `· if …`.
  - Run history shows **Skipped** rows ("Condition not met", with how likely the answer was yes on hover, or "Condition couldn't be checked"). Consecutive skips collapse into one expandable row.
- Regenerated the scheduled-action OpenAPI client, the SDK types and the GraphQL schema. The SDK is bumped to **0.2.1**, so **merging publishes** it; drop the bump commit if you'd rather not release yet.
- `docs/AGENT_GUIDE/navigation.md` documents the field and the skipped-run rows.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p jev --features outbound -p scheduled_action -p graphql_scheduled_action -p complete_graph`:
  - `jev`: 16 tests (wiremock adapter tests, service, value objects)
  - `scheduled_action`: 257 unit tests (new: gate, skip and retry-window dispatch tests, condition gate, content rendering, worker in-flight dedup, validation), 9 binary tests, 6 integration tests, and DB tests for `skip_pending` and for condition-agnostic matching
  - GraphQL crates: 60 tests
- Web: `vitest src/features/routines` (302 tests), `bun run check`, biome and `just check` all pass. Clippy is clean on the changed crates.
- **Real Jev calibration**: 12 realistic emails, messages and tasks in the gate's exact JSON shape scored 12/12 correct at 0.5. Yes answers scored 0.89–0.99 and no answers 0.01–0.17; statement-form conditions also work.
- **Local stack end to end** (Doppler keys, real Jev and models):
  - Created a routine in the UI with a condition on a channel trigger, then posted two messages.
  - The chatty message was skipped (2% likely yes); the help request ran the agent, which replied in the thread.
  - Both checks were metered under `jev-latest`.

## Before enabling

- [ ] Register `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` in Doppler `agent-schedule-service` (dev, prd).
- [ ] Create the `enable-routine-conditions` PostHog flag.
- [ ] Confirm TypeSafe's data-retention terms: the gate sends email bodies, channel messages and document excerpts.

## Not in this PR

Two bugs in local tooling surfaced while testing. Neither affects deployed environments:

- `local_env.rs` points services at the harness on port 8101, but it listens on 8080. This breaks local routine creation and agent runs.
- The harness's `INMEM_MODEL` default lacks the `anthropic/` prefix, which causes the composer's "Cannot verify model" warning. Production may hit this too unless Doppler sets `INMEM_MODEL`.

author: fuzzyslipper
body:
Two Den tasks under the compute exploration campaign 9496, as two commits on this branch: the compute pass foundation (9509) and its first candidate, screen-space ambient occlusion (9510). The candidate replaced the foundation's proof kernel, as 9509 intended, so the branch head is what to review.

## Commit 1: compute pass foundation (9509)

- Timestamp queries requested when the adapter has them; a timed pass resolves begin/end stamps into a mapped buffer read on a later frame without blocking, median over recent timed frames.
- Clean refusal when the adapter lacks compute shaders or the needed workgroup limits; the frame draws as before.
- Readout through `engine.renderer`, the live-debug panel and `rusty-scene-render`.

## Commit 2: screen-space ambient occlusion (9510)

- **Pre-pass.** A world view's opaque batches draw depth-only at half resolution before its render pass, reusing the shadow caster shaders (alpha masks and product caster stages included) with the world pass's culling. The camera sits in a spare slot after the shadow layers in the shadow matrices buffer, so no new shader variants.
- **Occlusion.** `ambient_occlusion.wgsl`: normal-oriented disc of 12 depth samples, normals reconstructed from depth, half-resolution output. Two paths from one module so they can be timed against each other: `cs_occlusion` (16×16 workgroup over a 32×32 depth tile in shared memory) and `fs_occlusion` (full-screen triangle). A separable 5-tap depth-aware blur follows (`fs_blur` with a `BLUR_AXIS` override constant).
- **Lighting.** The world pass multiplies the blurred occlusion into `Surface.occlusion`, which already scales only the ambient and hemisphere terms. Product shaders calling `standard_shade` get it for free; unlit materials and the viewmodel layer skip it.
- **Fallback.** No compute shaders or too-small workgroup limits → raster path, readout names the reason. Strength 0 or path off → no passes, frame pixel-identical to before.
- **Control.** `RustyEngineProductAmbientOcclusion` = `disabled` (default) | `compute` | `raster` and `RustyEngineProductAmbientOcclusionStrength` (default 1), written to the manifest as `renderer.lighting.ambientOcclusion`. Snapshots keep it; `rusty-scene-render --ambient-occlusion off|compute|raster` overrides it so one snapshot compares both paths. Marked "under evaluation" in the product project doc; `docs/lighting-and-sky.md` waits for the keep decision.
- **Readout.** `timing.rs` generalises the foundation into a `PassTimer` per pass. `engine.renderer` now carries `gpu`: the path taken, `computeRefused`, `timestamps`, `workgroups`, `occlusionTexture` and `passes` (`ao-prepass`, `ao-occlusion`, `ao-blur`) with median GPU ms. TypeScript contracts regenerated.

## Evidence (llvmpipe, this cloud container)

- Full `render-wgpu` suite passes with `WGPU_BACKEND=vulkan`, including every existing screenshot fixture (the new group-2 binding changes no pixels when AO is off). New `tests/ambient_occlusion.rs`: both paths darken 2.6% of a crate scene's pixels by more than 8 levels and brighten none, agree with each other within the screenshot tolerance, strength 0 is pixel-identical to off, half strength darkens about half as much, all three passes report timed frames. References blessed on llvmpipe.
- Shader composition test passes for every entry and feature set. Clippy with warnings as errors on render-wgpu, render-shaders, render-stream, product-host, csharp-product-runtime: clean. fmt, boundary, architecture and standalone checks pass. Browser typecheck and panel tests pass. Manifest parsing tests for the new setting pass.
- 1280×720 release frames on llvmpipe, 60-crate corner scene, medians: off 55 ms; compute 93 ms (prepass 1.7, occlusion 22.0, blur 10.1 ms); raster 81 ms (prepass 1.6, occlusion 14.0, blur 9.7 ms). The compute path is slower than raster on a CPU rasterizer, as the task anticipated; the deciding comparison is RADV on CraftSurvive.

## Not done here

- RADV timings and CraftSurvive snapshots (dungeon corridor, cave mouth) need a local run; the Den note drafts in the session list the exact commands.
- A C# `CameraView` entry for runtime control was not added: it needs the binding generator and .NET to regenerate the ABI identity, which this container lacks. The product-level setting above is the control path for the evaluation.
- No keep/drop decision: nothing is documented as a capability yet.

author: ekmett
body:
Native interface loading rejected ordinary datatype parameters, so even `Box a` could not execute. Decode parameters of kind `Type`, instantiate constructor and case types, and preserve lazy lifted fields in the existing runtime representation. Integer fields and nullary constructors retain their existing behavior.

The existing four-module GHC oracle now wraps an opaque suspended `Payload` call in `Box Payload`, passes it through polymorphic identity, and unpacks it across modules. Its five result rows are unchanged; no new fixture or test cases were added.

Validation: the previous decoder rejects those actual interfaces at the datatype parameter; the integrated decoder passes all three focused tests in each handoff mode, zero skips. Both backends match native GHC and an independent model, including the first compiled call forcing the suspended field. Compile plus both runs took about four seconds. Separate bounded decoder checks accept phantom parameters and reject unlifted parameters and existentials. Independent review accepted the change.

GADTs, constraints, representation polymorphism and broader constructor fields remain unsupported. Refs #1063.

author: nogod3524
body:
## What

- **BetterHuskyCT's Sync no longer takes you to HuskyCT.** With helper 1.11.0, pressing Sync opens HuskyCT in a **background tab**, or uses one already open. The helper reads there, the results arrive here, and the tab it opened closes itself when the sync is done. You stay on BetterHuskyCT the whole time.
- **The helper panel loses its own Sync button and the Diagnose recorder.** The automatic sync when HuskyCT opens stays.
- With an older helper, or none, Sync behaves as before and opens HuskyCT in front.

## How

A web page can only open tabs in front, and two sites' pages can only talk if one opened the other. The userscript manager can do both, so the helper now also runs on BetterHuskyCT:

- **Userscript header**:
  - `@match https://betterhuskyct.vercel.app/*`
  - `@grant GM_getValue / GM_setValue / GM_addValueChangeListener / GM_openInTab`. Before this it was `@grant none`.
  - **Tampermonkey will ask for these permissions on update.** The helper page now explains why (`helper.privacyBridge`).
- **Helper on BetterHuskyCT** (`startBridgeOnBhc`):
  - answers a `ping` with a `pong`
  - on `open`, calls `GM_openInTab(…/ultra/course, { active: false })` only when no HuskyCT tab has a fresh heartbeat
  - relays page ↔ HuskyCT through two queues in GM storage (`bridge.toHuskyct`, `bridge.toBhc`)
  - closes a tab it opened, 3 s after the sync's `done`
- **Helper on HuskyCT** (`startBridgeOnHuskyct`):
  - heartbeats into `bridge.huskyctAlive`. Background timers run about once a minute, so a tab counts as alive for 150 s.
  - only the **oldest live tab answers**, so HuskyCT is read once
  - a sync `request` goes to the same handler as a direct one (`answerSyncRequest`, split out of the old listener). Anything else is dispatched as the `MessageEvent` from BetterHuskyCT it would have been, so `sendTasksToBhc` / `sendGradesToBhc` / `nextFromApp` are unchanged.
  - a request already waiting when the tab finishes loading is answered if it is under 30 s old
- **BetterHuskyCT** (`src/lib/helper-bridge.ts`):
  - `pingBridge` once on mount
  - `openThroughBridge` returns one stable `bridgeTab`, so the sync's "only the tab I asked" check holds
  - `helperMessage` unwraps a bridged message only if **this window** posted it, wrapped, and naming a **HuskyCT origin**. The sync controller, the calendar's tasks receiver and the grades/materials receivers all go through it.
  - A background tab that never answers is given up on after **25 s** with *"probably need to sign in"* and an **Open HuskyCT** button, since a hidden sign-in page cannot be used. A tab in front still waits 90 s.

## Checks

- `tsc`, `eslint`, `next build`: clean
- `npm test`: 725/725 in the default time zone and with `TZ=Pacific/Auckland`

body:
## Summary

Make Settings understandable and enable complete development in locally hosted Codespaces through an enrolled companion, including private Git and pull requests.

## Related issues

Closes #287

## Changes

- Organize Settings into task tabs and separate environments, GitHub connection, and local computers; retain drafts, navigation, guides, and regional loading/error states.
- Add explicit owner-approved web control with finite resource ceilings, requested/applied revisions, seven-day maximum work leases, and durable stop/storage recovery.
- Reuse server GitHub authorization for repository-scoped private Git and typed PR create/find/get without exporting credentials to guests; support the first push to an empty repository.
- Update shared schemas, MCP consumers, native/browser/API tests, and English/Russian documentation.

Existing enrolled devices receive no implicit web-control approval. Existing VMs retain admitted resources and repository identity. The workflow engine and workflow definitions are unchanged; pending executions retain their continuation contract. The expanded MCP catalog uses the existing reconnect mechanism.

## Testing

- Command: `npm run verify`
- Outcome: Unit, integration, workflow, lint, formatting, type, and release-policy gates passed; platform/opt-in skips were classified.
- Command: `npm run verify:docker`

- Command: `npm run local:build`; `npm run typecheck:local`; targeted Testfold Settings/guide/locale and documentation consumers.

- Manual: Native APFS capacity/data preservation and real empty Git remote first/feature push checks.
- Outcome: Passed. Full private Mac VM through the production broker and GitHub PR lifecycle remains required immediately after deployment; component evidence does not substitute for it.
- Independent semantic review: Passed with no gaps against the complete original task baseline.
