author: sylvesterkaczmarek
body:
The fetcher decodes the user-supplied GitHub URL, then inserts the decoded Git ref directly into a new REST request URL. A branch named `release#blue` is consequently requested as `release`, with the rest treated as a fragment. When `release` also exists, the CLI can fetch and pin the wrong commit. A literal percent sign can instead cause an invalid-escape error or an extra round of decoding.

Escape the complete Git ref as a path parameter when building the commit lookup URL. Owner/repository handling, branch/subpath discovery, commit pinning and cache layout are unchanged.

## Validation

The regression drives `GitHubFetcher.Fetch` through an HTTP test server and real cache files for six valid branch names: plain, slash-separated, fragment-character, percent-character, literal percent-escape and plus-character forms. It checks the exact ref received by the server, resolved commit/subpath, bytes read from the correct revision, and reuse of a pinned cache entry. The fragment case includes a real decoy revision so selecting the wrong branch is observable.

- Three cases fail against unchanged main; all six pass after the fix.
- Each fixture name also passes `git check-ref-format --branch`.
- Full declarative package tests with the race detector: **123 top-level tests passed, 173 including subtests**. Ten opt-in live acceptance tests were skipped.
- Repository formatting, `./scripts/lint` and `git diff --check` passed.

```sh
go test -race -count=1 ./internal/declarative/...
./scripts/lint
```

GitHub documents the commit ref as a path parameter and permits special characters in branch names:
https://docs.github.com/en/rest/commits/commits#get-a-commit
https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/using-git/dealing-with-special-characters-in-branch-and-tag-names

Tested on macOS arm64 with Go 1.27.1. The test server is local; no real GitHub archives, cloud resources or live acceptance tests were used. No dependencies, public signatures or release metadata changed.

author: alexandrefimov
body:
Preserve declared i64 results for `sum:i64` aggregates. Isthmus exports this contract from SQL, but DuckDB currently returns HUGEINT and can expose values outside i64. This addresses the integer-sum case in DuckDB issue 276.

Keep DuckDB's wide accumulator and cast the final result to BIGINT. Select ERROR when overflow is omitted or offered; reject explicit overflow preferences without a supported behavior.

Regression coverage uses unchanged Isthmus plans for ordinary and grouped SUM, with empty-input, DISTINCT and overflow controls.

Validated at pinned DuckDB v1.5.5: 60 SQLLogic tests, 1772 assertions. The new regression fails before the fix. HTTPFS was skipped because it needs an S3 test environment. `git diff --check` passed.

body:
## Summary

Adds the connector's real-sshd fixtures and end-to-end tests (design §15): compose profile `connector` (`sshd-jupyter` with three sshd instances on 22/2223/2224, `jump`), `scripts/connector-fixture-keys.sh`, Go `fixture`-tagged tests, Playwright flows `e2e/tests/connector/` for A27–A31, and `.github/workflows/connector-e2e.yml` (path-filtered PR job, `workflow_dispatch`, weekly schedule).

Closes #48

## Scenarios

- A27: `a27-local-connector.e2e.ts` — `A27 a student pairs a local connector and runs a cell` (real Approve button; loopback-only listeners asserted on Linux)
- A28: `a28-ssh-connector.e2e.ts` (direct and through jump), Go `TestA28_RealSSHAndJump`
- A29: `a29-failing-stages.e2e.ts` (forwarding forbidden, Jupyter missing, token rejected), Go `TestA29_RealStages`
- A30: `a30-host-key-change.e2e.ts`, Go `TestA30_RealRotatedHostKey`
- A31: `a31-reconnect.e2e.ts` — `A31 offline then online runs the cell once`

## Decisions

- A30 rotates the host key on the third sshd instance (port 2224, own key volume) that the design left reserved, so the other tests' trust records are unaffected. `rotate-host-key` is shipped in the image.
- `locked` is implemented as a `jupyter_server_config.py` setting `c.IdentityProvider.token`, which overrides the injected `JUPYTER_TOKEN`; verified against a real Jupyter Server 2.21.1 (Go `token rejected` test passes), so the in-process fallback is not needed.
- `e2e/playwright.config.ts` ignores `**/connector/**` unless `CONNECTOR_E2E` is set, so the existing `e2e` job does not run them; `connector-e2e` sets it. The connector flows run with `--workers=1`.
- The flows alternate between the lab reader and instructor and pace Test connection starts, because the server limits a person to 5 pairing codes an hour and 6 connection tests a minute.
- Workflow path filter also lists `infra/compose.yml`, `scripts/connector-fixture-keys.sh` and the workflow itself. The weekly macOS/Windows jobs run `go test ./...` only (those runners have no Docker or Postgres); the Playwright flows stay on Linux.
- Env switches for running without containers: `CONNECTOR_FIXTURE_NO_DOCKER`, `CONNECTOR_FIXTURE_ROTATE_CMD` (skip the published-port check, replace the docker rotate command). CI sets neither.

- `pnpm lint` → no errors (13 pre-existing warnings)
- `pnpm typecheck` → pass
- `pnpm test` → 105 files, 1389 tests passed
- `pnpm scenarios` → 34 scenarios with tests, 34 recorded done
- `cd connector && gofmt -l . && go vet ./... && go vet -tags fixture ./... && go test ./...` → pass
- No Docker in this session: the compose images were not built here (`docker compose config` validates). The Go `fixture` tests (A28/A29/A30) and the Playwright flows A27–A31 (8 tests) were run locally, all passing, against a local sshd configured like the fixtures (same sshd configs, users, PATH, locked-user Jupyter config) and a real Jupyter Server 2.21.1. The first run in CI will be the first on the actual containers.

`FirestoreJournalSink.verify_chain()` verified only event-to-event linkage. A deleted tail could leave the shortened event chain internally valid while the persisted `next_sequence` / `head_hash` commitment still pointed at the missing tail.

- fail closed when the head is missing while events exist
- compare `next_sequence` with the actual event tail
- compare `head_hash` with the actual final event hash
- cover tail truncation and forged head metadata
- refresh proof test count from 612 to 614

- full verifier suite green
- collector-runtime green
- Vercel green
- no merge until exact-head evidence is complete

author: im-ian
body:
## Summary

- Kanban and canvas keep the pane layout mounted with `display: none`, so the active terminal stays there instead of in limbo.
- Skip PTY fit when that container has no non-zero layout box. FitAddon turns a 0px parent into a 2×1 terminal and reflows the scrollback.
- Theme refresh called `fit()` directly, so it uses the same guard. Limbo is still measured once before the first on-screen fit.

## Expected impact

Switching to kanban or canvas no longer resizes a live PTY down to a hidden or zero-size box. Opening the terminal again fits it to the pane, popover, or canvas card that actually has a box.

## Design notes

`shouldFitTerminal` is the single decision. A missing client rect and a 0×0 rect both refuse the fit. Limbo stays eligible until `fittedOnScreen` is set, because that host is a real 800×600 box used for the first measurement.

## Test plan

- `vitest run src/lib/terminalLimbo.test.ts` — 7 passed.
- Independent local review of the uncommitted diff found no issues.

## Notes

The running app was not opened to re-check the reported overlapping kanban popover.

author: ghdwlsgur
body:
## What

Refactor audit item 6 (priority 2/3). Before this PR, localrpc reached App actions in two ways, and the strict JSON decode was written out four times.

- **One route table.** Nine auth routes were a hard-coded `switch` in `serveHTTP` going through `dispatchAppAction`; they now sit in `appRoutes` as `authLoginRoutes` (new `auth_routes.go`). They are `/v1/auth/login/{sign-alias,sign-challenge,pending/sign-alias,pending/sign-challenge,restore-device-master,ensure-request-key}`, `/v1/auth/signup/{prepare,save-session-code}` and `/v1/auth/recovery-key/reissue-prepare`. `dispatchAppAction` and its two wrappers are deleted.
- **No re-encode.** `dispatchAppAction` ran the decoded input back through `json.Marshal`. `app_routes.go` warns against that because a round trip hides duplicate and missing keys. These routes now take the table's default path, so the action gets the bytes the App sent. A side effect: the password / RK24 / session code are copied one time fewer.
- **Result shaping as a hook.** The `suppressResult` flag and its type switch became the route field `shape func(data any) any`. `restore-device-master` answers `{stored: true}`, and `save-session-code` answers `{stored: true, promoted}`, the same as before.
- **One strict decode.** `decodeStrict(r, into)` means one JSON value, `DisallowUnknownFields`, nothing after it. All four sites use it: `serveAppRoute`, the old `dispatchAppAction`, `openSession` and `signRequest`.
  - `signRequest` gained `DisallowUnknownFields`. The App sends exactly the nine canonical fields (dragpass `app/src/shared/keeper/local-keeper-client.ts` `signApiRequest`), and no other dragpass client calls `/v1/request-signature`.
  - `openSession` gained the trailing-data check.
- `TestAppRouteAllowlistIsPinned` now lists the nine auth paths too, so the whole App surface sits in one pinned list.
- `docs/protocol.md`: every App request body is one strict JSON object, and the action receives the App's bytes.

## Tests

- Moving the routes is a refactor: the existing route tests (`app_login_pending_test.go`, `password_routes_test.go`, the signup / restore / save-session-code tests and the rest) pass before and after.
- `decode_strict_test.go` (red first):
  - `TestRequestSignatureRefusesAnUnknownField` answered 200 before, 400 now.
  - `TestOpenSessionRefusesTrailingJSON` answered 200 before, 401 now.

## Verification (local; GitHub Actions is down)

- Merged with origin/main (no rebase).
- `go build ./... && go vet ./...`: clean. `gofmt -l internal`: empty.
- `go test ./...`: 24 packages ok, 0 failures.
- dragpass e2e with this branch's `make build-macos-arm64` binary, dragpass at origin/develop (d860f657):
  - `DRAGPASS_E2E_KEEPER_BIN=<bin> pnpm test:app-keeper`: 3/3 passed.
  - `pnpm test:app-chat` (shared local ariadne :9999; sign-in goes through the moved auth routes): full run 43/47, 8 files. All 4 failures were in `app-chat-roles`: the first test timed out waiting for carol to join (`CHAT_ACCESS_DENIED` from sync), and the next three then got `CHAT_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`. Rerun of `app-chat-roles` alone: 9/9. That same first test also failed once under load with the #141 binary and passed on rerun there too, so it reads as an existing timing flake in that file, not this change.

author: wilfredonoyola
body:
La parte web del cobro (be#94, #92 y #152). **Va después de ng-creator-be#154**: usa `miPlan`, `planDeMarca`, `cobroConfigurado`, `iniciarSuscripcion`, `portalSuscripcion`, `suscripcionesAdmin`, `ajustarSuscripcion` y `duracionEstimadaSeg`.

## Mi plan (`/plan`)
Solo el titular de la cuenta. Muestra:
- el plan y su estado (prueba con días restantes, activo con fecha de renovación, cancelado, pago pendiente, vencido);
- las horas usadas del mes, que suman todas sus marcas.

Para elegir o cambiar de plan:
- Tiene el mismo selector mensual/anual y los mismos precios que la landing (`components/landing/planes.ts`).
- Sin suscripción, manda al checkout de Lemon Squeezy. Con una, cambia el plan sin checkout.
- "Administrar pago" abre el portal de Lemon Squeezy (tarjeta, facturas, cancelar).
- Al volver de pagar (`?pago=ok`) espera hasta 60 s a que llegue el webhook.
- Si el cobro no está configurado, los botones quedan deshabilitados con un aviso.

## Solo el dueño
- **Mi plan** aparece en el menú solo para el PROPIETARIO de la marca activa.
- Quien edita no ve precios ni cobro. Si ya no se puede subir, el aviso le dice que le avise al dueño.

## Aviso y subida
- `AvisoPrueba` (episodios) pasa a `AvisoPlan` (horas y días, desde `planDeMarca`). Con plan pagado aparece al llegar al 80% del mes.
- Al subir se manda la duración que lee el navegador (`lib/duracion-video.ts`, la misma función que ya usaba Grabar). Si no se puede leer, el backend estima por el peso.

## Admin (`/admin/suscripciones`)
- Para ADMIN: cada cuenta con su plan, estado, horas y fechas.
- Filtros: en prueba, vence pronto o pago pendiente, sin poder subir.
- Ajustes a mano: extender prueba, devolver horas, pasar a Interno, dar plan (con horas para Custom). Cada ajuste se muestra en el historial.

Mensajes, tipos, lint (5 avisos, tope 7) y build en verde.

author: meiiie
body:
Một phần #90 (T028, T030). T029b chờ KD-0005. Epic #79 · ADR 013 · FR-015, SC-004.

## Việc

Học sinh không được thấy đáp án hay một công thức chưa kiểm trong lời gia sư AI. PR này thêm job `POST /v1/kiem-loi-giang`. Module `tutor` của core (T034, làm tiếp) gọi job cho mỗi câu trả lời của mô hình, sau `/v1/filter`.

Mỗi câu của lời gia sư chỉ còn trong `cau_sach` khi mọi biểu thức của câu thuộc một trong ba loại:
- công thức khớp một dòng bảng đã khóa có trích dẫn (theo SymPy với `u(x)`, `v(x)` ký hiệu, hay bộ đọc định lí của `dong_cong_thuc`);
- trích nguyên văn đề (hàm, tử, mẫu, chỉ chuẩn hóa cách viết);
- trích nguyên văn một dòng bài làm, có khung «em viết …».

Câu quy tắc bằng lời chỉ được giữ khi trùng câu phát biểu của dòng bảng, hoặc bộ đọc định lí đọc ra đúng mục của dòng. Còn lại bị bỏ cả câu. Giáo viên nhận một mục `SAI` hay `KHONG_KIEM_DUOC` cho mỗi biểu thức bị bỏ. Lỗi, đầu vào sai hay quá giới hạn thì job không giữ gì.

Không làm: áp KD-0005 (T029b), module `tutor` của core, viết lại thang gợi ý.

## Hợp đồng

`specs/001-lat-cat-doc/contracts/math-v1.md`, mục `kiem-loi-giang`, nay có ví dụ vào và ra chạy thật, bảng sáu loại và điều kiện `DAT` của từng loại. Thêm `cac_cau` (giữ hay bỏ từng câu), `bieu_thuc[].cau`, `phan_vi_du` khi `SAI` và `loi` khi đóng mặc định. Core chỉ hiện `cau_sach` khi phản hồi có `cau_sach`, không có `loi` và `thay_bang_goi_y` là `false`. Ví dụ vào và ra vẫn khớp kết quả thật của job ở HEAD `467bb48`.

## Chỗ hợp đồng chưa nói, đều chọn chặt hơn

| Chỗ | Chọn | Lý do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bỏ đoạn hay bỏ câu | Câu có một biểu thức không `DAT` bị bỏ cả câu | Rút một đoạn giữa câu làm câu đổi nghĩa: «Hàm số đồng biến khi $x > 1$.» còn «Hàm số đồng biến khi.» |
| Trích bài làm | Trùng cả một dòng, chỉ bỏ khoảng trắng, khung «em viết / ghi / nộp…» đứng ngay trước | «Em viết $f'(x)=3x^2-6x$» khi học sinh chỉ viết vế phải là tự tính hộ |
| Công thức dạng quy tắc | Chỉ `DAT` qua bảng, không bao giờ là trích | «Em viết $(uv)' = u'v'$, đúng rồi.» không được xác nhận một quy tắc sai |
| Trích đề | Hàm, tử, mẫu tách từ `ham`; phải có `x`; không đổi thứ tự; nhận tiền tố `y =` hay `f(x) =` | Một mẫu số `1` không được thành «trích đề» cho mọi số 1 |
| Dòng bảng | Dùng được khi `trich_dan.tai_lieu` là chuỗi còn chữ sau khi bỏ khoảng trắng và tầng 1 tính lại ra `DAT` như lúc khóa; nhận thêm `tieu_de` | Job báo `tang` 1, 2, 3 thì phải có căn cứ; dòng điểm tới hạn cần tiêu đề để đọc lại |
| Toán viết trần | Danh sách trắng: ngoài chữ Latin (cả tiếng Việt), chữ số, khoảng trắng, dấu câu của lời văn và các dấu tùy chỗ `( ) + - * / '`, mọi ký tự là dấu hiệu toán | Danh sách đen để lọt dấu giống dấu bằng (`꞊`, `゠`, `⹀`), ngoặc `⟨ ⟩`, khoảng `]0; 2[` (lượt rà độc lập) |
| Ký hiệu chung đứng riêng | `y'`, `f'(x)` đọc như thuật ngữ «đạo hàm»; `x₀`, `y(x₀)` là ký hiệu điểm; `$x$`, `$y'(0)$` vẫn `KHONG_PHAN_TICH_DUOC` | Không mang giá trị nào; câu chứa chúng vẫn qua luật ứng viên quy tắc như khi viết bằng lời |
| Chữ né bộ nhận | Ký tự toàn khổ, ký tự định dạng (ZWSP), dấu thanh kiểu mới, dấu gạch Unicode đều quy về trước khi nhận | Họ câu lọt đã ghi ở #116 và ở lượt rà độc lập |
| `du_kien_bao_ve` | Nhận, không dùng | Lọc lộ đáp án là việc của `/v1/filter`; mọi biểu thức `DAT` là dòng bảng, chuỗi của đề hay dòng học sinh tự viết |

## Kiểm (HEAD 467bb48)

Máy Windows, Python 3.13, SymPy 1.14. Test sandbox cần Linux; CI chạy cả bộ.

- `python -m pytest tests/test_loi_giang.py` (từ `services/math`): **147 đạt, 1 bỏ qua** (test router, chỉ Linux). Trước lượt sửa: 107 đạt.
- Cùng lệnh với `test_dong_cong_thuc`, `test_thang_mau`, `test_leak*`, `test_bao_mat_dich_vu`, `test_verify_tang23`, `test_tang1`: **449 đạt, 2 bỏ qua, 3 hỏng**. Ba ca hỏng là test sandbox của `test_bao_mat_dich_vu`, lỗi môi trường `preexec_fn is not supported on Windows`; PR không đụng sandbox.
- Bộ ca KD-0005 bản 2 (#116, chưa áp, SHA-256 bản vá `8f4dda3eb2676924dc9eab23bb4a0aa4d6e75c8511c840374d1495cf16f76928`), chạy cục bộ theo luật kiểm 1–5 trong đầu tệp ca: **189 ca, 0 lỗi nghiệm thu**; trích bảng (loại 1) giữ **18/18**, trích đề (loại 7) giữ **10/10**. Kết quả trùng với HEAD `93ad1b5`. Hai mục báo cáo: đoạn `DAT` nằm trong câu bị bỏ (LG-3-24, LG-5-20).
- Thời gian trên bộ ca đó: p95 0,064 s mỗi câu. Ca nặng tự dựng (40 đẳng thức sai khác nhau, đủ 40 đoạn toán): 2,7–5,3 s qua bốn lần chạy, cùng khoảng với `e82b3c7` (2,9–4,2 s) vì thời gian nằm ở SymPy mà lượt sửa không đụng; dưới hạn 12 s. Máy đang tải nặng nên số dao động.
- `node --test .claude/hooks/*.test.mjs`: 192/192. `node scripts/kiem-khoa.mjs`: không có khóa.

Ca gài đáp án có trong test: «x = 2 là điểm cực đại» (viết trần và trong `$…$`), `$f'(x)=3x^2-6x$` của chính bài, «Cực đại bằng hai», «Cực đại tại 0, cực tiểu tại 2», «Hàm số nghịch biến trên khoảng (0; 2)», quy tắc sai đi kèm «đúng rồi», `x＝２` toàn khổ, ZWSP chen giữa «bằng». Tất cả bị bỏ.

### Lượt rà độc lập và lượt sửa

Lượt rà độc lập trên `93ad1b5` cho phán quyết FIX FIRST. Nó tìm câu job giữ nguyên mà `/v1/filter` cũng cho qua. Mỗi ca thành một test hồi quy với phán quyết viết sẵn. Commit test `0314139` đứng trước commit sửa `65f6e92`. Trên mã của `93ad1b5` cả 17 test mới đều hỏng.

| Ca lọt | Test |
| --- | --- |
| `y bằng 3 x x trừ 6 x.`, `Ta có 3 x x ‒ 6 x.` | `test_ca_lot_ra_doc_lap_bi_bo[nhan-viet-cach]`, `[gach-so]` |
| `Ta có y ꞊ 3 x x ‒ 6 x.`, `x ᐀ 2`, `x ⹀ 2`, `x゠2` | `[bang-chu-sk]`, `[gach-doi-canada]`, `[gach-doi]`, `[gach-doi-kana]` |
| `x thuộc ]0, 2[`, `Nó đi xuống trên ]0; 2[.`, `Đỉnh ⟨0; 2⟩, đáy ⟨2; −2⟩.` | `[khoang-nguoc-phay]`, `[khoang-nguoc]`, `[ngoac-goc]`, `test_khoang_nguoc_khong_bi_tach_cau_o_dau_cham_phay` |
| `Giá trị ở đáy là −2.` | `[tru-unicode]`, `[tru]` |
| Trích dẫn chỉ có khoảng trắng | `test_trich_dan_chi_co_khoang_trang_khong_phai_trich_dan` |
| Thêm cùng họ: `x \x00 2`, `y ‐ 2 ‐ x`, `x 🟰 2`, `〔0; 2〕` | `[ky-tu-nul]`, `[gach-noi]`, `[emoji-bang]`, `[ngoac-mai-rua]` |

Chạy lại các script tấn công của lượt rà (`ca1.py`…`ca7.py`, `fuzz.py`) trên `467bb48`:
- mọi ca lọt đã xác nhận nay bị bỏ; 28 câu đổi từ giữ sang bỏ (27 câu trong đó `/v1/filter` cũng cho qua), đều là câu có ký hiệu toán; thêm ca trích dẫn chỉ có khoảng trắng của phần đóng mặc định;
- 2 câu đổi từ bỏ sang giữ, đều đúng ý: `Em xem $f(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 + 2$ nhé.` (trích đề) và `Em xem $y'$ nhé.` (thuật ngữ);
- `ca4.py` (quy tắc sai phải bỏ, quy tắc trong bảng phải giữ) không đổi dòng nào;
- `fuzz.py`: 4000 câu ngẫu nhiên, không lần nào job lỗi bên trong.

Câu còn lọt cả hai lớp đều là lời thường không ký hiệu, ngoài phạm vi cổng này: ghi ở [#137](https://github.com/meiiie/du_an_em_linh/issues/137#issuecomment-6012139057).

Đột biến từng luật mới rồi chạy test nhắm tới nó: 6/6 bị bắt. Bỏ nhân viết cách (2 test hỏng), bỏ dấu trừ trước chữ số (2), đổi danh sách trắng về danh sách đen (9), cho tách câu trong khoảng (2), nhận trích dẫn khoảng trắng (1), thay `y'` bằng rỗng thay vì «đạo hàm» (3).

## Còn để ngỏ

1. **Thang gợi ý không qua cổng.** Đo bằng `do_thang.py` trên thang gợi ý v0 (tệp vàng T013): 272/397 câu bị bỏ (69 %), 73/176 thang bị thay cả lời. Trước lượt sửa: 309/397 (78 %), 101/176. Thang mẫu Sư phạm: 220/323 câu (68 %), 67/152 thay cả lời; trước: 244/323 (76 %), 82/152. Phần giảm đến từ việc đọc `y'`, `f'(x)` như «đạo hàm» (lý do «y′ đứng riêng» từ 137 và 105 câu về 0); danh sách trắng không làm tăng số câu bị bỏ. Ngưỡng của ADR 013 là 20 %. Lý do chính còn lại là câu ứng viên quy tắc không khớp dòng bảng: là lý do duy nhất ở 183/272 câu v0 và 153/220 câu Sư phạm. Cần chủ repo quyết ADR 014 («Đề xuất», #116) và lab Sư phạm viết lại thang (đặt toán trong `$…$`, dẫn `[n]`). Không nới cổng khi chưa có quyết định.
2. **Từ vựng.** Đang dùng nguyên văn KD-0005 bản 2. Lượt rà «đội đỏ» ghi ở #116 đo bản 2 lọt 61/75 câu dò. Câu không có từ quan hệ trong danh sách vẫn qua, ví dụ «Phương trình có hai nghiệm.», và câu tiếng Anh. Bản 3 hay ADR 014 sẽ thay.
3. **KD-0005 chưa áp** (T029b): `services/math/kiemdinh/loi-giang/` chưa có trong PR này. Khi

author: dominiquevienne
body:
Measures #674 and refutes its premise. **No adapter in this PR** — the route it needs is established instead of guessed.

### #674 says `/jobs/` is the list. It is not.

Exercised 2026-10-06. Neither `/jobs/` nor `/jobs-in-malawi/` is an advert list: both answer 200 and each carries exactly **one `<article>`**, which is the page's own prose, with **no `JobPosting`** anywhere in its JSON-LD (only `Place`, `Organization`, `WebSite`, `BreadcrumbList`, `WebPage`, `Person`). `/jobs/` names itself **`wp-json/wp/v2/pages/96`** — a PAGE, not an archive — and its listing sits behind a JavaScript category chooser. `/jobs-in-malawi/` has also lost a third of its bytes since 2026-09-17: **182 497 → 119 551**.

> *And counting a keyword measured the INTERFACE:* five matches for «Showing/results» are all UI strings — two menu toggles, a select's `data-no_results_text='No results match'`, and a noscript notice.

### Where the adverts are

`/wp-json/` registers **795 routes**, among them WP Job Manager's own publicly readable **`/wp/v2/job-listings`**, plus `job-types`, `job-categories`, `job_listing_tag` and `company`. Records: `type: job_listing`, `status: publish`, `id`, `date` (freshest read was the same morning), `link` as `/job/<slug>`, `title`, `meta`.

### The host states its own counts per type — a witness that is NOT our extraction

| jobs | | not jobs | |
| :-- | --: | :-- | --: |
| Internationally Recruited | 314 | **Tender** | **192** |
| Job Vacancy in Malawi | 202 | Grants for Individuals | 165 |
| Internship | 12 | Grants for NGOs & Institutions | 111 |
| VISA Sponsorship Job | 4 | Trainings, Conferences & Fellowships | 79 |
| | | Grants for Businesses | 60 |
| | | PhD & Postdoc | 53 |
| | | Consultancy | 42 |
| | | Opportunity · Scholarships | 28 · 10 |
| **≈ 532** | | **≈ 740** | |

**So the separation #674 asks for is the HOST'S OWN taxonomy and not a classification we invent.** *Emitting the post type as «jobs» would inflate the count by more than half, and the first page by date is entirely grants and fellowships.*

**The sum of 1 272 is NOT the board's size**: a record carries several types — one read showed `[65, 633, 63]` — so the sum double-counts, and **no total is stated anywhere**.

### Two more things an adapter needs, measured rather than assumed

- **Zero contact is exposed on this route**: `_application`, `_company_name` and `_job_location` are **empty on 5 of 5**, and the payload holds **no e-mail address at all**. *`_job_salary` is free text on 2 of 5 and one of them is a grant amount, so it is not a salary.*
- **The availability surface is the LISTING**: `_filled` is present on 5 of 5 — a per-record flag on the API itself, which is the `closure: listing` shape of #1003.

*And the city pages are named `<city>-jobs-and-tenders`, so they MIX both in one path and cannot separate what the taxonomy can.*

### I reproduced a defect I repaired the day before

The first version of this card's line used `·` as an inner separator for the taxonomy list — **15 where the contract allows 2** — which is exactly the malformation I fixed on `worklinkcy.md` in #1036 **yesterday, in the same field**. `AContentClaimSaysWhichOfThreeStatesItIsIn` caught it.

> **The rule did not protect its own repairer; the guard did.** *That is the argument for writing guards rather than remembering rules, and it is worth more than the measurement above.*

Suite **1549 OK**, gating the commit. Guard on each exact path in the same command as the act, `bin/fetch-body.py` throughout, as `Claude-User`.

body:
## 问题

`upload_media` 是**每一种回复类型都走的那一个入口** —— image / video / voice / file —— 而它的 `http(s)` 分支走的是 `download_to_file`：**只管大小，别的都不管**。

而这个 URL 就是 **Agent 回复里的东西**，抓到的字节随后**上传到钉钉** ⇒ 一段 prompt、或它读到的一页内容，可以把抓取指到本机：

```
http://127.0.0.1:8080/secret.png
http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/
http://10.0.0.5/internal.png
```

实测三个**全部被本机请求**（探针驱动真实的 `upload_media`，只替身传输层）。

而且 `requests` **默认跟随重定向** ⇒ 哪怕加了 host 检查，一个公网 URL 仍能 3xx 拐进内网。

## 修法

改用与 #3556（企业微信）**同一条**路径：`safe_get(..., guard="always", stream=True)` + `save_response`。

- `guard="always"` 用的是**无条件**那版地址检查（不是 `web_security_ssrf_protection` 那个默认关着的开关 —— 那个是给工具连本地 dev server / 局域网 MCP 用的，**投递路径不该因为它关着就变成 SSRF 通道**）；
- 声明长度仍在**读第一个 chunk 之前**检查，读取过程中仍限大小 + 限时 ⇒ **#3300 要求的那个上限没有变化**；
- 落盘仍是 temp + `os.replace` 原子替换。

## 测试

新增 `tests/test_dingtalk_media_ssrf.py`，15 例，**直接驱动真实的 `upload_media`**（只替身传输层与 DNS 解析，守卫本身是真的）：

- 未修复代码上 **13 红 / 2 绿**
- 修复后 **15 全绿**
- 精确关联套件（11 个文件，含 `test_media_download` 与 4 个既有 `test_security_ssrf_*`）**116 passed / 0 failed**

覆盖：5 个非公网地址 × 2 种 media_type（image / file）**共 10 例，连请求都不该发出、也不该上传到钉钉、且不留下任何文件**、公网图片正常上传（`stream is True` + `allow_redirects is False` + 落盘文件名是清洗后的路径段）、**公网 3xx 到回环被拒且第二个地址从未被请求**、声明超限在读 chunk 前被拒、**query string 里的 token 不进文件名**、以及一条把「必须用无条件守卫」钉住的断言。

同时更新既有的 `tests/test_dingtalk_bounded_media_download.py`：`cdn.example` 现在需要能解析（守卫在请求前解析并拒绝不可解析的 host —— 这正是它该做的），加 autouse fixture 提供可解析地址；stub response 补上 `is_redirect` / `is_permanent_redirect`（`safe_get` 读的是这两个属性而不是 `status_code`）；`_stub` 的 patch 目标从 `media_download.requests` 改成 `url_safety.requests`（下载现在走 `url_safety`）。

> 与 #3556 的关系：那是企业微信的 `_download_remote_media`（三处调用点），这是钉钉的统一入口。两处各自独立，`url_safety` 的守卫是同一份（两个 PR 改同一文件，若同时合并需去重 —— 后合的那个删掉重复段即可）。

**Submitter note**

Model: Claude Opus 5.5
Harness: Claude Code

# sha3-256-r5-exploratory: byte-aligned GLL+20 connector with charged advice and a pre-registered fresh-coin measurement, time_log2 = 49.35

## Summary

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| time_log2 | **49.35**, a hard cap that holds on every run (2^49.341) |
| success probability | 0.40 under H2 and H3 (the bound is 0.9791) |
| memory | 2^65 declared: the advice runs, bounded through H1's time. The algorithm itself uses < 2^23 bytes |
| preprocessing | 49.34 |
| advice | 271 bytes: the published colliding pair of Guo et al. |
| certificates | 16 organizer-verifiable collisions of 135-byte messages (the schema maximum; the first 16 by attempt index); an organizer experiment replays all 21 collisions found |

- **The measurement is pre-registered and uses independent coins.** The plan was written down
  before the run: label, seed rule, sample sizes, statistics and confidence levels. Attempt i
  draws its coins from SHAKE-256 of its own seed SHA-256(label || i), through the specified
  Fisher-Yates coin map.
  - 32,768 attempts: 992 accepted (3.03%).
  - The first 768 accepted spaces, each with exactly the specified 2^32-pair window: E output a
    pair in 21 of them (21 collisions in total).
  - H2 uses the one-sided 99% Clopper-Pearson lower bound of that count, s0 = 0.015.
- **No model allowance.** v4 asked for 1/19 of a Markov value. Here H2 is the measured per-space
  event itself. The Markov value appears only as context.
- **The score is set by the advice charge.** The advice is the published pair of Guo, Liao, Liu,
  Liu, Qiao and Song. Its connector and brute-force runs are charged at twice their published
  single-core times at 2^38 primitives per core-second (H1): 2^49.30. Its trail search is
  charged at 32 times the exact cost of our own executed search, which returns the same trail
  core bit for bit: 2^43.94.
- **Not claimed:** any improvement on the published method. The new parts are the byte-aligned
  connector steered by the published difference, the measurement, and the accounting.

## What changed since v4, and why

A committee simulation of v4 found no concrete flaw. It predicted not_evaluable for four
reasons:
1. The statistical bounds treated sequential MT19937 outputs as i.i.d. This premise was implicit,
   and earlier dossiers rated the same premise unsupported.
2. H2 relied on a 1/19 clustering allowance and on pooled development spaces outside the
   specified window.
3. H2's wording did not match the event that E detects.
4. H1 contained an unmeasured memory clause.

| v4 issue | v5 |
| --- | --- |
| MT19937 streams, implicit i.i.d. premise | per-attempt SHA-256 seeds with SHAKE-256 expansion; the premise is stated in H2 and H3; os.urandom-seed and homogeneity cross-checks |
| H2 = 1/19 of the Markov value | H2 = 99% lower bound of the measured per-space Bernoulli count in the specified regime |
| H2 says "contains a collision" | H2 says "E outputs a pair" |
| space test, so H2 and H3 conditioned on the past | the space test is removed; spaces are i.i.d. and success follows exactly from two single-attempt probabilities |
| H1 memory clause | removed; memory is bounded through H1's own time bound |
| P replaces the authors' GPU trail search | stated explicitly, and charged at 32 x P, the margin of the accepted precedent 654cb3d2 |
| 2^36 primitives per core-second | 2^38: 5 GHz x 8 micro-operations per cycle x 6.9 primitives each |
| attack used P's hard-coded output | the algorithm reads its trail from the advice pair; P is only the charged surrogate |
| C++ E and P not shipped | embedded as inert text; the Python E replays every certificate; the two E implementations agree |
| 160 organizer trials, vacuous check unstated | 256 trials; the vacuity is stated |
| replay from stored MT states | replay recomputes each seed from (label, i) |
| linearisation search outside the work counter | built and charged in setup S |

## Approach

Notation: L = pi o rho o theta. A 135-byte message, plus the 0x86 padding byte and the zero
capacity, forms one block, so 520 state bits are fixed. x = L(A0) is the round-0 chi input.

1. **Advice.** The published pair gives four differences: the round-0 difference beta0_pub, the
   round-1 difference beta1_pub, and the trail alpha2, alpha3 after rounds 1 and 2. The trail is
   core No. 3: w1 = 127, w2 = 24, P45 = 55/2^19.
2. **Why a new connector.** The published difference cannot be reused at p = 8. The fixed-bit
   equations plus its round-0 equations have one contradiction (rank 1403 of 1462 equations),
   though they are consistent at p = 4.
3. **Connector (rounds 0-1), per attempt.**
   - beta1 is fixed to the published one.
   - The difference phase picks, row by row in a random order, affine sets of input differences
     that contain the published beta0 row.
   - The value phase fixes each row's difference (the published one first) and its value
     equations.
   - Non-full linearisation, from a table built in setup, makes the 127 round-1 conditions
     linear.
   - The attempt is accepted if the system is consistent with DF >= 33. Each attempt is capped at
     2^18 work units and makes at most 21,930 coin draws.
4. **E.** E enumerates 2^32 pairs (x, x xor beta0) of the space in Gray order and tests the 10
   round-2 rows (probability 2^-24). The full 256-bit digests decide.
5. **Caps.** At most 2^15 attempts and K = 256 enumerated spaces. The algorithm halts at
   the first collision.

| spaces where E outputs a pair | 21 / 768 (s-hat = 0.0273; 99% lower bound 0.01548) |
| collisions | 21 |
| Markov-Poisson context | 0.0265 per space; s-hat is 1.03 times that |
| C++ E against Python E | all 197,291 C++ round-2 passes in 768 spaces confirmed; identical pass sets on 768 windows |

author: peters
body:
Part of #1268.

## Purpose

Progressive playback previously accelerated only when the receiver was more than a second behind, then stopped at 0.4 s. This controller trims lag above its current target and attempts progressively closer targets, down to 0.15 s, while playback stays calm.

## Behavior

- The target starts at 0.4 s. Four calm seconds lower it by 50 ms, down to 0.15 s. Lag above 1 s requests 1.5×; smaller excess lag requests up to 1.08×. Trimming starts more than 50 ms above the target and normally stops within 20 ms of it; conservative deadlines may restore normal speed earlier. Near the edge, a slower fallback accounts for lag sample age and preserves time to acknowledge the command and restore normal speed.
- Buffering for at least 500 ms at a target below 0.4 s raises the target and its session floor by 50 ms when the episode opened with less than 0.8 s lag. Short interruptions and large startup buffers do not abandon a target. Pauses do not count as calm time or seed buffering episodes.
- Notification and reply receipt times preserve buffering duration and ordering, including notifications queued behind a request. Newer notifications remain queued. Receipt metadata stays private; public Event construction and next_event signatures remain compatible.
- An explicitly refused speed-up disables further trimming. An uncertain speed-up triggers restoration to normal speed. An existing fast rate is restored when there is insufficient headroom for another trim; normal-rate restoration has at most three attempts. Lifecycle and stall confirmations restore normal speed first, including a possibly applied speed-up whose reply was lost. Failed commands retain buffer backoff learned while they waited.
- Internal LOAD, poll, and rate checks inspect every status in the reply before selecting the original LOAD session. Failed rate commands reconcile queued lifecycle notices before retrying; cleanup sends STOP only for the original media session, which also protects replacement media if ownership changes during cleanup. Mixed-session notifications stay queued for lifecycle handling. A detached lifecycle batch is checked for replacement media before any fallible confirmation; confirmation restores inspect newly queued replacement media before and after each command. Ownership loss ends the cast even when an older restore failed. Replacement media ends this cast without STOP. The event backlog is bounded at 64; overflow closes the connection and fails outstanding requests instead of silently losing a terminal notice.
- HLS does not use the adaptive rate controller.

No UI change, so no GIF applies.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p horizon-chromecast --lib`: 125 passed, including loopback TLS takeover/overflow tests, multi-status replies and lost-speed-up/rejected-restore takeover ordering (both new regressions fail on 85548d63), mixed-session notifications, delayed lifecycle confirmations after lost speed-ups, retained buffering backoff, fallback rate admission from delayed samples (these three regressions fail on 6c8124b3), stale-IDLE/takeover batch ordering and takeover during failed confirmation restores (both regressions fail on 69f0e317), delayed notification ordering, rate refusal/lost replies, and simulated sustained convergence through every target down to 0.15 s with conservative restore deadlines.
- Full local workspace tests, speech-enabled UI tests, formatting, maintainability checks, blocking and strict Clippy tiers, and `git diff --check` passed in the isolated checkout. The advisory pedantic tier reports the existing excessive-bools lint in `horizon-cloud::Description`; that unrelated source is unchanged.
- Updated `docs/testing/procedures/chromecast-live-progressive.md` separates automated controller checks from physical receiver measurements. This revision has not been tested on a physical TV; 0.15 s is an attempted controller target, not a measured glass-to-glass latency guarantee.

author: noorallah
body:
## What was wrong

Round 4 of the pricing check (PRCQ-48). Under "buy 10 get 1", an order of 2 BOX of 12 carries an engine line: 0 sold, 2 PIECE free, `free_promotion_id` set. A client that sent the order back as it read it sent that line as figures, and a figure sent is a figure typed: the goods stayed free, the offer was no longer named, no claim was staged, and an offer with a budget of 2 free units gave 4.

## What it does now

`SalesOrderService._without_what_the_engine_gave` runs at the top of `_replace_lines`, so on every save of a stored order:

- a line that sells nothing and names its offer (the loose pieces of a box line, or a gift of another product) is dropped where it comes back at its line number, and the engine adds it again if the offer still gives it. It is reconciled on its line number, so it keeps its id;
- free units an offer put on a line itself, echoed as the same figure, are read as silence (the "24 PIECE, 2 free" half of the finding);
- the "0 free" of a line sent back **beside** its own free line is silence too.

The stored row decides, never the description. A free-only line a person typed names no offer and stays theirs; a figure that differs from the offer's is typed and stands.

## One thing the round's table got wrong

The row "PUT with only the box line (the desktop's way)" sent `free_quantity: "0.0000"` on the box line, because the script echoes every non-null field of the read. That is the documented refusal (D-SELL-41) and is byte-for-byte what the desktop sends when somebody types 0 in the free box, so it still refuses the offer. The desktop's ordinary save omits `free_quantity`, and that shape already got its free line back; a test now pins it.

## Quotation

Checked, not changed: a quotation stages no claim, so there is no budget to get round, and `QuotationLineWrite.quantity` is `gt=0`, so an echoed free line is refused by the schema before the service sees it.

## Tests

`tests/unit/test_offers_count_stock_units.py`: seven new cases; four fail without the fix. Also run and passing: `test_promotions.py`, `test_promotion_budgets.py`, `test_sales_order_module.py`, `test_principal_claim_free_goods.py`, `test_offer_use_is_one_figure.py`, `test_imports_and_assets_through_the_chain.py`, `test_sales_document_terms.py`, `test_mrp_where_the_price_is_struck.py`, `test_claude_md_names_real_things.py`. `ruff`, `black --check` and `mypy` clean on the changed files. No migration.

author: rhofield
body:
## Problem

A math narration beat opened with "Here's a puzzle." (0.8 s). Continuity compared each segment only with the previous one:

- The 0.8 s first segment passed automatically ("no predecessor").
- All three attempts at segment 2 failed continuity at 0.55–0.64 similarity against that clip. Against the reference voice, the same attempts score **0.84–0.89**.
- Against the reference voice, the 0.8 s clip itself scores **0.59–0.64**. It is the outlier, and a listen confirmed the jump between segments 1 and 2.

Separately, every accent failure also reported `text unavailable`, because text is only checked after accent passes. That doubled the noise in caller warnings.

## Change

- `ContinuityValidator` keeps a window of accepted speech covering at least `WINDOW_SECONDS = 3.0`. It compares **speaker identity** with the provider's `reference_audio_path` plus that window. **Loudness** is still compared with accepted speech only.
- With a reference voice, the first segment is checked too. With neither a reference nor a predecessor, behaviour is unchanged.
- Evidence gains `reference_voice` and `anchor_seconds`. `loudness_difference_db` is `None` when there is no accepted speech yet.
- `base_tts` calls `validator.advance(selected)` instead of assigning features. `previous` is an immutable tuple, so snapshot and restore across decay rounds still work.
- After a measured accent failure, text is `skipped` (reason `accent failed`) and is left out of `rejection_reasons`. A missing classifier still reports `unavailable`.
- Version 1.3.5 and changelog entry.

## Verification

- Full suite: 533 passed and 8 skipped before the final test adjustment. Continuity and acceptance tests after it: 62 passed.
- New tests cover window trimming, the reference check on the first segment, the provider reference wiring, and the skipped text status.
- Replayed the real beat's 14 candidate clips through the new validator with the real encoder:
  - Segment 1 now fails at 0.59–0.64, so it would be retried.
  - Segment 2: one attempt fails on loudness against the quiet segment 1; the other two pass at 0.87–0.91.
  - Segments 3–6: every attempt passes.

## Caveat

Very short opening sentences may now get some false failures on speaker similarity. With `allow_fallback`, that means extra retries and a warning, never a blocked render.

**What changed**

A step that passes the run's gate but that the march refuses (from 2.7e-11 m on the tests' rocket) counts too.
- **#172** warns on every flight with a static margin, quoting 0.073 calibres and setting no threshold.
- **Where they show:** in the library, as `stability:` lines with a `kind` in `hpr sim`'s text and JSON, and in Python. The docs (VALIDATION, CLI and Python pages) and the regenerated examples show them.
- **Limits, recorded in ADR-181 and VALIDATION:** a model on its own normal-force table prints none. A staged flight asks the whole stack's model, so it can over-warn.

**Verified**
- Each edge is tested: the step at 2.6e-11 m against 2.8e-11 m and the ±1 mm cases; the lip at ×(1 ± 1e-9); the tip at 29.99° against 30.01°; Mach 1.2 exclusive, and NaN.
- Mutation probes fail the lip and tip tests.
- The full gate passed. After the review fixes, `test` (2045 tests), `refs`, `site`, `clippy` and `docs` passed again.
- Reviewers: physics, validation, code and docs. Their blocking findings were fixed: attribution to the body the run fails on, the step's true edge, and the docs' normal-force-table and staged-flight notes. A Sonnet re-review's remaining claim was disproved by a probe (a stepped part carries a slope of −0.145/rad).

body:
## Problem

The Android EAS Development Build fails in `:app:processDebugMainManifest` because both `expo-notifications` and `@react-native-firebase/messaging` declare Firebase Messaging default notification metadata.

Conflicting keys:

- `com.google.firebase.messaging.default_notification_channel_id`
- `com.google.firebase.messaging.default_notification_color`

RNFirebase remains the FCM transport. `expo-notifications` is only used as the local/system presentation layer for foreground notifications.

## Scope

- remove duplicate `expo-notifications` static manifest ownership for default channel/color
- preserve `enableBackgroundRemoteNotifications`
- keep `@react-native-firebase/messaging` unchanged
- keep runtime creation of Android channel `laz-general`
- do not patch generated Android files or `node_modules`

## Architecture

```text
FastAPI / FCM
      ↓
@react-native-firebase/messaging
      ↓
PushNotificationsProvider
      ↓
expo-notifications (local foreground presentation only)
```

Android channel ownership remains runtime-owned by `src/features/notifications/system.ts`, where `ensureSystemNotificationChannel()` creates `laz-general` with HIGH importance, vibration, red light and default sound.

## Changes

`app.config.js` changes from:

```js
[
  'expo-notifications',
  {
    color: '#D30A12',
    defaultChannel: 'laz-general',
    enableBackgroundRemoteNotifications: true,
  },
]
```

to:

```js
[
  'expo-notifications',
  {
    enableBackgroundRemoteNotifications: true,
  },
]
```

## Security

- no credentials or secrets changed
- no Firebase/App Check boundary changed
- no push token handling changed
- no arbitrary notification routing change

## Quality / SDLC

- focused branch from current `main`
- one-file configuration fix
- no generated native file edits
- no `node_modules` patch
- existing CI remains authoritative

## Verification

Required gates:

- NeuroMarket Mobile CI
- new Android Development Build
- confirm `:app:processDebugMainManifest` succeeds
- install APK on physical Android
- verify FCM foreground/background/cold-start behavior
- verify `laz-general` channel is created and foreground copies remain visible
- regression-test background radio playback

## Deployment impact

A new Android Development Build is required because this changes native Expo configuration.

```bash
npx eas-cli@latest build --platform android --profile development
```

## Rollback

Revert this single commit if the runtime notification presentation regresses.

body:
## Зачем

Собственный E2E-тест 1.2.1 на securecode-demo-app и повторный отчёт независимого тестировщика показали, что секреты всё ещё мешают анализу, а один путь их раскрывал.

## Безопасность

- **Утечка через Архитектора `analyze`** (с 1.1.0): Архитектор читал файл из Git без маскирования. Если находка была в файле с ключом, значение уходило в модель вместе с файлом и попадало во фрагмент кода и diff отчёта. Теперь Архитектор и отчёт читают замаскированный текст. Исправление, которое меняет строку с секретом, показывается в отчёте, но не пишется в `--patch-dir` (предупреждение: применить вручную и сменить секрет).
- Демо `p917_real_local_demo.py` отправляет модели файлы целиком и теперь останавливается до запроса к модели, если найден секрет.

## Исправлено

- **CWE-798 доходит до решения**: доказательство по секрету содержит строки вокруг значения с маркером вместо значения.
- **Файлы с секретом полностью доступны агентам в замаскированном виде**: «модельная» версия детерминированного исполнения пересобирает якоря Поиска и доказательства сканеров по замаскированному тексту (те же id и строки, хеши замаскированных байт). Репозиторий, где секрет есть в каждом файле, больше не блокирует Поиск, а находки сканера в файле с ключом проверяются Аудитором.
- **Поиск переспрашивает модель до двух раз** после ответа не по схеме, в том числе в одноходовом режиме, который использует `analyze` (в 1.2.1 повтор был один и только в многоходовом). Промпт закреплён хешем, поэтому в него ничего не дописывается.
- Каталог без Git или без коммита → код `4` и понятное сообщение.
- Версия 1.2.2.

## Проверка

- Живые прогоны DeepSeek ($0.002–0.01 за прогон) на четырёх корпусах: демо-приложение, «только секрет», «ключ и SQL-инъекция в одном файле», «три файла: SQL, команда, ключ». Итог всегда FAIL с ожидаемыми CWE, CWE-798 подтверждается, исправления VALIDATED. В 14 финальных прогонах значение ключа не встретилось ни в одном отчёте, патче или логе.
- Полный набор тестов: 3836 passed; 40 падений в `test_local_product_cli`, `test_artifact_upload`, `test_enterprise_end_to_end`, `test_quality_isolation` есть и на чистом HEAD (локальное окружение Windows).
- pre-push quality gate пройден.

- После двойного повтора: 10 живых прогонов на тех же корпусах — все HEALTHY, все ожидаемые CWE найдены (в одном прогоне повтор сработал и спас результат).

author: awaissulhry
body:
(Was stacked on #403 — merged; main merged in.)

## What was wrong
The ads strategy can hold a monthly spend cap per category or per product (W1-1/W1-2), and the Owner decided (D5 = A) that engines enforce it: ad groups holding a capped product get low bids until the 1st. After #403 only the market's cap stopped anything. Nexus also had no way to floor one ad group on its own. Floors existed only per campaign (`Campaign.bidsSuppressedAt/By`), and a campaign restore, re-floor or base-bid move by any engine rewrote every ad group of the campaign. So an ad-group floor could not have an owner that other engines respect.

## What changed
- **Schema (additive):** `AdGroup.bidsSuppressedAt`, `bidsSuppressedFloorCents`, `bidsSuppressedBy` (nullable). These are the ad-group twin of the campaign's floor columns. Migration `20261006c_ad_group_bid_floor` (3 × `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`). `baseline.sql` regenerated. AdGroup's ownership, grants and RLS are unchanged (no new model).
- **Ad-group floors** (`ads-bid-suppression.service.ts`):
  - `suppressAdGroupBids` floors the ad group's default bid and targets to the stop bid, remembers each bid and stamps the owner.
  - `restoreAdGroupBids` gives them back, retry-safe like the campaign restore.
  - Ownership holds both ways:
    - `restoreCampaignBids`, `refloorCampaignBids`, `applyBaseBidDelta` and `revertBaseBidDelta` skip ad groups floored on their own. So do rank's absolute base bid (`ad-rank-defend.job.ts`) and dayparting's multiplier entry (`ad-dayparting.job.ts`).
    - Inside a campaign that any engine or a person has floored, the ad group's owner only hands its memory over. Whoever lifts the campaign floor puts those bids back.
  - Engines that already skip remembered bids (the bid optimiser, rule `bid_apply`, Claude's bid tools) treat these targets as floored, as they do under a campaign floor.
- **Spend per scope** (`ads-strategy/spend.ts`, pure decisions plus one batched read):
  - Month-to-date spend per product comes from the daily advertised-product report. Each `PRODUCT_AD` row's ad is mapped to `AdProductAd.productId`.
  - Each product's spend counts on every category or product cap it falls under: its own row, its parent's, and its categories' (the resolver's chain).
  - Spend from ads Nexus cannot tie to a product counts on no cap. It is reported as `unattributedSpendCents`.
- **Budget engine** (`ads-budget-enforce.service.ts`):
  - When a scope's spend reaches its cap, every ad group of the market's enabled campaigns that holds ANY product under that cap is floored at its stop bid. This is the safer rule: the other products in that ad group stop too.
  - The floor is given back on the 1st, or when the cap is raised or removed. Only this engine's own ad-group floors are given back.
  - The preview gets `scopeCaps` (cap, spend, reached), `productSpendThrough`, `unattributedSpendCents`, `adGroups` (floor now, give back, or held, with the reached cap and the stop bid) and totals `adGroupsSuppressing/Restoring`.
  - The run line adds `adGroupFloors=N adGroupRestores=M` only when there are any. Each ad group asks the engine guard for its permit, so the market's "most actions per run" counts it.
- **A cap of 0 means no cap**, as for the market (#403) and as a €0 month in the Budget Manager. A category or product cap of 0 is never listed, never reached and floors nothing, and the read marks it `noCap`.
- **Claude's `restore-campaign`:** the preview counts only what the restore gives back. It names the ad groups that stay at their own floor (`staysFloored`).
- **Read:** each category or product cap in `ads-strategy` carries `thisMonth: { spendCents, reached }`, plus `scopeSpend` (`spendThrough`, `unattributedCents`). `readBy` of the monthly cap is now "budget engine (market, category and product caps)". Honesty test and texts updated.

## Where the product spend comes from, and how fresh it is
`AmazonAdsDailyPerformance`, `entityType = PRODUCT_AD`: Amazon's advertised-product report, **Sponsored Products only**. It is requested for yesterday at 01:50 UTC (`ads-report-create-ap`), polled every 10 minutes and ingested every 15 minutes. It is whole days and never today, so a category or product cap is seen as reached the morning after the spend that reached it. Sponsored Brands and Display spend is not counted on a product cap. The preview's `productSpendThrough` and the read's `scopeSpend.spendThrough` name the last day covered.

## LIVE EFFECT after deploy
**The caps count spend up to YESTERDAY** (Amazon's daily reports: campaigns at 01:15 UTC, advertised products at 01:50 UTC). Today's spend is never in them, so **a market, category or product can overshoot its cap by about one day of spend** before its bids drop.

- **At deploy:** three empty nullable columns on `AdGroup` (a push migrates production). With no category or product cap set, nothing else changes. The new skips in rank, dayparting and the campaign restore only match ad groups floored on their own, and none exist.
- **Once the Owner sets a category or product cap:** when that scope's month-to-date Sponsored Products spend reaches it, every ad group holding a product under it drops to its stop bid (else 2 cents) until the 1st. No ad group is paused. This includes the other products in those ad groups (the Owner can split ad groups to avoid this). Other ad groups of the same campaign keep serving. A campaign-level stop, a Min-bid window or a person's restore of the campaign does not lift these floors. As with #403, this acts only while the budget engine runs live (the Budget Manager's engine label says which mode it is in).
- **What the Owner sees:** the `ads-strategy` read gives each category or product cap's spend so far and whether it is reached. The Budget Manager preview lists the scope caps and the ad groups it would floor, with the cap and the stop bid.

| Schema drift | `npm run check:drift` | pass (474 models, 474 tables' columns) |

body:
Tests, release tooling and docs for MIK-7324.COV.3 and NFR.BUILD.1 C5/C6. No product code changes.

**Inventory.** Adds 11 rows to `docs/release/v4.0.0-critical-functions.tsv` (8 critical, 3 standard) for enforcers merged since #2872. They cover fail-closed delivery recording, stdio judging, peer-error screening and authorship, the OAuth send-time cleartext backstop and redirect policy, and the literal-key refusal in `accounts.keys`. Skipped by the doc's own rule: the stdio busy refusals (a global in-flight budget), record-size bounds (capacity), and delivery plumbing. The doc's Critical count goes to 330.

**Gaps closed.** Graded against probe run 37423361628 (at 409e95619), two of the new rows were below 95%:
- `OAuthClient::client_for`, 81.25%. The test drives the backstop directly. Cleartext off this machine is refused as a policy refusal that names the field without the URL. https takes the configured client, and loopback http takes the unproxied one. With no unproxied client, it fails closed rather than using the proxied client.
- `Gateway::judge_and_commit`, 93.75%. A request with no method goes through the real staged dispatch. The gateway-built refusal is judged and sent as written: the client's id, -32600 "Missing method", and no result.

**One-command grade.** `scripts/release/coverage_grade.sh <rev>` commits `<rev>` plus `scripts/release/coverage-probe.yml` to a `throwaway/coverage-grade-*` branch, waits for the run, and grades `<rev>`'s own source. It passes only when the run concluded success, `critical_function_coverage.py` exits 0, and the new `critical_path_coverage.py` (with a unit test) exits 0. `--self-check` regrades the baseline run and requires its known FAIL: one row, `query_and_commit` at 91.67%, which #3132 closes. It was run locally: it passes, and a copy with the expected row altered fails.

**Scope status.** The COV.3 row records the interim evidence and stays pending until the freeze grade.

**Base merge.** #3133 added `the_send_client_refuses_cleartext_off_machine_on_its_own` at the same place as this PR's `client_for_refuses_cleartext_and_never_proxies_loopback`. The merge keeps this PR's test and drops that one. It asserts everything the dropped test did (off-machine http refused as a policy refusal, https and loopback http served), plus the routing and fail-closed checks above. Nothing in the tree cites the dropped name.

author: yuto-trd
body:
## Description

Exporting to a filename with no extension or an unrecognized extension could throw `NullReferenceException` in `FFmpegSharp.MediaMuxer.Create`. `OutputFormat.GuessFormat` returns a non-null wrapper even when its native `AVOutputFormat` pointer is null, so the existing null-coalescing guard did not detect the failure.

Validate the native format pointer before opening the output file or creating the muxer. Invalid output formats now produce the intended descriptive error without creating an empty file or truncating an existing file.

## Affected areas

- [ ] `Beutl.Engine` (rendering / scene / track)
- [ ] `Beutl.ProjectSystem` (project / document persistence)
- [ ] UI (`Beutl.Editor`, `Beutl.Editor.Components`, `Beutl.Controls`)
- [ ] `Beutl.Extensibility` (plugin abstractions)
- [ ] `Beutl.NodeGraph` (node editor)
- [x] `Beutl.FFmpegIpc` / `Beutl.FFmpegWorker` (media IPC boundary)
- [ ] `Beutl.Api` (server API client)
- [ ] Build / CI / docs only

## Breaking changes

None. No public API changes.

## Test plan

- Added `EncodingOutputFormatTests` covering missing and unrecognized extensions with both new and existing output files. All four cases reproduced the reported `MediaMuxer.Create` null-reference before the fix; after the fix they verify the descriptive error, file preservation, and rejection before requesting media.

author: lusoris
body:
## Summary

Every Ubuntu tox leg of the Builds workflow failed on master (`48b068659`, `19e096750`) with `KeyError: 'dis_enc_width'` in `test_read_dataset_dis_enc_width_height`. The test was right and the code was right: the CI fixture cache wrote an old revision of a tracked fixture over the checkout. `prune-corrupt-fixtures.sh --restore-tracked`, which every workflow already runs right after the restore, now puts tracked files back to the commit's revision.

## Root cause

- The `python/test/resource` cache (Builds, Build, Tests workflows) holds the whole directory, including the 112 files git tracks there. Its key hashes `python/test/*_test.py` and `python/test/resource/test_*.py`.
- #2137 changed `test_read_dataset_dataset3.py` (`enc_width` / `enc_height` added). No exact key matched afterwards, so the `restore-keys` prefix restored the newest older cache (`vmaf-fixtures-resource-v1-513dfd84...`, log: "Cache hit for restore-key"), and `actions/cache/restore` wrote the pre-#2137 fixture over the checkout.
- The run then failed, so the success()-gated save of a fresh key never happened, and every later run restored the same stale file.

## Fix

- `scripts/ci/prune-corrupt-fixtures.sh` takes `--restore-tracked`: after pruning, every tracked file under the root that differs from the index is printed and checked out again. Untracked downloads stay. Without the flag a developer's uncommitted edit is left alone.
- `build.yml`, `libvmaf-build-matrix.yml` and `tests-and-quality-gates.yml` pass the flag on their existing "Drop unusable restored fixtures" step.

## Evidence

- Reproduced locally: with the pre-#2137 `test_read_dataset_dataset3.py` written over the checkout, `pytest test/routine_test.py -k dis_enc_width` fails with the CI's `KeyError`; `prune-corrupt-fixtures.sh --restore-tracked python/test/resource` reports `restoring tracked file python/test/resource/test_read_dataset_dataset3.py` and the test passes.
- `scripts/ci/test-prune-corrupt-fixtures.sh` gains a git-tracked case (stale tracked file restored, empty tracked file kept, untracked download kept, edit kept without the flag): 13/13 with this pruner, and the stale-tracked-file case fails with master's pruner (12/13).

### Reproducer

```bash
bash scripts/ci/test-prune-corrupt-fixtures.sh
git show 8eabe7c56^:python/test/resource/test_read_dataset_dataset3.py > python/test/resource/test_read_dataset_dataset3.py
bash scripts/ci/prune-corrupt-fixtures.sh --restore-tracked python/test/resource
(cd python && python3 -m pytest -q test/routine_test.py -k dis_enc_width)
```

## Type

- [x] `fix` — CI fixture cache

## Checklist

- [x] Commits follow Conventional Commits.
- [x] Touched files lint-clean (shellcheck, shfmt via the commit hooks); no native file touched, so no clang-tidy lane applies.
- [x] I did not modify any `assertAlmostEqual(...)` score.
- [ ] ADR — not applicable: bug fix in an existing CI step.

## State

- [x] `docs/state.md` — `T-CI-FIXTURE-CACHE-STALE-TRACKED-2026-10-06` added to Recently closed (opened and closed by this PR).

## Deep-dive deliverables (ADR-0108)

- [ ] **Research digest** — no digest needed: trivial CI fix, cause and evidence above.
- [ ] **Decision matrix** — no alternatives: only-one-way fix (the cache key cannot exclude tracked files; restoring them after the restore is the step that already exists).
- [ ] **`AGENTS.md` invariant note** — no rebase-sensitive invariants (fork-only CI files).
- [x] **Reproducer / smoke-test command** — pasted above.
- [x] **CHANGELOG fragment** — `changelog.d/fixed/ci-fixture-cache-tracked-files.md`.
- [x] **Rebase note** — `docs/rebase-notes.md`, "CI fixture cache: tracked fixtures put back after the restore".

author: noonghunna
body:
## What

`catalog.sh register --dry-run` wrote `scripts/lib/profiles-local/engines.d/<engine>.yml` whenever the compose's engine was unknown, even though the run ended with `[promote] dry-run — nothing written.`. A declined confirm left the file behind the same way.

## Why it happened

`catalog.sh` wrote the engine profile itself, in its own Python, *before* handing the spec to `promote.py`, which owns the plan, the `--dry-run` exit and the confirm. Nothing downstream could stop a write that had already happened.

It also hid itself in the tests: `test-catalog-cli.sh` runs several `--dry-run` registers with the same engine before its real round trip. So the round trip's "engine profile written" check passed on the file the dry runs had leaked.

## Fix

- **`catalog.sh`** puts the engine profile in the spec as `local_engine_profile: {id, yaml}` and no longer writes anything itself.
- **`promote.py`** handles it as part of its gated plan:
  - **Validation:** local layer only (the core layer refuses it: a curated engine profile is a PR to `scripts/lib/profiles/engines/`). A safe id. An existing profile is never overwritten; it's planned as `keep`.
  - **Plan:** it lists `write …/engines.d/<id>.yml (new local ENGINE profile)`, or the keep line.
  - **Write:** it's written first among the local artifacts. That puts it after the plan, the `--dry-run` exit and the confirm, and before the post-write `registry-emit` check, whose cross-reference validation needs the engine to exist.

## Validation

- **`test-catalog-cli.sh`:** new check 2d asserts that the dry runs leave no engine profile, that the dry-run plan names it, and that a second dry run still writes nothing. The existing round trip now proves the real register writes it through `promote.py`.
  - **Negative control:** against master's `catalog.sh` + `promote.py`, all three new checks FAIL.
- **`test_promote.py`, `TestLocalEngineProfile`, 5 tests:** a dry run writes no profile but plans it; a real write lands it; an existing profile is not overwritten; an unsafe id is refused before any write; the core layer refuses the key.
  - **Mutation check:** dropping the write, or overwriting existing profiles, turns them red.
- **Suites:** `test-catalog-*`, pytest modules (143 passed), local-slug-shape and the tree-wide guards, 32/32.

author: skyyuriofficial-stack
hellerve
body:
Closes #477.

new objects that reference each other in a cycle could not be applied in any order. netbox's device `primary_ip4` is the common case: device -> ip (`primary_ip4`) -> interface (`assigned_object`) -> device (key). apply ran everything outside the cycle and stopped with `unresolved references`, and re-running stopped the same way.

`plan` now breaks each such cycle at a ref that can wait, an optional attr that is not a key field: that create omits it, and an update of the same uid with no backend id sets it once the targets exist. the plan shows both, so nothing is written that the plan did not show.

- where several nodes could defer, the first in plan order does, so `primary_ip4` waits rather than the ip's `assigned_object`. a cycle held together only by key or `required` refs is left whole and fails at apply as before.
- apply ordering runs an update after the create of the same uid.
- the drift report counts such an object as missing, not also changed.
- write-only backends (`plan_write_only`) keep every object a whole create: an emitter resolves no ref against a backend, and the django emitter rejects updates.
- the generic adapter resolves an update without a backend id from the same write, as netbox, nautobot and infrahub already did (including on journal resume).
- `docs/external-adapters.md` states that an update without a `backend_id` targets an object a create earlier in the same `ops` made. existing external adapters only see this when a plan has a cycle.

verified against netbox 4.6.2: an inventory declaring a device, interfaces, a scoped prefix, an ip, and the device's `primary_ip4` plans as

```
plan: 9 to create, 1 to update, 0 to delete
...
update:
  dcim.device {"name":"leaf01"}
    primary_ip4: null -> "c4a0c0f0-ef8a-4c7f-9b0a-2ff3a4d14fd1"
```

applies as `applied 10 operations`, netbox shows the ip as the device's primary, and a replan is `0 to create, 0 to update, 0 to delete`.

tests: planner (breaks at an optional ref, never strips a required one, leaves an unbreakable cycle, write-only keeps whole creates, no cycle adds nothing), apply ordering, drift, and the generic adapter. fmt, clippy, the workspace suite and `scripts/agent_fixtures.sh` pass locally.

author: portare-ch
body:
Result of the suspend testing on build `cee17f8d`, with a correction to the earlier experiments.

- The earlier arms (and the previous day's) suspended through `/sys/power/state`, which skips `sleep.d/pre/004-cpuidle-state1`. cpu0 kept its deep idle state disabled, the CPU cluster's domain never entered its sleep state (0 entries across seven suspends in `pm_genpd` debugfs), and `apss` never counted. None of them reached `cluster_sleep_1`.
- Through `systemctl suspend`, 120 s arms: shipped resumes; bandwidth-only (`suspend_floor_cx=N`) resumes; CX-only (`suspend_floor_bw=N`) **restarts**. The DDR/LLCC sleep-set bandwidth is the half the firmware needs. Dropping the CX request measures nothing: `cxsd` stays 0, other holders keep CX enabled in the sleep set (gcc without runtime PM, `pcie_0_gdsc` for wake, enabled subdomains at the enable corner).
- 1090 did not make the drop survivable. ramoops in DDR came back empty after the restart, so the reset is cold; the 7.3 minidump-over-SRAM path is what would see it.
- Method note for future runs: `systemctl suspend`, `suspend_stats/success` as the completion signal, the cluster count as proof the sleep was real.

author: joyjeet045
body:
## Summary

Port of the RocksDB replicated state provider from `youyuanwu/kuberic#76` to the current V2 runtime, as a standalone application on the published `kuberic-runtime` crate (following the `kuberic-page` pattern). The original V1 implementation targeted the deleted `kuberic-core` API and is preserved at tag [`archive/pr-76-rocksdb-v1`](https://github.com/Joyjeet045/kuberic/tree/archive/pr-76-rocksdb-v1).

- `RocksState` implements `engine::DurableState` + `StateProvider`: typed `Put`/`Delete`/`Merge` mutations in a versioned, CRC32-checked envelope validated against canonical `WriteBatch` bytes; user data, applied/committed LSN, retained operation and undo history are written in **one** synced RocksDB write.
- Duplicate LSNs are idempotent only for identical bytes; gaps and conflicting reuse fail explicitly. Commit only advances up to applied progress and is a cheap synced metadata write.
- Exact-boundary copy reconstructs the frozen committed LSN from current values + undo history, producing byte-identical, bounded chunks across repeats and restarts; install writes a new generation and atomically publishes the active pointer.
- Retained catch-up fails closed when the requested range predates retained history.
- `RocksService` (`StatefulServiceReplica` via `DefaultReplicatorFactory`), read gating on partition access, and a `ReplicaHost` binary with `PUT/GET/DELETE /keys/{key}` and `POST /batch`; restarts use `ApplicationStorageState::Established`.
- Pinned `rocksdb =0.24.0`, default column family, fixed profile and deterministic `append-v1` merge operator; native I/O runs on blocking workers.
- CI installs `clang`/`libclang-dev`.

## Deviations from V1 (documented in the crate README)

- Copy is a deterministic logical snapshot instead of a physical checkpoint bundle (bounded by `MAX_COPY`).
- V1 epoch-rollback callbacks are not reintroduced; V2 runtime owns authority fencing and verified prefixes.
- Undo/operation history is retained without automatic pruning.

## Validation (Linux, `rust:1-bookworm` + clang/libclang)

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --locked --workspace --all-features` — 13 passed (10 `kuberic-rocksdb`, including a primary→secondary in-process replication test, idempotency/gap/conflict, restart recovery, exact-boundary copy repeatability after restart, chunk verify/finish retry, malformed envelopes, merge determinism, reserved keyspace)
- `git diff --check`

author: joyjeet045
body:
## Summary

Port of Reliable Collections (transaction log + transactional replicator + named-dictionary state manager) from `youyuanwu/kuberic#78` to the current V2 runtime, as a crate on the published `kuberic-runtime`. The original V1 implementation targeted the deleted `kuberic-core` API and is preserved at tag [`archive/pr-78-reliable-collections-v1`](https://github.com/Joyjeet045/kuberic/tree/archive/pr-78-reliable-collections-v1).

- `StateManager` / `Transaction` / `ReliableDictionary<K, V>` with `get`, `contains_key`, `insert`, `set`, `update`, `remove`, `get_or_add`, `add_or_update`, `clear`, `entries`; provider create/remove inside transactions; `ReliableValue` with stable type ID and version.
- Repeatable begin-time snapshots, read-your-writes, optimistic serializable validation (per-key versions, delete tombstones, provider/registry revisions). Commits are serialized through a gate spanning validation → `StateReplicator::replicate`; the V2 engine durably applies on the primary before `replicate` returns, so validation always observes every prior commit.
- One versioned, checksummed envelope per commit; retry identities with bounded retained results, `committed_result`, and confirmation of unconfirmed outcomes.
- The checksummed log (torn-tail recovery, corruption rejection, exclusive lock, generation checkpoints) is the `DurableState` persistence. Committed progress is a cheap durable record; checkpoints occur only under retained-log budget pressure or explicitly, so lagging peers can be repaired from retained history and frozen copy boundaries reproduce identical bytes after later commits and restarts. Retained ranges fail closed after reclamation.
- `ReliableCollectionsService` implements `StatefulServiceReplica` via `DefaultReplicatorFactory` with read/write access gating; backup/restore before attachment.

## Deviations from V1 (documented in the crate README)

- One crate with modules instead of three crates.
- V1 lifecycle channels and application epoch-rollback callbacks are replaced by V2 runtime authority fencing and election-safe prefix settlement.
- Reads inside a transaction on the primary may observe locally applied records whose quorum commit is in flight; a successful commit (including read-only) confirms the observed prefix.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --locked --workspace --all-features` — 15 passed (12 for this crate, including primary→secondary in-process replication, conflicts/write skew/tombstones, retry identity, copy retry determinism after commits and restart, retained-range fail-closed, torn tail/corruption, checkpoint/backup/restore)
- `cargo doc --locked --workspace --no-deps` with `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`
- `git diff --check`

Supersedes `youyuanwu/kuberic#78`.

author: basszurich-cyber
body:
## 📋 Summary

**Related Issue**: follows #313

The decision of 6 October 2026: a trial needs a card, one per card, and the flow is the upstream app's exactly. The app blocks with its access cover, the cover opens a web page for the card, and the app unlocks itself once the plan is on Stripe. The web app comes back for that one page and nothing else, in simeonlabs.com's own design. This PR wires that, and fixes two things that would have failed on the first real checkout. Deploy it before `SIMEON_DESKTOP_BILLING_REQUIRED` goes on.

## 🎯 What

1. **The web app is the billing page, and only that**, `app.simeonlabs.com/billing`, in the site's own clothes (its card style, pill buttons, colours and type). Two screens, the way the upstream app does it:
   - **Adjust your plan**: the title, a Monthly/Annual switch with the "Save 20%" pill, the three cards. Choose plan opens Stripe Checkout without a plan and the Customer Portal's plan change with one. The current plan's card is grey with a "Current plan" badge. One footer line: Manage billing on Stripe, Cancel trial or plan.
   - **You're all set**: the app icon and wordmark, the Download button, and for a person sent from the Mac's sign-in a button back to finish signing in. "Adjust your plan" opens the cards.
   - A frame: the Simeon wordmark, "Signed in as … · Log out". The banners are gone. The web app's front page goes to `/billing`. The site's pricing buttons were `<span>`s that did nothing; they now open the billing page with the plan chosen.
2. **No web app in the Mac's sign-in path.** A browser with no session goes to the API's own Google sign-in (`sign_in_url`) from `/loginDeepControl` and `/desktop/login`, and comes back. The web app is needed only to pay.
3. **The window's access cover**, the way the upstream app handles "no plan": `GetSandAccessStatus` answers from the allowance (payment required; "Start Trial" for a person who never had one, "Check Access" after); `EnsureSandBox` and the recreate calls refuse the box with `permission_denied` and no hint header, which the Mac's host connector reads as access denied and the window shows as the cover; the renderer patch points the cover's button at the billing page. The window keeps asking for its box, so paying on the web is all it takes.
4. **Stripe Billing's charges in the shop's webhook handlers.** `charge.succeeded`, `charge.pending` and `charge.failed` insisted on linking every charge to a shop checkout or order and raised `UnlinkedPaymentError` otherwise. A subscription charge comes off an invoice with none of that metadata, so the first real charge would have failed the worker. `belongs_to_the_shop` lets such charges through.
5. **`GET /v1/plans/subscription` while billing is off** answered `inactive` for everyone; it now answers `unmanaged`/`free` while no plan is required or the e-mail is exempt, so nothing sends anyone to billing before the flag is on.

## 🤔 Why

Billing is live but gated off. Each of these is in the path that opens when the gate opens, and the flow had to be the upstream app's: card first, one trial per card, the app unlocking on its own, and a page that looks like the site a visitor just came from.

## 🔧 How

- `BillingPage.tsx` with `BillingPage.module.css` carrying the site's values (`sites/simeonlabs.com`: `--ink`, `--font`, `.btn`, `.plan3`); `(main)/page.tsx` redirects to `/billing`; `PlanCards.tsx` removed.
- `sand/dashboard.sand_access_of`, `sand/box_broker.require_a_plan`, `integrations/stripe/payment.belongs_to_the_shop`, `plans/endpoints.current_subscription(free=...)`, `desktop/endpoints.sign_in_url`.
- One more `BRAND_PHRASE_REPLACEMENTS` entry in the renderer patch, counted like the others; a bundle without the string records 0 rather than failing.
- `docs/services-billing.md` sections 1, 3 (steps 6 and 7), 7 and 8; `docs/services-core.md` on the sign-in page.

## 🧪 Testing

- [x] I have tested these changes locally
- [x] All existing tests pass (`uv run task test` for backend, `pnpm test` for frontend) — see notes
- [x] I have added new tests for new functionality
- [x] I have run linting and type checking (`uv run task lint && uv run task lint_types` for backend)

Run here: `tests/desktop/test_app_sign_in.py`, `tests/desktop/test_allowance.py`, `tests/desktop/test_endpoints.py`, `tests/plans`, `tests/sand/test_connect.py`, `tests/sand/test_box_broker.py`, `tests/integrations/stripe`: 159 passed; the 12 failures are the proxy tests that fail on `main` too, plus the dunning test that needs the e-mail renderer binary. New tests: `tests/integrations/stripe/test_billing_charges.py`, `tests/plans/test_endpoints.py` (free while off, exempt, inactive once required), `tests/sand/test_connect.py::TestSandAccessWithBilling`, the sign-in tests' redirect to the API's Google sign-in. Desktop: `agent-run-error`, `simeon-account`, `renderer-brand-patch` and `renderer-pinned-anchors` pass (the sign-out test fails on `main`). Web: `pnpm typecheck`, prettier and eslint pass. The billing page was rendered in a browser against the local API with a signed-in test user (Playwright, desktop and phone: a new visitor, after a checkout, with a current plan). Ruff, mypy and `scripts/check_names.py` are clean.

### Test Instructions

1. Deploy the API and worker, then unpause Vercel and deploy the web app once (its 100-deploys-a-day cap was hit before; nothing should auto-deploy on every push).
2. As a new customer: on simeonlabs.com click Try it free. Sign in with Google, see "Adjust your plan", choose Standard, save the test card on Stripe, and come back to "You're all set" with the Download button. The worker log should show `plans.subscription.synced` and no error on the charge events.
3. Rebuild the Mac app. Sign in with that account: no cover, straight in, the usage summary saying trialing with 1,000,000 credits.
4. With `SIMEON_DESKTOP_BILLING_REQUIRED=true` on a test API, sign in with an account that has no plan: the cover should say "Start a Simeon trial…", its button should open the billing page, and the cover should go on its own after the checkout.
5. Cancel trial from the app's Settings and from the billing page's footer; both should set the trial to end without a charge.

## 🖼️ Screenshots/Recordings

Rendered locally; the screenshots are in the session. Not yet seen against Stripe or on a Mac.

- `SIMEON_DESKTOP_BILLING_REQUIRED` stays off until Bass has done the $20 test from the site's button.
