body:
## Summary

Mail and Calendar URLs named accounts and mailboxes by opaque JMAP ids (`/mail/account/mh/mailbox/a`, `/calendar/account/mh/week`). They now read the way Gmail's do:

```
/mail/a/0/#inbox
/mail/a/0/#sent/<threadId>
/mail/a/0/#all
/mail/a/0/#junk
/mail/a/0/#mailbox/Custom+Folder

/calendar/a/0/#week/2026/10/6
/calendar/a/0/#day/2026/10/6?event=<id>
/calendar/a/0/#agenda
```

### Shared

- **Account number.** Each `User Account` link carries a per-user `number`: `0` is the user's personal account, the rest count from 1. It is the same number in both apps. A number is never reused (`User Settings.last_account_number` remembers the highest). A patch numbers existing links.
- **Fragment.** Everything after `/<app>/a/<n>/` lives in the fragment. `router/fragmentHistory.ts` swaps the fragment and path forms at the router's history, so routes and guards still match plain paths. The plain path form still opens and is rewritten on arrival.
- **Unknown account number.** Opens the same page under `0`.
- The old URLs (`/mail/account/...`, `/mail/all-inboxes`, `/calendar/account/...`) no longer resolve. Account-less shortcuts (`/mail`, `/mail/contacts`, `/calendar/week/...`) are unchanged.

### Mail

- **Mailboxes.** Role mailboxes go by role, a folder of the user's own by its name under `#mailbox/`. A nested folder goes by its whole path (`#mailbox/Clients%2FBills`), so `get_mailboxes` now returns `parent_id`.
- **One place for the mapping.** `apps/mail/utils/locations.ts` turns JMAP ids into addresses and back; views and stores keep working in ids.
- **Other account pages** moved into the fragment too: outbox, screener, contacts, compose, starred and search.
- **Missing mailbox.** Shows "There are no messages in this mailbox." instead of redirecting.
- **All Inboxes** is `/mail/a/<n>/#all`. With a thread open, the number is the thread's own account.
- **Renaming an open folder** keeps it open and rewrites the URL.
- **Push notifications** link a mailbox by id (`#id/<mailboxId>/<threadId>`) and the app redirects to its address, so a rename does not break a delivered notification.

### Calendar

- Views, search and profile sit under `/calendar/a/<n>/#...`; `apps/calendar/utils/locations.ts` maps the number to the account.
- An account that only shares a calendar with the user has a number but is not one to switch to, so its number falls back to `0` like any other the user has nothing at.
- Event links made outside the calendar follow: the reminder alert (socket toast and push), Mail's upcoming events and invite banner, and the command palette's results.
- The `?account=<id>` query that names a shared event's owning account is unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] Frontend: `yarn test src/router/fragmentHistory.test.ts src/apps/mail/routes.test.ts src/apps/mail/router.test.ts src/apps/mail/utils/locations.test.ts src/apps/calendar/routes.test.ts src/apps/calendar/router.test.ts` (the URL codec against real browser history, route matching, both guards, and id/address mapping)
- [x] Backend: `suite.mail.doctype.user_account.test_user_account`, `test_jmap_client`, `test_suite_cloud_gating`
- [x] Migrated a site and checked the backfill gives each user `0` for their personal account
- [ ] Live Stalwart suites (`test_mail_mailboxes`, `test_mail_account_isolation`) not run: Suite Cloud was unreachable
- [ ] Not yet clicked through in a browser: account switching in both apps, opening a thread from All Inboxes, renaming an open folder, a mail push notification link, a calendar reminder link, opening an event from Mail's upcoming events

## What does this help someone do?

A core that closes its IPC channel while exiting for an update keeps its actual exit code. Previously a status send could emit a child error, which the master treated as exit 1 before the real exit 75 arrived; a good update could be rolled back.

`coreHandle.send` now gives Node an error callback for that send. Spawn failures and actual process exits keep their existing handling. This is separate from the restored-input fix in #866.

Run `E2E_BUNDLE=1 npx vitest run --config vitest.e2e.config.ts e2e/masterIpcExit.e2e.ts`. The first core closes IPC while its master is paused. After queued status replies fail, it exits 75. author: warny
body:
Closes **NTS-13** (Italian compound ordinals) for a sourced domain, opens **NTS-15**, leaves **NTS-14** open.

## Engine — `<OrdinalStem>`

**Why `removeTrailing` alone was insufficient.** It strips one fixed string. Italian needs an ending-dependent stem: drop the final vowel (`ventuno → ventun-`), but keep it after `sei` (`ventiseiesimo`), turn `tré` into `tre` (`ventitreesimo`) and `-mila` into `mill-` (`duemillesimo`). Whole-word `<Ordinal from to>` rules cannot cover soldered compounds, and a post-processing regex would run after the structure is lost (`ventisei` vs `ventisesimo`).

**Semantics.** `<OrdinalStem from="x" to="y"/>` on `<Ordinals>`: if the last word that receives the suffix ends with `x` (ordinal, case-sensitive `EndsWith`, no regex), that ending becomes `y`, then the effective suffix is appended. `from` is required and non-empty, `to` is required and may be empty.

**Precedence.** `OrdinalException` → exact last-word `<Ordinal>` → (suffix in effect) longest matching `OrdinalStem` → `removeTrailing` only if no stem matched → effective suffix (variant override or base). Declaration order is irrelevant; a duplicate `from` is rejected at load (including inside a `baseOn` child).

**Compatibility and immutability.** Without `OrdinalStem`, output is byte-identical (full dump of 73 cultures identical after the engine commit). Rules are validated, copied and sorted longest-first once at construction into an `ImmutableArray`; the copy constructor carries them; `baseOn` merges them by `from`. Public model: `OrdinalStemRule` record, `NumberToStringConverterOptions.OrdinalStemRules`, converter `OrdinalStemRules`, XSD `OrdinalStemType`. Variant-specific stem rules are intentionally not part of the contract (the variants reuse the base rules with their own suffix).

## Italian

- **Productive range:** 1–1999 **except 1010–1910**, and the round thousands 2000–999000, masculine and feminine (`ventunesima`, `ventitreesima`, `duemillesima`).
- Examples: `ventunesimo`, `ventitreesimo`, `ventiseiesimo`, `ventiquattresimo`, `novantanovesimo`.
- Hundreds: `centesimo`, `centunesimo` (Treccani, although the cardinal stays `centouno`), `centoduesimo`, `centotreesimo`, `centoseiesimo`, `centoundicesimo`, `centottantesimo`, `centottantatreesimo`, `duecentesimo`.
- **x10 family (review finding):** after a hundred, `dieci` keeps its lexical ordinal: `centodecimo`, `duecentodecimo` … `novecentodecimo` (feminine `-decima`). These are nine exact word rules; the mechanical `centodiecesimo` was attested nowhere. 1010–1910 fail closed (NTS-15).
- Thousands: `millesimo`, `milleunesimo`, `milleduesimo`, `duemillesimo`, `diecimillesimo`, `centomillesimo`.
- IT config: 8 stem rules replace `removeTrailing="i"` and the 13 whole-word rules of each gender (same outputs for the previously produced values).
- `ItalianOrdinalLanguageSpecifics` builds nothing and does not rebuild cardinals. It only rejects:
  - **zero**: the NTS-12 decision is unchanged, so no mechanical `zeresimo`;
  - **1010–1910**: only the analytic `millesimo decimo` is attested (NTS-15);
  - **non-round thousands above 1999**: no canonical source (NTS-15);
  - **≥ 1 000 000**: the cardinals are known wrong (NTS-14).
- Negative: `-21 → meno ventunesimo`, sign policy unchanged.

## Linguistic evidence

- Treccani, *La grammatica italiana* — "Aggettivi numerali ordinali" (vowel drop + `-esimo`; `tre`/`sei` compounds).
- Treccani vocabolario: "ordinale" (`ventunesimo … centunesimo … duemillesimo … diecimillesimo`), "centesimo" (`centesimo primo (o, più com., centunesimo)`), "centomillesimo" (100001 → analytic `centomillesimoprimo`).
- *Enciclopedia dell'Italiano*, numerali [prontuario]: `trentaseesimo / trentaseiesimo`, only the second one is used.
- DICO, Università di Messina (2020): vowels kept above cento; `milleunesimo, milleduesimo` are the official forms.
- Accademia della Crusca, "Quarantaquattro gatti…" (2016): `milleunesimo`.
- Vocabolario degli Accademici della Crusca, 5th ed., vol. 2 p. 753, s.v. *centesimo*: "Centodecimo, Centundicesimo, Centododicesimo ec."; Wiktionary, Appendix:Italian numbers: `centodecimo`, `duecentodecimo`. Treccani "ordinale" prefers the analytic `centesimo decimo` / `millesimo decimo` (not modelled).

**Canonical choices when sources differ:**
- `-seiesimo`, not `-seesimo`.
- `centunesimo` (Treccani) over DICO's `centounesimo`. It is extended by analogy to `duecentunesimo`.
- Round thousands keep the cardinal multiplier unchanged: `ventunomillesimo` comes from the chosen cardinal `ventunomila`.
- The analytic forms `millesimo primo` are not modelled.

Details: `docs/NTS-08-linguistic-sources.md`, `DONE-2026-10-06.md`.

## Validation

Tested commit: `738c566a`, branched from `15459d35`.

- `dotnet build Utils.sln -c Release`: 0 errors.
- `UtilsTest.Unit`: **9295 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. This includes 32 `NumberToStringOrdinalStemTests`, the `NumberToStringItalianOrdinalSweepTests` and the Italian feature.
- `UtilsTest.Functional`: **383 passed, 0 failed** on re-run. The first run had 1 failure in `MapFromInterfaceInIsolatedWorkerTest` (`IOException: Pipe is broken`), a known sandbox named-pipe flake in Utils.Reflection, which this PR does not touch.
- `UtilsTest.Security`: **227 passed, 3 skipped** (pre-existing non-Windows-only Authenticode/platform tests), 0 failed. This includes the new `OrdinalStem` snapshot test.
- XSD validation and initialization of every built-in configuration go through the feature tests and the dump.
- Before/after dump of 73 cultures (cardinals/ordinals 0–2100 + large samples, every variant value, clock times):
  - after the engine commit: identical;
  - after the IT commit: 5934 changed lines, all IT ordinals, all previously `NotSupportedException`;
  - after the x10 fix: 57 changed lines (IT ordinals 110–910 and 1010–1910 × 3 variant sets);
  - other languages: unchanged.
- Package CI: the `eng/*.ps1` scripts were not run locally (`pwsh` is unavailable); the `.nupkg` is produced by the Release build.

**Test change note:** the former "Unverified compound ordinals are rejected" scenario pinned the temporary NTS-13 limitation (it referenced the TODO). It is replaced by the reduced rejection domain: zero, non-round thousands above 1999, and millions.

**Sweep tests:** they are a mechanical guard only (structural invariants), not linguistic validation; `centodiecesimo` satisfied them all. The forms rest on the sourced examples of `Italian.feature`, one morphological family at a time.

**Scope limits:** NTS-13 does not claim arbitrarily large Italian ordinals. Millions stay blocked until NTS-14, and 1010–1910 plus non-round thousands above 1999 until NTS-15.

body:
## 작업 개요

이슈 #728 - SCSS 타이포 믹스인 중 20개가 TS `typography` 에 없었다(`*_bold` 15종, `caption`·`caption_bold`·`overline`·`subtitle`·`code`). React 에서 `style` 로 토큰을 쓰면 굵은 제목을 표현할 수 없어, #725 의 cookbook 은 손으로 쓴 700 을 500 으로 내려야 했다.

Closes #728

## 작업한 내용

- [x] 그룹마다 `largeBold`·`mediumBold`·`smallBold` (display·heading·title·body·label)
- [x] 최상위 `caption`·`captionBold`·`overline`(`textTransform: "uppercase"` 포함)·`subtitle`·`code`(monospace `fontFamily`)
- [x] 값은 SCSS 와 동일 - bold 의 letter-spacing(`-0.02em`·`-0.015em`·`-0.01em`)과 overline 의 `0.08em` 은 SCSS 도 리터럴이라 그대로
- [x] `typography.test.ts` 를 **양방향**으로
  - SCSS 글자 믹스인(`font-size` 를 선언하고 `@include`·`@media` 가 없는 것 - 반응형·유틸 믹스인 제외) 전부에 TS 짝이 있고, **선언 전부**가 같으며, TS 에만 있는 속성도 없다
  - TS 스타일 전부에 SCSS 믹스인이 있고, 개수가 같다
  - 경로 매핑: `display_large_bold` ↔ `typography.display.largeBold`, `caption_bold` ↔ `typography.captionBold`

## 검증

- **뮤테이션 5건** - `captionBold` 제거 → 2건 실패 / letter-spacing 변경 → 1건 / overline `textTransform` 제거 → 1건 / TS 에만 있는 스타일 추가 → 1건 / develop 의 TS 로 돌리면 `TS typography.display.largeBold (← @mixin display_large_bold): expected undefined to be defined` 로 빠진 자리를 이름으로 알려준다
- `pnpm test` 1300 · `tsc` · `biome check .` 0건 · `build` 통과 (`dist/index.d.ts` 에 `largeBold` 등 포함)
- 기존 키는 그대로 - 추가만 하므로 minor

## 전달할 추가 이슈

- foundation 의 typography 스토리에 새 스타일(의미 이름 5종) 표시는 foundation 스토리 정리 작업에서 함께 한다

author: alanmrsa
body:
## What changes

A local build used to load the request's URL once. Every later live step then inherited the page, tabs, cookies and storage that exploration left. Now each live step starts the way the authoring guide already describes.

- The first live step that isn't reset still loads the request's URL. Explore steps keep that deep path.
- A live example, a live test and a write session's first `act` step reset the page first.
  - Other tabs close.
  - A build that hasn't signed in clears exploration's cookies and every visited origin's site storage (local, session and IndexedDB).
  - A signed-in build restores the session saved right after sign-in. While a new sign-in is not yet confirmed, nothing saved describes the browser, so it keeps the current session.
  - The step then loads the site root. A root that fails to load is stopped, and the step still runs and may navigate deeper itself.
- A build counts as signed in only after its own sign-in steps typed the login's identifier and a password or code, or the user completed an approval, and the signed-in check then passes. A code the site sent for that sign-in, which the agent asked the user for, counts as its code once an explore's `fill`, `type` or `pressSequentially` call entered it in the page and completed. Source that only holds the code counts nothing. A check before that is refused with `credentials_not_submitted`, so a page that already shows an account leaves the build signed out. A field the host typed counts whatever became of its submit, since a page may submit its own form, unless the page kept the submit disabled, so it was never clicked. A fill whose answer was lost counts every field its step asked for. The page check is the gate.
- Every sign-in step drops the saved session, a signed-in check included. A verified sign-in is over, so a check after it starts a new sign-in and is refused until that sign-in's steps send the login. The next live step after a verified sign-in that isn't a sign-in saves the session (cookies, storage and IndexedDB) before it runs. A failed save stops that step with `Unavailable`, and the next step tries again.
- Later `act` steps, explores and inspects continue on the current page. A write session starts only once its first `act` has its page, so a failed save or reset leaves the next `act` to reset again.
- A run starts at the site root, as its example did, and no longer loads the URL's path. `pomerado run` and each served call open a new browser context, so they start with no cookies or storage. A library caller's run closes the scope's other tabs and keeps its session.

## Design

- `typescript/src/runtime/start-state.ts`, exported as `pomerado/core/runtime/start-state`, holds:
  - the pure decision `startStateFor` (`none | clear | restore | keep`), with `isFirstWriteStep` and `shouldSaveSession`
  - `makeStartTracker`, the per-build state: `signIn()` on every sign-in step, a signed-in check included, `sent(kind)`, `submitted`, `verified()`, `plan(step)`, `dispatched(step)` and `save(session)`. `plan` changes nothing, and a successful `verified()` forgets what the sign-in sent.
  - the browser code: `resetPageCode`, `stopLoadingCode` and `saveSessionCode`
  - `startPage(execute, targetId, origin, start, hooks)`, with the required `StartPageHooks { beforeEntry, navigateRoot }` and the local `localStartHooks`, a plain goto that is stopped after a failed load. `PageStart` requires `session` on `restore`, and `startPage` fails with "No saved session to restore" before any browser call when it has none.
- `standalone/mint-state.ts` replaces the navigate-once latch with `makeBuildStart`. It keeps the latch for the request's URL, runs the tracker, maps a failed save or reset to `Unavailable`, and exposes `before(step)`, `enter`, `signIn`, `sent(report)`, `approved`, `typedCode` and `verified`. The host can't see the request itself, so `sent(report, requested)` counts every field the fill typed unless its submit stayed disabled, and every requested field when the fill's answer was lost.
- `standalone/mint-execution.ts` calls `before` before each authored step. Every sign-in step calls `signIn`, and a fill step reports what it typed. A live explore runs while the host watches for the values of the code handles it lists for the sign-in under way (`signInCodes`), and calls `typedCode` when one was typed. The page-code worker wraps `fill`, `type` and `pressSequentially` on a page, frame, locator and keyboard, the calls a handle may type through, and marks a watched value typed only when such a call got it as its text and completed (`watchTyping` on the Playwright executor). The source text is not read for it. A signed-in check runs only once the sign-in sent the login.
- `standalone/run-operation.ts` starts the page with `keep`.
- Entry URL: the explore step keeps the request's URL, which may be a deep path a build needs to see first. Resets and runs use the site root, so a published script starts where its example did.
- Pinned Playwright 1.63.0 has `browserContext.setStorageState`. It clears every cookie and each visited origin's storage, then restores the given state, IndexedDB included. So the reset takes no list of extra origins. The other-origin test passes none, and fails if that call is skipped.
- The tracker is per build. In a library session that mints twice, the second build starts signed out until it signs in.
- The saved session travels through the page-code worker, whose results are capped at 1 MiB. A larger session, usually from a big IndexedDB, fails the save. Every later live step except a sign-in step then fails too, since each tries the save first, and signing in again hits the same cap. The docs and the CHANGELOG say so.
- `MintDependencies.priorAttemptMayHaveChanged` is removed, with the notice it added to the agent's first input. A host whose restarted write build must read back before it writes again can give the agent its own notice through `drainStartIncidents`, which feeds the first model request's `hostIncidentsBeforeStart`.

## Review fixes

- P2-1: the generated README says "Each call starts at the site root of the URL in deployment.json and opens any deeper page itself." A test pins the sentence.
- P2-2: the other-origin test passes no origins and also checks the other origin's cookie. Skipping `setStorageState` on `clear` now fails it.
- P3-1: `origins` is gone from `PageStart`, `makeBuildStart` and the reset code, since `setStorageState` already clears every visited origin.
- P3-2: `PageStart` is a union in which `restore` carries `session`. `startPage` fails with "No saved session to restore" first, with a unit test.

## 1. Overview

This Pull Request bumps Ruby from 4.0.6 to 4.0.7 across 4 files in `spreen-tracks`.  

Ruby 4.0.7 was released on 2026-09-15 as a routine bugfix update of the 4.0 series; the announcement lists no CVE.  
It fixes 24 tickets, most of them crashes and regressions — including two reported against 4.0.6 itself (Bug #22220, a `require` performance regression with `aws-sdk-ec2`, and Bug #22242, a SEGV in method dispatch).  

The change is confined to version pins, base images and environment documentation; no application code moves.  

## 2. Key Changes & Differences

**2-1. Ruby — 4.0.6 → 4.0.7**

|Area |Before (4.0.6) |After (4.0.7, 2026-09-15) |Changes & Differences |
|:-|:-|:-|:-|
|Regressions from 4.0.6 |2 open |Fixed |SEGV in method dispatch (Bug #22242); slow `require` of `aws-sdk-ec2` (Bug #22220). |
|Memory safety / crashes |— |8 fixes |Heap-use-after-free in `fiber_switch` with transfer-terminated async tasks (Bug #22196); `GC.auto_compact` corrupting a String / segfaulting in `String#tr` (Bug #22237); Arrays sharing a buffer segfaulting on concatenation (Bug #22259); win32 heap overflow in `Kernel#system` (Bug #22198); `EncodingError` from symbol interpolation crashing the process (Bug #22303); `Coverage.start` + ruby/debug segfault (Bug #22217); YJIT/ZJIT Struct accessor crash after an ivar is set (Bug #22292); `ObjectSpace._id2ref` returning the wrong object (Bug #22200). |

|Networking / process |— |2 fixes |`Socket.tcp` with `connect_timeout` returning a phantom connected socket (Bug #22223); `fork` behaviour when `Process._fork` raises (Bug #22243). |
|Coverage / TracePoint |— |2 fixes |`Coverage.line_stub` clobbering collected data (Bug #22269); line TracePoint missing a loop condition after a guard (Bug #22218). |
|JIT / misc |— |6 fixes |YJIT `rb_yjit_invalidate_ep_is_bp` regression with Ractors (Bug #22224); `Ruby::Box` + `BUNDLER_SETUP` ordering (Bug #22123); missing `parse.y` hash-literal warning (Bug #22264); addr2line with GCC LTO (Bug #22188); win32 `ENV.keys` encoding and stack address (Bug #20958, #11438). |

body:
## Summary
Implements the ledger-service gRPC server (ReserveFunds, CaptureFunds, GetBalance) with centralized error mapping, giving order-service a working synchronous contract to call.

## Changes
- `ledger.proto` — renamed `DebitWallet` RPC to `CaptureFunds` to match its real capture semantics.
- `LedgerEngine.java` — `captureFunds()` now returns `capturedCents` instead of `void`.
- `LedgerGrpcService.java` (new) — translates the 3 RPCs into `LedgerEngine` calls.
- `LedgerGrpcExceptionHandler.java` (new) — maps domain exceptions to gRPC `Status` via `@GrpcAdvice`.
- `LedgerEngineTest.java` — updated 2 cases for the new `captureFunds()` signature.
- `LedgerGrpcServiceTest.java`, `LedgerGrpcExceptionHandlerTest.java` (new) — 8 tests for the two new classes.

## Design Decisions
- Renamed `DebitWallet` → `CaptureFunds`: the RPC moves escrow to revenue, not a direct wallet debit.
- `captureFunds()` returns the captured amount because it can't be recomputed afterward — escrow nets to zero once captured.
- Exceptions propagate uncaught to `@GrpcAdvice` instead of being caught in the service, mirroring the REST `ProblemDetail` pattern.

## Test Coverage
| Class | Tests | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| LedgerGrpcServiceTest | 5 | request→engine argument mapping, response packing, exception propagation |
| LedgerGrpcExceptionHandlerTest | 3 | exception → gRPC Status code mapping |
| LedgerEngineTest (updated) | 2 | new `captureFunds()` return value and cached idempotency JSON |

50 tests passing (42 existing + 8 new).

- Depends on: task-1.4 LedgerEngine ✅ done
- Required by: task-2.6 order-service gRPC client ⬜ pending

author: kristianwind
body:
Three findings, one subject: what reaches outside the house, **who** may put it
there, and whether **"off" closes it**.

### A `server.control` delegate could open the router

`auto_forward` decides whether a server's ports are forwarded, and
`server.control` was enough to set it. The admin opts in to UPnP or UniFi once,
globally; this flag is what *spends* that opt-in. So a child trusted with their
own Minecraft server could open its ports to the internet, and nothing recorded
that they had.

Admin only now — and only when the value actually **changes**, so an edit form
that posts every field does not start failing. There is a test for that, because
a gate that refuses everything also refuses the attack and passes.

### A `server.control` delegate could claim a hostname

A `subdomain` containing a dot is a full domain, and the primary subdomain field
had **no clash check at all**. `handlers_routes.go` has had one since it was
written, checking both `server_routes` and `servers.subdomain`.

On the delegate's next start the NPM path deletes the existing proxy host for
that domain and points it at their container; the Cloudflare path drops the
tunnel ingress rule and adds its own. **The family shop's hostname could be
taken by the server next to it.** Admin only, plus the routes handler's own
clash check — scoped so a server may still keep the hostname it already has.

### Turning an integration off left everything it had opened in place

Every per-server removal path begins by checking its own enable flag and
returning when it is off. Sensible in isolation, and it means **the moment the
setting is cleared the panel loses the ability to undo its own work**.

Enable UPnP → start three servers → disable UPnP → stop them. The three mappings
stay on the router with a permanent lease (`upnpLease = 0`), while the settings
page reads "off". The same for UniFi rules, NPM proxy hosts, and Cloudflare
ingress rules with their DNS records.

The teardown now runs **before** the setting is written — that ordering is the
entire fix — and only on the on→off transition, so saving a settings form does
not tear down a working setup. Server ids are collected before anything is
removed: the removal paths write to the same database and the pool is one
connection deep, so removing inside an open cursor deadlocks.

## Tests

| planted | DelegateCannotOpen | DelegateCanStill | HostnameInUse | TearsDownBeforeSaves |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| nothing | PASS | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| admin check off `auto_forward` | **FAIL** | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| admin check off `subdomain` | **FAIL** | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| clash check removed | PASS | PASS | **FAIL** | PASS |
| gate widened to refuse unchanged values | PASS | **FAIL** | PASS | PASS |
| teardown moved after the save | PASS | PASS | PASS | **FAIL** |
| teardown deleted from NPM | PASS | PASS | PASS | **FAIL** |

The refusal tests assert the **database**, not the status code: a 403 with the
write already done is the same leak with better manners.

The teardown's ordering test is **structural** — it reads the four call sites and
checks the teardown is written before the save. Stated as such in the test,
because it proves the order is in the source, not that it ran; driving it end to
end needs a real router, proxy and Cloudflare account. The alternative was no
check at all on the one property the fix consists of. The behavioural half is
covered separately: the callback asserts the flag is *still on* when it runs,
which is what the real removal paths read.

## Review status

Remaining and smaller: the password-reset link is built from the request `Host`
header (rate-limited, single-use, TOTP still protects a 2FA'd admin); NPM
provisioning falls back to no TLS silently; UPnP writes no audit entry and
swallows every error.

author: sergey-chukhno
body:
## Summary

This PR completes **Card AUTH-003** (*Implement primary user authentication against Auth-owned credentials*), establishing the authoritative cryptographic authentication perimeter, domain credential validation models, session establishment engine, and security audit telemetry pipeline for the SecureCloud Auth service.

All 6 implementation tickets (`AUTH-003-T01` through `AUTH-003-T06`) are fully implemented, verified, and backed by a comprehensive test suite (60 unit tests, 11 integration tests) with zero regressions across existing services.

---

## Key Deliverables & Ticket Breakdown

- **`AUTH-003-T01` — Argon2id Cryptographic Verification Engine** (`commit 4db9f14`):
  - Integrated native OpenSSL 3 `EVP_KDF` for Argon2id key derivation ($m=65536\,\text{KiB}$, $t=3$, $p=1$, $32$-byte key).
  - Implemented strict RFC 9106 PHC string parser (`$argon2id$v=19$m=65536,t=3,p=1$<salt>$<hash>`).
  - Added constant-time verification using `CRYPTO_memcmp` and immediate buffer zeroization via `OPENSSL_cleanse`.
  - Implemented `execute_dummy_verification()` running identical Argon2id computational passes to defeat user enumeration timing attacks.
  - Added 9 unit tests in `tests/unit/auth/argon2id_hasher_test.cpp`.

- **`AUTH-003-T02` — Domain Credential Value Types & Input Sanitization** (`commit c582190`):
  - Created strongly-typed `CredentialIdentifier` enforcing whitespace trimming, length bounding ([3..255] chars), and rejection of ASCII control characters (`0x00..0x1F`, `0x7F`) to prevent CRLF log injection.
  - Created `PasswordCredential` with a hard 1024-byte ceiling to eliminate algorithmic Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks on memory-hard KDFs.
  - Enforced RAII memory zeroization using `SecretString` and `OPENSSL_cleanse` on destruction.
  - Overloaded `operator<<` with unconditional `"[REDACTED_PASSWORD]"` stream redaction.
  - Added 10 unit tests in `tests/unit/auth/credentials_test.cpp`.

- **`AUTH-003-T03` — Credential Verifier Component & Account State Rules** (`commit 97c4d3c`):
  - Implemented `CredentialVerifier` domain service coordinating user lookup, dummy verification, and password checks.
  - Enforced zero information disclosure: missing users and wrong passwords uniformly resolve to `AuthenticationStatus::InvalidCredentials`.
  - Enforced account lifecycle invariants: only accounts with `AccountStatus::Active` may authenticate; all other states (`PendingVerification`, `Suspended`, `Disabled`) fail with `AccountDisabled`.
  - Fail-closed error handling intercepting repository and KDF exceptions as `InternalError`.
  - Added 10 unit tests in `tests/unit/auth/credential_verifier_test.cpp`.

- **`AUTH-003-T04` — Session Manager & Device Ownership Association** (`commit 8a8ea4f`):
  - Implemented `SessionManager` enforcing device ownership invariants (`device.user_id == user.user_id`).
  - Enforced device lifecycle check (`device.device_status == DeviceStatus::Active`); revoked devices return `DeviceRevoked`.
  - Generated time-ordered RFC 9562 UUIDv7 session records stamped with `AuthenticationLevel::PrimaryOnly` and a 24-hour expiration TTL.
  - Persisted sessions to database and updated `device.last_authenticated_at` atomically.
  - Added 10 unit tests in `tests/unit/auth/session_manager_test.cpp`.

- **`AUTH-003-T05` — Security & Audit Event Publisher Pipeline** (`commit c0997f1`):
  - Created decoupled `IAuditEventPublisher` and `IAuditEventSink` interfaces.
  - Formatted structured JSON audit records for `auth.login.succeeded`, `auth.login.failed`, and `auth.account.disabled_attempt`.
  - Enforced non-blocking `noexcept` invariant ensuring audit sink errors never abort user authentication.
  - Implemented bit-level raw string assertions (`find("\"password\"") == std::string::npos`) to mathematically guarantee zero secret leakage into audit sinks.
  - Added 10 unit tests in `tests/unit/auth/audit_event_publisher_test.cpp`.

- **`AUTH-003-T06` — gRPC Authenticate RPC Wiring & End-to-End Suite** (`commit 41329c6`):
  - Implemented `AuthServiceImpl::Authenticate` method connecting all AUTH-003 domain services.
  - Mapped domain outcomes to deterministic gRPC status codes (`INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `UNAUTHENTICATED`, `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `NOT_FOUND`, `INTERNAL`).
  - Wired production server bootstrap in `src/auth/main.cpp` with dependency injection.
  - Added 11 unit tests in `tests/unit/auth/auth_service_authenticate_test.cpp`.
  - Added 3 live database integration tests in `tests/integration/auth_authentication_integration_test.cpp` against PostgreSQL 17 on container port 5433 with strict Port 5432 prohibition assertion.

- **Documentation & Walkthrough Report** (`commits 687cdf9, 73948f0`):
  - Delivered exhaustive, 1,068-line validation report in `walkthrough-auth-003.md` covering STRIDE threat modeling, cryptographic specifications, compliance mapping (SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST SP 800-63B, HIPAA), and an SRE operational runbook.

---

## Security Invariants & Defenses

1. **Algorithmic DoS Defense**: Enforces a 1024-byte hard ceiling on candidate passwords before invoking Argon2id, preventing CPU/memory cache exhaustion.
2. **User Enumeration Defense**: Missing user accounts trigger `execute_dummy_verification()` running identical Argon2id computation (64 MB RAM, 3 passes) against a pre-computed verifier, equalizing wall-clock latency to defeat timing side-channel probes.
3. **Log Injection Defense**: All ASCII control characters (`\r`, `\n`, `\0`, `\x1b`) are rejected during schema validation.
4. **Zero Plaintext Secrets**: Passwords are wiped from memory via `OPENSSL_cleanse`, redacted in output streams, and strictly excluded from audit event records.
5. **Host Isolation**: `PortForbiddenException` strictly prevents any connection to host PostgreSQL on port 5432; containerized PostgreSQL 17 on port 5433 is exclusively permitted.

---

author: rm3l
body:
## Summary

The Renovate config disabled all updates on release branches (`enabled: false` without `matchUpdateTypes`), then tried to selectively re-enable patch and digest updates. This never worked because Renovate skips dependencies entirely before determining the update type when the blanket disable matches — the re-enable rules had nothing to match against.

Replaces the three rules (disable-all, re-enable patch, re-enable digest) with a single rule that only disables `major` updates. Minor, patch, and digest updates are now implicitly allowed on release branches.

EOL branch rules (release-1.5 through 1.8) are unaffected — they use exact branch names and intentionally disable everything.

Same fix as redhat-developer/rhdh-must-gather#428, which was confirmed working after a Renovate cache bust.

## Test plan

- [ ] After merging, trigger a Renovate run and verify PRs are created for release branches
- [ ] A cache-busting commit on active release branches may be needed (Renovate caches extraction results keyed by branch SHA)

author: artui
body:
Every step in `upstream-drift.yml` that opens or closes an issue now runs only on `main`. Here that is `bundle-pin`'s issue step.

**Why.** Each issue reports on `main`'s state. Dispatched from a branch, the ungated steps would file that branch's failure against `main`, or close `main`'s issue on the strength of a fix that hasn't landed. resolve-latest was already gated. This covers the rest of the workflow, so a branch dispatch is now a trial that touches no issue, as it already was in the family's other ten drift workflows.

Each condition keeps its status function. An `if:` that names none still implies `success()`, which is why the step that had no condition behaves as before on `main`.

CI-only, so there is no changelog entry and no release.

## Checklist avant RfR

### État de la PR
- [ ] Le titre respecte la convention : `#ID_ISSUE - Message clair et en français, compréhensible par quelqu'un du métier`
- [ ] Auteurs assignés sur la PR et l'issue liée
- [ ] Description du travail commentée sur l'issue (cf. `/document-issue`)
- [ ] L'issue est en **RfR** dans le [projet GitHub](https://github.com/orgs/Immersion-Facilitee/projects/1?query=sort%3Aupdated-desc+is%3Aopen)

## Points d'attention pour le reviewer

<!-- Optionnel : indiquer les zones qui méritent une attention particulière -->

- Le workflow se déclenche via `workflow_run` : il ne tourne qu'une fois mergé sur `main`, et chaque nouveau workflow ayant son propre déclencheur doit être ajouté à la liste `workflows` (GitHub ne documente pas de joker). Les workflows réutilisables (`workflow_call`) n'y figurent pas : leurs logs font partie du run de l'appelant.
- zizmor signale `workflow_run` comme déclencheur dangereux : ici, aucun code ni artefact du run analysé n'est récupéré ou exécuté, seuls ses logs sont lus, et les valeurs de l'événement passent par des variables d'environnement, jamais interpolées dans les scripts.
- gitleaks est épinglé (8.30.1) avec vérification de l'empreinte SHA-256. Les logs sont téléchargés job par job en texte brut (un fichier `<id du job>.log`), sans passer par l'archive zip.
- gitleaks tourne une seule fois et son rapport non masqué reste sur le runner, supprimé en fin de traitement. Les logs du run sont supprimés dès la détection, avant toute autre étape.
- Un script TypeScript (Node 24, sans dépendance) construit tout le rapport : résumé affiché dans le job (règle, job, ligne, nom de variable), alerte d'une ligne, détail et extraits pour le fil Slack (30 lignes avant, 10 après chaque détection). Chaque valeur détectée est remplacée partout, y compris encodée pour une URL, et le script échoue si une valeur subsiste. En cas d'échec, une alerte minimale part quand même.
- Testé en local sur les runs récents de chaque workflow : aucune fausse alerte après exclusion du mot de passe du Postgres de test et des valeurs déjà masquées par GitHub. Parcours complet (scan, extrait, Slack) simulé avec un faux serveur Slack : aucune valeur détectée dans les messages.
- À vérifier avant merge : le bot Slack doit être membre du canal `#if-dev`, sinon l’alerte est refusée par Slack.

Adds two new layouts to the **Monthly allowance** view, next to the existing ranking: a `Ranking / Cards / Compare` switch in the toolbar. Web only; no data, pipeline or derived files change.

## 1. Overview

This Pull Request bumps Ruby from 4.0.6 to 4.0.7 across 4 files in `spreen-wiki`.  

Ruby 4.0.7 was released on 2026-09-15 as a routine bugfix update of the 4.0 series; the announcement lists no CVE.  
It fixes 24 tickets, most of them crashes and regressions — including two reported against 4.0.6 itself (Bug #22220, a `require` performance regression with `aws-sdk-ec2`, and Bug #22242, a SEGV in method dispatch).  

The change is confined to version pins, base images and environment documentation; no application code moves.  

## 2. Key Changes & Differences

**2-1. Ruby — 4.0.6 → 4.0.7**

|Area |Before (4.0.6) |After (4.0.7, 2026-09-15) |Changes & Differences |
|:-|:-|:-|:-|
|Regressions from 4.0.6 |2 open |Fixed |SEGV in method dispatch (Bug #22242); slow `require` of `aws-sdk-ec2` (Bug #22220). |
|Memory safety / crashes |— |8 fixes |Heap-use-after-free in `fiber_switch` with transfer-terminated async tasks (Bug #22196); `GC.auto_compact` corrupting a String / segfaulting in `String#tr` (Bug #22237); Arrays sharing a buffer segfaulting on concatenation (Bug #22259); win32 heap overflow in `Kernel#system` (Bug #22198); `EncodingError` from symbol interpolation crashing the process (Bug #22303); `Coverage.start` + ruby/debug segfault (Bug #22217); YJIT/ZJIT Struct accessor crash after an ivar is set (Bug #22292); `ObjectSpace._id2ref` returning the wrong object (Bug #22200). |
|VM / method caches |— |3 fixes |Stale super caches after `prepend` (Bug #22257); ivars on anonymous objects bloating future classes (Bug #22290); `Class#subclasses` missing clones of classes that include modules (Bug #22190). |
|Networking / process |— |2 fixes |`Socket.tcp` with `connect_timeout` returning a phantom connected socket (Bug #22223); `fork` behaviour when `Process._fork` raises (Bug #22243). |
|Coverage / TracePoint |— |2 fixes |`Coverage.line_stub` clobbering collected data (Bug #22269); line TracePoint missing a loop condition after a guard (Bug #22218). |
|JIT / misc |— |6 fixes |YJIT `rb_yjit_invalidate_ep_is_bp` regression with Ractors (Bug #22224); `Ruby::Box` + `BUNDLER_SETUP` ordering (Bug #22123); missing `parse.y` hash-literal warning (Bug #22264); addr2line with GCC LTO (Bug #22188); win32 `ENV.keys` encoding and stack address (Bug #20958, #11438). |

When a `delayRender()` retry replaces page 0, the old page stays open and both main tabs answer media extraction requests, causing `Invalid message` errors.

Close the timed-out page before reusing its index. Each main tab now announces a unique instance ID, so other tabs replay pending extraction requests once when the replacement becomes ready, including requests sent while no main tab exists. Clean up request listeners and timers on success, error, and timeout; retain the existing extraction timeout budget.

Closes #12018.

Validation:

- `bun run build` and `bun run stylecheck` pass.
- 30 existing tests pass across the affected renderer and media packages.
- A four-tab, 60-frame render with a forced frame-0 retry and a delayed video response completes successfully.
- A browser diagnostic confirms pending requests recover after main-tab replacement, repeated readiness announcements do not duplicate requests, and completed or expired requests are not replayed.

author: mauro-mascia
body:
## Summary

When text is selected in the WYSIWYG editor and sent to the Claude Code VS Code extension (no Claude terminal open), the editor jumps back to the top of the document.

Root cause: `_handleSendToClaudeChat` opens a temporary text editor to carry the selection. That editor becomes active with the cursor still on line 1 (the selection is set right after `showTextDocument` resolves), so the `onDidChangeActiveTextEditor` listener calls `setPendingNavigation(fsPath, 1)`. When the handler then calls `webviewPanel.reveal(...)`, `onDidChangeViewState` consumes that pending navigation and posts `scrollToLine: 1`.

A related issue: with `defaultMode: "preview"`, the `onDidChangeTabs` listener can intercept the temporary text tab, close it and reopen the file in WYSIWYG mode, because the URI is not in `suppressAutoSwitch`. The text editor carrying the selection may then disappear before Claude reads it.

## Changes

- Call `suppressNavFromTextEditor()` and add the URI to `suppressAutoSwitch` before opening the temporary text editor, the same way the `switchToTextEditor` handler already does.
- Call `suppressNavFromTextEditor()` again before the second `showTextDocument` in the "Claude panel not open" branch, since the 700 ms wait plus command execution can outlast the 1.5 s suppression window.
- Remove the URI from `suppressAutoSwitch` shortly after the handler finishes (also on error).

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactoring (no behavior change)
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] CI / tooling

## Testing

- `pnpm build` and `pnpm test` pass (150/150). `tsc --noEmit` reports the same 3 pre-existing errors in `src/__tests__/markdownDocument.test.ts` before and after this change.
- Manual check: select text deep in a long Markdown file in the WYSIWYG editor, send it to the Claude Code panel, and confirm the view keeps its scroll position and the `@file#Lx-Ly` mention is inserted.

author: qarlus
body:
# PR-E7a — Header, footer and page number ## What changed Three of E7's five `soon` controls become operational: **Header**, **Footer** and **Page number**. E7's other two controls — Insert footnote and Table of contents — are **not** here. They are E7b and E7c, stacked on this branch. **Editing-story state** (`use-editing-story.ts`) The workspace now has an explicit editing story: the body by default, or a header/footer story while one is open. `editingKind` is the state; the story itself is re-resolved against the current model every render, so a reload retargets it instead of stranding the editor on a stale part. Opening a story moves the caret into its first paragraph and makes the body inert — `editableIds` becomes that story's paragraph order — and closing returns the caret to the body with nothing selected. A document switch resets the kind, so an open story never spans documents. Which story: the part referenced by the **body's final section**, the same resolution the margin paint already uses. **Contract** — `insert_page_number` — `{ paragraphId, offset }`, `.strict()`, offset bounded like the other offset-bearing operations. It inserts at that offset in whichever story the paragraph belongs to, so it works in a header, a footer or the body. **Writer** (`packages/ooxml/src/page-number-edits.ts`) — a five-run `PAGE` field spliced at the offset: ``` PAGE ``` It reuses the splice helpers E6b built for the cross-reference rather than adding a second splicer, and it is part-aware via `requireEditablePart(paragraph.partName)`. **The result run stores nothing, deliberately.** The reader already resolves a `PAGE` instruction at paint (`runDisplayText` returns the page number for a run whose fragments carry `instrText` + `PAGE`), so a stored digit would paint a second, stale number beside the resolved one. This is the opposite choice from the `REF` field in E6b — correctly, because a `REF` result is stable text while a `PAGE` result changes per page. **Pending paint** reuses E6b's zero-width field marker, so a pending page number contributes no characters to the editable text. ## Why Header and footer content was already *read* as stories and painted, and the writers were already part-aware — `ParagraphAnchor` carries `partName` and writers call `requireEditablePart(paragraph.partName)`. The actual gap was one line of client code that hard-coded the editable story to `'document'`. E7a opens that up and adds the page-number field. ## Testing | gate | result | | --- | --- | | `@obiter/contracts` | 185 pass, 0 fail | | `@obiter/ooxml` | 334 pass, 0 fail | | `@obiter/api` | 1915 pass, 0 fail | | `@obiter/app-shell` | 1375 pass, 0 fail | | `bun run typecheck` | all workspaces clean | | `bun run lint` | clean | | `bun run format:check` | clean | | `perf:bundle-budget` | initial 184.1/212 kB, lazy 394.7/400 kB, largest lazy 173.1/200 kB — ok, after a real build whose provenance is this commit | New coverage: story resolution and flow order, per-story last-paragraph protection, save plan and find scoping in a margin story, list numbering there, the editable band render, the inert body, and body-click exit. Plus the page-number writer round-trip. ## Real-browser evidence Run against this head in real Chromium: `document-header-footer.spec.ts` **1 passed / 0 failed**, plus a temporary spec (deleted afterwards) covering the two defects the previous browser pass found, and `document-structure-inserts.spec.ts` + `document-links-and-references.spec.ts` **2 passed / 0 failed** for no regression. Frames below are from the final round. **1. Header, footer and page number** — the header paints read-only in the margin until its story is opened; once open it is editable, and a page number inserted there survives save and a fresh-context reload. | | | | --- | --- | | ![Header painted read-only](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ObiterDictum/obiter/evidence/pr-276-e7a/01-header-readonly-before.png) | ![Header story editable](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ObiterDictum/obiter/evidence/pr-276-e7a/02-header-editable.png) | | Painted read-only in the margin | Story opened, header editable | | ![Page number inserted](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ObiterDictum/obiter/evidence/pr-276-e7a/03-page-number-pending.png) | ![Painted after reload](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ObiterDictum/obiter/evidence/pr-276-e7a/05-reloaded-painted.png) | | Page number inserted | **Painted after a fresh-context reload**, body editable again | **2. Two saves in a row with no reload** — this is the defect the previous browser pass found and this round fixes. A header save containing a page number used to leave the history unreconciled, so the next save was refused until a page was reloaded. Both saves are now accepted with no banner, and both persisted server-side: the version list reads **v1 / v2 / v3**. | | | | | --- | --- | --- | | ![First save](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ObiterDictum/obiter/evidence/pr-276-e7a/07a-double-save-first.png) | ![Second save, no reload](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ObiterDictum/obiter/evidence/pr-276-e7a/07b-double-save-second.png) | ![Both persisted](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ObiterDictum/obiter/evidence/pr-276-e7a/07c-double-save-versions.png) | | First save settled | Second save accepted, no banner | **v1 / v2 / v3** — both saves recorded | The third frame is a read of persisted state, not just a render: the reload banner's absence alone would not prove the write landed. **3. A trailing page number on a wrapping paragraph paints once** — the other defect found by review. A field at the end of a wrapped paragraph used to paint its number on every wrapped line. The header below wraps to three lines and contains exactly one `1`, at the end. ![Trailing page number on a three-line header](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ObiterDictum/obiter/evidence/pr-276-e7a/08-wrap-painted-once.png) Measured geometrically on the painted band, not by eye: the header `

` is 50.6 px tall (~3 lines of 16 px), exactly one `1` glyph exists in it, and its bottom sits 0.9 px above the band bottom. **4. A page number in the body still paints after reload**, so the paint path is not header-only. ![Body page number after reload](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ObiterDictum/obiter/evidence/pr-276-e7a/09-body-page-reloaded.png) All frames above are also browsable as files on the `evidence` branch: [evidence/pr-276-e7a](https://github.com/ObiterDictum/obiter/tree/evidence/pr-276-e7a) — assets only, never merged. **Stored-package claim.** The committed spec reads the exported `.docx` and asserts ` PAGE ` is present in `word/header1.xml`, so the field is written to the package and not merely painted. The export view for the same save is below. ![Export](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ObiterDictum/obiter/evidence/pr-276-e7a/06-exported.png) ## Deliberate exclusions - **Only the final section's header and footer are editable.** Other sections' header/footer parts are preserved and still painted, but not independently editable. Recorded in the Known Divergences table in `docs/architecture.html`, in the same style as E5's section limitation. - **Page number and margin edits fail closed under track-changes**, consistent with the other insertions — an insertion is not recorded as a tracked change. - **Structural controls stay body-only.** Table, picture, link and cross-reference show honest disabled reasons in a margin story rather than being offered. A user might reasonably expect them in headers; that is future work. - **A saved page number cannot be undone away.** The contract carries no operation that removes a spliced field, so once a page number is saved, undo restores the surrounding tex

author: arimendelow
body:
Slice O7: the new Outlook for Mac store as a second calendar source in the sync, behind a flag. Built on main after #70.

## What it does
- `--outlook-root DIR` (`TEAMSCRAWL_OUTLOOK_ROOT`), or `TEAMSCRAWL_OUTLOOK=1` for the default directory. Off by default. Off when `--teams-root` is set without an Outlook root, so fixture runs never read a real profile; `none` turns it off. A `--account` run leaves it out.
- Runs after every Teams source. Each profile is its own source, `outlook|<profile>`, account `outlook/<profile>`, and fails alone: a store the guard refuses (`outlook_store_unrecognized`, `outlook_store_version`, `outlook_layout_unsupported`) is a coded source failure, the run is `partial` when Teams committed, and nothing of Outlook is kept. With Teams not installed Outlook runs alone.
- One copy per `OutlookMinReadInterval` (5 minutes, assumed), from the last attempted copy; a skipped read is `skipped_interval` with `next_read_after`, not a loss. An unchanged store reads nothing and reports the losses of its last read.
- Reuses what #65 added: the calendar savepoint (`isolated`), the calendar loss codes (`calendar_unmapped` for events that do not map, `calendar_refused` for core refusals, `calendar_all_day_unaligned` counted) and the run row. Damaged blocks keep the reader's `outlook_blocks_damaged`. No new schema. The `calendar_losses` table is keyed to `records`, which Outlook has none of, so an unchanged run reads its losses from the last run row instead.
- Gone detection off; covered days are the days with at least one non-master event, cumulative.

## Mapper version and re-derive
- `outlookcal.MapperVersion` feeds the Outlook fingerprint (`outlookdesktop.Versions.Mapper`) and a derivation stamp (`meta.outlook_derivation:<account>`: mapper, zone, scrub rules). A bump reads an unchanged store again (`TestSyncOutlookFixture`).
- Finding: `Capture` keeps a stored flag over an unknown incoming one, so a stored all-day false from mapper 1 could never become unknown. When the stamp differs, the batch's events are blanked first, so they are captured over nothing. `TestOutlookMapperBumpMakesStoredAllDayUnknown` shows both: the same stamp keeps the false, a new stamp makes it unknown. A zone change also takes the covered days of archived events again in the new zone (the Outlook counterpart of #73).
- `blankCalendar` now shares its column logic with the event blank.

## Not in this PR
No account link (`--outlook-account`) and no read-command change, as the slice table says. The "unlinked accounts" hint from slice 5 cannot name a flag that does not exist; the link slice (O11) adds the flag and updates the hint with its test.

## Tests
Syncer tests are lean (one fixture sync with the version bump, interval, isolation, Outlook alone, one failure table, omissions); store tests cover the stamp, zone and every database call with the fault sweep. 100% coverage, test, golangci, fmt-check, vet and tidy-check pass locally. SPEC 4.2, the flag rows, the README and the CHANGELOG are updated.

author: mshamanskyi
body:
## Problem
EL-6847 lists several UX problems with chat participant selection and chat templates:

- In the **Add users** modal, clicking outside while the user dropdown was open closed the whole modal, so people had to collapse the dropdown first to reach OK/Cancel.
- Chat templates were edited in an inline card with Set/Unset default buttons, and the design calls for a Create/Edit modal with a "Set as default" checkbox.
- The participant dropdown used chip-style filters that clash with our tab component, and every row repeated its type ("Agent", "Pipeline"…).
- Template cards had a border and a custom dashed "+ New template" button instead of our shared button.

## Change
**Click outside a modal with an open dropdown** (`useDropdownAwareModalClose`, new shared hook)
- The first click outside only collapses the dropdown; the next one closes the modal. ✕ and Escape always close.
- Scoped to the modal's own content, so a dropdown open elsewhere on the page doesn't block it. Used by the Add users modal and the template modal.

**Template Create/Edit modal** (`ChatTemplateEditor`)
- Moved into `Modal.BaseModal` with the title "Create Template", "Edit Template", or "View Template" for users without edit permission.
- Fields: Name, a "Set as default" checkbox, and Participants. Spacing follows the Figma spec.
- The default flag is now applied when the user clicks Save (`useChatTemplates.handleSave`), instead of immediately. The modal closes after save. If the template saves but the default call fails, the user gets a separate error, so re-saving can't create a duplicate.

**Template list** (`ChatTemplateList`, `ChatConfigurationSection`)
- Edit and Delete icons appear on row hover or keyboard focus. Rows themselves are no longer clickable.
- The "Default" badge sits next to the name.
- Delete moved out of the modal. Its confirmation dialog stays open with a loading state until the request finishes.
- Cards have no border and use the white 5% / 10% surface tokens. Creating a template uses the shared `iconLabel` "+ Template" button, disabled with a tooltip at 5 templates.

**Participant picker** (`ChatParticipantPicker`, rebuilt on MUI `Autocomplete`)
- Search happens in the field itself. The dropdown has `BaseTabs` (the same tabs as the Add Dimension modal) and no per-row type labels.
- The dropdown always opens above the field with a fixed height. The chip field shows up to 3 rows, then scrolls.
- Lazy loading had three problems, each fixed:
  - MUI scrolled the list back to the top whenever a page arrived. The scroll position is now restored.
  - `useParticipants` re-sorts merged sources (project + public) on every page, which shuffled rows already shown. Once paging starts, existing rows stay in place and new items are appended.
  - A footer spinner shows while a page loads, and partial first-page results are hidden until every source has answered.
- `useParticipants` now also returns `isFirstPageFetching`. `useLoadToolkits` reports its first page separately, so toolkits/MCPs showed no loading state at all on their first load. Existing consumers keep the old `isFetching` meaning.

**Backup & Restore** (separate commit)
- After a successful real restore, the submit button turns into a disabled "✓ Restored" and the other button reads "Close".
- "Choose a backup file" no longer wraps, and the section has bottom padding.

## Testing
- New tests:
  - `useChatTemplates.hooks.test.js` (6): the default flag is set/unset only when it changed; the modal closes even if the default call fails; missing id after create; save failure keeps the modal open.
  - `useDropdownAwareModalClose.hooks.test.js` (4).
  - `ChatTemplateList.test.jsx` (5): row actions, View label, no row click.
  - `ChatTemplateEditor` tests updated for the modal and checkbox.
- `npx vitest run src/[fsd]/features/settings src/[fsd]/features/chat src/hooks` passes (47 files, 503 tests). Shared hook tests also pass. Lint, Prettier and `npm run build` are clean.
- Checked in the running app with Playwright on a local dev server: the Toolkits tab shows "Loading…" until the full first page is in, then pages with a spinner on each request. Pipelines and Agents page sequentially without duplicate requests.
- Not checked in a running app: the Backup & Restore "Restored" state (needs a real restore), and the light theme.

author: flotilla-crew[bot]
body:
## Summary

Export original live Kitty virtual declarations, including undrawn placements, alongside the existing resolved strips. A `U=1,c=4,r=2` declaration remains one 4×2 record even when placeholders resolve into two 4×1 fragments.

```text
Kitty control headers ── original p presence, handle, creation order
Ghostty live getters ── declaration geometry, image generation, deletion
                        ↓
C snapshot/render accessors + negotiated atomic render envelope
```

Provider ABI 11 and existing C struct layouts remain intact; new declaration structs use version 1. Protocol 13 supports 12. Peers opt in with `"virtual_placements":true` in `/connect`; other peers keep their exact protocol-12 hello, render payloads and visible-image transfers. This is additive, so #296 is not folded into this PR.

Per the governor's omitted-ID ruling, omitted `p` exports zero with `placement_id_explicit=false`; explicit `p=0` exports zero with the flag true. Opaque handles and creation-order sequences belong to the cleat VT instance. Zero-ID fragments remain ambiguous; clients recreate declarations in original order and let their receiving terminal resolve placeholders. Nonzero explicit IDs match fragments exactly together with image ID/generation.

The pinned fork drops the internal/external namespace tag and does not expose a fragment's resolved target. The original C reproducer and captured output are included in `tests/fixtures/kitty-virtual-declarations`; real-Ghostty tests cover its collision pattern. A namespace/target API extension is a possible follow-up only for consumers needing exact mapping of ambiguous fragments; no fork change is made here.

Driver: [rjwittams/katzensteg#121](https://github.com/rjwittams/katzensteg/issues/121), convoy `session-window-images`. Flotilla's cleat provider consumers gain the additive accessors. Wheelhouse continues rendering resolved fragments and does not consume declarations. See `docs/kitty-virtual-declarations.md` for the contract and lifetimes.

Closes #317.

## Evidence

- **Before:** virtual declarations were dropped from the ordinary placement walk; only resolved strips reached clients. The C probe also reports colliding raw placement IDs.
  **After:** real-Ghostty scenarios expose one 4×2 declaration before cells, then the same record plus two strips, and remove both on deletion. Tests cover omitted/explicit-zero IDs, replacement, image generations, namespace twins in either order, resets/screens, chunked transmission, every write split and geometry boundaries.
- Provider tests cover accessor borrowing/release and declaration envelopes between polls. An actual daemon test verifies capability negotiation, the legacy hello and suppression of undrawn image transfers.
- Validation: pinned Ghostty helper; workspace tests with ambient vessel CLEAT coordinates unset; default and no-default-feature Clippy with `-D warnings`; no-default-feature build/tests in an isolated target directory; pinned nightly format check; C header syntax check. Exact results are recorded in the test artifact.

## Mutation check

Both targeted mutants failed their intended regression test and were reverted:

1. Drop the render update's declaration export → `declaration_precedes_cells_and_survives_as_one_four_by_two` fails.
2. Export Ghostty's raw numeric ID instead of the original `p` → `namespace_collision_probe_preserves_original_ids_and_order` fails.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

The change can be reverted without migrating stored data or coordinating an ABI boundary.

**Blast Radius:** terminal

The observer reconciles original header metadata with Ghostty's authoritative live set. Existing fragments and their direct renderer remain intact. Declaration handles establish a new namespace when a VT instance is recreated, including adoption on another host.

author: ludger-aimable
body:
[AIM-2321](https://linear.app/aimableai/issue/AIM-2321), follow-up to #25 (AIM-2283).

**What went wrong (live, 10-06, meeting rdd-qvrc-krj):** after the join, Google Meet showed the "Others may see your video differently" popup. It intercepted the click on "Chat with everyone", the click timed out, and the panel stayed closed. The watcher opened the panel only once at start, so the bot never read a chat message. Clicking "Got it" by hand on the bot's display fixed that meeting at once.

**Fix**
- Browser leg: when the chat button is there but its click fails, click the popup's "Got it" / "Dismiss" / "Close" button (inside `[role="dialog"]`), or press Escape when there is none, then click again. No chat button at all: do nothing.
- `open()` is single-flight: the watcher and a send opening at the same time no longer click the toggle twice (which closed the panel again).
- Watcher: every poll calls `open()` (returns at once when the panel shows), so a panel that did not open, or closed later, is retried. Seeding happens on the first successful open, so a late open never publishes older chat (Teams keeps it across meetings). Messages sent while the panel was still blocked are not answered; with the popup fix that window should be seconds.

**Tests:** `meeting-chat.test.ts`, all checks pass. New case: panel blocked at start → retried on later polls → history at the first open not published → the next message published once.

**Not verified:** live against a fresh bot. The popup click itself was done by hand on the running bot with xdotool (same "Got it" button).

author: troycheng
body:
Adds the independent `qwen35-4b-block-fp8-v1` profile with four selectable paths: SM120 n64 Pingpong GEMM, ordered low-M GEMM, SiLU/block quantization, and mixed FA2. The pinned Dockerfile builds both native extensions and installs exact source patches, launch checks, and stock RMS compilation recipes. Existing MXFP6 and MXFP8 profiles remain separate.

On one RTX 5090, Qwen3.5-4B compressed-tensors block-FP8, TP1, 3k input/1k output, the all-feature profile measured **+9.03% / +6.18% / +5.97% / +6.99%** output throughput at c4/c16/c32/c64. Both arms completed all 680 requests. This is one paired run per point, not a per-feature or statistical-significance claim; the qualification report includes mean/p99 TTFT and the small c4 TTFT increase.

Fixed M4/M32/M64 teacher checks each cover 256 queries and 10,479 raw gold logprobs: zero changed values and identical record bytes versus the matching stock reference. Initial RMS autotuning drift was corrected with source-matched recipes before qualification. Precision claims are scoped to these checks; the private corpus is not published.

Validation: 76 CPU tests in the final image; 20 linear and 41 activation GPU tests; real mixed-FA2 component checks; final Docker build with all 85 runtime/native file hashes identical to the tested image. Torch's existing E4M3 mutable-output schema-opcheck limitation is documented separately from the passing fake and actual dynamic-compile tests. Online weight updates require worker restart, and unsupported serving configurations fail startup.

See [build and launch guide](https://github.com/troycheng/vllm-mach/blob/c83c6a0748fd77ea65d92cf2d22a396be4d27ed5/docs/fp8-profile.md), [qualification data](https://github.com/troycheng/vllm-mach/blob/c83c6a0748fd77ea65d92cf2d22a396be4d27ed5/docs/data/fp8-qualification-20261006.json), and [qualification report](https://github.com/troycheng/vllm-mach/blob/c83c6a0748fd77ea65d92cf2d22a396be4d27ed5/docs/fp8-qualification.md). body:
## Summary

The standards review could not catch members numbered outside the licensed ID range. Two new enums in a customer app (range 55000–55999) passed review with `value(0..7)` (P2103508-11, PR !14703). `naming/cmfrt-object-id-ranges` already states the rule, but its keywords (`object-id`, `enum-value-id`, …) never occur in AL source, so token overlap never brought the article into the worklist, and the review skill had no structural check for it.

## Changes

- **`cmfrt-standards-review.md`**: new **ID-range shape** worklist bullet next to *Declared name length* and *File path shape*.

  - Released members are reported only through remediate-on-touch at `minor`, never as a request to renumber.
  - The licence-gate enumextension is excluded because it is already checked by `cmfrt-license-feature-gate` (c).
- **`cmfrt-object-id-ranges.md`**:
  - Best Practice now covers the blank/None member pattern and says member IDs come from the range even when AL Object ID Ninja is unavailable.
  - Anti Pattern now covers enums that start at 0 and out-of-range enums copied from older code.
  - Adds the keywords `field` and `value`.
- **Samples**: `.bad.al` gains a 0-based enum in a customer app; `.good.al` gains the in-range enum and a field defaulting through `InitValue`.

author: dlrivada
body:
Phase 2 of 7 of the #1705 implementation plan (`docs/plans/security-context-population-implementation-plan-1705.md`, tasks 1-13): declared service identities and the delegate-only scope API.

## What changes

- **Service identities**: `AddEncinaServiceIdentity(name, builder)`, a validated catalog (`ValidateOnStart`; name pattern, uniqueness, `encina.` reserved, no identity-granting claim types in `WithClaim`), internal `AddBuiltInServiceIdentity`.
- **`IRequestContextScopeFactory`** (delegate-only, ROP): `RunAsServiceAsync`, `RunAsPrincipalAsync`, `RunInboundAsync`, `RunRestoredAsync(persisted, PersistedIdentitySource, work, trustedTenantId)`; internal `RunAsBuiltInAsync`/`RunHostInboundAsync`. Refusals never invoke `work`; inbound input is normalised, never refused.
- **Accessor**: `Pop` becomes `End` (invalidate only); holders carry immutable origin/kind facts that survive invalidation and are inherited, so the refusals walk the whole chain; the setter preserves identity and origin and stores a snapshot; `ReadContext` checks the issuer is live.
- **`RequestIdentity`**: `ForService`; issuer binding; `Principal` returns a copy of the authenticated identities only; `IsSameAs` ignores the union of per-token claim types (`RequestIdentityOptions.PerTokenClaimTypes`).
- **Resolve** rule order of Design 1 plus the tenant rule; 5 new error codes; EventIds 166-175 (core range).
- **Architecture tests**: identity minting and binding primitives only in the scope factory/accessor/dispatcher; no production assembly references `Encina.Testing`.
- **Tests migrated, none deleted**: 86 setter lines in 11 files, 40 `Push`/`Pop` calls, the issuer-less explicit dispatches. New unit, guard, contract and property tests for every task-13 bullet.
- **#1884**: FsCheck 3.3.2's overload is `Gen.Sample(generator, numberOfSamples, size)`; all 35 calls now use named arguments (200/200 consecutive passes of the flaky test).

## Verification

Build 0 warnings; UnitTests 23315 passed (1 skipped), GuardTests 7710, ContractTests 1891, PropertyTests 1328 (1 skipped); crap-gate: 155 changed methods, none over 10; `--check-missing-manifest` clean, per-file targets justified (#1762); format and changelog checks clean. Adversarial review (Opus): no blocker; the major and three minors fixed; two spec gaps tracked in #1892.

## Interim note

Until Phase 3 (HTTP integration in `EncinaContextMiddleware`) the middleware still installs an anonymous context without the inbound marker, so an anonymous HTTP request can open `RunAsServiceAsync` without `AllowOverInbound`. Pre-1.0 and no release is planned before Phase 3; Phase 3 is the next front of #1705.

Refs #1705
Fixes #1884

author: hung3a8
body:
Team fix 29.

## Problem
With `@AccessTokenOptional()`, `AccessTokenGuard` set `request.user` before checking the role. When the role check threw, the optional `catch` returned `true`. `IPAddressGuard` then skipped its own check because `request.user` was set. As a result, a coach or guest token could read remote-control scripts (`GET /remote-control/scripts/:name`).

## Change
- `request.user` is set only after the role check passes.
- Jest's `moduleNameMapper` still used the old `@app/*` aliases, so no spec could import library code. It now maps `@libs/*`. The same mapping change appears in the other new utilities-v2 PRs and merges cleanly.

## Testing
- New `accessToken.guard.spec.ts`. It fails on `main`.
- **Lab `internal` with the real guards, `GET /remote-control/scripts/<name>`:**

| Request | Status |
|---|---|
| Coach token, `main` | 200 |
| Coach token, this branch | 401 |
| Admin token | 200 |
| No token, contestant machine's VPN IP | 200 |

#41360 리뷰 대응이에요. #41360 은 리뷰가 오기 전에 병합돼서, 반영분을 새 PR 로 올려요.

## 바꾼 것

1. **Muse 사용률 출처를 하나(`muse.subscription_usage`)로 합쳤어요.**
   - `usage/changed` 와 `usage/read` 는 같은 두 창을 같은 행 키(`limit_id`, 창 종류)에 써요.
   - 그런데 complete snapshot 은 자기 출처가 쓴 행만 지워요.
   - 그래서 출처가 둘이면, 5시간 창 길이가 바뀐 `usage/read` 가 와도 `usage/changed` 가 쓴 "5h" 행이 Overview 에 남아요.
   - 이제 둘 다 같은 출처로 기록해요. 어느 경로였는지는 로그 문장에만 남아요.
2. **다 쓴 계정을 쉬게 하는 처리를 기록보다 먼저 해요.**
   기록은 이력 파일 쓰기로 끝나고, 턴과 함께 취소될 수 있어요. 예전 순서에서는 그 사이에 취소되면 쉬게 하는 처리가 빠졌어요.
3. `changelog.d/41360.md` 의 출처 이름도 새 이름으로 고쳤어요.

#41360 은 아직 배포 전이라 옛 출처 이름으로 저장된 이력은 없어요(`provider_usage_history/2026-10/06.jsonl` 0행).

| 지적 | 처리 |
|---|---|
| P3-1 쉬게 하기가 파일 쓰기 뒤에 있음 | 순서 바꿈 |
| P3-2 두 출처가 같은 행을 쓰고 자기 것만 지움 | 출처 하나로 합침, 테스트 추가 |

author: andrew666ai
body: ## Summary Phase 3.4 of the Photon → PhotoCraft gap: Select and Mask refine without Photon weights or a hair-matting download. - `select.refineEdge` detects the edge band, uses smart radius (hard edges stay at the measured transition; hair and fur open to the full radius), and mixes a colour-line alpha into the guided filter. Smooth, feather, contrast, and shift edge still run after that. - Decontaminate colours solves the matte equation `C = α F + (1−α) B` and writes the recovered foreground. Selection and layer-mask output upgrade to a new layer with a mask when decontaminate is on. - `select.refineBrush` limits that refine to a stroke (`refine`, `add`, or `subtract`). The Refine Edge Brush is in the W flyout; Shift adds and Alt subtracts. - CLI and MCP call the command ids. The `select-and-mask` skill plans `select.refineEdge` on an existing selection. - Docs: `docs/photon-gap-phase-3-select-and-mask.md`. Roadmap row 3.4 is MVP. ## Quality limits This is not a learned hair matte. - The colour line assumes one foreground colour and one background colour in the window. Wisps that do not match the solid selection, or that sit on a background of the same colour, stay wrong. - Colour samples stop at about 48 px. A strand farther than that from both a known foreground and a known background is left alone until you paint it with the brush. Raising the radius does not extend that colour window. - A busy background inside the radius can pick up partial alpha when its colour falls on the foreground–background line. Smart radius can also open on other high-frequency texture (foliage, fabric). - Decontaminate uses one background colour. A fringe over two backgrounds keeps a compromise. - The colour line is estimated in RGB, then the matte is applied in the document’s own channels. - There is no separate Select and Mask workspace (view modes, onion skin, or a live radius preview). ## 1. Overview

This Pull Request bumps Ruby from 4.0.6 to 4.0.7 across 3 files in `template-creators`.  

Ruby 4.0.7 was released on 2026-09-15 as a routine bugfix update of the 4.0 series; the announcement lists no CVE.  
It fixes 24 tickets, most of them crashes and regressions — including two reported against 4.0.6 itself (Bug #22220, a `require` performance regression with `aws-sdk-ec2`, and Bug #22242, a SEGV in method dispatch).  

The change is confined to version pins, base images and environment documentation; no application code moves.  

## 2. Key Changes & Differences

**2-1. Ruby — 4.0.6 → 4.0.7**

|Area |Before (4.0.6) |After (4.0.7, 2026-09-15) |Changes & Differences |
|:-|:-|:-|:-|
|Regressions from 4.0.6 |2 open |Fixed |SEGV in method dispatch (Bug #22242); slow `require` of `aws-sdk-ec2` (Bug #22220). |
|Memory safety / crashes |— |8 fixes |Heap-use-after-free in `fiber_switch` with transfer-terminated async tasks (Bug #22196); `GC.auto_compact` corrupting a String / segfaulting in `String#tr` (Bug #22237); Arrays sharing a buffer segfaulting on concatenation (Bug #22259); win32 heap overflow in `Kernel#system` (Bug #22198); `EncodingError` from symbol interpolation crashing the process (Bug #22303); `Coverage.start` + ruby/debug segfault (Bug #22217); YJIT/ZJIT Struct accessor crash after an ivar is set (Bug #22292); `ObjectSpace._id2ref` returning the wrong object (Bug #22200). |
|VM / method caches |— |3 fixes |Stale super caches after `prepend` (Bug #22257); ivars on anonymous objects bloating future classes (Bug #22290); `Class#subclasses` missing clones of classes that include modules (Bug #22190). |
|Networking / process |— |2 fixes |`Socket.tcp` with `connect_timeout` returning a phantom connected socket (Bug #22223); `fork` behaviour when `Process._fork` raises (Bug #22243). |
|Coverage / TracePoint |— |2 fixes |`Coverage.line_stub` clobbering collected data (Bug #22269); line TracePoint missing a loop condition after a guard (Bug #22218). |
|JIT / misc |— |6 fixes |YJIT `rb_yjit_invalidate_ep_is_bp` regression with Ractors (Bug #22224); `Ruby::Box` + `BUNDLER_SETUP` ordering (Bug #22123); missing `parse.y` hash-literal warning (Bug #22264); addr2line with GCC LTO (Bug #22188); win32 `ENV.keys` encoding and stack address (Bug #20958, #11438). |

**2-2. Files Updated in This Repository**

|Files |Before |After |Changes & Differences |
|:-|:-|:-|:-|
|`.ruby-version` |4.0.6 |4.0.7 |Pinned interpreter read by rbenv and `ruby/setup-ruby` in CI. |
|`SECURITY.md` |4.0.6 |4.0.7 |Updated the supported-versions table. |
|`ruby/README.md` |4.0.6 |4.0.7 |Updated the environment section. |

## 3. Summary

- Bumped Ruby from 4.0.6 to 4.0.7 across 3 files (+3 / -3).
- A bugfix-only patch release with no CVE; the regressions from 4.0.6 (Bug #22220, #22242) are the main reason to move.
