author: sandyorz
body:
## 🚀 Descripción del PR
Implementación completa de la arquitectura **Offline-First**, migración de IDs y motor de sincronización bidireccional con Firebase, fusionado con el nuevo flujo de sesión de administrador.

### 🛠 Cambios Principales (Core & Base de Datos)
* **Migración a UUID v4 (Base de Datos v9):** Se cambiaron las llaves primarias de SQLite de `INTEGER` a `TEXT`. Esto garantiza cero colisiones al crear registros offline.
* **Tombstone Pattern (Borrado Lógico):** Los registros ya no se borran físicamente. Se agregaron las columnas `eliminado_en`, `eliminado_por` y `restaurado_en` para la sincronización con la nube.
* **Estandarización UTC:** Todas las fechas generadas localmente ahora se guardan en UTC puro para evitar desajustes horarios entre dispositivos.
* **Aislamiento de Catálogos:** Se agregó la columna `taller_id` a los catálogos (Técnicos, Tipos de Servicio, Marcas, Grupos). El `ConfiguracionController` ahora inyecta el ID del taller desde la sesión actual.

### ☁️ Sincronización (Firebase)
* **SyncService Bidireccional:** Un servicio en segundo plano que escucha el `ConnectivityService`. Al volver el internet, sube las citas pendientes a Firestore y descarga los cambios de la nube a SQLite vía `onSnapshot`.
* **Código Visible Diferido:** Las citas creadas offline nacen con código `PENDIENTE`. Al subir a la nube, una transacción en Firestore les asigna su código secuencial definitivo (`CITA-0001`), el cual baja automáticamente a la interfaz local.

### ✅ Integración con Main
* Conflictos resueltos: Se priorizó el login real con Firebase (`SesionAdmin`) implementado en `main`, eliminando el login anónimo de desarrollo. El `taller_id` ya fluye correctamente hacia la pantalla de Configuración.

author: djbclark
body:
## Summary

`LegacyShizukuBinderProxy` (r2739) subtracts 1 from every transaction code for apps that request `moe.shizuku.manager.permission.API_V23`, and since c643e740 only for those that request no ShizukuPlus permission. That is exactly the set of apps built on the stock `dev.rikka.shizuku:api`, and those apps do **not** send positional codes. An AIDL method declared `= N` is transaction `FIRST_CALL_TRANSACTION + N` (N + 1) on the wire, in the stock library and in the ShizukuPlus one alike; the generated `IShizukuService.Stub` already expects those codes. With the −1 offset each call that reaches the stub runs the method one below it, for example `addUserService` (wire 12) arrives as `setSystemProperty` (wire 11), and `bindUserService` fails with `IllegalStateException`. We hit it with our own app on an SM-S921U1.

The proxy only seemed to work for some calls because the hand-written switch in `Service.onTransact()` (api submodule, `server-shared`) matches bare N for a few methods, which cancels the offset for those calls and nothing else.

This PR:

1. Removes `LegacyShizukuBinderProxy` and `isLegacyOriginalShizukuApp`. Every app gets the real binder.
2. Handles the three wire codes that the `Service.onTransact()` switch mis-numbers, first, in `ShizukuService.onTransact()`. It decides by the shape of the parcel, never by who is calling:
   - **3**: `getVersion` (the switch answers `getUid`).
   - **14**: `attachApplication(IBinder, String)` from API ≤ 12. This is the same parcel the library's own `attachApplicationV11` sends. The switch runs `requestPermission` on it.
   - **17**: `shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale` when the parcel has no arguments (`data.dataAvail() == 0` after the interface token). With arguments it is the ShizukuPlus library's `attachApplicationV13` (bare 17, `binder, int, Bundle`). That call falls through unchanged to `Service.onTransact()`, which rewinds the parcel and attaches as it does today.
3. Adds a CHANGELOG entry.

## Why #567's premise does not hold

#567 / c643e740 assume Installer X Revived and Universal Installer X "declare the original permission for backward compat while actually using ShizukuPlus explicit AIDL codes". Installer X Revived is built on the **stock** library: `gradle/libs.versions.toml` has `rikka-shizuku = "13.1.5"` with `dev.rikka.shizuku:api` and `dev.rikka.shizuku:provider`. Its `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` requests no `af.shizuku.*` permission. The stock library sends exactly the codes the generated stub expects, so the −1 offset is wrong for it. Because it declares no ShizukuPlus permission, the narrowed predicate in c643e740 still matches it, so it is still wrapped. That is from reading the code; we have not tested Installer X Revived on c643e740. Total Commander (#566) is in the same position for the same reason. No caller-identity predicate can be correct here. Stock-library apps and Plus-library apps send the same codes, so there is nothing to translate.

## Why decide by the parcel and not by the caller

Only code 17 is ambiguous: the generated rationale call and the Plus library's hand-coded attach both use it. They differ in their arguments. An app can request both permissions, and the manager is itself a client, so any rule keyed on which permissions an app requests will give some app the wrong answer.

## Testing

1. `:server:compileDebugJavaWithJavac :manager:compileShizukuplusDebugKotlin` pass on this branch (based on `master` at bba70c4c).
2. The same change is in our fork (ShizukuTendCF). Removing the proxy was checked on a device: a stock-API client's `addUserService` / `bindUserService` work on an SM-S921U1. The code-17 split by parcel shape comes from reading both client libraries, not from a device test: the generated rationale call sends no arguments, and `attachApplicationV13` sends `binder, int, Bundle`.

Refs #566, #567.

body:
Part (a) of #5939 — experiments as data. Every experiment write-up in `scripts/eval/experiments/` gets a small YAML header (status, verdict, measure, stage, languages/scripts/canons, n, decision, superseded_by, issue). This PR defines the header and enforces it on new files. It does not backfill anything yet.

## In scope
- **Schema**: a new section, "The header (#5939)", in `scripts/eval/experiments/README.md`. That README is copied verbatim into the generated EXPERIMENTS.md.
  - `stage`: ocr | translation | metadata | image | pipeline.
  - `measure`: the eval-design.md §2/§5.2 enum (accuracy | agreement | stability | preference | judged | judged_vs_reference), plus `none` for plans, censuses and repair logs.
  - `languages`: ISO 639 codes. `scripts`: ISO 15924 codes.
  - `canons`: canon-gap corpus and tradition ids, checked against `canon-gap-status-*.json`.
  - `n_books` / `n_pages`, one-line `verdict`, `status` (adopted | rejected | undecided | superseded | informational), `decision`, `superseded_by` (must exist), `issue`.
- **Reader**: `scripts/eval/lib/experiment-header.mjs` (split, parse, validate, serialize). It reads a flat YAML subset with no dependency, because js-yaml is only a transitive dependency here. I checked that what it writes parses the same under js-yaml.
- **Lint**: `scripts/eval/experiments-lint.mjs`, run in `unit-tests.yml` next to the existing generated-ledger gate (#5436).
  - It refuses a dated entry the PR **adds** without a valid header, and an invalid header on any file.

- **Builder**: `build-experiments.mjs` drops the header, so EXPERIMENTS.md reads exactly as before. `--check` still passes on main's tree.
- **Tests**: `tests/unit/experiment-header.test.ts`. They cover the round trip, quoting, enum, code and canon errors, superseded_by, the builder dropping the header, and the lint grandfathering an old file vs refusing the same file when it is new (negative control).

- (b) the backfill of the 162 existing entries.
- (c) `index.json` plus switching /quality and the canon pages over to it.

author: sebr214
body:
Part of SEB-264. First of its three numbered fixes; see the issue for the other two and why they are not in this PR.

**What changed**

1. `tools/check_copy_lock.py`: `owner_label()` no longer requires the `copy-approved` label to post after the PR's *latest* commit. It still passes instantly in that usual case. When a later push happened, it now compares copy.json's text at the moment of approval against copy.json's text now (via the PR's own commit list + `git show`); if the words are unchanged, approval still holds. A push that only touched layout/js/a merge from main no longer forces re-approval of words nobody re-wrote.
2. `agents/RULES.md` and `agents/REVIEWER.md`: wrote down the rule SEB-262 exposed — a merge waits for an actual posted reviewer verdict, not green checks alone. PR #406 merged 2 minutes before its own CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict posted, so the fail had nowhere to go. This is process documentation; nothing in this PR changes merge mechanics (no PR here is self-merged on it).

**Why not items 2 and 3**

- *Split copy.json into one file per page*: ~30 call sites read `copy.json` today (every page's own JS, every `tools/emit_*`/`bake_*` script, `check_copy_lock.py`, `check_copy.py`, `check_page.py`, `.github/workflows/checks.yml`'s path matching). A correct split touches all of them plus the writer's own workflow and deserves its own PR with its own verification, not folded into this one under the same review pass.
- *Deterministic cold reader + stored verdicts*: the default backend shells out to the `claude` CLI, which has no `--temperature` flag to pin to 0 (confirmed via `claude -p --help`); only the optional OpenRouter backend already sets temperature 0. Making the primary path deterministic means either a CLI capability that doesn't exist yet or switching the default backend, which is a cost/policy call (RULES.md: "no new running cost without a number stated first"), not a code-only fix. Persisting verdicts durably (so a passed sentence stays passed) needs a cache file committed back from CI, which means a new write-permission path into a PR branch or a separate scheduled job — more surface than this fix. Logged on SEB-264 for a follow-up PR.

**Verification**

```
python3 tools/check_copy_lock.py --self-test
```
New cases cover: text-equal despite reformatting, text differs blocks, and the commit-at-label-time lookup (all pure, no network).

body:
Codex independently loads `.codex/config.toml` and `.codex/hooks.json`. Existing spyc reporters in both files caused prompt, permission and stop events to arrive twice.

Keep spyc reporters in TOML and migrate only its handlers out of legacy JSON. Preserve user handlers in shared matcher groups, user-only files and trust records. Refuse tracked reporters or malformed/unreadable legacy sources before adding canonical reporters. Include both sources in cleanup and presence checks, retain shared ownership when migration is refused, and flag JSON-only changes as requiring a Codex restart.

The support plan records #543 as merged and the remaining approval/question recovery audit. This change leaves those recovery semantics open.

Validation:
- `RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 make check`: 2,740 library tests passed, one existing ignored test, plus integration/reporter and VT-system tests.
- Migration regressions reproduced the original failures; mutations demonstrated restart, handler-preservation, cleanup and ownership coverage.

author: buddas-bible
body:
HyruleEngine과 Phyzzle의 원래 C++ 물리엔진·게임 클라이언트에서 반복되는 계산·주석·배치 패턴에 맞춰 Distance/Mouse Joint와 관련 데모 코드를 다듬습니다. Hyrule 충돌/강체/행렬/입력, Phyzzle DistanceJoint·RigidBodyHelper·Player·AttachHoldState·AttachSystem·RewindSystem을 비교했고, 참고 파일과 적용 규칙은 docs/coding-style.md에 기록했습니다.

물리 개념 → 중간 계산값 → 적용 순서로 계산과 한국어 주석을 정리했습니다. 작용점 상대속도를 v_a/w_a/v_b/w_b/v_p2/v_r로 드러내고, bodySim/bodyState와 A/B 역할을 명확히 했습니다. 헤더에는 물리량의 의미를 짧게 적고, 데모 입력·설정·장면 생성·드래그는 선언/구현에서 같은 순서로 배치했습니다. 과도한 호출 줄바꿈과 압축된 대입·분기도 정리했습니다.

작업 중 작성자가 직접 제거한 짧은 조인트 구조체·Mouse Solver의 region과 데모의 계산 단계별 여백도 참고했습니다. Region은 긴 솔버·데모의 의미 있는 그룹에 사용하며 짧은 코드에는 형식적으로 붙이지 않습니다. 사용자의 원래 작업 폴더에 있는 미커밋 변경은 보존했습니다.

공개 API·멤버 순서·기본값·UI 표시·알고리즘을 유지합니다. 상대속도의 덧셈/뺄셈 순서, 각 제한이 읽는 최신 속도, chained assignment의 오른쪽부터 적용 순서를 유지했습니다. 문서화한 local 이름 변경·순수 중간값 분해·대입 분리만 정규화한 코드 비교, 헤더/CPP 순서와 region 검사를 통과했습니다.

최종 검증: Sandbox ON Debug/Release 빌드 및 전체 테스트 각각 43/43. Sandbox OFF Release 빌드와 Distance/Mouse 단위·World 및 데모 테스트 5/5. 실제 OS/GPU 화면 조작은 이번 스타일 작업에서 검사하지 않았습니다. 이전 프로젝트 파일은 참고용으로 읽었으며 변경하지 않았습니다.

author: kevbite
body:
## Context

The Cases API declares `IsValidForInheritanceTax` on the Pension, Land and Building write representations as `[Required] bool?`, and the domain excludes an item from IHT only on an explicit `false`. The SDK's write models (`Post`/`Put*ResourceRepresentation`, via the `*ResourceRepresentationBase` classes) exposed it as a plain `bool`, so a caller that never set it sent `false` and the item's date-of-death value silently dropped to 0.

## Changes

- **`IsValidForInheritanceTax` defaults to `true`** on `PensionResourceRepresentationBase`, `LandResourceRepresentationBase` and `BuildingResourceRepresentationBase`. This matches the legacy rule ("true unless explicitly false").
  - The base classes are write-only. The GET models (`PensionResourceRepresentation` and the others) are separate classes and already `bool?`, so deserialisation is untouched.
  - The type stays `bool`, so `ICanBeValidForIht` and existing callers still compile. The frontend's write mapper always sets the property explicitly, so its behaviour is unchanged.
- **`LandResourceRepresentationBase.IsHeritable` is marked `[Obsolete]`.** The API's land write representation has no such field, because land is always heritable.
  - The property is kept and still serialised, so the wire shape and source compatibility are unchanged.
  - Consumers get a CS0618 warning. exizent-frontend does not set `TreatWarningsAsErrors`.
- **Wire-shape tests.** POST and PUT for each of the three types assert that an unset `IsValidForInheritanceTax` serialises as `true`. All 6 fail without the default.

## Release

Publishes from main as `0.0.<run number>-preview`. The frontend picks it up in a later bump.

author: andreas203
body:
YOK-48 (part of the YOK-39 vertical slice): the demo flow from boot to "demo complete".

## What it does
- **Boot:** straight into Ryo vs Kitsune, Kihon, on a fresh `RunState` (Ryo at 1,000, C1).
- **Loss:** the HUD lose screen with the real `data/story/lose-screen.json` text. **Restart** starts a fresh run at the first fight.
- **Win:** the KO slow-down (V4), then the binding line card (`data/story/binding-line.json`), then the reward screen with three Kitsune cards (`RewardDraft.Build(run, pool, "kitsune", RunSeed + duel)` through `DraftRewardSource`). The pick is applied to the run, then the **rematch** starts with the pick active and Ryo at health left + 50, capped at 1,000 (R3).
- **After the rematch:** a win shows a "Demo complete" card with Restart. A loss shows the lose screen.
- **Recordings:** each duel finishes its own recording (`DuelRecordings`). The rematch and every restart start a new recording at tick 0, stamped with the run (carried health, drafted slots and modifier, run hash).
- **Debug builds only:** **F9** opens a menu that pauses the fight. From it you can pick the Kitsune's temperament (aggressive / patient), restart the run or resume. `-- --temperament=patient` picks one before the first fight. F9 avoids the E9 keys and the F1–F8 debug keys. F6 still swaps temperament.

The code lives in the new `FightScene.Flow.cs` partial and `DemoScreens.cs`, plus these small hooks:
- `NewMatch(run)` overload
- `_Ready`/`Step`/`_Process` calls
- HUD Restart rewired to `RestartRun`
- "R to reset" dropped from the win banner
- `Dismiss()` on `StoryCard` and `RewardScreen`
- the recorder takes `DemoRun`

The static `FightScene.Run` is respected if set, but never written.

## Tests
- `dotnet build`: 0 errors.
- `test_runner.tscn`: **202 passed, 0 failed** (194 before, plus 8 new in `DemoFlowTests.cs`):
  - boot state
  - win → binding → reward → rematch, once for each of the NEW / UPGRADE / MODIFIER cards
  - health cap
  - loss → Restart
  - a lost rematch drops the pick on Restart
  - a won rematch → demo complete → Restart
  - restart mid-draft
  - the debug temperament menu
- A one-off check on real `data/` (not committed) went KO → "Forgive me, Kitsune. I'll give it back." → Foxfire / Spirit Wave Lv 2 / Will-o'-wisp → rematch with Foxfire in slot C.
- `python tools/validate_data.py`: 77/77 valid. `python -m unittest discover -s tools -p "test_*.py"`: OK.

## Run from a clean checkout (under 2 minutes)
Requirements: .NET SDK 10 and Godot 4.7 .NET (mono).
```
git clone https://github.com/Andreas203/yokai-fighters.git && cd yokai-fighters/game
git checkout YOK-48-demo-flow
dotnet build
<godot-mono-console-exe> --headless --path . --import      # first run only, imports assets
<godot-mono-exe> --path .                                    # plays the demo (debug build: F9 menu)
<godot-mono-console-exe> --headless --path . res://tests/test_runner.tscn   # optional: tests
```
Controls (Kihon, E9): WASD to move; U/I/O punches; J/K/L kicks; Space plus a direction for a special. On the cards: Enter continues, Left/Right choose, Enter picks, Tab shows frame data.

## Designer review
- The "Demo complete" / "Thanks for playing." copy is placeholder UI text. Does it want a story card from habit-writer?
- Restart from the debug menu keeps the chosen temperament. Restart from an end screen keeps it too, because the AI profile isn't part of the run.
- R after a KO still replays the current duel (debug convenience). Should it be debug-only?
- The draft seed is `RunSeed` 48 + duel number, so every run offers the same three cards. Should it be per-run random?

author: artui
body:
Every step in `upstream-drift.yml` that opens or closes an issue now runs only on `main`. Here that is `pydantic-ai-interop`'s issue step.

**Why.** Each issue reports on `main`'s state. Dispatched from a branch, the ungated steps would file that branch's failure against `main`, or close `main`'s issue on the strength of a fix that hasn't landed. resolve-latest was already gated. This covers the rest of the workflow, so a branch dispatch is now a trial that touches no issue, as it already was in the family's other ten drift workflows.

Each condition keeps its status function. An `if:` that names none still implies `success()`, which is why the step that had no condition behaves as before on `main`.

CI-only, so there is no changelog entry and no release.

author: mcollina
body:
Adds coverage for `server.portAssignment: 'perWorkerIncrement'` when workers are replaced.

- **High-ELU replacement keeps the port** (all platforms): a worker pushed over `maxELU` is replaced, and the replacement answers on the same incremental port while the other ports are untouched. This was the only replacement path without a test. Restart, health update and crash restart were already covered.
- **Ports never refuse connections with `reusePort`** (Linux only, skipped where `features.node.reusePort` is false): the ports are polled during `restartApplication` and during a high-ELU replacement, and any `ECONNREFUSED` fails the test. Nothing tested this before, for per-worker ports or the shared port.

The `multiple-workers/node` fixture gets a `POST /busy` route that keeps the event loop busy.

### Connection resets during a handover

On Linux each replacement still causes some `ECONNRESET`s, though the port stays open. A plain-Node reproduction (two `http` servers sharing a port with `reusePort`, closing the old one) shows two causes:

| Client | `net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req=0` (default) | `=1` |
|---|---|---|
| Fresh connection per request | 15–22 resets per 20 handovers | 0 |
| Keep-alive | 80 (one per pooled socket per handover) | 80 |

- Connections queued on the closing listener are reset by the kernel unless `tcp_migrate_req` is enabled.
- `server.close()` closes idle keep-alive sockets while clients may be reusing them.

The tests assert on `ECONNREFUSED` only. Making the handover reset-free would be a separate change.

On macOS (no `reusePort`) the old worker is stopped before the new one starts, so the port is closed until the busy worker exits. The cross-platform test allows up to 30s for that.

author: adamawan
body:
## Why

A watched dependency-bot PR with a red build got the same one-line `pr-ci-fix` prompt as the fleet's own work. In practice the agent had to be steered into asking whether the *update* was at fault, checking upstream, and suggesting we abandon the PR and wait for the next bump. This makes that the default path.

## What changed

**Dependency brief on the CI fix** (`src/botPrs/ciBrief.ts`): when `pr.botAuthored`, `pr-ci-failing` appends a brief (appended, never interpolated, so overridden templates still get it) with:
- package and from/to versions (`readDependencyUpdate`)
- release notes from the PR body, and the dependency's repo to search issues/releases
- the risk verdict on this head, if any
- the four outcomes to decide *before* changing code: `adapted`, `upstream-bug`, `intended-break`, `unclear`

**`dependency_outcome` MCP tool** (`src/mcp/tools/dependencyOutcome.ts`, `src/botPrs/outcome.ts`):
- advertised on `pr-ci-failing` only; refused off a `pr:<n>:ci` origin or on a PR that isn't a bot's
- written against the head the world holds, into new table `bot_pr_outcomes` keyed `(pr, head)`
- `upstream-bug` requires `upstream_url`; `fixed_in` optional
- for anything but `adapted` the brief asks the agent to then `escalate`

**The hold**: an outcome other than `adapted` on the current head suppresses `pr-ci-failing` for that PR (`ciHeldByOutcome`, fed via `DispatchContext.botPrOutcomes`). Fails open on every arm — not a bot's PR, no reported head, outcome on another head. A bot rebase/re-bump moves the head and the fleet tries again.

**Close from the tab**: `POST /api/bot-prs/:number/close` → `BotPrReader.close` → connector `closePr` (closed on GitHub, abandoned on Azure). Refuses numbers not in the bot reading (404). The Bot PRs tab draws the outcome (summary, fixed-in, upstream link) and a **Close and wait for the next** button; the strip counts these as "to close or take on". Renovate and Dependabot both treat a closed PR as "skip this version".

**Specs**: 37 (new *When CI fails on one* and *Closing one*), 05, 07, 11, 14, 16.

## Reviewer notes

- New table only, no `ALTER TABLE` needed.
- The brief reads only world + store synchronously; it does not fetch GitHub releases the way the risk desk does.
- `test/botPrCiOutcome.test.ts` covers the hold, the brief, tool refusals, the tab payload and the close route.
- Locally: typecheck, typecheck:web, lint, knip and Prettier pass; 16 related suites pass under tsx. `npm test` couldn't run on this Windows box (test build spawns `.bin/esbuild` without the `.cmd` shim) — CI will be the full run.
- Verified in the demo cockpit: outcome row renders and the close button removes the PR.

## 1. Huỷ ⇒ thu hồi hết (commit e48aa68f)
**Gốc lỗi** (tái hiện test D1 thật, đỏ trước khi sửa): `huy` chỉ đổi `trang_thai`. **Luật**: huỷ = như chưa từng giao; kết thúc (`dong`) KHÔNG đổi; không xoá/sửa dữ liệu thật (sổ làm bài, điểm, EXP giữ nguyên).

body:
## Summary

While the device is locked, `AdbStartWorker.handleAuth()` promotes itself to a foreground service and waits for `ACTION_USER_PRESENT`, then for the adbd authorization dialog. It asks for `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_SHORT_SERVICE`, which Android 14+ allows for only about 3 minutes. After that the system calls `Service.onTimeout` and WorkManager (2.10) stops the worker; a shortService that does not stop in time gets an ANR instead. So a phone left locked after boot for more than ~3 minutes, or a slow answer to the dialog after the unlock, loses the boot-time start.

- The worker now asks for `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_SPECIAL_USE`. It has no time limit and is not one of the types Android 15 forbids from `BOOT_COMPLETED`.
- WorkManager's `SystemForegroundService` declares `shortService|specialUse`, because a worker's `ForegroundInfo` type must be listed there or the OS throws `InvalidForegroundServiceTypeException`. `WatchdogWorker`'s short heal keeps `shortService`. The service carries the `PROPERTY_SPECIAL_USE_FGS_SUBTYPE` that `specialUse` requires.
- `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_SPECIAL_USE` is already requested in the manifest.
- Adds a CHANGELOG entry.

## Testing

- `:manager:compileShizukuplusDebugKotlin` and `:manager:processShizukuplusDebugMainManifest` pass. The merged manifest has `foregroundServiceType="shortService|specialUse"` on `SystemForegroundService` with the subtype property.
- The same change ships in our fork (ShizukuTendCF 1fc75ffb). There the built APK's merged manifest type is `0x40000800` (specialUse|shortService).

Depends-On: https://github.com/DEFRA/nrf-backend/pull/331

## Summary

Gets `npm run security-audit` (and therefore the Docker build audit step and CI) green again after the October 2026 advisory wave, and clears every npm audit finding that has an upstream fix.

## Changes

- **chokidar `^4.0.3` override under `nodemon` and `nunjucks`** — chokidar v4 dropped the `braces` globbing dependency, and `braces` itself has **no patched version** (GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm, stack-exhaustion DoS). The nunjucks chain was the only one reaching production deps. `--polling-interval 100` (chokidar's own default cadence) is passed in `server:watch`/`server:debug` because nodemon forwards `interval: undefined` to `fs.watchFile` under `--legacy-watch` polling, which Node rejects (`Internal watch failed: The "interval" argument must be of type number` — seen crashing containers in journey CI; details in DEFRA/nrf-backend#331). Legacy-watch restarts and nunjucks template-watch cache invalidation verified. Both overrides dedupe to a single chokidar copy.
- **Clean lockfile regen** picks up the semver fixes: `source-map-js` 1.2.2, `serialize-javascript`, `stylelint-config-recommended`, `stylelint-config-standard`.
- **`security-audit` script now runs `npm audit --omit=dev`** — the 11 remaining highs are all in the dev-only `stylelint` → `globby`/`fast-glob`/`micromatch`/`braces` chain. Those packages are unmaintained with no patched release, and stylelint 17.16 (latest) still depends on them, so no bump or override can clear them. Production images install prod deps only (`npm ci --omit=dev`), so the build gate now covers exactly what ships. This can be reverted to a full audit once upstream releases fixed versions.

## Audit results

| Scope | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--omit=dev` (the gate) | 4 | **0** |
| Full (incl. dev) | 16 | 11 — all in the unfixable stylelint/glob dev chain |

`npm ci`, lint (eslint + stylelint) and the full test suite (1238 tests) pass locally.

The `Depends-On:` above points the "Run Journey Tests" job at DEFRA/nrf-backend#331's branch (audit gate green, container runtime fix included) instead of backend `main`, which is still red.

## 1. Overview

This Pull Request bumps Ruby from 4.0.6 to 4.0.7 across 15 files in `tutorials`.  

Ruby 4.0.7 was released on 2026-09-15 as a routine bugfix update of the 4.0 series; the announcement lists no CVE.  
It fixes 24 tickets, most of them crashes and regressions — including two reported against 4.0.6 itself (Bug #22220, a `require` performance regression with `aws-sdk-ec2`, and Bug #22242, a SEGV in method dispatch).  

The change is confined to version pins, base images and environment documentation; no application code moves.  

## 2. Key Changes & Differences

|:-|:-|:-|:-|
|Regressions from 4.0.6 |2 open |Fixed |SEGV in method dispatch (Bug #22242); slow `require` of `aws-sdk-ec2` (Bug #22220). |
|Memory safety / crashes |— |8 fixes |Heap-use-after-free in `fiber_switch` with transfer-terminated async tasks (Bug #22196); `GC.auto_compact` corrupting a String / segfaulting in `String#tr` (Bug #22237); Arrays sharing a buffer segfaulting on concatenation (Bug #22259); win32 heap overflow in `Kernel#system` (Bug #22198); `EncodingError` from symbol interpolation crashing the process (Bug #22303); `Coverage.start` + ruby/debug segfault (Bug #22217); YJIT/ZJIT Struct accessor crash after an ivar is set (Bug #22292); `ObjectSpace._id2ref` returning the wrong object (Bug #22200). |

author: cellomario
body:
### Why

ffmpeg_encoder_decoder's Decoder already supports setOutputMessageEncoding(), but this plugin never exposed it as a ROS parameter, so there was no way to tell the subscriber what encoding the incoming packets actually use.

This matters for single-channel/Bayer sources. ffmpeg_encoder_decoder supports a documented "single-channel hack": the raw mosaic is wrapped with zero-padded chroma and encoded directly, skipping the CPU demosaic step. That saves real CPU/bandwidth, but only works if the decoder also knows the packet isn't genuine YUV, otherwise it does an ordinary YUV→RGB conversion on zero chroma and produces an all-green image instead of the original mosaic. We hit this on real hardware.

This MR adds the decoder-side piece: a new output_encoding parameter wired to the existing setOutputMessageEncoding(). Opt-in, empty by default, no behavior change unless set.

A companion MR will add the matching encoder-side parameter (cv_bridge_target_format → setCVBridgeTargetFormat()), kept separate since it's a different class/file with its own review considerations. The two are independent at the code level but are meant to be used together for the Bayer passthrough case above.

### What changed

New output_encoding ROS parameter on FFMPEGSubscriber (default "", no-op when unset).
When set, calls decoder_.setOutputMessageEncoding() before each decoder init attempt (re-applied per attempt since a failed initialize() resets the decoder).
Compatibility
Fully additive and backward compatible. No existing parameter, method, or behavior changes. Unset = identical to current behavior.

author: eborden
body:
Closes #177. Closes #131. Part of #61. Follows #172 (`max_blocks`) and the cap PRs #176, #179, #182 and #130.

**Merge after #184.** The new text points at `context-efficiency.md` section 7, which #184 adds. Until it lands the pointer dangles (3 of 3 interim runs flagged it, see below).

## What changed

- **`references/mcp-tools-reference.md`** (the whole code change is in this file; no `src/`):
  - `logseq_search_blocks` (#131): `limit` default 100 and max 500 (the reference said 10 and never named the maximum), clamped not rejected. The result's second content block is always there and carries `totals.matches`. The cut keeps the newest blocks and drops the oldest. The three `results_truncated` cases (M of 500 or fewer, M above 500, `limit` already at 500) and what each `howToFetchAll` and `hasMore` says.
  - `logseq_get_backlinks` (#176): `max_pages` (20, 100) and `max_blocks_per_page` (10, 50), clamp and floor, `pages_truncated` and `page_blocks_truncated` with their `howToFetchAll` rules, `totals: { pages, blocks }`, "the first ones listed, not ranked", and that the second content block comes only when there is something to say (a cut, an alias or date name that was resolved, a page with aliases).
  - `logseq_query_by_property` (#179): `limit` (100, 500), `results_truncated`, `totals.matches`, sorted by page id then block id (so not a ranking, and a per-page count from a cut list is a lower bound). Below 500 `howToFetchAll` names `limit <total>` and returns all. Above 500 it names 500, which returns **500 of N, not all**, and `hasMore` stays true. At 500 there is no `howToFetchAll`. There is no offset. To count, pass a small `limit` and read `totals.matches`.
  - `logseq_search_by_relationship`: `limit` (50, 500). The meta fields are inside the result object (no second block, unlike the other three). `connected-within` counts the top-level blocks of the two pages, topic A's first, and the warning says how many of the kept ones came from each topic; kept blocks keep their children, which aren't counted. `max_distance` doesn't get round the cap.
  - A "Caps that cut a result" table in Best Practices: parameter, default and max, warning code, where the meta is, order of what's kept. It includes `query_by_date_range`.
  - A **Size** paragraph per cap with measured sizes (below).
  - `query_by_date_range`, per the coordinator's note on #184: dropped "Pass 1000 for a work week or a month", now "page at the default of 200", and the warning's raise-to-1000 `howToFetchAll` is marked as not to be followed for a range of days, with a pointer to `context-efficiency.md` section 7.
  - Other stale defaults found while there (the #131 ask): `get_context_for_query` `max_topics` 3 to 5, `max_search_results` 10 to 20 (max 100).
- **`references/context-builder.md`:** one bullet in Workflow 5, Phase 2 (below).

Not touched: `weekly-summary.md`, `monthly-summary.md`, `context-efficiency.md` (#184), `SKILL.md`, `src/`.

## Design

**Do the three `get_backlinks` workflows raise the caps? No.** Workflows 1 and 4 and Session 2 ask for connections, and 20 source pages of 10 blocks fit that (the examples show 12 and 15 pages). The defaults' worst case (200 blocks) is about 40,000 characters on short blocks, already close to what Claude Code shows. Raising them by default to 100 and 50 would risk a result that is saved to a file and loses its meta. Workflow 5 gets one bullet instead: say the list is partial when the warning appears, and raise only for a question that needs every referrer (a blocker hunt), to the numbers the warnings name, both caps in one call while `totals.blocks` is a few hundred or fewer. An earlier version said "one cap at a time", which cost a third call per run for no gain (see the interim row), so it was changed.

**Why sizes are in the reference.** #184 measured that Claude Code saves a result of about 50,000 characters or more to a file and shows only the first 2 KB. The same applies to the other caps' maxima, and the cut warnings don't know about it: `query_by_property`'s own `howToFetchAll` says "set `limit` to 500", which on short blocks is about 83,000 characters. The baseline shows why this matters (below). Sizes measured through the real server on made-up, one-line blocks (about 165 characters per slim block, 150 for search, 200 per backlinks block, 215 per full block for relationship, each plus any extra block text):

| Call | Characters |
|---|---|
| `query_by_property`, `limit=100` / 250 / 300 / 500 | ~17,000 / ~41,000 / ~50,000 / ~83,000 |
| `search_blocks`, 180 matches | ~27,000 (500 would be ~75,000) |
| `search_by_relationship`, `limit=50` / 80 | ~11,000 / ~17,000 (500 would be over 100,000) |
| `get_backlinks`, defaults (20 of 32 pages, 84 blocks) / all (32 pages, 138 blocks) | ~17,000 / ~29,000 |

The reference gives approximate thresholds (about 250 for `query_by_property`, 330 for `search_blocks`, 200 for `search_by_relationship`) and says to narrow the query rather than raise a cap to its maximum. Whether the 50,000 figure holds on other hosts or versions isn't known; it was measured by #184.

**What the reference doesn't do.** It doesn't change any warning text, since that is `src/`. `get_concept_evolution`'s `max_entries` is a #61 cap with no reference entry; it's outside #177's list and left alone.

## ADR-0024: baseline and after (counts only)

**Method (as #172 and #184):** headless helpers (`claude -p`, Opus, `--strict-mcp-config`) calling the real tool through a stdio proxy that serves a fake LogSeq HTTP API on a random 127.0.0.1 port (never 12315) and forwards each call to this checkout's server code unchanged. Bash, Edit, Skill and Agent were disallowed; helpers could only call the one tool, Read and write their report, and were told not to save tool results to files. Each ran in its own `/tmp` folder with a copy of the skill (`main`'s for the baseline). Nothing touched a real LogSeq, `~/.logseq` or `~/.logseq-mcp`. The harness is under the gitignored `.logseq-instance/`. Each helper was told the user's question, to read `SKILL.md`, follow its loading instructions and read `context-efficiency.md` and the tools reference, and to report its calls and any doc gaps.

**Data (made up):**
- backlinks: 32 source pages (138 linking blocks), one of them with 16 blocks. Three blockers: one visible by default, one past the per-page cap (13th block of the 16), one past the page cap (page 26).
- property: 620 blocks with `status:: doing` over 14 pages, the biggest page (150) last in id order.
- search: 180 matching blocks over 12 pages; the only cancellation note is the oldest.
- relationship: 80 blocks on page A referencing page B; three delay blocks, at positions 12, 66 and 79 (the last two past the default cap of 50).

body:
### What

Return `PAD_ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE` (0x80920003) from `scePadReadState` for a handle that is not open, instead of throwing `invalid argument`.

PPSA14632 (LEGO Horizon Adventures, Unreal Engine) opens one pad with `scePadOpen(0x10000000, 0, 0, NULL)` (handle 1) and then calls `scePadReadState` (eboot 0x4593a8) for that pad and for a second pad slot it never opened, whose handle is still 0. The title skips only negative handles before the call and does not check the result. On `main` the second call throws. The other functions in `libScePad` already return `PAD_ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE` for an unknown handle, and shadPS4's `scePadRead` (which its `scePadReadState` calls) does the same. `scePadRead` passes the error on. A null `data` still throws.

### Tested
<!-- OS, title or homebrew, what was checked. "Not tested" is a valid answer. -->
- Arch Linux, GCC 16.2, Release. `guest_pad` now checks handle 0 and an unopened handle with `scePadReadState` and `scePadRead`, and a read of the open handle; it fails on `main`. Full ctest: 359/359.
- LEGO Horizon Adventures (PPSA14632) on Linux, together with #861, #722, #723, #732, #734, #889 and local stubs for its other missing imports: both reads return, and the title runs on until the shader recompiler rejects a compute shader (`CFG shared merge splitting exceeded budget`), which is unrelated.

body:
When a sub's or same's PR checks fail while its routine run is `watching`, slop leaves the fix entirely to the routine's cloud session (auto-fix through Claude's GitHub integration) and shows nothing if that session never reacts. On s15t2 the session went silent after 12:36 while the `sub-gate` lint failed, and the only safety net is `runTimeoutReason` (`packages/core/src/domain/machine.ts`, around line 791), which fails a run after `runNoProgressHours` (2 h on board 15) without any mention of the failed checks.

What to do:
- Add a stuck hint, alongside the existing ones in `domain/attention.ts` and `domain/readiness.ts` (e.g. "ready sub with no gate result after 15 minutes"): "checks failed on the head N minutes ago and the routine hasn't pushed or reported since". Use 15 minutes, like the other hints, unless there is a reason not to.
- The hint shows on the card, with a Fix link that suggests take over (`sstor --glob <id> --take-over`) or opening the run's session (`run.sessionUrl`).
- If a failed check is followed by no run progress for that long, count it toward the readiness item "the Claude GitHub App on the repo" (red when a recent failure points to it), because auto-fix depends on that app.
- Depends on head checks reporting failures correctly (see the sibling bug: an unstable merge state counted as passed); build on that fix or include the minimal part of it.
- Core unit tests for the hint rule; no new Playwright tests.

Done when: a sub whose head checks fail while its run is watching shows a stuck hint on the card within about 15 minutes if the routine doesn't push or call slop, and the hint clears when the routine pushes, the run ends or someone takes over.

Slop glob **s15t3** (sub, task). Merge from the glob or here; squash merge only.

author: obaid08642-ops
body:
Acceptance spec for **D-16** (owner decision item 16, #335). OpenCode makes it pass and may not edit it.

## How it runs
The spec builds the backend and starts the **real compiled server** (`dist/main.js`: every module, every guard, the production bootstrap) **twice** on one in-memory MongoDB and a local Redis, like the production workers, and talks to it over HTTP. Needs `redis-server` on the PATH. `acceptance/d-16/live-server.ts` is part of the spec.

## Contract
- 12 keys: `pharmacy, consultations, labs_radiology, nursing, nutrition, maternity, mental_health, family, insurance, loyalty, ai, articles`. Never switched = ON.
- `GET /api/v1/modules` (public) → `{ modules: { key: boolean } }`.
- `PUT /api/v1/admin/modules/:key { enabled, reason }`: admin only (patient 403), reason ≥ 5 chars (else 400), unknown key 400/404.
- OFF module: sample patient/public routes (reads **and** writes, 2–4 per module) answer **403** with `module_disabled` + the key before anything else; an anonymous visitor gets 401 or the same 403; no write happens (`mood_entries` unchanged). Every other module keeps working; admin routes are never blocked.
- Instant everywhere: instance B follows a change made through instance A within 5 s, off and back on, no restart.

## Proof
- On `main`: `Tests: 40 failed, 2 passed, 42 total` / FAIL (the two passes are the "no false positive while everything is on" and "admin routes" checks).
- Trial implementation (middleware + store with a 1 s cache + controller; reverted, not in this PR): `Tests: 42 passed, 42 total` / PASS.

## Decisions I took (owner may overrule)
1. **403** `module_disabled`, not 5xx: a 5xx would make the web's stale-if-error cache keep serving a switched-off module.
2. Admin routes are never blocked; provider-app routes are not covered here.
3. The existing `kill-switches` (stored but enforced nowhere) and the three separate feature-flag stores are left as they are; not part of D-16.

Not tested: the app/web navigation hiding and the deep-link "friendly state" (design session).

Runner files are byte-identical copies from `fix/audit-2026-09` (same as #315).

author: sarthakjain004
body:
Taleo Enterprise's `posted_at` flipped by whole hours between reads, so every few reads recorded a spurious `changed` Job fact: **1,428,574 of the 2,290,917 `changed` facts** from 2026-09-29 to 10-06, and the reason the Restatement's memory grows ~0.55M versions a day (ADR-0330). Served dates were off by up to ~10 h too.

**Cause, measured live** (`docs/taleo_enterprise/2026-10-06_posting-date-timezone.md`):
- The listing API states a date (no time) in the timezone of the `tz` header we already send (`GMT+00:00`); it answers 500 without it, and `GMT-12:00` moves a date back a day. Stable.
- The detail page states date + time in a timezone the server picks per request: the `tz` header, the `locale` cookie and a warmed session leave it unchanged, and the same bare request read 11:11 AM and, twenty minutes later, 8:11 AM. Not pinnable from the client.

**Change:** `posted_at` is the listing's date when it has one, else the detail page's (it was the reverse), and `_date` keeps the day only, at midnight UTC.

**Verified live:** two full scrapes (detail pages included) — Elsewedy 52/52 Jobs identical (it flipped every few reads before); Ansell, a Board whose listing has no date and falls back to the detail page, 68/78 identical, the rest midnight-crossing shifts the owner accepted over dropping those dates. 90.3% of 8,143 Jobs on 29 sampled Boards carry a listing date.

**One-off effect:** every Taleo Job's `posted_at` moves to its day at midnight once, so the next scrape of each records one `changed` fact; after that they stop. Full suite: 10,241 passed.

author: muhittink
body:
## Description

Adds `partition/roles/mgmt-firewall-rutos-upgrade`, which upgrades a Teltonika RutOS management
firewall with `sysupgrade`, keeping the configuration:

- leaves a device alone that already runs the requested firmware
- refuses to run with uncommitted uci changes or an unfinished mgmt-firewall-rutos deployment
- verifies URL and SHA256 on the controller; with the defaults nothing is flashed until
  `mgmt_firewall_rutos_upgrade_apply` is true
- verifies the image again on the device and with `sysupgrade -T` before flashing
- waits for SSH to go down and come back, then requires `/etc/version` to match

Tested on one RUTXR1, upgraded from `RUTX_R_00.07.24.3` to `RUTX_R_00.07.24.5`:

- read-only run reports the version change and verifies the image on the controller, nothing on the device changes
- a wrong SHA256 fails the download, an uncommitted `uci set` fails the staging check
- the flash took 5:35 in total; SSH closed 25 s after sysupgrade started and answered again 283 s later
- `uci export` before and after differs only in `device_fw_version`; mgmt-firewall-rutos in read-only mode
  computes no commands
- a second run with `mgmt_firewall_rutos_upgrade_apply=true` changes nothing
- `ansible-lint`, `markdownlint-cli2`, `typos`: no errors

Known limits:

- no rollback; a firmware that does not boot has to be fixed on the device
- one device model and one upgrade path tested; the timings are a single measurement
- the check for an unfinished mgmt-firewall-rutos deployment was not exercised on the device

#### Used AI-Tools ✨

- deepseek-v4.1-flash
- Claude Code

References:

- #745
- #746

author: trueadm
body:
## Summary

Closes #1788.

An inferred dependency for a one-level method call such as `source.subscribe()` compared only the own function `source.subscribe`. When two objects share one own function, replacing the receiver kept that identity. The inferred effect stayed subscribed to the first object, and the inferred memo kept showing `first`. The explicit `[source]` controls behaved correctly.

`__methodDep` now chooses the dependency value from the method itself:

| Method on the receiver | Dependency | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Own arrow function | The function | Unchanged |
| Any other own function: ordinary `function`, method shorthand, async, bound, native, proxy | The receiver | Was the function |
| Inherited method | The receiver | Unchanged |
| Absent (`props.onReady?.()`) | `undefined` | Unchanged |

An arrow binds `this` lexically, so no receiver reaches its body. That keeps the existing optimization the issue asks to preserve: `props.onChange(...)` with a stable arrow callback (inline arrows, `useCallback(() => …)`, state setters) stays quiet when the props container is rebuilt. Any other function can read `this`. React Compiler 1.0 also tracks the receiver for these calls: it compiles `() => props.onChange(1)` to `$[0] !== props`, and `source.read()` to `$[0] !== source`.

### How the arrow check works

- **Source text is the only reliable tell.** The check reads `Function.prototype.toString` and matches it against an anchored pattern: a leading `(`, `x =>`, `async (` or `async x =>`. Ordinary functions start with `function`, classes with `class`, and methods with their property key. Bound, native and proxied functions read as `function … [native code]`.
- **Methods named `async`.** Their source also starts with `async(`, so source that doesn't start with `(` must also have a `name` other than `async`. A parenthesized arrow such as `{ async: () => … }` skips that check, per Bugbot.
- **Anything unrecognised tracks the receiver.** That includes every function on engines that hide source text. The worst case is a spurious recompute, never a missed one.

### Guarded plain reads get a `read` flag

The helper also serves guarded plain reads, such as `if (x) use(props.handler)`. A read passes no receiver, so it keeps comparing the function value. The compiler now marks those reads with a fourth `read` argument.

All seven emitters take their flags from one `methodDepFlags` helper:

- component hooks (`hook-deps`)
- plain hooks and Strong caches (`slot-hooks`)
- inline hook memos (`plain-hook-memo`)
- signal captures (AST and text forms in `signal-declarations`)
- binding-program inline refs
- the `use()` argument probes #1817 added to `collectDepPaths` (`compile.js`), which are reads

The binding-program ref emitter previously dropped the guarded flag entirely. It now passes the same flags as the other emitters.

## Behavior change for `vi.fn()` callback props

A `vi.fn()` / `jest.fn()` mock is an ordinary function that records `this`. When a test passes one as a prop and a component calls it as `props.log(...)` from an inferred hook, the hook now re-runs whenever the props container is rebuilt. That is sound: the mock does observe the new receiver. It is also what React Compiler or `[props]` deps would do.

14 existing tests asserted the old behavior with `vi.fn()` props: 9 in `auto-hook-deps-behavior`, 3 in `hooks`, and 1 inline-ref step in `behavior-root`, in each of the dev and prod projects. They now wrap their spy in one stable arrow, which keeps each test's intent and its call-count assertions. The changeset calls this out.

The `octane.inferred-hook-deps` eval grader hit the same case. Its reference solution calls `props.onTotal(total)` from an inferred effect, and the grader passed `vi.fn()` observers. After discussion, the call keeps the React-parity rule. The grader now passes each spy through a stable arrow, as a parent component passes a callback, and its `graderDigest` is regenerated. Its assertions still read the spies, so a solution with a `null` or hand-written array still fails the "unrelated repeat" step.

## Validation

- [ ] `pnpm format:check` — not run repo-wide; `pnpm format:files:check` on every changed file passes
- [ ] `pnpm typecheck` — not run repo-wide; `pnpm typecheck:files` on the six changed source files passes. Tests are outside the package's typecheck program, and the new fixtures use untyped `props` like their neighbours.
- [ ] `pnpm test` — not run in full. Before the test edits, `--project octane --project octane-prod` ran in full with the fix: the only failures were the 14 `vi.fn()` cases above.
- [x] targeted tests, on the final head (`--project octane`): `auto-hook-deps-behavior`, `signal-local-selectors`. Earlier in the change, also `hooks`, `behavior-root` and `guarded-hook-dependencies`, in both octane and octane-prod.
- [x] `pnpm sync` — no generated changes

New regression coverage (each new case was seen failing first):

- **The issue repro, in dev and prod.** Inferred effect, guarded effect, Strong effect and inferred memo. Each runs over a shared `function` method and over a method shorthand copied by spread. Before the fix, the effect stayed on `first` and the memo showed `first`. A Strong `const` declaration is pinned as a neighbour: it already keyed on the receiver.
- **Plain JavaScript hooks**, with and without inline memo lowering.
- **Signal captures**: the existing `method captures in signals and effects` scenario now runs a "shared own methods" receiver in all four dev/prod × Strong modes, for both `derived$` and plain-hook declarations. That shape fails on main's helper.
- **Callback shapes.** Arrow, async arrow, bare-parameter arrow, minified arrow and async bare-parameter arrow must stay inert across fresh props. `function`, async `function`, method shorthand, async method and a method named `async` must re-run with the new props as `this`.
- **Guarded reads of a stable non-arrow function stay inert**, through the component, plain-hook and inline-memo emitters and the binding-program inline ref.

Mutation checks (each turned exactly its test red):

- dropping the `async` name guard
- ignoring `read` in the runtime
- dropping `read` in `slot-hooks`
- dropping `read` in `plain-hook-memo`
- dropping the binding-program flags
- making every own function track its receiver

## Performance

`__methodDep` micro-benchmark, 4M calls on Node 24. Only own functions pay for the source probe:

| Case | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Own arrow, method or ordinary `function` | ~9 ns | ~40–50 ns |
| Inherited method | ~5.5 ns | ~5.5 ns |
| Absent optional handler | ~9 ns | ~10 ns |

That is one `toString` slice plus an anchored regex, per one-level method-call dependency per render. A `WeakMap` cache measured about 8 ns for stable arrows but about 155 ns for a fresh arrow each render, and it adds ephemeron churn, so it was left out. An earlier version also had a `prototype` pre-filter and a `(` fast path, each worth about 20 ns. They cost about 100 raw bytes, so they were dropped.

Emitted code grows only for guarded plain reads (`, true, true`).

### Bundle size: needs #1819 first

The weather app ships the helper: framework +215 raw / +119 gzip, which exceeds its 32-byte headroom. octanejs/octane#1819 is the budget-only raise required by CONTRIBUTING, and it lists the exact bytes. #1819 also ratchets `main`'s `deferred-hydration` budget down: #1771's ratchet currently fails test shard 1/4 on `main` itself, so shard 1 fails here too. **Merge #1819 first**, then merge `main` into this branch.

## Risk / follow-ups

- **Hooks may re-run more often for non-arrow callbacks.** This is limited to non-arrow functions passed through a rebuilt container and called as `container.fn(...)` from an inferred hook or inline ref. That includes test mocks. Such hooks now re-run when the container changes, which matches React Compiler. Arrow callbacks, the common case, are unchanged.

author: lorddetson
body:
**Before:** the site sent no security response headers, and a room WebSocket could be opened from any website's origin.

**After:** Caddy sets `Strict-Transport-Security`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and `Referrer-Policy` on the app and its web client, but not on the Grafana dashboard, which sets its own. `X-Frame-Options: DENY` stops the site being framed, so a room cannot be placed in a hidden iframe to steal clicks on the votes. The backend is given `STOMP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` so a room WebSocket is opened only from the site's own domains; the example env files list them and keep the duckdns names while they still serve the site.

This changes only configuration. Non-browser clients that send no `Origin` header (the smoke test and the live E2E) are unaffected, and the health checks keep working.

**How:** a `header` directive scoped with `not path /grafana*` in the shared `(pipoker)` snippet; `STOMP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` added to the backend service and to `prod.env.example` / `qa.env.example`. Caddy already replaces any client-sent `X-Forwarded-For` with the real connecting address, so the per-address feedback limit cannot be dodged with a made-up header; a comment records switching to `CF-Connecting-IP` once the site is behind the Cloudflare proxy.

Pairs with the pipoker-app change that reads `STOMP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`. The real `qa.env` / `prod.env` on the server need the same `STOMP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` line added for the restriction to take effect.

author: nickdarvey
body:
`create_pr` used to record nothing: the gate's tool line was the only
trace, and nothing could fold it. Opening a pull request is a place in
a session worth coming back to, so it is now a durable event,
`PrCreated`, holding the number, the title it was opened with, head,
base, draft, and who asked. The timeline shows it as an act note
("PR octo/hello#7 opened", with the title and branches as its
particulars).

`PrService.Create` now takes the whole `Authority`, as `Watch` and
`Merge` do, because the event is attributed to whoever asked. Asking
again for a pull request that is already open records nothing, since
nothing was opened.

The chapter policy does not open chapters at it yet. That follows in a
separate change, once transitions also carry their title.

author: agners
body:
## Problem

In read mode, `SecureTarFile.open()` opens the file and then calls `tarfile.open` in stream mode, which reads the first block immediately. A wrong password, corrupt or truncated data raises inside `open()` before `__enter__` returns, so `__exit__` and `close()` never run and the file descriptor leaks.

Running the test suite with `-W error` shows this as `ResourceWarning: unclosed file` in 11 tests (on 3.14 and 3.15.0rc2).

## Fix

- Move the cipher setup into `_open_encrypted()` and call `close()` when it raises, releasing the file and cipher stream.
- Add a regression test that captures the file returned by `os.fdopen` and asserts it is closed after a failed open (fails without the fix).
- Set `filterwarnings = ["error"]` in the pytest config so resource leaks fail CI.
- The `InnerSecureTarFile` open test used `Mock()` as the file name and never closed the tar, leaving `<Mock id=...>` files in the working directory. It now writes to `tmp_path` and closes.

author: khaliqgant
body:
## Summary

- verify the transitive registry closure of required `@relayfile/*` dependencies and non-optional SDK peers before publishing their consumers, including partial-release retries
- keep the parallel release matrix, read-only preflight, dry runs, and immutable already-published reconciliation unchanged
- bound dependency queries and backoff under one ten-minute budget; retry transient command failures without publishing, and reject malformed dependency metadata immediately

## Production evidence

X Reply Radar run `41499d7d-11f0-4f45-bf5e-adb6f1fe8e37` failed at `2026-10-06T01:09:27Z` with `npm_install_failed`: `ETARGET No matching version found for @relayfile/core@0.10.73`.

The registry published `@relayfile/sdk@0.10.73` at `01:07:24.214Z`, with a required exact dependency on `@relayfile/core@0.10.73`. Core did not become public until `01:11:51.148Z`. The parallel publish workflow exposed a broken consumer during that window.

Production has recovered: all twelve hourly schedule fires from 02:09 through 13:09 UTC succeeded. The 13:09 run completed its local Grok Agent Flow without fallback, posted 15 results, and finished with exit 0. No agent redeploy is required to recover this already-completed publication; this change prevents the next release from exposing the same incomplete graph.

## Validation

- new regressions fail on the previous implementation (consumer publishes before its dependency is ready)
- `npm run test:release` — 118 passed
- `git diff --check`
- Veto diff review: PASS; no actionable code, security, or secrets findings

Optional platform packages/peers and dev dependencies do not block publication. The shared strict release-version parser preserves prerelease/build metadata. Workflow-generated caret peers wait on their declared version floor; the required release graph is core → sdk → cli/agents.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes when packages become installable on npm and can delay or fail parallel publish jobs, but behavior is bounded, fail-closed, and heavily tested on the release path only.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Release reconciliation now blocks `npm publish` until required internal packages are registry-visible**, closing the parallel-publish window where consumers (e.g. `@relayfile/sdk`) could ship while dependencies (e.g. `@relayfile/core`) were still propagating and installs hit `ETARGET`.
> 
> Before publishing, `reconcile-package.mjs` walks the **transitive `@relayfile/*` closure** from local `dependencies` and non-optional `peerDependencies`, polls the registry with backoff under a **shared ~10 minute budget**, expands the graph from returned manifests (so a published SDK still waits on core), and **fails closed** on ambiguous queries, bad metadata, unpinnable ranges, or oversized graphs. **Preflight and dry-run stay read-only** and skip this wait; the publish workflow comment documents the ordering intent (core → sdk → cli).
> 
> Coverage is added in `reconcile-package.test.mjs` for transitive waits, peer floors, budgets, and partial-release scenarios.
>

author: aztecbot
body:
## Problem

A trait stores some types once, on its declaration, and reuses them at every use. These are:
- the trait's `Self`
- the trait's generics, as written inside its parent bounds
- the associated items that a parent bound leaves out
- a generic impl's own generics

Wherever one of these is used without being substituted, or is handed out as a bindable `Type::TypeVariable`, the first unification with a concrete type binds it for the whole program. A later use can then pick the wrong impl, or be wrongly accepted or rejected.

Issues addressed:
- [noir-claude#2042](https://github.com/noir-lang/noir-claude/issues/2042): the assumed `Self: CurrentTrait` bound inside a default body used the bindable `Self`.
- [noir-claude#2061](https://github.com/noir-lang/noir-claude/issues/2061): `UnresolvedFunctionMeta.self_type` was built the same way.
- [noir-claude#2055](https://github.com/noir-lang/noir-claude/issues/2055): `trait Child: Parent<Self>` gave `X: Parent<?Self>`.
- [noir-claude#1232](https://github.com/noir-lang/noir-claude/issues/1232): `X::get` under `X: Child<u16>` resolved through `X: Parent<U>`.
- [noir-claude#1811](https://github.com/noir-lang/noir-claude/issues/1811): an associated item left out of a parent bound was one shared placeholder of kind `Any`.
- [noir-claude#1967](https://github.com/noir-lang/noir-claude/issues/1967): `Self::Out` inherited from `impl<let M: u32> P for S<M>` stayed `[u8; M]`.

## Changes

- `Trait::self_type()` returns the rigid `Self`. It is used by `with_trait_scope` and `UnresolvedFunctionMeta.self_type`. `parent_bounds()` and the parent-skip check handle the rigid form, and the implicit `Self: CurrentTrait` bound is registered as implied.
- Every place that reads a parent bound now instantiates it for the bound or impl in hand:
  - `instantiate_parent_trait_bound` binds `Self`. Each instantiation gets its own placeholder for any associated item the bound leaves out.
  - `find_methods_or_constants_in_trait`, the `T::item` path.
  - `lookup_associated_type_in_parent_impls`, which resolves `Self::Out` in an impl.
  - `trait_to_impl_bindings_helper`, which checks an impl against its trait.
- A parent impl's associated type is substituted with the impl-search bindings, in both `lookup_associated_type_in_parent_impls` and `trait_to_impl_bindings_helper`.
- For a function bound `T: Sub`, `collect_parent_associated_types` registers its per-function rigid `<T as Par>::N` in scope, with the declared kind. The assumed-impl merge replaces the bare placeholder with it.
- In release builds, an error is reported if a trait default body binds the trait's `Self` (from [noir#13874](https://github.com/noir-lang/noir/pull/13874)).
- `nargo expand` no longer prints supertraits twice now that `Self` is rigid.

Two existing tests returned `<T as Level1>::A` from a function declared `-> Field`. That only type-checked because of the shared placeholder, so they now return the projection.

## Tests

- **`trait_default_methods.rs`:** the 7 tests from #13874.
- **`trait_inheritance.rs`:** regression tests for #2055, #1232 (3 routes), #1811 (4), #1967 (2), and 3 tests for `Self::Out` from a generic parent bound inside an impl, where the type has two `Parent` impls.

Each new test fails on the commit before its fix. `cargo test -p noirc_frontend --lib` passes (2421), and fmt and clippy are clean. The rest of the suite is left to CI.

## Remaining plan

[Commit plan](https://gist.github.com/AztecBot/e8816ce2421be5911e685416dc1dc09a)

1. Structural change, with no behavior change:
   - wrap declaration-side bounds and signatures in a binder whose only accessor is `.instantiate(args)`
   - the rigid args come only from the trait-scope context
   - elided associated items are instantiated as rigid projections
   - `self_type_typevar` becomes private
2. Make `Self` the trait's first generic parameter, and remove the special cases for `Self`.
3. Fix method lookup:
   - the #2055 `pin` case
   - [#1956](https://github.com/noir-lang/noir-claude/issues/1956)
   - [#1946](https://github.com/noir-lang/noir-claude/issues/1946)
   - [#1842](https://github.com/noir-lang/noir-claude/issues/1842)

Known separate gap: a parent's associated type written as `Self::Out` in a `let` annotation inside an impl method body is rejected, even with a single parent impl. Body type resolution doesn't consult parent impls.

Supersedes [noir#13874](https://github.com/noir-lang/noir/pull/13874).

Closes noir-lang/noir-claude#2042
Closes noir-lang/noir-claude#1232
Closes noir-lang/noir-claude#1967
Refs noir-lang/noir-claude#1811
Refs noir-lang/noir-claude#2055
Refs noir-lang/noir-claude#2061

body:
## Summary
The long-term plan for Goliradile Isle, written down so implementation can follow it. **Docs only: no game code changes.**

- **`docs/DESIGN.md`**: what we are building: a tower-defence / survival-crafting hybrid sold as a $5 full 1.0 launch. Three difficulties, run structure and saving, 10 boss fights (9 croc-type bosses plus the Great Goliradile), towers, automation, the 160×160 world and biomes, co-op rules, accessibility, art/audio sourcing.
- **`docs/ROADMAP.md`**: the phased execution plan (foundation → run structure → boss slice → world and biomes → player power → towers → all bosses → automation → launch polish → co-op), with exit criteria, quality gates, dependencies, risks and a pace estimate.
- **`docs/DECISIONS.md`**: every design decision taken in the review (eleven rounds of multiple-choice questions) with the implication for the plan, and what is still open.
- **`docs/PLAYER.md`**: levels 1–65, stats (cap 30), 48 perks in 4 branches, gear and attunement, nine five-piece boss sets with weapons and abilities, 20 cooked meals with buffs, co-op rules.
- **`docs/PROGRESSION.md`**: 10 tiers tied to the bosses, pacing targets per difficulty, biomes, station and tower unlocks, caps by tier, summon components.
- **`docs/TOWERS.md`**: the 12 towers (the 9 existing plus Repair, Terrain and Collector), each with 3 upgrade paths of 4 tiers, supply, targeting and boss counters.
- **`docs/BOSSES.md`**: shared boss rules (anatomy, telegraphs, escalation, targets) and a sheet for each of the 10 bosses, with `--bossfight` test scenarios.
- **`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`**: measurements of today's code, target module layout and core types, fixed timestep, save v2, large-world design, testing and CI, migration strategy, and the Phase 0 task breakdown (P0-01 to P0-18) with acceptance tests.
- **`docs/PHASES_1_2.md`**: 27 PR-sized tasks with tests for run structure/difficulty and the boss framework, plus two playtest checklists.
- **`docs/ASSETS.md`**: open-licence policy (no NC/ND), manifest format and CI check, credits, 16 px style rules.
- **`LICENSE`**: proprietary, all rights reserved, holder `ssebrobless` as a placeholder.
- `README.md` links to the docs.

## Status
- The owner has read the docs and approved the merge. Interpretations that were flagged for confirmation (attunement, five-piece sets, perk thresholds, tower-kill XP, War cry level, respawn) are confirmed and recorded in `DECISIONS.md`.
- The content docs are **drafts**: every number is a starting proposal, tuned with the simulation tools and playtests.
- Still open (owner tasks): trademark and Steam name check, and a legal or studio name for the `LICENSE`.

## Notes
- Measured costs behind the 160×160 decision (croc path rebuild 5.3 ms, world tick 1.1 ms, night/day swap 7 ms on today's 50×50 map, each growing about 10×) are recorded in `DESIGN.md`, `ROADMAP.md` and `ARCHITECTURE.md`.
- The repository is currently public; `DECISIONS.md` notes the consequence of keeping design docs public until the first public build.

## Testing
Docs only. Nothing in the game changed.

author: hopkins385
body:
The TDD rules for `apps/api` move from `AGENTS.md` into a new skill, `.agents/skills/tdd/SKILL.md`. `AGENTS.md` now only says to load it for `apps/api` changes, the same pattern as `clean-code`, so the rules live in one place.

## New rules, from the self-hosting work
- **Strict response schemas:** API tests parse responses with `z.strictObject` and list every returned field. Plain `z.object` silently strips unknown keys, so a leaked or reintroduced field would pass unnoticed. Applies to new and touched tests.
- **Proven regression guards:** a test that exists to stop something coming back is proven once by breaking the code on purpose.
- **Red for the right reason:** a failing test must fail on its assertion, not on an import error.
- **Deterministic env:** values that tests depend on are pinned in `.env.testing`.
- **Rebuild packages** before running tests.

No code changes. Existing tests still use `z.object`; converting them is a separate follow-up.

author: lv2002
body:
## The dashboard

The client said the CRM looks plain. The colours were not the problem — they were worked
over in September. The dashboard was: eight `StatTile`s in two rows of four, each a
bordered box with a label and a number.

Eight figures of identical weight is a wall, not an answer. Nothing said which to read
first, and none of them said whether it was *good* — 7 admissions is a fine month or a bad
one depending on what last month was, and the person reading the screen should not have to
remember.

So three are promoted — **what came in, what closed, who is being let down right now** —
each with last month beside it and the shape of the last fortnight under it. Every other
figure stays in a compact row beneath, each exactly once. Both the counsellor's card and
the centre head's, because they are the same screen.

Also new on both: **a 30-day chart of arrivals** with a crosshair and tooltip, and
**progress against target** where somebody has set one.

Four things done deliberately:

- **A delta is never colour alone.** The arrow, the colour and the sentence all say *Up 3
  on last month (9)*, so it reads the same in greyscale and to somebody who does not see
  the green.
- **The sparkline has no axes and no numbers.** It answers which way this is going; the
  figure beside it is the value. A flat line at zero is not drawn at all — a straight line
  across an empty fortnight is noise pretending to be information.
- **Leads and admissions are not on one chart.** Leads run in tens and admissions in ones,
  and two scales on one axis is the mistake that makes a good month look flat.
- **The pace line says what it is** — where an even month would have you today — rather
  than passing judgement, and the whole block is absent when nobody set a target.

## Insights

Every tab computed real figures and rendered them only as a table. A table is where you
look something up; it is not where you notice that Shiksha brings a sixth of the leads and
a fortieth of the admissions.

Two components do most of it. **`ChartFigure`** is the frame — caption, chart, and the same
numbers as a screen-reader table, which is not politeness: a chart that exists only as
pixels cannot be read by somebody using a screen reader or quoted by anybody who wants the
figure. **`BarList`** is a ranked bar list in plain CSS with no charting library, so it
renders on the server inside the page that computed the numbers and works before
JavaScript does — the five pages using it ship **868 bytes**.

Sources, Segments, Referrals, Targets and Handovers each get one, sorted biggest first.
The optional reference line is the institute's own average: *18%* is a number, *18%
against an overall 11%* is a decision.

**Timing** gets the one chart here that genuinely needs colour — a line per arrival month,
where which line is which is the whole question. It uses the dataviz skill's validated
categorical theme, now in `globals.css` as `--series-1` … `--series-6` in its fixed slot
order, which is the colourblind-safety mechanism rather than a palette somebody liked.
Validated in both modes before shipping: worst adjacent CVD ΔE 9.1 light / 8.4 dark,
normal-vision 19.6 / 19.3. Six lines maximum; a seventh hue stops being separable, and the
table still lists every month.

**What the charts refuse to do:** invent a number. A segment too small for a meaningful
rate is left out rather than drawn at zero, and a cohort too young for a 90-day figure has
a gap in its line rather than a fall to the floor. They also do not replace the table —
each shows the top twelve and the table below lists everything.

## The enquiry sheet's colours

A CSV export loses cell colour, and in AFD's enquiry register colour carries the outcome
of the whole conversation. The exported `colour` column is empty on all 1,153 rows, so it
only exists in the `.xlsx`.

`scripts/import-prep/` reads it back. The client went through them colour by colour: the
greys mean negative or wrong target, orange means they joined a competitor, yellow is
warm, red is hot, cyan is a grade above hot, green is a closed admission. 667 of the main
sheet's 1,042 leads now carry a mark made by hand.

Two judgements worth stating: **an outcome beats a temperature** (32 rows carry two
colours, and somebody who joined a competitor in March was warm in February), and **the
colour beats the status column**, because it is the mark somebody applied on purpose.

`--ad-archive` also takes the Google and Meta files from the monthly sheets in the
feedback workbook rather than a single month's CSV: 250 Google leads across nine 2026
sheets and 604 Meta leads, where the CSVs held 26 and 123.

## Testing

`tests/dashboard-scoreboard.spec.ts` gains 6 cases: the previous-month window excludes the
last instant of the month before it, a dropped admission counts in neither month, the
daily series buckets an 11pm Kochi enquiry into the right IST day, keeps empty days, and
ignores an admission belonging to somebody else's lead.

**1628 tests pass.** Typecheck, lint and `next build` clean.

I cannot render the app in this container — signing in needs a real Supabase auth server
and there is no Docker here — so the Vercel preview on this PR is the first place the new
screens can actually be looked at, and the browser test crawls them as all six roles.
