author: ryry79261
body:
Closes #174

## Why

On the kitchen iPad a dialog could only be left with Escape, which a touch screen has no key for, and a bounty's "Log …" sheet had no way out at all. Now every kit `Dialog` closes from a 56px × in its header or a tap on the dimmed page around it, and the log sheet also gets **Cancel**. Once something is typed in a dialog, a tap outside does nothing, and while its form is sending, × and Cancel are greyed out until the result shows (two owner rulings 2026-10-06, SPEC §12 decision 32).

## Decisions

- **One hook** (`packages/ui/src/use-modal-dialog.ts`) for `Dialog` and `KioskModal`:
  - A tap outside is a press *and* a click on the `<dialog>` itself; the element has no padding, so the panel and its padding never count.
  - Every way out closes the `<dialog>` the way Escape does. `onClose` fires once, and only when someone closed it, not when the caller set `open` to false. This fixes KioskModal's double `onClose`.
  - `close` and `cancel` count only when their target is this dialog, since React passes them up the tree; closing a dialog inside another no longer closes its parent.
- **The ruling, applied literally:** since it opened, an `input` event from a text field or editable area in this dialog (not a radio, checkbox, file or slider, and not a nested dialog), or a digit on its PinPad (`DIALOG_TYPED_EVENT`), turns a tap outside off. The × and Cancel still close it. Escape keeps the browser's behaviour and closes it, like the ×. In Ask Baumy, typing in its text box counts too, even after the text was sent.
- **`busy`:** while a sheet's form is sending (`useReportPending`: the log sheet, note add/edit/delete, the kiosk and hub calendar's add/edit/delete, New bounty, Edit bounty, Report a bug, Deactivate member, and the PIN dialogs inside `AttestedForm`, `EventForm` and `NoteForm`), the × and the form's own Cancel or Keep it (and the PinPad's Cancel) are disabled, the log sheet's "Who did it?" and photo are locked (the form is keyed by who did it), a tap outside is ignored, Escape is refused, and a close the browser forces anyway (a second Escape) is undone. The kitchen screen still closes it when it takes the whole screen (going home, a reminder, the screensaver): `closeOpenDialogs` goes through `forceCloseDialog`.
- **Ask Baumy:** its ×, Escape and a tap outside do what its Cancel does, so the next person never sees or confirms someone's open card, an answer that lands after the sheet closed is dropped (a generation guard like the cat's), and reopening it right away finds it ready, not "thinking". It is also `busy` while Confirm all saves.
- **Layout:** the × sits in a header row that doesn't scroll, so it never covers the body, and it comes last in the page order, so the dialog still focuses its own first control when it opens.
- The footer "Close" buttons in Ask Baumy and the no-PIN notice are gone; the × replaces them.

## Database

None.

## Testing

- [x] `pnpm turbo run format:check lint typecheck test build` (23/23)
- [x] E2E areas, `E2E_SERVE=build`, fresh DB, `--workers=1`:
  - `specs/kiosk`: 32 passed, 34 skipped by project
  - hub, baumy, feedback, calendar, notes, confirm-its-you, bounties (edit and mass edit), chores, claims, photo-proof, membership, pixel-kit, weights, admin-connections: 91 passed, 29 skipped
- [x] Each new test was seen to fail with the code broken:
  - `dialog.test.tsx` against the PR's first Dialog/KioskModal: 11 of the 16 tests go red (the other 5 cover what didn't change: the tap/drag checks and that radios and Escape are not blocked).
  - The reopen reset and the nested-typing guard, broken one at a time, each turn their own test red.
  - `chore-grid.test.tsx` without `onPending`; `baumy-sheet.test.tsx` with `onClose={close}` and without the generation bump; `attested-form.test.tsx` without the pending report and with the PIN dialog not busy.
  - `sheets-busy.test.tsx` (note board, kiosk calendar) against the pre-fix boards: all 4 red.
  - The forced-Escape reshow, the forced-close bookkeeping, PinPad's typed event, the contenteditable check and both nested-dialog guards, each broken alone; `idle-reset.test.tsx` with `closeOpenDialogs` calling plain `close()`.
  - e2e: kiosk-dashboard fails at the tap-outside step without the backdrop close; kiosk-calendar fails at the "typed title, tap outside, still open" step without the typing check.

Not locked yet, and said so in decision 32: Ask Baumy while a question is on its way (only Confirm all locks it), and "Confirm it's you" while it checks.

## Risk

Every Dialog in the app changes. A caller that relied on `onClose` firing after it set `open` to false itself would now miss it; I checked every caller, and each `onClose` only resets its own state.

## Follow-ups

None.

author: tobbe
body:
## Summary

Baremetal deploys can now drive systemd as well as pm2. Closes #2649, closes #2653 (its systemd docs track), closes #437 (jobs workers restart on deploy).

### Deploy: `monitor` adapters

- New `monitor` option per server in `deploy.toml`: `pm2` (default, so existing configs behave exactly as before), `systemd-user` or `systemd-system`. Each adapter supplies the commands and task titles for first run, restart, stop and start, in `packages/cli/src/commands/deploy/baremetal/monitors.ts`.
- pm2's first run is unchanged: `start current/ecosystem.config.js --only <name>`, then `save`. systemd's first run is one `daemon-reload`, then `enable --now <unit>` per process. `daemon-reload` is included because the first run is exactly when the unit files were just copied to the server, and it is idempotent and needs no root for user units.
- `monitorCommand` stays as the command the adapter is invoked with. It defaults per monitor (`pm2`, `systemctl --user`, `sudo systemctl`), so prefixes such as `doppler run -- pm2` keep working and a root deploy user can set plain `systemctl`.
- The startup check only requires `deploy.toml`. The pm2 adapter checks for `ecosystem.config.js` as a deploy task when `--first-run` is passed, which is the one time pm2 reads it, with an error that points at setup or at deploying without `--first-run`. The stub-file workaround from the issue is no longer needed.
- `verifyServerConfig` rejects unknown `monitor` values.

### Setup: `setup deploy baremetal`

- Asks which monitor to generate config for (pm2, systemd user units, systemd system units), or takes `--monitor <pm2|systemd-user|systemd-system>`.
- pm2 gets `ecosystem.config.js` as before. systemd gets `systemd/<app>.service`, where `<app>` is the project directory name made unit-safe. The units run from `/var/www/app/current` through a login shell so `node` from a version manager is on the `PATH`; system units add `User=deploy` and `WantedBy=multi-user.target`. The header comments say where to copy the files and, for user units, to run `loginctl enable-linger`.
- Background jobs: when `api/src/lib/jobs.ts` exists (presence only, no parsing), the generated config includes a worker process: a `jobs` pm2 app, or a templated `systemd/<app>-jobs@.service` with `<app>-jobs@0` in `processNames`. The template comment explains one instance per `workers` entry. Deploys then restart the workers along with the app.
- `deploy.toml` is generated with `monitor = "..."` and the matching `processNames`; its comments document `monitor` and `monitorCommand`.

### Docs

`docs/docs/deploy/baremetal.md` gets the systemd track: first-run lifecycle per monitor, the `--monitor` prompt and generated files, a "systemd units" section, the `monitor`/`monitorCommand`/`processNames` options, `loginctl enable-linger` under "Starting Processes on Server Restart", and `systemctl status`/`journalctl` under "Monitoring". `cli-commands.md` lists `--monitor`. `background-jobs.md` points at the generated worker process and drops the "Baremetal integration" TODO.

Open questions from the issue, decided: two monitor values rather than a `user` flag (they differ in default command and privileges); `daemon-reload` runs in first run; `systemd-system` defaults to `sudo systemctl` and the docs state the passwordless-sudo requirement.

## Testing

- `packages/cli/src/commands/deploy/__tests__/baremetal.test.ts`: 133 passed. New: adapter command sequences for all three monitors, `monitor` validation, `monitorCommand` defaults and override, maintenance stop/start through systemd, first run for pm2 (ecosystem check task, missing and present) and systemd (reload + enable per unit, exec arguments), systemd restart with `sudo systemctl`.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/setup/deploy/__tests__/baremetalHandler.test.ts` (new): 11 passed. Covers `appNameFromPath`, the file set and `processNames` for each monitor with and without jobs, unit file contents (user vs system), the prompt and its cancellation, `--monitor` skipping the prompt, `--force` passing through, unknown monitor rejection.
- ESLint and Prettier clean on all changed files.

author: exoridus
body:
Follow-up to #813 from its review: three lifecycle gaps and one topology gap in the audio effect layer.

## Destroyed worklet processors kept rendering

`WorkletEffect.destroy()` and `BeatDetector.destroy()` disconnected the `AudioWorkletNode`, but every processor returned `true` from `process()` unconditionally. A processor that keeps returning `true` stays active and is called every render quantum until the AudioContext closes, connected or not, so each destroyed effect kept costing CPU for the rest of the session.

- New `DisposableProcessor` base (bundled into each worklet): it listens for `{ type: 'destroy' }` on its port and makes `process()` return `false` from then on. BitCrusher, Granular, PitchShift, Vocoder, Ducking and the beat detector extend it; the PCM stream already had its own destroy message.
- `WorkletEffect.destroy()` and `BeatDetector.destroy()` post the message before disconnecting.
- A `BeatDetector` destroyed while its worklet module was loading used to create the node afterwards anyway, which then could never be released; it now skips creation.

## `AudioEffect.ready` settles on failure and destroy

`_deferSetup` only handled a resolving setup: a rejecting one left `ready` pending forever, and a setup finishing after `destroy()` still resolved it. `WorkletEffect` swallowed a failed module load, so `ready` resolved for an effect that never got its processor.

`AudioEffect` now tracks `pending`, `ready`, `failed` and `destroyed`:

- a setup that rejects or throws rejects `ready` with that error (a synchronous throw still propagates from construction);
- a worklet that fails to load rejects `ready`; it is still logged and the effect stays a dry passthrough;
- destroying an effect before it is ready rejects `ready` with an `AbortError`, and a setup settling later can no longer resolve it;
- destroying an effect that is already ready leaves `ready` resolved.

`ready` is still created lazily, so a failure nobody asked about raises no unhandled rejection.

## Reactivated channels start silent

The stereo worklets grow per-channel state when the input widens, but kept the old state when it narrowed. Stereo, then mono, then stereo again (a bus whose connected voices change) replayed the right channel's history from its first activation: a held BitCrusher value, old samples in the Granular ring buffer, PitchShift input/overlap-add history, vocoder carrier filter state. A channel that comes back now starts from cleared state; a fully disconnected input counts as all channels gone.

## `AudioTap` releases deferred retries

A tap waiting for a bus to build its nodes registered a callback with `onceSetup()` and dropped the returned disposer, and the non-bus fallback used `onAudioContextReady.once()`, which cannot be removed individually. Both are now kept and cancelled on source change, destroy and re-deferral, so an old source is no longer referenced until its bus happens to finish setup.

## Tests

- `processor-lifecycle.test.ts`: every processor returns `false` after `destroy` (and not after other messages); each stereo processor emits nothing on a reactivated, silent right channel. The reactivation cases were checked to fail with the reset disabled.
- `AudioEffect`: rejection on async and sync setup failure, `AbortError` on destroy while locked and during an async setup, resolved `ready` surviving destroy.
- `WorkletEffect` and `BeatDetector`: destroy posts the message before disconnecting; a failed load rejects `ready`; no node after destroy during load.
- `AudioTap`: source change and destroy call the bus disposer.

`pnpm gates typecheck`, `lint`, `sync`; core `test/audio` (635), `exojs-audio-fx` (1347), `test:browser:audio` (28); API reference regenerated.

author: erastusm
body:
From the production readiness audit: production runs Node 18 and MongoDB 6.0, and both are end-of-life.

## Node 18 → 24
- The API, customer and business images move from `node:18-alpine` to `node:24-alpine`.
- CI already tests on Node 24 (`setup-node` 24), so production will run exactly what's tested.
- No native add-ons (`bcryptjs` is pure JavaScript).
- Goes live with the normal deploy.

## MongoDB 6.0 → 7.0 (manual workflow, nothing changes on merge)
- `docker-compose.yml`: `mongo:${MONGO_VERSION:-6.0}` for both `mongodb` and `backup`.
  - `MONGO_VERSION` lives in `/app/.env`, which the deploy preserves, so **a deploy never changes the database version**.
- New **MongoDB upgrade** workflow (`workflow_dispatch`, target `7.0`):
  1. Checks the running version (6.0.x) and featureCompatibilityVersion (6.0), and stops otherwise.
  2. Takes a backup.
  3. Starts 7.0 on the same data. If it isn't healthy within 3 minutes, it switches back to 6.0 automatically; that's safe because FCV hasn't changed yet.
  4. Runs `setFeatureCompatibilityVersion: "7.0"` (`confirm: true`).
  5. Waits for the API to be healthy, and restarts it if needed.
- The workflow's log is public, so it prints only versions and yes/no.
- **Backup restore test:** restores into the same version as the live database.
- **Why 7.0 and not 8.0:** 7.0 is the newest server the current driver (mongodb 5.9 via mongoose 7.8) officially supports. CI's in-memory Mongo already runs 8.2.6 and every test passes, so 8.0 should be low-risk once mongoose is upgraded, in a separate PR.

## Run plan
1. Merge this. The deploy rolls out Node 24.
2. At a quiet time, run **MongoDB upgrade**. Expect about 10–30 s of API unavailability.
3. Run **Backup restore test**.

author: skogutovska-diana
body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: lorddetson
body:
**Before:** the rooms WebSocket (the SockJS endpoint) accepted a connection handshake from any website's origin.

**After:** the backend accepts a room WebSocket only from the origins it is told to allow; a handshake from any other origin is refused. With nothing configured it still allows any origin, which is only for local development where the web client runs on its own port. Non-browser clients that send no `Origin` header (the smoke test and the live E2E) keep working.

**How:** `application-prod.properties` binds `broker.stomp.endpoint.allowedOriginPatterns` to `STOMP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` (default `*`), which `WebSocketConfig` already applies to the SockJS endpoint.

The deployment supplies `STOMP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` (see the pipoker-docker-config change). This server image must ship before the origins are set in production, so a restricted value never meets an older image that ignores it.

- **Heardle:** 1s of intro, then 2, 4, 7, 11, 16s. Hard (½→8s) and chill (2→30s) ladders, guess song only or artist + song. A wrong guess or "+ more" unlocks the next snippet, and points equal the number of snippets left. The app pauses and resumes Spotify itself. Skip takes the next song from the queue and starts it at second zero using `context_uri` + `offset` (falls back to `uris`). A solved song then plays from the top. Polls every 1.5s in this mode, and stale polls are ignored while the song switches. Needs Premium.
- **Hitster:** you get a free starter card, then place each song before, between or after your cards. 5/10/15 cards to win, 1/3/5 lives. A miss shows in red where it belonged. The timeline is kept in localStorage.

**Versus:** Heardle and Hitster are solo. Turning VS on switches to Quiz and greys them out, and guests see the host's mode (button disabled).

Mode and settings are remembered in localStorage (`gtt_game`, `gtt_hitster`).

Tested in Chromium against a mocked Spotify (tracks, queue, play/pause/seek) at 1280×860 and 390×860. I played through Hitster (starter, right, wrong), Heardle (snippet → pause, wrong → longer snippet, right → points + full play, skip → next song at 0), Pick 5/Quiz switching, the VS lock, both bubbles open, and Esc/scrim closing. Not yet tested against a real Spotify account.

author: yyqdbngt
body:
## Why

`eval_sem` and `eval_shmmni` gate their SysV IPC sizing rules on a raw
`p.name == "postgres" || == "mysqld" || == "oracle"` scan, while the rest
of the engine detects databases through the boundary-aware
`is_database_present` (built on `has_process`, the #4100 fix). The raw twin
misses what the shared predicate catches:

- role-suffixed worker comms — a busy PostgreSQL host's process list is
  mostly `postgres: writer` / `postgres: walwriter` entries, and the raw
  equality ignores every one of them;
- the collector filter — raw equality happens to stay strict here, but the
  duplicated predicate keeps drifting (it already disagrees with
  `is_database_present`'s callers on the MariaDB daemon name).

So the sem/shmmni recommendations could silently skip a database host the
engine itself classifies as a database.

## What changed

`src/ktuner/src/rules/mod.rs`: route both gates through
`is_database_present`, and split `eval_sem_at` / `eval_shmmni_at`
path-injectable forms (the established `eval_*_at` idiom) so the gate is
unit-testable against a temp file instead of the live /proc.

## Related issue

no-issue: un-migrated raw twin of the #4100 boundary-aware database detection

## User / Agent impact

Hosts whose process list only shows role-suffixed database worker comms now
get the kernel.sem / kernel.shmmni sizing recommendations like every other
database host.

## Risk and compatibility

- [ ] Public CLI, API, configuration, or documented behavior changed
- [ ] Privileged or security-sensitive behavior changed
- [ ] Cross-component contract changed
- [ ] Migration or rollback guidance is needed

Low risk: the gate can only widen to the exact set every other db-gated
rule already uses; thresholds and recommendation values are untouched.

## Validation

On the v100 box (Linux; repo synced from the Mac clone, umask 022).

Red first — `_at` forms present with the raw gate, new test
`sysv_ipc_rules_gate_on_boundary_aware_db_detection`:

```
$ cargo test --lib -- sysv_ipc_rules
test rules::tests::sysv_ipc_rules_gate_on_boundary_aware_db_detection ... FAILED
  # "postgres: writer" did not gate the sem/shmmni rules in
test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed
```

With the gate switched to `is_database_present`:

```
$ cargo test            # full crate suite
passed=397 failed=0
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check    # clean
```

## Documentation and rollback

No docs change. Revert the single commit to restore the raw-name gate.

author: lemmonchess333
body:
## Summary

Three passes (#2588, #2592, #2594) fixed about forty places where the iPhone app's larger text ran a word out of its card or a control off the screen. Nothing would have noticed any of them coming back. This PR adds that check, and fixes what it found on its first run.

### The check

`e2e/screenshots/largeText.capture.spec.ts` runs in CI's existing capture-specs job, against the same seeded emulator rig. It takes about 2.5 minutes and no screenshots. It opens:
- Home, Train, History (overview, Lifting, Running, Body, Food), Food with manual entry, and Settings;
- Train's exercise menu, a workout, and the run screen before and during a run;
- the welcome screen, sign-in, sign-up and every setup step, with a new account each time;
- the Pro offer and plans.

Each screen is opened at 393 and 320 px, with the root font at 135% (the largest standard size) and 200% (where the app's scaling stops). It fails on:
- any element reaching past the screen;
- text wider than its own box, unless it ends in an ellipsis on purpose;
- a page that scrolls sideways, measured on both `<html>` and `<body>`.

It measures `aria-hidden` text too. Much of that is visible text announced another way, like a chart's dates or a row's status word, and it breaks the same as anything else. It skips:
- rows that scroll sideways on purpose;
- text only for screen readers;
- what's inside SVGs;
- anything laid out but invisible.

`ACCEPTED` holds the one kept break (the set table's "kg"/"Reps" headers at 320 px and 2×, from #2592), with its reason. CLAUDE.md now says to fix the layout rather than add to the list.

`layoutBreaks` (the helper the feed and food labs already use) gains an `ignore` selector and skips invisible elements.

The run never ends a workout or a run, and both keep their in-progress state in localStorage, which each Playwright context gets fresh. So it leaves nothing behind in the shared seeded account for the specs that follow.

### What its first run found: History with a real season of data

The earlier passes measured History with sparse data. With `seed:season`, Lifting, Running and Food broke even at 1.35×, and the Lifting page scrolled sideways at 2×.

- **Your lifts** and **Fastest kilometres**: the figure column drops under the row's text when the two don't fit, and the lift's picture gives way under 16em. The text had been squeezed to one word a line, with the top set drawn over it.
- **Volume**: three figures across, or one per row under 17em, as `PeriodSummaryCard`'s are.
- **Chart dates** (both summary charts): under 11em of card, a row naming only the two ends replaces the grid. Hidden middle labels had still taken up room. The volume chart's dates were held to one line, so they made the page scroll sideways.
- **Sets per muscle**: the row's fixed widths alone were wider than the card. Under 15em each row is two lines, name and count, then the range bar and status, and the name wraps instead of ending in "…".
- **Race predictions**: two tiles across, or one under 13em. **Pace by run type**: the pace drops under the run type.
- **Food**:
  - the stat pairs go one per row under 17.5em of page; at 1.35× on 393 px "1,790" was already too wide for half of it;
  - a stat's unit wraps under its figure, which is never cut;
  - the macro legend goes under the ring;
  - the ring stays a 96 px drawing, and above 1.35× its centre figure gives way to the "Avg calories" card directly above, which shows the same number. Scaling the ring would have needed a percentage chart height, which `chartContainerHeight.test.ts` bans for a first-render warning.
- **`EmptyState`**'s side padding is px, the same 24 px at normal size. **Home**'s weight caption hyphenates a word wider than its tile.

## Schema migration check

No schema change.

## Test plan

- [x] The new spec, red first:
  - against `main` before #2594 merged, it failed on exactly the setup and Pro breaks #2594 fixes, plus the History breaks above;
  - after the fixes, all 8 tests pass, and the 10-test run with the History photographs passes too.
- [x] Checked by eye: History's four pages photographed at 393 and 320 px at 1.35× and 2×. No page is wider than the screen, and the rows read in full.
- [x] Unit tests for the two summary charts now target the full label row by test id. A new test pins the narrow row to the chart's two ends, year included.
- [x] `npm run verify`: 11,910 tests, plus lint, typecheck, build and the size check.

This PR introduces a complete football (soccer) simulation game built with Godot 4.4, featuring Argentine football legends from the top 20 historical clubs.

## Summary
A fully-featured 3D football simulation game with:
- Complete match simulation engine with realistic physics
- 3D player models with procedural animation
- Team management with 22 legendary players per club (3 kits each)
- Single-player and multiplayer modes with AI opponent
- Web-based companion for team/kit selection
- Procedurally generated audio effects

## Key Components

**Core Simulation Engine (`sim.gd`)**
- 2058-line physics and gameplay engine running at 60 FPS
- Realistic ball physics with drag, Magnus effect, and rolling friction
- Player movement, stamina, and skill-based mechanics
- Match state management (kickoff, free kicks, penalties, corners)
- AI decision-making system with difficulty levels

**3D Rendering (`partido.gd`, `estadio.gd`, `jugador_3d.gd`)**
- Full 3D stadium with procedural grass shader, stands, and lighting
- Procedurally generated player models with skeletal animation
- Dynamic camera system with multiple viewing angles
- Goal replay system with frame history
- Real-time HUD with match statistics

**Game Flow (`menu.gd`, `main.gd`)**
- Team and player selection interface
- Formation and kit customization
- Match configuration (difficulty, duration, camera mode)
- Web-based HTML companion (`clasico.html`) for team data management

**Data Management (`datos.gd`)**
- Player roster system with attributes and specialties
- Kit/uniform customization system
- Formation templates (4-3-3, 4-2-3-1)
- JSON-based team data (`equipos.json`)

**Audio & UI**
- Procedurally synthesized sound effects (`sonido.gd`)
- Touch-friendly mobile controls (`tactil.gd`)
- Shared UI system with theme management (`ui.gd`)
- Kit artwork rendering system (`kit.gd`)

## Notable Implementation Details
- Headless simulation support for testing (multiple test scripts included)
- Web export configuration with Godot's HTML5 platform
- Procedural player model generation using capsules, cylinders, and spheres
- Custom shader for grass with noise-based variation
- Node.js script for exporting team data from web interface to Godot
- Comprehensive control scheme supporting keyboard, gamepad, and touch input

body:
Closes TSI-3695

Issue: TSI-3695 (multica `01a11110-4699-7441-973f-b6a77d5963f1`)

## 改动

- `classify_mount_error(kind: io::ErrorKind, probe: impl FnOnce() -> FuseProbeResult) -> i32`：挂载失败三分支判据收为单一出口（`PermissionDenied` → 2、探测命中 → 100、其余 → 1）；探针以闭包注入，使 `PermissionDenied` 在探测之前短路，与 `main-entry.md` 步骤 18 的「否则 → 探测 `open("/dev/fuse")`」一致。
- `probe_fuse_device()` + `FuseProbeResult::{Blocked, NotBlocked}` 承接原 `fuse_device_unusable_exit_code()` 的 IO 与 errno 映射（`EACCES`/`EPERM` → `Blocked`，其余含 `ENODEV` → `NotBlocked`）。
- `main()` 挂载失败分支只做 IO 与转发：分类 → 按退出码输出对应日志 → 停引擎 → `exit`。
- 单测：三分支逐一断言（含 exit 2 分支探针不被调用）+ 探针 errno 映射。

## 设计依据

tsic/torrentfs-design@e34b3aa — `03-contracts.md` §1.1 退出码 2/100/1；`05-modules/main-entry.md` §主流程步骤 18。

## 验证

- `cargo test --bin torrentfs`：27 passed, 0 failed（含 4 个新单测）。
- 判别力探针：把 `PermissionDenied` 判据改为恒假 → exit 2 分支单测 FAILED（改动前该类回归无法被捕获）。
- 端到端：真实 daemon 走挂载失败分支——helper 以 `user_allow_other` 文案失败 → exit 2 + `Mount failed: Operation not permitted. Possible causes:`；helper 以其它文案失败 → 探针命中设备可用 → exit 1。
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`：exit 0（`src/main.rs` 唯一告警为既有锁文件 `create(true)`，非本次改动）。

## 未纳入

容器级 exit 2 断言（seccomp/apparmor profile + 新增 CI job）属容器级新增门禁，本次不改 CI；如需补容器级门禁，走独立设计单。

## Summary by Sourcery

Make mount-failure exit codes distinguish direct permission errors, blocked FUSE-device access, and generic failures according to the documented contract.

Bug Fixes:
- Correct mount-failure exit-code classification so direct permission-denied failures return 2, blocked FUSE-device failures return 100, and other failures return 1.
- Ensure permission-denied mount failures do not perform the FUSE-device probe.

Enhancements:
- Separate FUSE-device probing from mount-error classification and centralize mount-failure handling in main().

Tests:
- Add coverage for all mount-failure branches, including the no-probe guarantee for exit code 2 and errno mapping for FUSE-device access failures.

body:
> [!NOTE]
> Written by Claude Code (Opus 5.5) at olgabot's request. Posted from her account, so replies here are to Claude, not to her.

`nextflow-runs/disprot-benchmark/bin/parse_disprot.py` kept 504 of the 1_339 human DisProt entries, and took regions from every annotation term instead of consensus disorder.

## What was wrong

1. It asked for `page=1` first. DisProt pages count from 0, so the first page was skipped.
2. It read the entry count from `count` or `total`. The API calls it `size`, so the loop stopped after one page. With `page_size=2000`, only entries 2001 onwards were kept (DP03004 is the lowest human ID in the June table).
3. It read `entry["regions"]`, which holds every annotation (disorder, transitions, functions). Consensus disorder is `entry["disprot_consensus"]["Structural state"]` with `type == "D"`.

## The fix

- Asks for human entries only (`ncbi_taxon_id=9606`), 500 per page, from page 0, until it has `size` entries; exits if the count does not match.
- `--local` refuses a file that holds fewer entries than its `size` (one page of a paged download).
- Regions are consensus "Structural state" regions of type "D". The output columns are unchanged.

## What read the June table

Full list in `nextflow-runs/disprot-benchmark/parse_disprot_audit_2026-10-06.md`.

- Every DisProt number from the `--database disprot` runs in `~/data/disprot-benchmark/` (`disprot/`, `disprot_null/`, `null/`) and every DisProt column of notebook 081: 271 queries, where the full release gives 710 (same `map_disprot_pfam.py`, which reproduces the June mapping byte for byte from the June table). This includes the AUC-PR table (MMseqs2 0.715 vs kmerseek k26 0.570), recall at 5% FDR, the false-positive rates, the score statistics and the DisProt figures.
- Bug 3 changed the regions of 16 of 503 proteins, but nothing downstream reads the region columns, so it changed no reported number.
- Not affected: the MobiDB columns (`parse_mobidb.py` does not page), notebook 251 (its own `scripts/fetch_disprot.py` took 3_337 of 3_337 entries and picks regions by namespace), and the regions-index pilot fetcher.

## Needs rerunning (not run here)

1. The `--database disprot` run, without `-resume` for the download: `downloadDisprot` calls the script by path, so its cache would hand back the June table. Not with `--reuse_results true`, which reads the old ground truth. To pin the release notebook 251 used: `--disprot_json ~/data/disprot-region-transfer/raw/disprot_2026_06.json` (same 3_337 entries as `current` today).
2. The `disprot_null/` and `null/` runs, if still wanted.
3. Notebook 081, then its summary.

## Checks

- `pytest nextflow-runs/disprot-benchmark/tests`: 8 passed. The new tests check page 0 first, the `size` stop, the short-download exit, and consensus-only regions; the old `parse_entry` returns the extra function region the region test rejects.
- Live API: 1_339 / 1_339 human entries. `--local` on the cached `2026_06` release gives the identical table.

author: daavoo
body:
## Description

Today every workspace on an Otari deployment searches the web through one search account, the deployment's, so the operator pays for everyone's searches and they all share one quota. This lets an organization bring its own search key, so its workspaces' searches bill to its own account instead. It is "bring your own key" for web search, the same thing Otari already offers for model providers, and it follows the provider key design decided at otari-ai#1748.

**What an organization can do.** Its owners and admins add keys for a search provider (Tavily or Brave), rename or replace one, archive it, and make one key per provider the organization's default. Only the last four characters of a key are ever shown back. Whitespace around a pasted key is trimmed, and a key with whitespace or a control character inside is refused, since it cannot be sent in a header.

**Which key a workspace uses.** Each workspace searches with exactly one key, for a model's `otari_web_search` calls and for direct search (`POST /api/v1/search`) alike: the key it pinned as its own, otherwise an organization default (Tavily before Brave), otherwise the organization's oldest key. A workspace's owners and admins can pin a key or turn one off, and any member can see which key it uses, in a paged list (`skip`, `limit`, `count`) whose effective key is chosen across every key, not the page. Choosing a key reads the pin and the defaults first, and the oldest keys only when none of those is usable. A key the workspace turned off, an archived key, or one this deployment cannot decrypt is passed over.

**What does not change.** A workspace with no usable key searches exactly as before, with the deployment's search. A key changes who pays, not whether search exists: the deployment must still have web search configured, and the workspace's web-access policy (veto, domains, result limits) still applies. The key is never logged and never returned to a caller.

**Across deployment modes.**
- Standalone: a request from a workspace with a key searches with it. On direct search the named search tool must still be configured, and the request is still allowlisted, rate-limited, priced and timed out as that tool; only the provider call moves to the organization's key. A Brave key localizes to the request's `country`; Tavily takes a full country name, so a Tavily key is not sent one.
- Hosted: serves the same management API. It runs no inference itself, so its organizations' keys are used by the hybrid gateways that serve them.
- Hybrid: the gateway reads the key from an optional `credential` field on the control plane's web search answer. `docs/hybrid-mode-protocol.md` specifies it: read strictly, so a malformed one (including a key that cannot go in a header) fails closed, while a provider this gateway does not know is ignored, and an older gateway ignores the field entirely.

**Not in this PR, and worth a decision:**
- **The control plane side.** otari.ai has to choose the key and return `credential` in `/gateway/web-search/resolve`. Until it does, hybrid workspaces keep using the deployment's search. The issue asks for the peer to agree the field; this PR is the proposal.
- **A dashboard page.** The API is in place; the page to manage keys is not.
- **Pricing.** A search on a workspace's own key is still recorded under the gateway's `web_search` tool price, as before. Whether a search the organization pays its provider for should still carry that price is a product call this PR does not make.

## How to test it locally

Automated:
- `tests/unit/test_web_search_keys.py`: the choice of key (pin, then default with Tavily first, then oldest; turned-off and undecryptable keys passed over), the key winning over the deployment's own provider in the search backend, admission carrying it only for a declared search, a credential never printing its key, the choice reading only the rows it reaches (pin and defaults, then batches of the oldest), and a keyed direct search forwarding the tool's timeout and `country`.
- `tests/integration/test_web_search_keys.py`: the management API end to end (secrets not echoed, unknown provider refused, duplicate names refused on create and on rename, one default per provider, delete only after archive, a restored key not becoming a default again, a pasted key trimmed and an unsendable one refused, workspace pin and turn-off, and paging that never changes the effective key), who may do what (a plain member cannot list or add keys, a workspace member can see but not change the choice, another organization's key reads as absent), and a real `/api/v1/messages` request searching with the organization's key, with the deployment's search when the workspace turned its key off, when the key is archived, and when there is none.
- `tests/unit/test_web_search_providers.py`: Brave sends only a two-letter `country`, Tavily none, and a key that cannot go in a header is refused before any request and never quoted in the error.
- `tests/unit/test_web_search_policy_resolve.py`, `tests/unit/test_container.py`: the stored policy gets the workspace's key through the injected resolver, falls back to the deployment's search without one, and the container refuses to build the policy without the resolver builder.
- `tests/integration/test_hybrid_mode_chat.py`: a key in the control plane's answer is used; a malformed one is refused with `502`; one for an unknown provider is ignored.
- `tests/integration/test_hosted_mode_surface.py`: the management API is mounted on a hosted control plane.
- `tests/integration/test_search_endpoint.py`: direct search runs on the organization's key with the named tool's timeout, and on the named tool when the workspace turned its key off.
- The full unit suite and the affected integration files pass, as do the architecture check, ruff, mypy, the migration chain and schema parity tests, the OpenAPI and Postman drift checks, and the dashboard typecheck.

Also run by hand against a gateway booted from this branch (SQLite, a fake SearXNG): deployment search with no key, then the organization's key on direct search, paging, Tavily default over the oldest key, a workspace pin, and turning keys off falling back to the deployment's search; no key appeared in a response or the log.

By hand, on a standalone deployment with web search configured and `OTARI_SECRET_KEY` set:
1. `POST /api/v1/organizations/me/web-search-keys` with `{"provider": "tavily", "name": "ours", "api_key": "<a Tavily key>"}`.
2. `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/web-search-keys` shows that key as `is_effective`.
3. A request declaring `otari_web_search` searches through Tavily with that key.

- [x] New Feature
- [ ] Bug Fix
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] Infrastructure / CI

Fixes #1724

- [x] I ran the Definition of Done checks locally (`make lint`, `make typecheck`, `make test`). The Python checks, the dashboard typecheck and every affected test file; CI runs the full suite.
- [x] Documentation was updated where necessary. `docs/tools.md`, `docs/hybrid-mode-protocol.md`, `docs/domains.md` and `src/gateway/AGENTS.md`.
- [x] If the API contract changed, I regenerated the OpenAPI spec (`uv run python scripts/generate_openapi.py`). Also the Postman collection, the dashboard client and the SDK endpoint manifest.
- [x] If this changes a rule in `ARCHITECTURE.md` or `scripts/check_architecture.py`, the description names the rule and says why. author: chraibi
body:
### visibility: end vismap time grid at FDS run end

_build_vismap set the time points to arange(0, t_end + step, step),
so a step that does not divide T_END added a point past the last FDS
frame (T_END 400 s, step 30 s: 420 s). fdsvismap 0.3.2 answers it
with the last frame; fdsvismap#86 rejects it. The grid is now the
steps before T_END plus T_END itself. Values at every stored time up
to T_END are unchanged (bit-identical on assets/vis_slice_height). A
query between the last step and T_END may now pick the T_END frame
instead of the earlier grid point, which is the fresher frame (step
1.5 s, t = 1.8 s: sight 3.004 m instead of 3.008 m on that fixture).

VisibilityModel also raised FdsHorizonError for any query past its
last time point, and reported the vismap step as the "output
interval". The preflight (_fds_horizon_overrun) and the slice
samplers accept one FDS output interval past the last frame, as
docs/howto-create-scenario.md and docs/scenario-json.md document. With
the default step and an integer T_END, a run the preflight accepted
could fail mid-run in sign visibility. The model now stores the
extinction slice's output interval with its cache and uses that same
window.

This changes what tests/test_fds_horizon.py asserted:
test_visibility_raises_past_the_vismap_time_points encoded the
narrower window ("no extra step"). It becomes
test_visibility_raises_past_one_fds_output_interval, because sign
visibility must follow the documented run-wide window rather than
narrow it, or the preflight would accept runs that cannot finish.

The cache stores the interval, and its format goes from 5 to 6, so
caches with an overshooting point are rebuilt. Clear-air caches are
rebuilt once too; their behaviour is unchanged.

The fdsvismap pin stays at 0.3.2 until #86 is released.


### docs: describe the run-wide sign visibility window

docs/fds-sampling.md still said VisibilityModel raises past the first
vismap step at or after the FDS end, and the wayfinding page did not
say where the stored times end. Both now describe the behaviour of the
previous commit: stored times end at the last extinction frame, and a
query raises only more than one output interval past it, the window
the setup check and the slice samplers use. CHANGELOG gets a Fixed
entry that names the cache format change (5 to 6, caches rebuilt once).

Two tests are added. One builds a model over a format-5 cache on
assets/vis_slice_height, checks that it is rewritten as format 6 with
times ending at T_END and the slice interval, and that a second model
reuses it without a rebuild and gives the same answers. The other
fixes the near-end rule: a grid point within 1e-9 x T_END of T_END is
merged into T_END. It reads the same last frame (FDS frames are never

author: chrisbrooksbank
body:
## Summary

Three bug-hunting passes over the game, then a new README with GIFs, screenshots and Galaga history.

### Round 1: state transitions
- Resuming from pause (and returning from a challenging stage) re-ran `OnEnter(Playing)`. That **reset the score and lives** and spawned a duplicate player, formation and HUD. New-game setup now runs only on `Menu → Playing`.
- Gameplay music restarted from the beginning on every unpause.
- Enemies, bullets, HUD and other leftovers from a finished game were never despawned. They showed through the title screen and carried into the next game.
- A ship lost during the stage-clear delay never respawned during the following challenging stage.
- Black clear color instead of Bevy's default grey.

### Round 2: tractor beam, dual fighter, scoring
- Shooting a Boss mid-beam left the player **frozen for the rest of the game** and stopped any further beams. A Boss whose captive died hovered at the stop point forever. A new `tractor_beam_watchdog` system recovers from both.
- A Boss already holding a captured ship could beam again, which destroyed the first captured ship.
- Losing the main ship in dual-fighter mode cost a life and left the second ship orphaned. The surviving ship now carries on (arcade behaviour).
- The perfect bonus and splitter bonuses skipped the extra-life check. All scoring now goes through `scoring::add_points`.

### Round 3: arcade faithfulness
- Bosses gave no feedback after the first of their two hits. They now turn purple.
- `Esc` now pauses during challenging stages, and resuming doesn't restart the stage.
- The ship can no longer fire while it's being pulled up by a beam.
- The tractor beam caught the player **anywhere on screen**. It now only catches a ship under the beam and times out after 3.5 s.

### README
Rewritten with gameplay, tractor-beam and challenging-stage GIFs (in `docs/media/`), an enemy and scoring table, controls, and a short history of Galaxian and Galaga. It also has Linux/macOS build notes, since `.cargo/config.toml` targets Windows only. A claim in the old README about escort scoring up to 1600 was dropped because that feature isn't implemented.

## Testing
- `cargo build` / `cargo test` (15 tests, 6 new unit tests for the watchdog and scoring), built for `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`
- Played the game under Xvfb with scripted input and checked: score kept across pause/resume, clean field after game over, ship outside the beam not captured, pausing a challenging stage.
- The beam and challenging-stage GIFs were recorded with a temporary local build that made the beam trigger immediately and skipped stages 1–2. That change was not committed.

author: harshal0001
body:
Follows KoSIT on which rule sets apply to which document, the part #40 left alone.

Each scenario in `scenarios.xml` lists the Schematron stylesheets it validates with. The XRechnung, extension and CVD scenarios name two: the EN 16931 core and the German CIUS. The plain EN 16931 scenarios name one. The service ran both on every document, so an invoice claiming only EN 16931 — a typical ZUGFeRD PDF — came back with `BR-DE-*` errors for a CIUS it never claimed.

## What changes

- `Scenario.stylesheets` is read from `validateWithSchematron`. The engine runs the stylesheets the matched scenario names, and refuses a scenario naming one it does not hold. A test over the real rule set asserts that never happens for a shipped configuration.
- A document no scenario recognises is still run through everything, as before.
- When a rule set was not applied, the report carries an informational finding, `NATIONAL-RULES-NOT-APPLIED`, in German or English, naming the scenario. Without it, "no XRechnung findings" and "XRechnung rules never ran" look the same.
- The page shows a "Geprüft als / Checked as" fact with the scenario name.
- `ValidationEngine.reports()` exposes the raw SVRL per stylesheet run, for the mutation search to use the service's engine instead of its own.

## Checked

The same reference invoice with its buyer reference removed, in both syntaxes:

| Claims to be | Scenario | Blocking findings |
|---|---|---|
| XRechnung | EN16931 XRechnung | BR-DE-15 |
| EN 16931 | EN16931 | none, plus the notice |
| nothing recognised | none | BR-DE-15 |

A plain EN 16931 invoice with an invalid currency code still fails the core. All 86 reference messages still validate with no blocking finding. 2,452 backend tests, 21 frontend.

## Not decided here

ZUGFeRD BASIC and EXTENDED, and Peppol BIS, carry identifiers no KoSIT scenario recognises, so they are still held to the German rules. KoSIT's own validator rejects them outright as unknown. Neither is obviously right for this service.

author: sbj-ee
body:
## Root cause (plain words)

v1.3.0 Mac `.dmg` crashes at launch:

```
Library not loaded: @executable_path/../Frameworks/QtSerialPort.framework/Versions/A/QtSerialPort
Reason: code signature … not valid for use in process:
  mapping process and mapped file (non-platform) have different Team IDs
```

PR #30 (`sec/release-hardening`) changed Mac packaging from:

```bash
codesign --force --deep -s -          # v1.2.0 — works
```

to:

```bash
codesign --force --deep --options runtime --timestamp=none -s -   # v1.3.0 — broken on end-user Macs
```

**Hardened runtime** turns on **library validation**, which requires every loaded library to share the main binary’s **Team ID**. Ad-hoc signatures (`-s -`) have **no Team ID**. dyld then treats the separately signed nested Qt frameworks (QtSerialPort, QtCore, …) as a Team ID mismatch and aborts — even when `codesign -dv` shows `TeamIdentifier=not set` on both.

Evidence from the published DMGs (parsed on Linux from the Mach-O code directories):

| | v1.2.0 | v1.3.0 |
|---|---|---|
| Main + QtSerialPort Team ID | empty | empty |
| `CS_ADHOC` | yes | yes |
| `CS_RUNTIME` (hardened) | **no** (`flags=0x2`) | **yes** (`flags=0x10002`) |
| Launch on Stephen’s Mac | OK | SIGABRT / dyld |

CI on the signing runner could still launch the app (and did for v1.3.0); the failure shows up on a different Mac after download. `codesign --verify --deep --strict` does **not** catch this — it only checks signature integrity, not library-validation Team ID policy.

Linux 1.3.0 is unaffected.

## Fix

1. **`cmake/MacDeploy.cmake.in`**: after `macdeployqt` + rpath fixes, explicitly ad-hoc re-sign every nested piece with the **same** identity, then the `.app` last:
   - `Frameworks/*.dylib` and `PlugIns/**/*.dylib`
   - each `Frameworks/*.framework`
   - MacOS helpers (askpass)
   - `zterminal.app` last  
   All with `codesign --force --timestamp=none -s -` — **no `--options runtime`** (matches v1.2.0). Developer ID + notarization can add hardened runtime later once there is a real Team ID (`docs/HARDENING.md`).

2. **`tools/macos/check-bundle.sh`**: fail CI if nested Mach-Os disagree on `TeamIdentifier` / `Signature`, or if ad-hoc + hardened runtime creeps back in.

3. **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**: assert `Signature=adhoc` and that the runtime flag is **absent**; keep the launch smoke test.

4. Docs: `docs/HARDENING.md`, comments in `Hardening.cmake` / `Packaging.cmake`.

## Workarounds for Stephen right now (until 1.3.1)

| Workaround | Helps? |
|---|---|
| `xattr -cr /path/to/zterminal.app` alone | **No** — this is not a quarantine-only issue; it’s library validation under hardened runtime. |
| Re-sign **without** hardened runtime after mounting/copying the app | **Yes (expected):** |
| | `codesign --force --deep --sign - --timestamp=none /path/to/zterminal.app` |
| | (omit `--options runtime`; optional: also `xattr -cr` first) |
| Re-sign **with** `--options runtime` | **No** — same failure mode. |
| Use **v1.2.0** `.dmg` | **Yes — safe fallback** (no hardened runtime; same empty Team IDs). https://github.com/sbj-ee/zterminal/releases/tag/v1.2.0 |
| Linux 1.3.0 on vertex | Fine; unchanged. |

## After merge

- **Do not bump version in this PR.**
- Cut **v1.3.1** (version bump + tag) so a new Mac `.dmg` supersedes the broken v1.3.0 asset. The published v1.3.0 Mac `.dmg` stays until then.
- Developer ID / notarization remains a follow-up when an Apple account is available.

## Test plan

- [ ] macOS arm64 CI green (package + `check-bundle` + `codesign --verify` + launch smoke test)
- [ ] CI log shows `Signature=adhoc` and **no** `runtime` in flags
- [ ] `check-bundle` reports matching Team ID / Signature across nested Mach-Os
- [ ] Linux jobs still green (unrelated but required)

author: draganm
body:
A jobs-build image object can now list other repo paths its build may reference:

```yaml
image:
  type: jobs-build
  path: /services/tally-mev
  sources:            # optional
    - /proto
  platform: linux/amd64
```

Until now assimilate ingested the directory named by `path` and nothing else, so a monorepo could not share source between two images. The case behind this: validator-watch has eight Go services that each carry a byte-identical copy of one `.proto` file and its 1,200-line generated bindings. jobs-iroh has supported builds in a wider context since v0.11.0 (sibling sources) and v0.12.0 (`closure=`); assimilate just never set `Dir`.

Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-06-image-sources-design.md`.

## What it does

- **With `sources`:** the project root is ingested once per run, pruned with `PruneTree` to `path` plus `sources`, and submitted with `Dir` set to the service and `Ctx: CtxWidened` — field for field what jobs-iroh's own client builds for a subdirectory. Only the pruned tree is pushed.
- **Without `sources`:** nothing changes. Same subtree ingest, same definition bytes, same K. Adopting this re-tags nothing.
- **The tag stays offline-computable**, so `render` still needs no server. Rejected alternatives: tagging by the server's covered key (known only after pin; `render` would need the server) and deriving the list from `go.mod` (ecosystem logic in assimilate).
- `deploy` resolves every image with sources before it dials the server, so a listed path that is missing, ignored, or — for `path` — not a directory stops the run before any build.

What a tag depends on:

| | without `sources` | with `sources` |
|---|---|---|
| content and modes under `path` | yes | yes |
| content and modes under each source | — | yes |
| anything else in the repo | no | no |
| mtime, uid, gid | yes | no (`PruneTree` normalizes them) |

`sources` is the bound on what a build may reference; what it uses is still the recipe's business (its directory or `closure=`, its `sources=`, its plugins' paths). The README says so, with the plugin-go case.

## Verification

- `gofmt`, `go vet` and `go test ./...` pass (11 packages).
- Tests pin: normalization of entries; the scanner's errors; that a spec without sources has the definition bytes and K it always had; that with sources `Dir`/`Ctx` are set and K ignores changes outside the covered paths and mtimes inside them; the existence, `.amberignore` and not-a-directory errors; one root ingest per run; grouping by source in the build runner and in `render`; the deploy preflight.
- On a real project (validator-watch, 10 images):
  - with no template using `sources`, this branch renders the same tag as v0.7.5 for every image;
  - adding `sources: [/proto]` to one image changes that image's tag only; changing mtimes under `/proto` or adding an unrelated file moves no tag; changing content under `/proto` moves exactly the images that list it;
  - the root walk takes `render` from 0.12 s to 0.66 s there (0.21 s with a root `.amberignore` excluding local tool directories).
- An independent review found no correctness or compatibility defect; its findings (errors surfacing only after other images had built, a README that implied listing a path was enough, a misleading hint on case-insensitive filesystems, `path` accepted when it is a file, non-string entries) are fixed in the last commit.

**Not verified:** a build against a real server. I cannot run one; the first is validator-watch's `assimilate deploy hoodi` (its consumers use `replace … => ../../proto` with plugin-go's `go_closure`). The cluster's server is v0.31.0, which has both features.

## Known limits

- The root walk ingests the whole repo into the local store; a root `.amberignore` is the lever, and an unreadable file anywhere fails every image with sources (the error names it).
- A failed root ingest is not memoized: in `deploy` the preflight stops at the first error, so this only costs repeated walks inside the build runner if the tree changes between the two.
- The with-sources and without-sources twins of one path share a display name in the TUI.
- The branch adds the design spec and the implementation plan under `docs/superpowers/` (jobs-iroh keeps such documents there too). Say if you would rather have only the `docs/design.md` and README changes.

author: rnagrodzki
body:
## Summary
Fixes a bug where the review command's dimension cap kept the least severe review dimensions active and skipped the most severe ones. Also adds a per-project config key to raise the cap, and makes queued (skipped) dimensions visible in review output.

## Business Context
Any project that defines more review dimensions than the fixed cap of 8 had its review coverage silently inverted: the review command kept low-severity dimensions active and queued high-severity ones, so the most important checks were the ones most likely to be skipped. There was also no way to raise the cap without a plugin code change.

## Business Benefits
Review coverage now prioritizes correctly: when a project defines more dimensions than the cap, the most severe dimensions are reviewed and the rest are queued, not the other way around. Projects can also raise the cap for their own needs through config, and anyone reading review output can now see exactly which dimensions were queued and why.

## Technical Design
The dimension-cap sort in `refinePlan` compared severity ranks with `diff := rj - ri; return diff > 0`, which is equivalent to sorting dimensions by ascending severity — the opposite of the intended "keep the most severe" behavior. The comparator now sorts descending (`ri > rj`) so the highest-severity dimensions are kept first.

The cap itself is now configurable: a new `[review] maxDimensions` key in `.sdlc-v2/local.toml` (default 8, minimum 1) is read and validated by a new `resolveDimensionCap` function. Validation rejects non-whole numbers, infinite values, and values below 1 with a `DomainError` that names the fix; a value larger than `math.MaxInt32` is clamped rather than overflowing on the float-to-int conversion.

Queued dimensions are no longer silent: the review manifest's `plan_critique` now carries `dimension_cap` alongside the existing `queued_dimensions`, and the review skill's dry-run and posted-comment output both list every queued dimension name and the active cap, with a "partial coverage: N dimension(s) queued" note added to the verdict heading when applicable.

Separately, the nested-execution-authorization review guardrail was widened: it previously only covered `execute` running as a nested dispatch; it now covers any nested skill dispatch (including `review` itself) and adds a new requirement that abandoned background workers be explicitly cleaned up via `TaskStop` or equivalent in stall handlers, cleanup steps, and error-recovery paths.

## Technical Impact
Affects the `review_prepare` MCP tool and the `review` skill's output formatting only — no external API surface changes beyond the new optional `maxDimensions` config key, which is backward compatible (absent key keeps the previous default of 8). The config schema and setup documentation were updated to describe the new key. No database, migration, or breaking changes.

## Changes Overview
- Fixed the dimension-cap sort so it keeps the most severe dimensions active and queues the least severe ones, instead of the reverse.
- Added a configurable per-project dimension cap (default 8, minimum 1), replacing the previous hardcoded limit.
- Added validation for the new cap value: rejects non-whole numbers and values below 1, rejects infinite values, and clamps an excessively large value instead of letting it overflow.
- Review output (dry run and posted PR comment) now names every queued dimension and the active cap, and flags partial coverage in the verdict heading when dimensions were queued.
- Widened a review guardrail so it covers any nested skill dispatch, not just `execute`, and added a requirement to clean up abandoned background workers in nested dispatches.

## Testing
Added unit test coverage for the new `resolveDimensionCap` validation (non-whole numbers, values below 1, infinite values, the overflow clamp) and for the corrected sort order in `refinePlan`, plus a config-schema sync test confirming the new `maxDimensions` key is documented consistently. No manual testing beyond the automated suite was performed as part of this change.

---
<!-- release-level:patch -->
<!-- release-pre:rc -->
<!-- release-notes-start -->
## [Unreleased]

- Fix: review_prepare's dimension cap no longer inverts severity order — it now keeps the most severe dimensions active instead of the least severe.
- Add: configurable `[review] maxDimensions` key in `.sdlc-v2/local.toml` (default 8, minimum 1) to raise the review dimension cap per project.
- Add: dry-run and posted review output now names every queued dimension and the active cap, and flags partial coverage in the verdict heading.
<!-- release-notes-end -->

author: albersg
body:
Adds a Utilities row and a screen that show the values in the user's
`.wslconfig` next to the recommendation for this machine and let them be edited
and written. The recommendation stays `PlanWSLResources(DetectHostResources())`
-- the same function the installer already used -- and the content and the
writing go through one shared implementation: the install step, the interactive
script and the menu all end in `wslConfigContent` and `writeWSLConfig`. A guard
mounts the same pre-existing file through both routes with the same host and
compares the bytes.

**The utility is offered only on a WSL host** with a resolvable Windows profile
and a checkout carrying the template; elsewhere the section says why, naming the
system. Memory, processors and swap are editable; the keys that change how WSL
networks or reclaims memory are merged but not offered as knobs, because they
are not the size of the VM and were not asked for.

**Writing preserves what is not ours**: the managed keys are updated in place
and under their section, and other keys, comments, blank lines, ordering and
unknown sections survive literally. A key the render omits (unknown host) is
left as it is -- a limit that cannot be computed is never deleted -- and a file
the repo wrote round-trips unchanged. A backup is taken before any write and
dry-run is respected. The screen says the values take effect only after
`wsl --shutdown`, and does not run it.

**The pre-existing state is worth naming**: the interactive script wrote the
full render with `install_artifact`, skipping the merge the Go step already did,
so on the route a TUI install actually takes, a user's own `.wslconfig` keys
were dropped. The merge now happens before that write, guarded by a test.

Found while writing this: `renderedRepoWSLConfig` merged under a name that said
render -- renamed to `mergedRepoWSLConfig`, so nobody edits it without knowing
the user's keys are inside. And the Utilities panel was a second list; it now
derives one entry per utility from the same model state the section reads.

Verification: `make check` clean; `go test ./... -count=1 -timeout 30m` 4874
passed; frame guards at twelve sizes; no golden moved.

## Problem

#11259 bumped `effect` to `^4.0.0`. Effect v4 removed `Context.GenericTag`, still used by the homepage visual effects (`VisualEffect.js`, `DependencyInjectionVisual.jsx`). Verified with `effect@4.0.1`: `Context.GenericTag` is `undefined`.

body:
Closes #314

## Summary

Ran the skill-creator retrofit loop (Path B, Subpath B1) against `skills/devops-pipeline`. **Verdict: PASS.** Both numeric gates were already green at baseline (`asm eval` 92/A, `quick_validate.py` clean). The Gate 1 inspection still found three of the five human-review checks failing (controlled instructions, output contract, understanding criteria), and the `docs/README.md` Resources table left out `references/cli-e2e.md`. This PR repairs all of them. `metadata.version` moves from 2.2.2 to 2.3.0 (minor: a new final-report section, a new reference file and a new eval suite). The skill's name, description and core purpose are unchanged, so `codebase-modernizer` (#311), which recommends this skill by name, is unaffected.

## Approach

Option 2, "Balanced retrofit": measure both gates, fix Gate 1 first, walk the predictability audit, and touch only the devops-pipeline skill plus its README row and CHANGELOG entry. `asm eval --fix --dry-run` reported "No fixes needed", so Phase 1 made no edits. No category was below 8 at any point, so Phase 3 made no score-chasing edits. No SKILL.md content was deleted: the replaced code blocks in Steps 2 and 4 became numbered instructions with the same commands.

## Decision Record

- **Root cause:** The skill was valid (asm 92) but predates the human-review part of the current standard. Step 2 ran `pre-commit install` *before* `pre-commit run --all-files`, which contradicted the Safety Rails rule to dry-run before installing hooks, and it never ran the `validate-config` or foreign-hook checks the rails required. The merge rail packed five actions into one sentence ("write a backup first … ask them to confirm before writing") and gave no outcome for a declined merge. Step 3 said "Create `ci.yml`" with no condition for an existing workflow. Step 4 ran `bash scripts/e2e_test.sh` unconditionally, though only CLI projects have it. Runs ended on step reports with a bare `Result:` line and no evidence, uncertainty or decision. The acceptance criteria checked correctness only, and there were no evals.
- **Options considered:** Option 1 — Minimal (output contract only); Option 2 — Balanced retrofit (all failing Gate 1 checks, a final-report reference, an eval suite, README fixes); Option 3 — Comprehensive (also move Edge Cases and the tool table to references, deduplicate Edge Cases against Safety Rails, convert to per-step delegation)
- **Options rejected:** Option 1 leaves the controlled-instruction and understanding checks failing, so Gate 1 stays BLOCKER. Option 3 restructures safety wording and adds a Subpath B3 conversion that the issue did not ask for.
- **Selected option:** Option 2 — Balanced retrofit
- **Residual risk:** The devops-pipeline workflow and its new evals were not run against a real target repository, so the behavior is untested. Human understanding of the final report is unconfirmed because no reviewer feedback was collected. The file is 2810 words by `wc -w` (190 below the cap), so the next addition should link out.

Analyzed at: `main @ 5c14be1` (2026-10-06)

## Skill-creator retrofit result

**PASS** (2 measured iterations: the retrofit edits, then one QA fix to the hook-path check; version 2.2.2 → 2.3.0)

### Gate 1 evidence

| # | Check | Baseline | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `quick_validate.py skills/devops-pipeline` | `Skill is valid!`, exit 0, no WARNING lines | same |
| 2 | Frontmatter Audit | pass (allowed keys, name = dir, quoted strings, semver + author, `effort: medium`) | pass |
| 3 | Size (evaluator body count / whole file by `wc -w`) | 292 lines / 2383 body words / 2434 file words | 301 lines / 2759 body words / 2810 file words |
| 4 | Description | one line, negative trigger ("Skip for Terraform/K8s, deployment pipelines, or non-GitHub CI providers.") | unchanged |
| 5 | Version / author | 2.2.2, author present | 2.3.0 |
| 6 | `docs/README.md` | AI-skip comment and template sections present; **Resources table omitted `references/cli-e2e.md`**; Output described CI as "matrix testing and coverage" with no bypass guard | Resources lists every `references/` file plus `evals/`; Output names the bypass guard and the final report; a bypass-guard row added to What Runs Where |
| 7 | Bundled scripts | none (`scripts/` absent) | unchanged |
| 8 | Referenced paths exist | 3 reference files, one level deep | plus `references/final-report.md` (new) |
| 9 | Step Completion Reports + Repo Sync | both present | unchanged |
| 10 | Dependency preflight | not needed: the skill invokes no other skill | no preflight added (correct) |
| 11 | Human-review checks | **3 of 5 failed** (1, 2, 5) | 4 of 4 applicable pass; check 4 not applicable |

Human-review repairs:
1. **Controlled instructions.** The merge rail is now five ordered steps: copy to `.bak`, prepare the merge, show the diff, write only on confirmation (a decline leaves the original unchanged and is recorded), and keep the backup until the user confirms. Step 2 now runs `validate-config` (a non-zero exit stops before any install), then the `run --all-files` dry run, then the foreign-hook check in the directory `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` prints, then both `install` calls. Step 1 has a done-when line and asks for the stack when no manifest matches. Step 3 states the existing-workflow condition, and duplicate CI steps are proposed removals that need confirmation. Step 4 is numbered with expected exit codes, runs E2E only for CLI projects, and records failures as findings without suppressing them.
2. **Output contract.** A new `## Write the Final Report` section points to `references/final-report.md`. The report starts with `Result:` (`COMPLETE`, `PARTIAL — reason`, or `BLOCKED — reason`; the status depends on whether a repository write happened), followed by `Evidence:` (only commands that ran, with exit codes), `Uncertainty:` (always the CI workflow that has not run yet) and `Decision:` (or `No approval needed.`). The reference has COMPLETE and BLOCKED examples and maps step-report results to statuses. An audit-only run uses the same report.
3. **Format selection:** passed at baseline (fixed concise text for a quick operation).
4. **Interactive reports:** not applicable. Pipeline setup is a quick operation, and its report is a fixed block that is read once with nothing to filter.
5. **Understanding criteria.** A new acceptance criterion requires the four reader checks and states that human understanding stays unconfirmed without user feedback. The new `evals/evals.json` has six cases (two happy-path, three edge, one negative-trigger), each with expectations. They include process assertions (validate and dry-run before install, both hook types, diff-scoped bypass guard) and final-report assertions.

author: emiloffingen
body:
## Summary
Searching (for example "Бугарија") renders `/api/news?q=…` on the server and shows a full error page if that request fails or takes more than 8 seconds. The semantic half of the combined search query is the part that can fail or run long:
- it scans every recent article instead of using the vector index (it orders by `1 - distance`), taking about 0.4 s at 150,000 articles on a fast machine and more on weaker hardware;
- its only time limit was the 120 s `statement_timeout`;
- any exception in it failed the whole request.

This change makes the semantic half optional:
- `core/database.py`: `async_execute` / `async_hybrid_search` accept `timeout_ms`, applied with a transaction-local `set_config('statement_timeout', …)`. Postgres cancels the statement itself and the pooled connection is left clean.
- `routes/news.py`: the semantic query gets a 4 s budget (`SEARCH_SEMANTIC_TIMEOUT_MS`); on any error or timeout it logs a warning and returns plain text-search results (a few milliseconds) instead of a 500.

Results for a healthy search are unchanged.

## Not fixed here
I could not reproduce the production error, so I do not know that this is its cause. If the failure is elsewhere (database connections exhausted, a page-side problem), this will not help and the logs are needed. The index scan itself is not changed: ordering by distance returns far too few rows once the date filter is applied, so a correct fix needs pgvector's iterative scans (0.8+).

## Test plan
- [x] Route tests: falls back on error; no fallback when the hybrid query succeeds
- [x] Real-Postgres test: a slow query is cancelled in under 3 s, the pool stays healthy, the limit does not leak into the next query
- [x] Both mutation-checked (removing the fallback or the timeout fails the matching test)
- [x] 638 backend tests, ruff check/format, bandit, pip-audit, secrets scan
- [ ] CI on this PR

author: joseph-zhong
body:
# Summary

Recover existing muxai worktrees into usable persistent tmux sessions, including nested names, surviving branches, and panes whose working directory was deleted.

## Before

- If an agent exited during startup, its tmux session disappeared and the dashboard repeatedly returned to an empty/stopped tile.
- Creating the same name again failed when its worktree or branch already existed.
- Worktrees with `/` in their names were omitted from discovery.
- A tmux session could retain a deleted pane working directory even when its configured session path looked valid, causing `getcwd` and `os error 2` failures.
- The package version was `0.1.0`.

## After

- Agents run inside a persistent interactive shell, so an early exit leaves an inspectable, usable prompt.
- Creating an existing name recovers and attaches its worktree; a surviving branch is reattached when the worktree registration is gone.
- Nested worktree names are discovered and recoverable.
- Recovery validates the active pane path and replaces a session whose pane is stranded in a deleted directory.
- New panes explicitly change into their worktree and verify their process directory before launching the agent, even when the long-lived tmux server inherited a directory that was later deleted.
- The five revisions monotonically bump the minor version to `0.2.0`, `0.3.0`, `0.4.0`, `0.5.0`, and `0.6.0`.

## Highlights

- `ba65926` / `0.2.0`: persistent shells, reusable registered worktrees, and nested-name discovery.
- `b9d85fb` / `0.3.0`: reattach surviving Git branches instead of failing with “already exists.”
- `1ebdeaa` / `0.4.0`: compare `pane_current_path` with the worktree and replace stale tmux sessions safely.
- `47e84ec` / `0.5.0`: keep a new worktree when tmux UI setup fails so a live shell never loses its working directory and the same name remains recoverable.
- `483e541` / `0.6.0`: override tmux's stale server working directory for every new pane and verify the pane path before sending the agent command.
- Same-name tmux sessions belonging to a different worktree remain protected by an explicit collision error.

## Learnings

- tmux's `session_path` can remain valid while `pane_current_path` points to a directory that no longer exists.
- tmux 3.7c can report the requested `session_path` while starting the pane in the server's deleted original `PWD`; `new-session -c` alone does not prevent it.
- Removing a Git worktree can leave both its branch and tmux process behind, so recovery must reconcile all three states independently.

## Follow-ups

None.

## Test Plan

From the repository root:

```console
$ cargo test
running 24 tests
test result: ok. 24 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.23s

$ cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 0.25s

$ cargo build
Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 0.55s

$ git diff --check
```

MANUAL — fresh creation with a tmux server whose original working directory was deleted:

1. Run:

```sh
set -e
test_root=$(mktemp -d /private/tmp/muxai-v060-stale-server.XXXXXX)
mkdir "$test_root/old" "$test_root/home"
git init -q "$test_root/repo"
git -C "$test_root/repo" config user.email test@example.com
git -C "$test_root/repo" config user.name Test
git -C "$test_root/repo" commit -q --allow-empty -m initial
cd "$test_root/old"
TMUX_TMPDIR="$test_root" tmux -L muxai new-session -d -s sentinel
cd "$test_root/repo"
rmdir "$test_root/old"
HOME="$test_root/home" TMUX_TMPDIR="$test_root" target/debug/muxai new alpha --repo "$test_root/repo" -- /bin/sh -c false
TMUX_TMPDIR="$test_root" tmux -L muxai show-environment -g | rg '^PWD='
TMUX_TMPDIR="$test_root" tmux -L muxai list-sessions -F '#{session_name} | #{session_path} | #{pane_current_path} | #{pane_current_command}'
test -d "$test_root/repo/.muxai/worktrees/alpha"
printf 'worktree_exists=yes\n'
```

2. Captured output:

```text
created session 'alpha' running '/bin/sh -c false' in /private/tmp/muxai-v060-stale-server.oLKlKv/repo/.muxai/worktrees/alpha (branch 'alpha')
  attach: muxai   (then select it and press Enter)
PWD=/private/tmp/muxai-v060-stale-server.oLKlKv/old
alpha | /private/tmp/muxai-v060-stale-server.oLKlKv/repo/.muxai/worktrees/alpha | /private/tmp/muxai-v060-stale-server.oLKlKv/repo/.muxai/worktrees/alpha | zsh
sentinel | /private/tmp/muxai-v060-stale-server.oLKlKv/old | /private/tmp/muxai-v060-stale-server.oLKlKv/old | zsh
worktree_exists=yes
```

body:
## Resumen
Slice de cimientos del Sprint 16 (la parte de Dev A, ADR-082). **No incluye la API**: CRUD, Kanban, importación y `POST /capture/{token}` quedan para Dev B (matriz del Sprint 16 añadida a `METHODOLOGY.md`).

- **Migración 025:** `leads`, `lead_pipeline_stages` y `lead_sources` con RLS forzada; `clients.icp_config` y `lead_scoring_weights`; `contacts.lead_id` e `is_lead`; función `capture_lookup_source()` (SECURITY DEFINER) para la captura pública sin tenant.
- **Modelos y schemas** de leads, etapas y fuentes.
- **Servicios base:** `compute_total_score` (pesos por tenant), `ensure_default_stages` (11 etapas, idempotente y seguro con concurrencia), token de captura.

## Desviaciones del spec (justificadas en ADR-082)
- `email` y `phone` **cifrados** con índice ciego por tenant (CLAUDE.md exige cifrar emails y teléfonos); deduplicación entre leads no borrados.
- `total_score` es columna normal, no `GENERATED`: el spec lo fijaba a 40/30/30 y a la vez lo hacía configurable por tenant.
- Sin ENUM de PostgreSQL, sin `leads_count`, y `UNIQUE (client_id, position)` diferible para poder reordenar etapas.
- El token de captura no se guarda: solo su SHA-256.

## Pruebas
- Integración + e2e completos con Postgres/Redis reales: verdes. 42 tests nuevos (aislamiento RLS incluido `WITH CHECK`, cifrado, deduplicación y soft delete, CHECK, reordenar etapas, `ON DELETE SET NULL`, etapas por defecto concurrentes, función de captura con el rol sujeto a RLS).
- 74 tests unitarios nuevos. `alembic check` sin drift; downgrade/upgrade de la 025 sin errores. `ruff` y `bandit` limpios; `mypy`: mismos 9 errores previos.
- Mutación comprobada: sin recalcular `email_hash` fallan la deduplicación y el cambio de email.
- Unit: solo fallan los 3 tests de `tiktoken` (sin red en el entorno).
- El test del reset del sandbox falló al añadir las tablas, como debe; decisión: no se clonan ni se purgan.

## Pendiente antes de exponer la API (Dev B)
1. **RGPD:** exportar y anonimizar los leads vinculados a un contacto (guardan email y teléfono).
2. Las FK no garantizan el mismo tenant: resolver etapa, fuente y usuario dentro de `tenant_session()`.
3. `lead_activities` (#30) no está en este slice.
4. Revisar el sandbox en los Sprints 17-18 si un agente crea leads desde una conversación.
