author: joker66613
body:
Przywraca miazmę, gnicie zwłok i gibsów oraz kwiat trupi, usunięte w https://github.com/BeeStation/BeeStation-Hornet/pull/6445 z powodu lagów. Usunięcie było uzasadnione, ale problemem nie był sam gaz, tylko sposób jego emisji. Ta wersja przepisuje mechanizm emisji.

## Co robi
- Gaz `miasma`: alarmy powietrza, kanister, scrubbery filtrują go domyślnie, reakcja sterylizacji suchym gorącem (miazma → tlen, punkty badań)
- Gniją zwłoki (po 2 min od śmierci, nie w trumnie, worku na zwłoki ani kostnicy, nie z formaldehydem, nie spalone ani zamrożone) i gibsy
- Kwiat trupi: mutacja ostu, wydziela miazmę po dojrzeniu
- Oddychanie miazmą: zapach, moodlety, wymioty, wstręt, czasem losowa choroba

## Optymalizacja względem BeeStation
- Jeden subsystem `SSmiasma` (w tle, co 10 s) zamiast komponentu `rot` na każdym obiekcie (co 1 s)
- Emisja sumowana per kafelek i dodawana jednym `adjust_moles_temp` do powietrza: bez tymczasowych `gas_mixture` i bez `ImmediateCalculateAdjacentTurfs()` przy każdej emisji
- Limit 20 moli na kafelek oraz skończone pule: zwłoki 20 min, gibsy 10 min
- Zwłoki rejestrowane w `death()` zamiast `LoadComponent` w każdym ticku `Life()`
- Oddech obsługiwany tylko w płucach, moodlet czyszczony raz zamiast sygnału przy każdym oddechu
- Mniej opłacalne farmienie: eksport 2 kr/mol (było 10), badania 10 pkt/mol (było 40)

## Różnice względem oryginału
- Emagowany atmosbot nadal wypuszcza CO2, artefakty nie produkują miazmy (oba byłyby źródłami bez limitu)
- Płuca nie usuwają miazmy z oddechu (w oryginale linia odejmowała przez pomyłkę ciśnienie stimulum)
- Miazmę obsługują tylko płuca człowieka (oryginał miał też drugą ścieżkę w `carbon/life.dm`)

## Wydajność
Benchmark w pokoju testowym, na tych samych gibsach, z kodem komponentu `rot` z BeeStation przepisanym 1:1:

| Źródła | BeeStation | Ta wersja |
|---|---|---|
| 100 | 6,3 ms CPU / s gry | 0,024 ms / s (~260× mniej) |
| 500 | 79 ms / s | 0,086 ms / s (~900× mniej) |
| 1 oddech | 3,8 µs | 0,9 µs |

Nie zmierzono pracy auxmos przy rozprzestrzenianiu gazu. Zależy ona od ilości miazmy w powietrzu, którą tu ogranicza limit na kafelek, pule źródeł i scrubbery.

## Testy
- Kompiluje się (0 błędów, 0 ostrzeżeń)
- Nowy test `/datum/unit_test/miasma` (rejestracja gazu w auxmos, gnicie i formaldehyd, wskrzeszenie, usuwanie, gibsy, limit na kafelek, sterylizacja): wszystkie asercje przechodzą. Test oznacza FAIL tylko przez runtime `movable_moved overridden` z organu `butt`, który naprawia https://github.com/aq33/NSV13/pull/333
- W pełnym przebiegu `create_and_destroy` i `subsystem_metric_sanity` przechodzą
- Nie testowane w prawdziwej rundzie

Zmiany w rdzeniu są oznaczone `// AQ EDIT - Miasma` i opisane w `aquila/LEGACY_OVERRIDES.md`.

:cl:
rscadd: Wraca miazma: zwłoki i gibsy gniją, kwiat trupi wydziela smród
balance: Miazma jest wyraźnie mniej opłacalna przy eksporcie i do badań
code: Nowy, dużo lżejszy system emisji miazmy (SSmiasma)
/:cl:

<!-- GitHub Copilot コードレビューへの指示: このプルリクエストは日本語でレビューすること。 -->

## 概要
サイトマップを Next.js 標準の `app/sitemap.ts` に移し、`lastmod` に正しい値だけを出すようにします。

これまでは、更新していない固定ページにもアクセスのたびに「今日」の日付が入っていました。間違った `lastmod` が続くと、検索エンジンがサイト全体の `lastmod` を信用しなくなります。

> [!NOTE]
> `chrom/breadcrumb-from-nav`（#148）から派生しています。前の PR のマージ後にベースを変更してください。

## 関連するIssue
- Closes #155

## 主な変更内容
- [x] `app/sitemap.ts`（新規）：`MetadataRoute.Sitemap` を返す。`app/sitemap.xml/route.ts` は削除
- [x] `lastModified` は次のとおり
  - 記事：frontmatter の `date`
  - `/`・`/news`：最新の記事の公開日（記事の一覧を表示しているページのため）
  - その他の固定ページ：**付けない**（Issue の提案のうち「付けない」を採用。git の最終更新日を使う案は、CI の shallow clone や Cloudflare のビルド環境で履歴が取れず、かえって不正確になるおそれがあるため見送り）
- [x] `changefreq`・`priority` は Google が使っていないため出力しない。これに伴い、使われていなかった `NavItem` の `accent` も削除
- [x] `NAV_LINKS` の子ページを再帰的に集める

## 影響範囲
- `/sitemap.xml` の内容（URL は同じ。`public/robots.txt` の `Sitemap:` もそのまま使える）

## 動作確認手順
1. `npm run format:check` / `npm run lint -- --max-warnings 0` / `npm run typecheck` / `npm run build`：通過
2. ビルド結果で `/sitemap.xml` が静的に生成され（`○ /sitemap.xml`）、URL が 22 件（固定ページ 10・記事 12）、`/` に最新記事の日付（2026-09-19）、`/about` などには `lastmod` がないことを確認

## スクリーンショット（UI変更がある場合）
UI の変更はありません。

## レビュアーに確認してほしいこと・特記事項
- 以前は `Cache-Control: s-maxage=3600` を付けていましたが、ビルド時に静的生成されるようになるため不要になりました

author: rans0r
body:
## What was wrong

A picture pasted on a phone and then removed from a desktop stayed on the phone. Every later sync left it there. The two other desktops let it go at once.

On Google Drive and OneDrive, a change's path comes from the tree the adapter builds from the change feed. An item this device uploaded is not in that tree until the feed reports it back. In this case the item was removed on another device before the phone's next pull, so the feed reported it once, already trashed: an id with no path.

`clipboardIn` in the engine flags the clipboard only for a path inside `.clipboard/`. So the pull did not flag it, and the cursor moved past the only change that would ever name the item. Nothing listed the folder again until the next clipboard change or a reload.

## What changes

A deletion that arrives with an id alone now counts as possibly the clipboard's. The cost is one listing, only where the clipboard is shown. The same applies to the rare note or file deleted this way.

`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §7, "The clipboard", is amended to match.

## Tests

- A Drive replay over the stub, in `gdrive.test.ts`. The device uploads an item, a second adapter trashes it, and the first device pulls. It checks that the feed's only entry is `{ deleted: true, remoteId }` and that the pull flags the clipboard.
- An engine test with a deletion by id alone.

Both tests failed before the fix. `pnpm verify` passes: core 7291, api 367, web 3271.

## Dependencies

No dependencies added.

Changeset: `@skysa/core` patch.

body:
Share SDK v2 elicitation requests, schemas, responses, scopes, IDs, and errors through the existing owners, UI, and native producers. Keep production ACP traffic and capability advertisement v1 with explicit adapters. Based on main with #65235 merged.

- Preserve every runtime SDK schema field, ordered choices/items/required names, constraints/defaults, optional versus empty values, nested metadata, opaque IDs, and raw `Other` payloads.
- Convert decoded v1 requests once; lower v2 responses inside the existing RPC cancellation boundary; retain v1 error code/message/data. No production serde bridge, schema normalization, or wire-parsing shim.
- Preserve existing scoping, local request identity, weak owners, settlement/events, HTTP(S)/host validation, consent-before-completion, and stale-submission guards. Unsupported modes still reject before pending insertion.
- Keep unknown string formats as annotations without bypassing known patterns, inferring URLs, or adding controls. UI projection/submission does not modify the canonical request.
- Native producers build v2 directly and wrap legacy session/tool ID Arc payloads without normalization. Preserve `ask_user` answer precedence and error/cancel handling; unrelated tool APIs stay v1.
- Unknown actions remain `Other` on wire and retain the existing local canceled fallback, never acceptance.

## Review guide

- [explicit adapters](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/7901b34731332cc102a3629707214f92abd6582b/crates/acp_thread/src/elicitation.rs#L5); [canonical store](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/7901b34731332cc102a3629707214f92abd6582b/crates/acp_thread/src/acp_thread.rs#L527).
- [v1 wire boundary](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/7901b34731332cc102a3629707214f92abd6582b/crates/agent_servers/src/acp.rs#L6512): genuine v1 requests/responders, lowering inside `run_until_cancelled`, exact local-entry cleanup.
- [native producer](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/7901b34731332cc102a3629707214f92abd6582b/crates/agent/src/thread.rs#L6535): direct v2 values and opaque-ID conversion.
- [borrowed format helpers](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/7901b34731332cc102a3629707214f92abd6582b/crates/agent_ui/src/conversation_view/elicitation.rs#L1723); [canonical request/form regression](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/7901b34731332cc102a3629707214f92abd6582b/crates/agent_ui/src/conversation_view/elicitation.rs#L977): unknown annotations, known validation, nested metadata, snapshots, exact answers, unchanged canonical requests.
- [actual SDK auth-time regression](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/7901b34731332cc102a3629707214f92abd6582b/crates/agent_servers/src/acp.rs#L3238): complete decoded v1 input matches canonical v2 state; response metadata/content are checked over real SDK v1 traffic.

author: lagentcooper
body:
## Quoi et pourquoi

Veille vise le **testament écrit à la main (olographe)**, qui n'exige pas de notaire. Les textes laissaient entendre le contraire (« le notaire doit… », « vous devez voir un notaire »).

- **Encart du hub** : nouvelle partie « Les formes de testament », courte et en langage courant :
  - écrit à la main (olographe, celui de Veille) : pas besoin de notaire, gratuit, même valeur s'il est écrit en entier de sa main, daté et signé. Points faibles : perte, destruction, mauvaise rédaction, contestation plus facile ;
  - authentique (chez le notaire) : sous dictée, devant un second notaire ou deux témoins, conservé, très difficile à contester, payant ;
  - mystique (rare) : remis fermé à un notaire devant deux témoins, contenu secret.
  - Le notaire reste **facultatif** pour l'olographe : relecture, conservation, inscription au fichier central.
- **Avertissement permanent** : « Un notaire n'est pas obligatoire pour un testament écrit à la main, mais le faire relire est une bonne précaution. »
- **Mode d'emploi, dernière étape, synthèse** : le notaire est « conseillé », pas obligatoire.
- **Cas bloquants** : « Un notaire doit… » devient « Faites-vous accompagner par un notaire ». C'est une limite de Veille (« Veille ne peut pas vous guider seule »), pas une obligation légale. Le comportement du produit ne change pas : 🛑 bloque toujours la synthèse et le PDF.

## Session / domaine

Web. Textes (`will-fr.ts`) et l'encart `Explainer.tsx`. Domaine inchangé.

## Preuve d'exécution

```
pnpm format:check / lint / typecheck → verts
pnpm --filter @veille/web test → 12 fichiers, 144 passed
pnpm --filter @veille/web test:e2e e2e/will.spec.ts → 16 passed
```
Tests ajoutés :
- le texte de l'olographe dit « pas besoin de notaire » ;
- aucun texte ne présente le notaire comme obligatoire ;
- E2E sur l'encart et l'avertissement permanent.

J'ai relancé uniquement `will.spec.ts`, pas `shell.spec.ts` : cette PR ne touche pas ses écrans.

## ⚖️ Points juridiques

À faire relire par un juriste avant tout usage réel (`will.explainer.forms.*`) :
- « même valeur qu'un testament fait chez un notaire » (valeur légale de la forme olographe) ;
- description des formes authentique et mystique ;
- « notaire facultatif » en présence d'un cas 🛑 : le texte dit seulement que Veille ne peut pas guider seule.

## Definition of Done

- [x] Code, tests, documentation (`progress.md`)
- [x] Aucun secret, aucune dépendance, aucune PII

body:
## 🗒️ Summary
In the diff branch of `KernelList.validate()`, `fromfile = kernel_lists[-1]` ran before the `try`, so an empty release-list glob raised an uncaught `IndexError` that the neighbouring `except` could not catch. The block now checks for an empty `kernel_lists` first and logs `-- Current list not available.`, since in that case it is the current list that is missing. A single-entry `kernel_lists` still logs `-- Previous list not available.`, and behavior with two or more lists is unchanged. The two TODOs that described this bug (in `list.py` and in the previous-list-unavailable test) are removed.

Adds `test_validate_diff_current_list_unavailable`, which mocks `glob.glob` to return an empty list. The mock is needed because `validate()` opens the current list near the top, so a really missing file fails before ever reaching the diff block.

body:
Merge after the foundation PR (https://github.com/Avunu/docusystem/pull/1). This branch is based on `feat/foundation` (`afdbedc`); once that merges, retarget the base to `main`.

## What it delivers (WP7, site assets)

Everything WP7 owns in section 11 of the decision record: `site/**` except `site/data/**` (WP1), and `test/site/**`. Nothing else is touched.

**`site/`** (31 files, 291 kB unpacked and about 142 kB gzipped; no new dependency):

- `public/`: Figtree and JetBrains Mono (6 `.woff2`) with their OFL texts, the two Avunu marks, `favicon.svg`, `favicon.ico`, `.nojekyll`. No `CNAME` (generated).

They are the starter template at Avunu/docs commit `1820d01` (the commit the three pilots copied) with exactly the four changes of section 10.3 and nothing else: (1) the resolved config is `docusystem.config.json` (layout id, descriptions, `project.base.json` config source), (2) the edit-this-page URL reads `docsPath` from the config instead of the literal `docs`, (3) the docs-enhance 1px fix (`scrollWidth > clientWidth`), (4) `public/CNAME` is not shipped. **`test/site/`** (102 tests run, 9 skipped until neighbours merge; about 1.6 s including two real Jx builds):

| `rules.test.ts`, `contrast.test.ts` | agreement of WP3's route rules and nav with `project.base.json` and of WP4's contrast gate with the shipped tokens; skipped while those modules are the WP0 stubs (see below). |

## How each acceptance item was verified

All commands in `/home/batonac/Development/docusystem-wt/wp7` (Node 26.10.0; CI will use 24).

1. **`npm ci --ignore-scripts && npm run check`** is green: format check, lint, `tsc --noEmit`, and vitest: 14 files passed, 1 skipped; 235 tests passed, 9 skipped (133 of the foundation plus 102 of this package). Each of the five commits was also checked out on its own and passed the same gate. `npm run build` and `npm pack --dry-run` runs.

body:
### Summary

Publishing Rust crates with `rust-cd.yml` required a separate `AWS_ACTIONS` approval for every crate, because each crate had its own publish job in that environment. Approval was also requested for crates whose version was already on crates.io. This PR publishes all crates from a single job, so a publish run requires a single approval.

### Issue link

Part of #6906

### Features / Behaviour Changes

- A `publish=true` run requires exactly one `AWS_ACTIONS` approval, instead of one per crate.
- No crate is published until the tests of all crates pass. Previously, each crate waited only for its own tests and its dependencies' publish jobs.
- `publish=false` (dry run) behaviour is unchanged and requires no approval.

### Implementation

- `rust-cd.yml`:
  - Replaced the four `publish-*` jobs with a single `publish-crates` job.
  - `publish-crates` uses the `AWS_ACTIONS` environment when publishing.
  - Each step still checks crates.io and skips crate versions that are already published.
  - `publish-crates` sets `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` so each crate's `cargo publish` verification build reuses dependencies already compiled for earlier crates.
- `publish-rust-crate/action.yml`: removed the unused `name`, `version`, and `needs-publish` outputs.
- The workflow file name and environment are unchanged, so existing crates.io trusted publisher configurations still match.

### Limitations

- A dry run fails for any crate that depends on a version of another GLIDE crate that is not yet published to crates.io, and later crates are then not checked. This was already the case before this PR, and is documented in a comment on the `publish` input.

### Testing

- `actionlint` and `prettier --check` pass on the changed files.
- Ran the crates.io check script locally against all four crates and confirmed the expected published/unpublished results.
- Ran `cargo publish --dry-run` locally for `glide-logger` and then `glide-telemetry` with a shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`; both succeeded.
- Not yet run on GitHub Actions. To verify, run the workflow from this branch with `publish=false`.

### Checklist

Before submitting the PR make sure the following are checked:

author: erwinkn
body:
A fresh Workers deployment now redeploys itself on every push to `main`, wired by `coffre setup` with no dashboard steps beyond, at most, one pre-filled token form.

## What changes

**`coffre init --workers` writes `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`** (in `examples/workers`, so the init diff test and `test:consumer` cover it). It is shaped like erwinkn/secrets#2: push to main plus `workflow_dispatch`; `actions/checkout` and `actions/setup-node` pinned by the same SHAs as `validate.yml`; Node 24; `corepack enable && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`; `printenv DATABASE_OWNER_URL | pnpm exec coffre migrate --yes`, with the URL in that step's `env` alone; then `pnpm run deploy`. It uses `concurrency: { group: deploy, cancel-in-progress: false }` and `permissions: contents: read`. A new test in `init.test.ts` checks the pins against `validate.yml` and checks the rest of that shape.

**`coffre setup`**, when the deployment's `origin` is on the GitHub its sign-in uses, adds a step after the app deploys: *Have owner/repo deploy on every push*.

1. **GitHub sign-in.** Setup uses `gh auth token --hostname <host>` when gh is signed in there and may read the repo's secrets. Otherwise it asks whether to set the secrets now. *Yes* prints GitHub's pre-filled form for a fine-grained token with `secrets=write`, `target_name=<owner>` and `expires_in=1`, then takes the token at a hidden paste prompt and checks it against the repo's public-key endpoint. *Not now* skips the step.
2. **The Cloudflare token**, made only when the repo has no `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` or `--rotate-deploy-token` is given. Setup first asks Cloudflare's API to create `coffre deploys: owner/repo` (`GET /user/tokens/permission_groups`, then `POST /user/tokens`). It gets *Workers Scripts Write*, *Account Settings Read*, *Workers KV Storage Write* and *Hyperdrive Read* on the account, plus *Workers Routes Write* on the zone coffre is served through: the custom domain's zone, the SaaS zone, or no zone on workers.dev. **wrangler's OAuth login has no token-management scope** (wrangler 4.142's `DefaultScopes`), so this only succeeds when `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` is set to a token with API Tokens Edit. When Cloudflare refuses, setup says so and lists the exact permissions. It prints the dashboard's token-template URL (`permissionGroupKeys`, plus the name) and takes the pasted token only after reading one endpoint per permission. If one is missing, it names it, e.g. "that token lacks Hyperdrive Read, which the deploy needs".
3. **The secrets.** `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` (when made), `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` and `DATABASE_OWNER_URL` are each sealed to the repo's public key with libsodium's sealed-box format and `PUT` through GitHub's API. No value is printed, logged or written. Each one goes into setup's redaction list.
4. A deployment without the workflow file gets it, to commit.

On a rerun, setup keeps the token and sets the other two again. `--rotate-deploy-token` makes a new token. Setup then deletes the same-named old token when its login may, and otherwise says to delete it on the dashboard.

**Without a GitHub remote**, setup adds no step. The summary's *Deploys* row says how to wire it later: push with the workflow and rerun setup, or set the three secrets by hand, or use Workers Builds.

**Docs.** `docs/deploy.md` has a new section, *Deploys on every push*, first under *On Workers*. *Workers Builds* follows as the alternative, with a note to delete the workflow if you switch. The *Setup does Cloudflare too* list, the upgrade steps, both READMEs and the CHANGELOG are updated too.

## Choices, and alternatives not taken

- **The sealed box is hand-written** in `packages/cli/src/sealed-box.ts`, about 150 lines. It uses Node's X25519, with XSalsa20-Poly1305 and BLAKE2b-24 written from their specs. Node lacks XSalsa20, Poly1305 and variable-length BLAKE2b, and the CLI bundles every runtime dependency. Bundling libsodium-wrappers (wasm) or tweetnacl plus blakejs would add a lot for one call. `libsodium-wrappers` is a **test-only devDependency**: `sealed-box.test.ts` opens our output with `crypto_box_seal_open` at 12 lengths around block boundaries and compares BLAKE2b with libsodium. It also checks the RFC 7693 vector. The fake GitHub opens every uploaded secret with libsodium, as GitHub does. (D74)
- **No device flow.** It needs an OAuth app client ID that coffre owns, and borrowing gh's would be impersonation. setup uses gh's token, else a one-day fine-grained token made for the run. Registering a coffre OAuth app would make device flow possible later. (D75)
- **The dashboard form uses `accountId=*&zoneId=all`**, the only documented values. The person narrows the account and zone on the form, and setup says so. The pasted-token check catches a silently dropped template key (Cloudflare documents that wrong keys are ignored). `hyperdrive` as a template key is my best inference and isn't documented. The check would catch it if the form dropped it.
- **The step runs after the app deploys and before the wait for DNS or `/livez`**, so Ctrl-C during the SaaS wait doesn't skip it, and a GitHub hiccup can't block the first deploy.
- **Rotation is a flag** (`--rotate-deploy-token`), like `--reset-passwords`, not a question on every rerun.

## Verification

- `pnpm build`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm check:pins`, `pnpm check:docs`
- `pnpm test`: 1135 pass, 0 fail
- `pnpm test:schema`, including `scripts/test-setup.sh`: 35 pass. That includes a new end-to-end setup run in a git repo, where the OAuth login is refused, a token is pasted and checked, and the three secrets are set through gh and opened. The *everything done* run now asserts the no-remote message.
- `pnpm test:consumer`: passed for both kinds, with the packed CLI's `init` writing the workflow.
- New unit suites: `deploy-on-push.test.ts` (remote parsing, the forms, the manual path with refusals, the API path's exact policies, keep and rotate, *Not now*) and `sealed-box.test.ts`.

Nothing was run against a real Cloudflare or GitHub account.

## Open points

- `docs/architecture.md` (*Expand, then contract*) still says "with Workers Builds, each Worker's build does". That file was outside this task's scope.
- `coffre update` doesn't add the workflow to existing deployments. setup writes it when missing.

author: jakeomega
body:
Draft. Adds five barracks training methods to vanilla's main group (`pmg_training`), from the design discussion. Nothing here is play-tested.

## The methods

| Method | Unlock | Training/level | Officers | Other effects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Officer Academies | Combined Arms (era 6) | 26 | 30% | Counts toward **Academy Officer Corps**: Armed Forces +20% political strength, +10% attraction, scaled by the share of regular battalions trained this way |
| Expeditionary Logistics | Predictive Logistics (era 8) | 10 | 15% | `building_mobilization_cost_mult` −0.1: the +100% goods surcharge while mobilized becomes +90%. For a short war you're winning, not a slugfest |
| Neural Grafting | Bioenhanced Soldiers (era 11) + Regulated Augmentation Market / Unrestricted / Mandatory Augmentation | 120 | 20% | Buys 8 Drugs (`opium`) + 4 Electronic Components per staffed level; servicemen mortality +25% |
| Reserve Cadre | National Militia or Mass Conscription | 12 | 20% | 2 **Reserve Battalions** per staffed level; each lets the state raise one more conscript battalion |
| Political Commissars | Single-Party State or Council Republic (hidden otherwise) | 20 | 5% | Counts toward **Commissar Indoctrination**: +15% attraction to the IGs in government, scaled by share. The count type carries an AI weight (below) |

For reference, vanilla's ladder runs 8 → 24 per level (Mobile Warfare Tactics, 25% officers). Every method keeps vanilla's unscaled +50 and the Warrior Caste lock. The group's `ai_selection = most_productive` means the AI takes the highest training rate. So AI armies move to Officer Academies and then Neural Grafting. Expeditionary Logistics and Reserve Cadre are player choices.

**Steering the AI to Commissars.** `building_training_rate_add` carries `game_data = { ai_value = 100 }` in vanilla, and nothing else on a barracks method has one. So the AI evidently scores a barracks method by its modifiers' ai_values. `country_commissar_battalions_add` now carries `ai_value = 5000` (about 50 training points a level). Barracks make no goods, so if the mod's stickiness applies, every switch counts as a downgrade and needs ×1.67 (`PRODUCTION_METHOD_STICKINESS_DOWNGRADE` 0.6). On that model a single-party AI moves from Officer Academies to Commissars on barracks of 2+ levels (×1.86 at level 2), and from Commissars to Neural Grafting only on barracks of 11+ levels. No `is_ai` script.

## How the national and state effects work

You asked for a state-scoped Armed Forces modifier. The engine has none: `interest_group_ig_armed_forces_*` and `country_officers_pol_str_mult` exist only at country/IG scope. A PM's `country_modifiers` would stack once per barracks, so this uses the pattern you asked for on Reserve Cadre throughout:

- Three new modifier types (`barracks_training_modifier_types.txt`) hold **counts**, declared `workforce_scaled` by the PMs: `state_reserve_battalions_add` (2/level), `country_academy_trained_battalions_add` (1/level), `country_commissar_battalions_add` (1/level). They show in the tooltip with a per-source breakdown, and any other content can declare them.
- Two monthly pulses turn the counts into static modifiers (`barracks_training_effects.txt`, one refresh site each, through never-removed variables):
  - country: share = count ÷ `army_size` (max 1) → `te_officer_academies_standing` / `te_political_commissars_indoctrination`
  - state: conscription rate = reserve × 1000 ÷ state population (max 0.25) → `te_reserve_cadre_conscription`, plus +1 conscription-center max level per reserve battalion → `te_reserve_cadre_capacity`, so a reserve still counts in a state already at the Army Model's cap of 100.
- New concept: `concept_reserve_battalions`.

This is more machinery than the in-chat sketch had (two pulses, four static modifiers, three types). Reserve Cadre needed it to be population-independent: a per-level conscription rate is worth ten times more in a dense state, and with the mod's tech barracks-cap increases, National Militia's 5-per-state cap doesn't bound it.

## Owner calls

1. **The AI loses Academy Officer Corps at era 11.** It moves to Neural Grafting (highest training). Option: let Neural Grafting also declare `country_academy_trained_battalions_add`.
2. **Commissars' AI weight (5000 a level)** and whether the late-game single-party AI should hold Commissars over Neural Grafting (it currently gives way on large barracks). Also: should Commissars carry an explicit Armed Forces penalty? Currently the fewer officers are the only one.
3. **Academy Officer Corps magnitudes:** +20% strength / +10% attraction at full share (vanilla grants run +10% Prussian education to +50% age of caudillos). Commissar Indoctrination +15% (Single-Party State itself is +20%).
4. **Reserve Cadre:** 2 reserve battalions per level (a 1:2 standing-to-reserve ratio; historical reserve systems run 1:3–1:5), the 0.25 rate cap, and the law gate (militia + mass conscription).
5. **Expeditionary Logistics gate:** Predictive Logistics (era 8, its description is about cheaper logistics) vs Rapid Deployment Forces (era 9, matches the name).
6. **Neural Grafting cost:** goods ~£720/level/week at base prices is a first estimate (mortality +25% and training 120 are your numbers).
7. **Officer Academies gate:** Combined Arms (era 6) fills the era 6–7 gap after Mobile Armor.
8. **Expeditionary Logistics' −10% is `unscaled`.** It has to be: a level-scaled building multiplier would multiply by level. A level-1 barracks gets the full cut, but at −10% on one battalion's mobilized surcharge there's little to farm.

## In-game checks

1. Conscription centers: in a Reserve Cadre state, the max conscription-center level rises by about the reserve count. If it rises by about half, the engine sizes conscription from workforce, not population (the define and the modifier text disagree), and the 1000 needs doubling.
2. A Neural Grafting barracks buys its Drugs and Electronic Components. Barracks are proven to *produce* goods (Engineering & Logistics) but no vanilla army method consumes any.
3. `building_soldiers_mortality_mult` shows in the servicemen pop's mortality tooltip. No vanilla or mod content uses it yet.
4. The three counts render in the barracks/method tooltip and in the country and state modifier lists.
5. Academy Officer Corps / Commissar Indoctrination appear after the first monthly tick, at a sensible share, and drop a month after switching every barracks away. `army_size` is the denominator, so check the share against the barracks level total.
6. A mobilized Expeditionary Logistics barracks shows the reduced goods surcharge (goods input +90% instead of +100% while mobilized).
7. The AI moves to Officer Academies once it has Combined Arms, and a Single-Party State / Council Republic AI moves to Political Commissars. If the AI stays put on existing barracks, the stickiness model above applies to them, and Mobile Warfare → Academies (×1.08) never clears it. In that case only newly built or expanded barracks pick up the new methods, as with vanilla's own small ladder steps.
8. Switching method on a staffed barracks: how the officer/servicemen reshuffle plays out (Commissars at 5% officers, Academies at 30%). The "slower method in peace, switch back before a war" framing depends on switching being cheap.

## Checks run (sparse worktree)

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s . -p 'test_*.py'`: 5112 tests OK (15 skipped)
- `ruff check .`, `compileall`, `format_paradox_tabs.py --check`, `check_localization_files.py`, `organize_loc.py --check`: clean
- All CI `--strict` audits pass, plus `loc_coverage`, `pm_employment`, `concept_reference`, `modifier_visibility` and `effect_trigger_validity`. One exception: `gui_reference_audit --strict` fails with the same 131 errors on unmodified `main` on this machine (GUI files this branch doesn't touch).
- `build_player_guide.py --check`: up to date

author: 99linesofcode
body:
## What

The skeleton's eslint config now enforces the module matrix for real: modules consume the shared kernel and never each other, the kernel imports from no one, and every `src/` file must declare its place from the first commit.

## Why

The boundary config looked complete but enforced nothing — a bite test (module importing module, the exact forbidden edge) passed lint clean. Two defects hid behind the green checkmark: the config used `boundaries/element-types`, a rule name the installed plugin v7 deprecated (parses, silently does nothing), and the plugin delegates import resolution to `eslint-import-resolver-typescript`, which wasn't installed — so every intra-src import resolved to "unknown" and no policy ever evaluated.

## Behavior

- `boundaries/dependencies` (the v7 rule) with the element matrix: entry → module + shared; module → shared; shared → nothing (custom message).
- `eslint-import-resolver-typescript` wired via `import/resolver` so intra-src imports resolve and the policies fire.
- `pnpm-workspace.yaml` carries the `allowBuilds` verdict for the resolver's native build script (`unrs-resolver`) — without it pnpm v11 exits non-zero and CI installs break.
- `no-unknown-files` stays armed: any `src/` file outside the three element patterns fails lint.

## Done when

- [x] Bite matrix: module→module fires; shared→module fires with the kernel message; entry→module and module→shared pass
- [x] `pnpm lint` and `pnpm typecheck` green (exit 0) inside the devshell
- [x] `pnpm install` exits 0 (build-script verdict in place)

author: ippitenin
body:
Баг нашёлся попутно, во время замера Nemotron: архив звука в библиотеке называется `audio.m4a`, а внутри у него контейнер CAF.

## Что было не так
Архив писался во временный файл `audio.m4a.part`, а `AVAudioFile` выбирает контейнер **по расширению**: на незнакомое `.part` система выбирала CAF. Потом файл переименовывался в `audio.m4a`. Плеер такой файл играл, а `AVURLAsset` (наш `AudioFileDecoder`) — нет. Отсюда:
- **«Повторить» из архива** (исходник перенесён или удалён) → «В файле нет звуковой дорожки»;
- **«Распознать заново»** без исходника — то же;
- загрузка архива на сетевой сервис уходила бы CAF под видом m4a.

У тебя так записаны обе записи библиотеки (`afinfo` → `File type ID: caff`). Тест архиватора писал сразу в `test.m4a`, поэтому ловушку не видел.

## Исправление
- Временное имя — `audio.part.m4a`: расширение `.m4a`, контейнер настоящий M4A.
- Старые архивы один раз на старте перепаковываются в M4A **без перекодирования** — AAC тот же, качество не теряется (`repairLegacyArchives` → `SourceAudioArchiver.remuxCAF`). Идут задачами стора по одной записи: удаление записи или «Стереть аудио» перепаковку отменяют, перенос «Папки данных» её дожидается. Фиксация — тем же `commitAudio`: только если запись ещё на месте.
- Огрызки старого имени подчищает sweep.

Перепаковка проверена на копии твоего архива: `m4af`, тот же AAC, размер 1,52 → 1,53 МБ.

## Проверка
- `swift test` — 872 + 5 живых пропущенных. Новые: `testLibraryPartNameProducesM4AContainer`, `testRemuxCAFMakesLegacyArchiveReadable`, `testRepairLegacyArchivesRemuxesCAFOnly`. Мутация (вернуть старое имя `.part`) роняет 3 теста.
- Релизную сборку этой ветки отдельно не ставил — соберу общую вместе с остальными PR.

## Ручной smoke
- [ ] После запуска новой версии: `afinfo ~/Library/Application\ Support/DOKA/transcripts/*/audio.m4a | grep "File type"` → `m4af` у обеих записей.
- [ ] Плеер записи играет как раньше.
- [ ] Новая транскрибация файла → архив `m4af`.
- [ ] Перенести исходный файл → «Повторить» распознаёт по архиву.

WISLIP: не задет.

body:
## 概要
- 遺族年金シミュレーター（`pages/nenshu-hub.html` / `js/izoku-nenkin.js`）のFAQ・ディスクレーマーに自己申告されていた未対応事項「夫が遺族厚生年金を受け取る場合に適用される年齢要件」を実装した。
- 妻の死亡時点で**55歳未満の夫**には遺族厚生年金の受給権自体が発生しないため、試算を0円にして注記を表示する。
- **55歳以上60歳未満の夫**は、遺族基礎年金の対象となる子がいない場合、原則**60歳まで支給停止**となる旨を注記で表示する（金額は60歳から受け取れる見込み額としてそのまま表示）。
- 遺族基礎年金の対象となる子がいる場合はこの支給停止の例外となり、55歳以上であれば60歳前でも全額を受け取れる（既存ロジックの`childCount`をそのまま利用）。

Automatic subscription maintenance now has a dormant composition inside the actual RuntimeServer, ProductionNativeOwner and existing batch supervisor. It reuses one coordinator, global batch registry, supervised worker slot, shared four-fetch pool, planner, preference, durable attempt journal and typed completion receipts. Default remains Off. Normal startup—including a binary compiled with the non-default `developer-subscription-schedule` feature—registers no new timer, worker or method.

Stacked only on #332 at `696a46982e9fd1f6287dc4005bc4097800de4dab`. Exact reviewed and tested head: `b8375c505a71e06b969d3e83527922602573c530`. The earlier owner/driver and test-allocator checkpoints remain preserved. Execution policy #662 is copied from `b8c967f2039bdad8a385429a212b977318adc9dc`; no retained-manager actor source or lifetime protocol is adopted.

Explicit developer registration supplies trusted clock/wakeup callbacks. Dormant fixed private-socket Get/Set methods accept only daemon instance, preference revision and bounded interval; clients cannot supply time, force wakeup, choose providers or set paths. Automatic admission shares the existing Full Quit gate. Real private-socket and production HTTP loopback tests cover enable→wake→durable begin→GET→commit→terminal, responsive concurrent status, one worker and shared permits, Off/Disconnect, stale members/ownership, shutdown cancel/join and Full Quit races. Connected selected-profile changes or removal defer the whole batch with zero lifecycle calls; unchanged selected configuration inputs allow metadata refresh.

The dormant acknowledgement method accepts exact instance, attempt sequence, preference revision and owner revision. It requires the original supervisor's private non-cloneable drain, minted only after actual join or proven captured-work drop on spawn refusal. The owner retains exact interrupted identity and distinguishes attempt-local uncertainty from independent recovery barriers. Under the existing migration lease acknowledgement requires explicit Off, no active/queued work, valid current store/desired state, exact native generation, no transaction/lifecycle/auxiliary recovery, and a present non-missing target for connected intent. It writes AcknowledgedUncertain—not success, failure, rollback or reset—and preserves identity/time/failure history. Existing version-2 normal records remain supported.

Only a confirmed acknowledgement grants same-context rearm permission. A separate enable anchors a full normal interval; no immediate fetch occurs. Restart cannot inherit the drain or rearm permission. General prior-instance disposition remains blocked and requires a separate lifetime design. Publication/readback uncertainty, live workers, wrong/replayed origin, corrupt/missing journal/store, stale owner/revision and recovery barriers refuse.

Review/evidence:

- Root primary and independent Astra source review give scoped GO on exact `b8375c50`, before acknowledgement fixture execution. The first `61aa0614` review refusal for missing lifecycle/auxiliary recovery checks is preserved; its successor adds those checks and semantic connected-target validation.

Six dormant socket tests, five acknowledgement control/socket tests and one pure journal fault/history test cover the new composition. Acknowledgement's positive joined/never-spawned and negative/fault fixtures actually executed after review.

author: ibrahimdans
body:
## What
New action *Tools → i18n Support Plus → Generate i18next Types*. For each i18next module, it writes an `i18next.d.ts` that augments i18next's `CustomTypeOptions`: `resources` holds every namespace with its nested keys typed `string`, and `defaultNS` is set when a file holds that namespace.

- Keys are read from the reference locale: the module's, `en` otherwise.
- Plural forms (`_zero/_one/_two/_few/_many/_other`, plus `_ordinal_*`) collapse into the base key.
- Names that are not valid identifiers are quoted and escaped.
- Output is sorted, so it is deterministic.
- The file goes to `<module root>/src/@types/i18next.d.ts`, or `<module root>/@types/` when there is no `src` folder. A notification shows the path.
- A file without the generated header is only replaced after the user confirms.
- Regeneration is manual only. The action is hidden for non-i18next modules.

## Why
Today keys are only checked in the IDE. Teammates who don't use the plugin, and CI, never see a wrong key. The generated file is meant to be committed so that `tsc` catches them.

## Tests
- `I18nextTypesGeneratorTest` (pure, 9 tests): namespaces, nesting, plurals, plural vs object conflict, escaping, defaultNS, deterministic order.
- Full `./gradlew test` passes.
- Manual check on a scratch copy of `examples/react-multi-namespace` with `tsc` 5.9 and i18next 26:
  - The generated file gives exactly the same diagnostics as the hand-written `typeof json` declaration.
  - A probe file compiles: valid keys and plural base keys are accepted, an unknown key or namespace is rejected.
  - `examples/` is unchanged.

author: flugifix
body:
## What it does

A tap on Urban's value rows in full screen opens *Telemetry*: up to twelve readings as tiles, three
to a row, each with its name, its figure and, where the flight record keeps them, the least and the
most the flight reached (`min .. max`). A key can open it too: *Telemetry page* is a new choice on
the *Keys* page.

The tiles are chosen on a fifth settings page, *Telemetry* (*Tile 1* … *Tile 12*), from the same
catalogue the five value rows choose from, so a tile shows a reading exactly as its row does: the
same name, figure, colour, and the *Units beside the values* setting. Nine tiles are on by default;
a tile set to nothing is left out and the others close up.

## How

- `themes/urban/telemview.lua` is a new theme view (`urban_telemetry`), drawn with `viewkit.lua`
  like the link view.
- The catalogue entries in `layout.lua` name the flight record's keys for their reading
  (`minKey` / `maxKey`, `places`). The range is read as `Utils.statFromRecord` reads it: the flight
  in progress where it has a value, the last flight otherwise. No host change.
- The tiles' derived readings (ESC load, ESC status, air rate, rate floor) are added to the flight
  view's `sources`, because a view declares none of its own.
- On a host with theme views, `L.valuePanel` lays a press under the panel; its separators are
  drawn as lines so nothing over the press is a rectangle.

## What the range is, and is not

It is the flight record's, not the radio's sensor extremes: empty until the model has been armed
once, covering the armed time only. A side the record does not keep reads `-` (MCU temperature,
power, throttle, altitude and capacity have a most only; fuel a least only), and a reading the
record does not keep at all has no range line.

## Cost

- `bin/accounting/measure.lua`: `theme.urban` worst pass 14032 → 14051 (+19, the value panel's build:
  its full-screen check and the separator branch), sweep unchanged, every other row unchanged;
  `--check` passes.
- The view itself is not priced by the accounting. Counted offline with the same count hook and
  `bin/themes/validate.lua`'s stubs: nine tiles build in 8869 instructions cold and 4586 warm, with
  831 per sweep; twelve tiles in about 11200 cold and 5700 warm, 1020 per sweep. The link view, for
  scale: about 2400 cold, 2060 warm, 224 per sweep.

## Checks

- `bin/themes/validate.lua` green at 800x480, 480x320 and 480x272; it sees the flight view's new
  press and builds the new view (a broken close action in the view turns it red at all three sizes).
- The translation coverage job, the i18n precompiler and resolver tests, and the documentation
  rule (`bin/docs/verify_documentation_rule.py`) pass locally.
- On EdgeTX 2.12.2's simulator (TX16S MK3, 800x480) against a running Rotorflight SITL: a tap on the
  value panel opens the page and RTN returns to the flight view; TELE set to *Theme: Telemetry*
  opens the same page. On master the same tap leaves the flight view unchanged and TELE opens the
  quick menu. Not run armed there, so the range lines on that frame read `- .. -`; the figures were
  checked offline against a populated flight record (`3.68 .. 4.18` per cell, `3.2 .. 70.5` A).

## Relations

- Rebased onto #529: the new key choice is *Theme: Telemetry* like the other choices on the Keys page.
- #551 lets a fullscreen view name its own sources; #552 (stacked on this one) adds
  the radio's telemetry sensors to the rows and tiles, and #553 moves the tiles' sources
  onto this view. This one stands alone and goes first.
- #544 adds Urban's battery page beside this one: both add a view to `init.lua`, a press to the flight view in `layout.lua`, strings and a section of `docs/dashboard/urban-theme.md`, so the two conflict textually in those files and whichever merges second takes master in. #549 also edits `docs/dashboard/urban-theme.md`.
- `Releases.md`: the entry is at the end of 0.1.7 *Features & Enhancements*, where every open pull request of ours adds one (#543 to #549), so each of them conflicts there with this one.

Documentation: `docs/dashboard/urban-theme.md` (the page, the settings table, what it reads, what it
does not do) and `docs/dashboard/README.md`; `Releases.md` entry at the end of 0.1.7 *Features &
Enhancements*.

## Summary

Nikon Precision's lithography field service engineers work at Intel's Chandler fabs. Its job board runs on UKG Pro (UltiPro), and in the live check it had a **Field Service Engineer** opening in Chandler and Phoenix. This adds that board and the three things its pages needed.

- **UKG Pro reader** (`ukg_search`, `parse_ukg`)
  - The board loads its openings from its own `JobBoardView/LoadSearchResults` API, using the session its page sets up. The search therefore reads it in a background tab, rewriting the page's own call to ask for 200 openings instead of 50, and matches titles here.
  - Locations come from each opening's address ("Chandler, AZ; Phoenix, AZ").
  - Postings link to `OpportunityDetail?opportunityId=…`.
  - `ats` detects `ultipro.com` as "UKG Pro".
- **Notes over a posting**: UKG can open a posting under an "Accessibility Note" that hides the page's buttons. When a page has nothing else to press, a **Dismiss / Dismiss Note** button is pressed once. Cookie and consent dialogs are not touched by this.
- **Web-component buttons**: UKG draws **Apply now** and **Sign In** as `<ukg-button>` elements, with the real button inside a shadow root, so the form reader saw no buttons at all. Common web-component button tags and `data-tag-name="button"` now count as actions.
- **Small fixes**:
  - A dropdown whose menu didn't open is opened again (seen once on Onto's Phone Device Type).

- UKG detection.

## Part 2/6 of pi-memory Layer 1 (LANA-2026-10-06)

Implements the markdown mirror, per-project scoping, SOUL.md bootstrap, STANDING.md rules, and read-only skills listing per the review (Appendix C.4) and the shared contracts in the LANA-2026-10-06 mission brief.

### What ships

**New modules (7 files, ~1.1k LoC)**
- `src/store/paths.ts` — `storagePaths()`, `projectRoot()`, file-name constants
- `src/store/markdown.ts` — render/parse the three-file format, `atomicWrite` (temp + rename), `ensureDir`
- `src/store/user.ts` — `USER.md` read/write helpers (thin facade over `markdown.ts`)
- `src/store/mirror.ts` — `MarkdownMirror` (target routing, `write`/`remove`/`rebuild`) + `MirroredStore` (wraps `MemoryStore`; SQLite first, mirror error surfaced via `mirrorError`)
- `src/store/standing.ts` — `StandingStore` with 20-entry / 2,000-char caps; every add runs through `scanForWrite` in block mode
- `src/store/skills.ts` — read-only `SkillsStore` listing from `skills/<slug>/SKILL.md` frontmatter; project overrides global on slug clash
- `src/store/project.ts` — `resolveProject(cwd)` (git toplevel → cwd basename), `slugify`, `projectTag`, `bootstrapSoul()` ingesting CWD/SOUL.md paragraphs as `project` memories tagged `soul-bootstrap` + `project:<slug>`

**Edits to `src/store/memory.ts` (minimal, ~12 LoC)**
- Added optional `tags?: string[]` to `SearchOptions` and `ListOptions`
- AND-semantics filter: every requested tag must be present in the JSON tags column
- Empty `tags` array is a no-op; exact match, no fuzzy/partial
- No other changes (PR5 owns `markSynced`; minimal diff to avoid conflicts)

### Tests
- 7 new test files in `tests/store/`, 64 new tests
- `npx vitest run`: 197 passed (was 133 baseline)
- `npx tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck`: clean
- `bun run build`: clean

### Scanner contract
`MirroredStore` never sees raw caller input. The store\u0027s `add`/`replace` are scanner-gated; we read the post-scan record back via `store.get` so the markdown always reflects what landed in SQLite (redactions included). Standing rules and SOUL.md paragraphs also flow through the scanner.

### Note on `bun.lock`
The committed lockfile at f858fa73 pinned older versions that don\u0027t match the current `package.json` (`vitest ^5.0.3`, `memory-client ^2.2.1`, `pi-coding-agent ^1.0.4`). A fresh `bun install --frozen-lockfile` against that lockfile fails (vitest 5 needs a newer vite peer than the pinned 5.4.21). This PR regenerates `bun.lock` from the existing `package.json` so installs are reproducible. CI on the latest main run failed with the same lockfile drift; this PR fixes that for `@lanonasis/pi-lanonasis-memory` independently of the other PRs.

### Out of scope (other PRs own these)
- `src/index.ts`, `src/hooks/*`, `pi-extension.json`, `package.json` (metadata) — PR1
- `src/sync/*` — PR5
- `src/injection/*` — PR3
- `src/tools/*`, `src/commands/*`, wiring — PR4
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` integration — PR6

- [ ] Diff is `feat/pi-mem-2-mirror-scoping` only (16 files)
- [ ] 197 tests pass locally
- [ ] tsc + build clean
- [ ] No edits to `src/index.ts`, `src/hooks/*`, or `pi-extension.json`

body:
Supersedes #91 (thanks @mdsumner for the report and the fix).

1. `get_affine` built a wrong affine from ascending-y coordinate arrays: the origin came from `y[-1]` but the scale stayed `+dy`. Now `y[0] - dy/2` for either sign. `test_assign_index_from_coords` asserted the buggy value; fixed, plus a round-trip test.
2. With a correct `e > 0` affine, rusterize and exactextract (which assume north-up) gave y-flipped results. Before (1) they gave empty results. For `e > 0`, `rasterize`, `geometry_mask` and `coverage` now run on the y-flipped object and flip the result back. rasterio was already correct.

New tests: ascending-y for each engine, eager and chunked.

#92 is an xarray bug (`CoordinateTransformIndexingAdapter._oindex_get` keeps integer-indexed axes); fixed upstream in pydata/xarray#11679.

author: fubeo
body:
Pacchetto FD-710 di FubDraw: **la cronologia**, l'undicesimo passo della serie che porta l'editor dei disegni al livello degli strumenti professionali. Sopra #155.

Cinque commit: il salto nella pila e i segni, col motore che lo rende veloce; poi il pannello e l'editor che lo usa; poi i documenti; poi una correzione del pannello, trovata guardandolo in un browser e rileggendo; infine il nome del pulsante «Segna» nella pagina della cronologia. Tutto vale dal livello Standard, e nel Personalizzato è la parte nuova «Cronologia» (`history`).

**Il salto** (`tools/history.ts`, `scene/engine.ts`).

- **Dove si va:** `History.goTo` porta a un punto qualsiasi della pila, annullando o ripetendo in un colpo i passi in mezzo. Un punto è il numero del passo dopo cui sta (`Step.serial`). Il numero resta del passo quando si fonde, si annulla o si ripete. `start` è il punto prima del passo più vecchio, e `trimmed` dice se la pila ha dimenticato i passi oltre i 1000.
- **Un cambiamento solo:** `SceneEngine.undoAll` applica la fila di undo come `undo`, uno dopo l'altro, ma scrive il testo una volta sola, alla fine. Il documento riceve una `TextOperation` sola, con l'origine `undo` o `redo`.
- **Quanto costa:** un salto di mille passi passava da 945 ms a 6 ms su questa macchina. I byte sono quelli di mille undo uno per volta, e tornando avanti si ritrova il testo di prima, byte per byte.
- **Il passo che non va:** il salto si ferma al primo passo che non si annulla, o non si ripete. Quel passo esce dalla pila, come già fa con annulla e ripeti; quelli prima restano fatti.

**I segni.**

- **Dove stanno:** su un punto, con un nome, e durano quanto la sessione. Non vanno nel file.
- **Quando se ne vanno:** quando il loro punto non si raggiunge più. Succede se un gesto nuovo toglie i passi da ripetere, o se la pila dimentica i più vecchi. Il segno di un passo che esce passa al punto prima.
- **Il passo dopo:** mettere un segno chiude il passo in cima, e il gesto dopo non si fonde con quello prima del segno.

**Il pannello** (`tools/history-panel.ts`). «Cronologia», nella barra dopo «Oggetti», lo apre accanto al foglio, in fondo agli altri pannelli, e il fuoco ci va.

- **Le righe:**
  - In cima c'è «Disegno aperto», o «Inizio della cronologia» quando la pila ha dimenticato i passi più vecchi; una nota lo dice.
  - Sotto ci sono i passi dal più vecchio, col nome degli annunci di annulla, e i segni sotto il passo dopo cui sono stati messi.
  - La riga di adesso ha il fondo attivo, il grassetto, il triangolo e la parola «adesso». I passi da ripetere sono grigi e in corsivo, e il nome lo dice a parole. Un segno ha la bandierina.
- **Col puntatore:**
  - Un clic porta alla riga.
  - Col mouse o con la penna, premuto e trascinato, il disegno segue la riga sotto il puntatore. Oltre il bordo l'elenco scorre col puntatore.
  - Il dito scorre l'elenco, e un tocco porta alla riga.
- **Che cosa succede andando:**
  - Il salto si annuncia, «Indietro fino a «Spostamento»: 3 passi annullati.», e se si è fermato dice anche perché.
  - La selezione segue l'ultimo passo del salto, come dopo un annulla.
  - Un testo in scrittura o un tracciato di Bézier a metà si concludono prima, come cambiando strumento.
- **I segni:** «Segna», nell'intestazione, mette un segno dove si è e ne apre il nome, che parte da «Segno 1». `F2` o un doppio clic lo cambiano. `Canc` o la croce in fondo alla riga lo tolgono.
- **Da tastiera:**
  - L'elenco è un listbox ARIA. La riga attiva sta in `aria-activedescendant`, e quella di adesso ha `aria-current="step"`.
  - Le frecce, `PagSu`, `PagGiù`, `Home` e `Fine` scelgono la riga; `Invio` o `Spazio` ci vanno; `Esc` torna al foglio.
  - `Ctrl+Z` e `Ctrl+Y` funzionano anche dall'elenco. Quando il punto cambia da fuori, la riga attiva torna su quella di adesso.
- **Mille righe:** le righe sono alte 44 px, e si disegnano soltanto quelle che si vedono. La riga del segno che si rinomina resta ferma nel DOM mentre l'elenco scorre, e le altre si ordinano attorno a lei: spostarla toglierebbe il fuoco al campo.
- **In sola lettura** il pannello si guarda soltanto.
- **`?`** elenca i tasti della cronologia.

**I documenti:**

- Una pagina nuova, `docs/product/drawing-history.md`.
- Cambiano `drawing.md`, `drawing-custom.md`, l'indice e il §7 di `scene-operations.md`, coi salti.
- In `drawing.md` due paragrafi si accorciano di una riga, per restare entro la misura della pagina.

### Scelte da rivedere

**Il salto:**

- Un salto è un cambiamento solo del documento, con l'origine `undo` o `redo`, non uno per passo.
- Si ferma al primo passo impossibile, invece di saltarlo e proseguire: la riga d'arrivo resterebbe una promessa falsa.
- La selezione segue l'ultimo passo del salto, quello accanto al punto d'arrivo.
- Ciò che si sta scrivendo o tracciando si conclude prima del salto. Se il salto andava avanti, quel passo nuovo toglie i passi da ripetere, e il salto non parte.
- Un clic sulla riga dove si è già non fa niente.

**I segni:**

- Valgono per la sessione e il riquadro, non per il file.
- Stanno sui punti, non sui passi.
- Un gesto nuovo toglie i segni dei punti da ripetere; la pila che dimentica i passi vecchi toglie i loro segni.
- Il segno di un passo che esce passa al punto prima.
- Mettere un segno chiude il passo in cima.
- Il segno nuovo apre subito il suo nome. Il nome di partenza è «Segno N», e N non torna indietro quando un segno si toglie.

**Il pannello:**

- Il mouse e la penna scorrono la cronologia tenendo premuto; il dito scorre l'elenco e va col tocco.
- La riga scelta segue le frecce, come in ogni elenco a scelta singola, e andarci è `Invio`.
- La prima riga si chiama «Disegno aperto», o «Inizio della cronologia» quando la pila ha dimenticato i passi più vecchi.
- Il pannello sta in fondo al dock, e il pulsante dopo «Oggetti».
- «Segna» sta nell'intestazione, con la parola che comincia il suo nome. Accanto alle proprietà così si vede una riga in più.
- Nessun tasto globale apre il pannello: `Ctrl+Maiusc+H` nasconde la selezione, e `F9` o `Alt+F9` non dicono niente a chi non viene da Photoshop.
- La parte è del livello Standard.

### Da sapere

- **Guardato in un browser:** ho fotografato il pannello in Chromium, chiaro e scuro, con una pagina di prova fuori dal repo: righe, segno, campo del nome e intestazione. Accanto alle proprietà aperte si vedono quattro righe.
- **Lo scorrimento oltre il bordo** segue il puntatore che si muove. Col puntatore fermo fuori dall'elenco, l'elenco non continua a scorrere da solo.
- **Un test della shell rosso in CI dalla #155 in su:** `shell.e2e.test.ts`, «un comando di sola lettura non flussa», trova un `writeDocument` che non aspetta, in tutte e due le corse. Passa qui, anche da solo (1,9 s), e passa su `main`. Sotto la #155 la pila era rossa solo per i temi, che la #156 sistema. Il test non tocca i disegni; va guardato prima di accogliere la pila.
- **Il testo arrivato da fuori:** dopo un salto oltre un passo che è uscito, il punto «Disegno aperto» non è più il disegno com'era all'apertura. La riga lo chiama così lo stesso, e l'annuncio dice che il passo non si annullava.

### Verifica

**Test nuovi:**

- `engine.test.ts` (2): una fila di undo con un cambiamento solo e gli stessi byte di uno per volta; la fila che si ferma al primo rifiuto
- `history.test.ts` (12): andata e ritorno con gli stessi byte, mille passi, il passo che non va, i numeri che restano, la pila che dimentica, la revisione; i segni coi punti, i nomi, i gesti nuovi, la pila che dimentica, il passo che esce, la fusione chiusa
- `history-panel.test.ts` (19): le righe e l'accessibilità, il vuoto e la pila tagliata, mille righe; la tastiera, i tasti che non arrivano all'editor, la riga attiva che segue il punto; lo scorrimento col mouse, oltre il bordo, il rilascio perso, il dito; i segni, il nome, la riga che si rinomina ferma mentre l'elenco scorre, Canc e la croce; la sola lettura. La prova della riga ferma fallisce sul codice di prima della correzione

author: adriihdezz
body:
## Change

El `.gitignore` intenta permitir `.env.example`:

```gitignore
.env*
!.env.example
...
.env
.env.*
```

Pero `.env.*` aparece después de la excepción y la anula, así que `.env.example` queda ignorado. Además ese archivo no existe: para saber qué variables configurar hay que leer `docs/search.md` o `turbo.json`.

Cambios:

- `.gitignore`: se eliminan `.env` y `.env.*`, que ya cubre `.env*`. La excepción `!.env.example` vuelve a funcionar y `.env`, `.env.local`, etc. siguen ignorados.
- `.env.example`: las variables de la sección «Credenciales» de `docs/search.md` y `SEARCH_MODE`, sin valores. `DATABASE_URL` aparece comentada con el valor del `compose.yaml` local.
- `docs/search.md`: la puesta en marcha indica `cp .env.example .env`.

Sigue el PR del `.env` raíz en Windows (`cdab530`).

## Verification

Antes (`main`), con un `.env.example` vacío creado para la prueba:

```
> git check-ignore -v .env.example
.gitignore:17:.env.*    .env.example
```

Después:

```
> git check-ignore -v .env.example
.gitignore:10:!.env.example    .env.example
> git status --short
?? .env.example
> git check-ignore .env .env.local
.env
.env.local
```

- [x] `pnpm exec prettier --check --end-of-line auto docs/search.md`
- [x] Copiado como `.env`, `pnpm dev` arranca en modo preview sin `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`
- Ponytail Review del diff: sin hallazgos.

## Impact

Solo afecta a archivos de configuración local y documentación. No cambian contratos, datos, permisos ni despliegue. Solo `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` queda sin comentar y vacía, lo que equivale a no definirla (modo preview); el resto está comentado.

## Agent assistance

Claude (Cowork) redactó `.env.example`, este cambio e hizo la Ponytail Review. Los comandos y las comprobaciones los ejecuté yo en local.

author: pietroppeter
body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"pietroppeter"} -->
_Requested by **Pietro** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_015yneFPggc3zZ1LnzPqGFmh?thread=cmsg_015yneFPggc3zZ1LnzPqGFmhMUtnrxXcK6eEbVHNJheQq9)_

Follows #1 (merged).

Before: not1d sorts with a radix sort written in Nim, and only that.

After: building with `NOT1D_SORT=pdqsort` (e.g. `NOT1D_SORT=pdqsort uv run benchmark.py`) makes not1d sort with ot1d's own C++ `pdqsort.h`, so both can be benchmarked. `not1d.core.sortAlgorithm()` says which one a build uses, and `benchmark.py` prints it.

How: `sorting.nim` imports `pdqsort` with `importcpp` under `-d:pdqsort`. nimlang's hatch hook always runs `nim c`, so `src/not1d/core.nims` (read by nim for core.nim) switches to the C++ backend when `NOT1D_SORT=pdqsort`, and points Nim's C++ compiler at nimlang's own `zig cc` shim with `-lc++`, so zig's libc++ is linked statically. Without that, Nim used the system `clang++` and the module depended on `libstdc++.so`. With it, the module needs no C++ runtime, and the pdqsort build cross-compiles to nimlang's 5 wheel platforms like the default one (checked by hand; the Linux wheel needs only glibc ≤ 2.16). `[tool.uv] cache-keys` include `NOT1D_SORT` and the `.nims`/`.h` files, so uv rebuilds when the choice changes. CI runs the single Linux job (install from the sdist, tests including the ot1d comparison) once per sort, and checks the build used the expected one.

Results (1M points, ms, in the README): with pdqsort not1d matches ot1d single-threaded (Mac: 32 vs 31 uniform, 97 vs 89 weighted), so the Nim code adds no overhead; the radix sort is faster (Mac: 16 uniform, 27 weighted), most of all with weights, where pdqsort moves (point, mass) pairs through a comparator.

nimlang findings: there is no way to pass Nim flags (backend, defines) to the hatch hook from `pyproject.toml`; a `.nims` next to the module works but needs an env var for the choice. A C++ mode in nimlang would also need zig's libc++ wired in as done here.

author: loganbnielsen
body:
Adds the shared Sol workload-authentication primitive for TypeScript HTTP services.

- `createWorkloadAuthenticator` reads `SOL_TRUSTED_WORKLOAD_ISSUER`, `SOL_UNIT`, and derived `SOL_CALLED_BY` from Sol projections; application code does not choose a trust root.
- Verifies bearer JWT signature, issuer, audience, fixed signing-algorithm allowlist, and expiry/not-before claims, then maps the Kubernetes ServiceAccount subject to a Sol workload principal.
- Keeps OIDC discovery, JWKS resolution/cache, synchronization, route selection, and framework response behavior outside the security core through one injected JOSE key resolver.
- Returns 401 for absent/invalid tokens, 403 for authenticated non-workload or undeclared callers, and 500 when key resolution is unavailable. Missing issuer/unit projection fails startup.

Validation: `npm run build && npm test` passes for the full TypeScript workspace.

This is the TypeScript workload-auth core slice of Sol issue #1111. It does not add an HTTP-framework adapter; a conforming Fastify/Express adapter can consume the same primitive.

author: moyu929
body:
海尔是站内第三多的品牌（52 款）。接口纯 HTTP、无签名、无 token、无验证码。

```
GET https://www.haier.com/igs/front/search.jhtml?code=<常量>&siteId=2&searchWord=<型号>
GET https://www.haier.com/<品类>/<日期>_<metaId>.shtml   详情页 SSR，规格在 HTML 里
```

基线说的「官网稳定 302」复核结论：**302 不是封锁，是 CDN 下发 `C3VK` cookie 的自跳转挑战**，而这两个接口根本不需要 cookie。

## 修掉两个静默失败/写错的 bug

**1. `spec_pairs` 锚点错位 → 恒解析 0 项。** 原来从 `js_specificationTab` 截断，但那是 `<li>` tab 按钮，真规格表在 140KB 开外，而 `js_koubeiTab` 就在按钮旁边（相距 124 字符）—— seg 被切成 124 字符。改锚点为 `js_params`。

**2. 只补空字段的守卫恒为假 → 84 个已有值被覆盖。** 原写法 `if field in holes and not blank(_cur.get(field))`：holes 本身就是按 `blank()` 筛出来的，「field in holes」为真时 blank 必为真，条件永不成立。修后产出 115 → 34 字段，但那 34 个全都是原本为「查不到」的。

## 内外机天然分列

规格表里 `内机尺寸`/`外机尺寸`/`内机噪音`/`外机噪音` 各自成行，直接映射 `size_indoor`/`size_outdoor`。轴序是 `宽*深*高`，与美的 BFF 的 `Length×Width×Height` 不同（那边要换轴，这边不用）。

`bookUpTime`/`docPubtime` 不采作 `year`（是资料上架时间，与苏宁丢弃「上架日期」同源）；`price` 不采（当前促销价，与参考价口径冲突）。

**产出**：17 款 / 34 字段。剩余空字段 8589 → 8572。`npm run check` 全绿。

author: schowsf
body:
---

Title:
Supervise resource lifecycle with DeathWatch; close silent-crash and terminate leaks

Body:
## Summary

A `ResourceInstance` that stopped on an uncaught exception, or a `ResourceMgr` that
did the same, previously went silent: the typed default is to STOP, so the workflow
waited forever on a `ResourceTerminated`/`ResourceInstSpec` reply that never came, and
any cluster the dead actor owned could leak. This replaces that with explicit
DeathWatch supervision plus backstop teardown.

## Changes

**ResourceMgr → ResourceInstance**
- `watchWith(rscInst, ResourceInstanceDied(instId))`; `deathActionFor` maps the
  persisted status to `Respawn` / `Fail` / `Ignore`.
- Bounded recovery: respawn up to `MaxRespawnAttempts` consecutive crashes with no
  confirmed progress in between; a progress signal resets the budget.
- Epoch/incarnation guard: a crash-respawn reuses the same `instId`, so a stale
  `ResourceInstanceProgressed` from a crashed predecessor is matched on both `instId`
  **and** `epoch` (`isCurrentIncarnation`) before it may reset the budget.
- `terminateResourceBackstop` drives a direct provider terminate on every path where
  no live instance will (budget exhausted, failed re-spawn-to-retry, or a child
  reporting its `terminate()` returned `Left`), folding a thrown exception and a
  returned `Left` into one leak-logged outcome.

**ResourceInstance**
- Re-adopting a persisted `Running` row reports progress up front when the cluster
  confirms `Running` (`readoptShouldReportProgress`), so a respawned-but-unpolled
  instance resets the manager's budget instead of parking passively.
- A failed status poll routes through `shuttingDown` (so `terminate` is actually
  called) rather than marking `Failed` and orphaning a live cluster.
- A clean `Left` from `resourceIO.terminate` hands teardown back to the manager
  (`ResourceInstanceTerminateFailed`) instead of recording a normal finish and
  silently leaking.

**WorkflowMgr → ResourceMgr**
- `watchWith(rscMgr, ResourceMgrDied(resourceId))`; handler is membership-guarded,
  since the cooperative path removes the id before stopping. A crash unblocks the
  workflow (cancel dependents, fail the resource) instead of hanging.

**ActivityAttempt**
- Standing `CheckProgress` watchdog in `waiting` survives a lost `GetResourceInstSpec`
  reply; `running` ignores a now-expected late/duplicate `ResourceInstSpec` instead of
  failing the already-started activity.

**EmrResource**
- `terminate` wrapped in `retryToEither` so a provider error surfaces as a `Left`
  rather than a thrown exception.

## Tests

- Adds `ResourceMgrDeathWatchSpec` and `ResourceInstanceReadoptSpec` — pure-function
  coverage of `deathActionFor` / `isCurrentIncarnation` / `respawnBudgetExhausted` /
  `readoptShouldReportProgress`.
- `sbt orchardCore/test` → 17/17 passing.

Bumps version `0.30.8` → `0.30.9`.

---

body: Production is on an empty Neon database, and nothing in this environment can run `npm run db:migrate` without copying `DATABASE_URL`. This adds two ways to apply `db/migrations` through the existing migrator, plus a public check that does not need the secret. `POST /api/storage/migrate` requires `Authorization: Bearer $RESONANCE_SYNC_SECRET`. It runs the same path as `db:migrate` ( `schema_migrations`, `IF NOT EXISTS`, a second call is a no-op) inside one transaction that holds `pg_advisory_xact_lock`, so overlapping calls cannot race. Missing the bearer is 401. An unset `DATABASE_URL` is 503 `Postgres is not configured`. The body is `{ applied, skipped }`. Production builds run that step before `next build` only when `VERCEL_ENV` is `production` and `DATABASE_URL` is set. Preview and local builds skip it, because previews share the production database. A failed production migration fails the build and leaves the previous deployment live. The log lists file names and does not print the URL. `GET /api/storage/status` is public. It returns `{ backend, schema: { migrated, applied, pending }, reachable }` with `Cache-Control: no-store` and never includes a connection string or hostname. If the production build migrated before this route existed, or the build-time step did not run, apply the schema with: ```bash curl -sS -X POST https://resonance3.vercel.app/api/storage/migrate \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $RESONANCE_SYNC_SECRET" ``` Then confirm with `GET https://resonance3.vercel.app/api/storage/status`.

body:
Fixes the GraphRAG with Qdrant and Neo4j example so it runs end to end and matches the updated tutorial at qdrant.tech/documentation/examples/graphrag-qdrant-neo4j/ (landing_page PR linked once opened).

**What changed and why**
- Paragraph embeddings were paired with unrelated entity IDs (`zip(node_id_mapping.values(), embeddings)`). Each paragraph is now a `Chunk` node linked to its entities by `MENTIONS`, and its Qdrant point uses the chunk ID, which `QdrantNeo4jRetriever` matches to Neo4j.
- Entity IDs are reused across paragraphs, so an entity mentioned in several paragraphs is one node.
- Chunk IDs come from `get_search_results` records instead of parsing `str(record)`.
- `create_collection` uses `collection_exists`; the answer returns `.content`; repeated edges are dropped from the graph context; credentials load once.
- Models: `gpt-4o-2024-08-06` and `gpt-4` replaced by `gpt-5-mini`.

**Tested** on 2026-10-06 against Qdrant Cloud and Neo4j Aura with qdrant-client 1.19.1, neo4j 6.4.0, neo4j-graphrag 1.22.0, openai 3.24.0: 25 paragraphs, 59 entities, correct answer to "How is Bob connected to New York?".

##### Impact

A memory-related vulnerability has been discovered and fixed in the upstream librsvg dependency. When certain runtime-specific conditions apply, this vulnerability can lead to possible remote code execution (RCE) on glibc-based Linux.

##### Patches

##### Using prebuilt binaries provided by sharp?

Most people rely on the prebuilt binaries provided by sharp.

sharp.block({ operation: ["VipsForeignLoadSvg"] });

body:
## Summary

#16 listed seven comments, help lines and doc lines that are wrong about the code, under "Follow-ups (not in this PR)". This PR fixes each one so that it matches the code. Each claim was checked against the code on this branch first. Two of the counts in #16 were off, and the entries below say so.

Where a number would go stale again (a line count, a `~line` reference, "the Nth step"), the new text names the function, the variable or the section instead.

1. **`bin/github-guard`, "one of the four".** `GUARDED` and the dispatch `case` hold five commands: `gh api`, `gh pr`, `gh issue`, `git push` and `wt pr`. The comment now says "one of the commands in GUARDED".
2. **`install.sh`.**
   - `hook_bashrc` is the eighth step after the EXIT trap, not the seventh. The `check_bashrc` comment now says that it "runs after the linking steps".
   - Three steps build a temp file with `mktemp` and record it in `TMPFILES`: `copy_config`, `hook_bashrc` and `hook_cmux_config`. The `report` comment now says "the mktemp steps".
   - `--with-claude-ui` leaves out four entries: `.tui`, `.voice`, `.theme` and `.env.CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE_CLICKS`. The `report_skipped` comment now says "the UI keys", which is the term that the rest of the file uses. The "three keys" at line 327 is correct and stays: there it means the three top-level keys beside the env var.
3. **`test/install-smoke.sh`.**
   - The `assert_claude_ui` comment in scenario 3 now says "`--opinionated-config` includes `--with-claude-ui`".
   - The scenario 8 header now names `--with-claude-ui`, not "the sixth flag", and compares it with "the other `--with-…` flags".
   - The "all six" comment in scenario 1 is subtler than #16 said. The loop checks six flags, but `report_skipped` names seven on a Mac. So the comment now says that `report_skipped` must name each flag that the run did not get, and that scenario 17a checks the Mac-only `--with-cmux-config`.
4. **`test/wt-smoke.sh`.**
   - The comments now cite "`cmux_bin` in bin/wt" and "`is_remote()` in bin/wt", not `bin/wt:~76` and `bin/wt:~88`. The two functions are at lines 122 and 135 now.
   - "bin/wt is 1500 lines" is gone. The file has 2145 lines, and the sentence now reads "bin/wt creates and DESTROYS work".
   - `wt_run` unsets six `CMUX_*`/`WT_*` variables. The comment now says "the `CMUX_*`/`WT_*` variables" with no count.
   - Only one header needed a new number. The second `# 11.` header (`lib_cleanup`'s backstop) is now `# 12.`, which matches its `begin_scenario "12. …"` label. No header follows it. The one citation of a scenario number above 10, "Scenario 11 at least parses bin/wt", points to the first scenario 11 and is still correct.
   - The renumbered header also said "Both suites build `$TEST_ROOT`…". It now says "Every suite", for the reason in item 5.
5. **`test/lib.sh`, "two suites".** Seven suites source it, not six as #16 said. The seventh is `agent-status-linux-smoke.sh`. The header, the "Why it exists" paragraph and the `lib_cleanup` comment no longer give a count. All seven make `$TEST_ROOT` with `mktemp -d`, resolve it with `pwd -P`, refuse a root inside `$HOME` before they arm the trap, and install `lib_cleanup`. But only `install-smoke.sh` (`guard_scratch_home`) and `wt-smoke.sh` (`guard_scratch_root`) have a fixture guard, so the comment now says that.
6. **`bin/wt`, `$B` in `rm_reasons`.** The comment now names `$b`, the local that the function uses. (`$B` is the global that `require_wt` sets, and `cmd_rm` passes it in as `$b`.)
7. **The `wt rm` refusals.** `rm_reasons` makes five refusals, and `--force` skips all of them. `wt prune` reads the same function. The code refuses in both situations that #16 named, so the help text and the README now list the same five, in the same order:
   - uncommitted changes
   - commits that are not merged and not pushed
   - a base ref that `wt rm` cannot compare the branch with. The help text gains this item.
   - a HEAD that is not on `wt/<name>`. The README gains this item.
   - an edited or newly created `.wt-include` file

   Two README bullets were also wrong about the code, and this PR corrects them:
   - The base-ref bullet said "compare the worktree against". `rm_reasons` compares the branch, never the worktree's HEAD.
   - The `.wt-include` bullet said "no longer matches its source in the main checkout". `changed_includes` compares with the hash recorded at `wt new`, so a secret that changes in the main checkout does not block removal. It also refuses files that were created inside the worktree.

   That bullet was the first use of "main checkout", so its definition moves to the next use, in the self-removal steps.

## What stays the same

- No code changes. In the scripts, each changed line is a `#` comment or a `wt` help line. The one exception is a trailing comment on an `assert_claude_ui` line, whose code part is unchanged.
- The `wt` help keeps its column alignment and stays within its existing width, and `wt new  [name]` (two spaces) is still there. The headings and anchors that other files cite are unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] All test suites that run on a Mac pass, with the same counts as #16: `install-smoke` (648), `wt-smoke` (627), `github-guard-smoke` (430), `agent-status-smoke` (72), `remote-new-smoke` (27) and `hosts-smoke` (21).
- [x] `bash -n` passes on every changed script, and `/bin/bash` 3.2 `-n` passes on `bin/wt`. None of the changed files is a zsh script.
- [x] shellcheck 0.11.0 (`-x`) gives the same result as `origin/main` for each changed file: no findings.
- [x] `bash bin/wt help` renders with its alignment intact.
- [x] The `grep` checks in "Check a change" in `docs/documentation-style.md` each print a line, and `#remove-a-task` still resolves.
- [ ] `test/agent-status-linux-smoke.sh` (Linux only) has not been run. This PR changes no file that it runs.

## Further follow-ups (not in this PR)

These are outside the seven items and not in lines that this PR changes:

- **`wt prune` is not stricter than `wt rm`.** The README says that "`wt prune` is stricter still: it only removes worktrees whose branch is merged and whose tree is clean". The help says something similar. But `cmd_prune` calls `rm_reasons`, like `wt rm` does, so it also removes the worktree of a branch that is pushed but not merged. A scratch repo shows this: `wt prune --dry-run` printed `would remove pushed (nothing to lose vs origin/main)` for such a branch. Decide which one is right, the text or the code.
- **`home/.agents/skills/worktree-teardown/SKILL.md`, "Safety contract".** It has the same gaps that the README had. It omits the HEAD refusal, says that a `.wt-include` file "now differs from its source in the main checkout", and says "cannot compare the worktree with its base". This is an agent-instruction file, so it needs its own careful change.
- **README, "`--discard-commits`" paragraph.** "The dirty-tree, `.wt-include` and HEAD checks still apply" leaves out the base-ref check, which `--discard-commits` does not waive either.
- **README, Layout tree and test notes.** `lib.sh  the assertion vocabulary both suites speak` and "Both suites build their scratch root with `mktemp -d`" date from when two suites used `test/lib.sh`. Seven use it now.
- **`install.sh`, `claude_ui_opted_in`.** The comment says that `copy_config` makes the same jq probe "eleven lines further down". It is about 65 lines further down, in the kept-copy warning. Name the place instead of a count.
- **`test/install-smoke.sh`, scenarios 3 and 8a.** The scenario 3 header and its `begin_scenario` label say "all five linked". On a Mac, `--opinionated-config` also links `cmux.json`, which `assert_machinery "$h" yes` checks. Scenario 8a says that `report_skipped` "still names the five that it did not install". On a Mac it names six, `--with-cmux-config` too. The label is test output, so it is code and stays here.

body:
## Summary

Makes the mockup builder faster to use and lets a mockup span several linked screens. Everything stays in the single `index.html`.

- **Save / Save as / Open:** Save overwrites the open mockup and Save as makes a new copy. **Start from** opens a copy of an older mockup. The toolbar shows unsaved changes, and ⌘S / ⌘⇧S work. Mockups can be downloaded and imported as JSON. Mockups saved in the old single-screen format still open.
- **Pick several in the library:** press **+** (or Shift-click) on cards to collect them in a tray, then add them all at once. They are placed in rows without overlapping existing content.
- **Palette previews:** hover cards, an optional thumbnail view, and a drag ghost shown at canvas scale.
- **Layout guides:** 18 presets (header, left · center · right, list · detail, dashboard, landing page, column grids, mobile shells). Edges snap to them, the export names the panel each element sits in, and the guides can be turned into Region elements.
- **Blocks:** about 30 ready-made combinations (headers, button pairs, forms, KPI rows, pricing, landing sections) that adapt to the frame size. A block moves as a group, and Alt-drag moves one piece.
- **Help me choose:** a guided picker, e.g. *options → how many → one or several*, with ranked suggestions.
- **Screens and flow:** each element can link to another screen (or Back). The **Flow map** draws arrows between screen thumbnails, and **Play** lets you click through the mockup.
- **Copy for Claude** can export all screens plus a FLOW section.

## Testing

Tested by hand in the browser: picking and adding from the tray, placing blocks, applying layouts and snapping, group drag and undo, flow map arrows, Play navigation including Back, export of one screen and of all screens, Save / Save as / Open / Start from, loading drafts in the old format, and a phone-width layout with no horizontal scroll. No console errors.

body:
## Problem
check-static fails: scripts/test_ced_resume_cpu.py worker b2 raises `IndexError: list index out of range` at train.py resume block (`_on = _order[_oi]`).

The engram change 39276606 replaced the unconditional `opt.load_state_dict(sd)` with a by-name state remap built from v42's three optimizer groups (muon/sinkhorn/adamw). The classic CED/hybrid stack (`Cfg.arch != "v42"`) builds **four** optimizers via build_optimizers (muon/embed/scalar/head), so iterating to `_oi=3` indexes `_order[3]` and crashes.
