author: ferrumvir
body:
## Summary

The **ARC Proof Kit**: an opt-in tool volunteers run on their own computers. It downloads the public SmolLM3-3B weights, converts them on-device with ARC's deterministic converter, verifies the package against the pinned manifest, runs the golden bit-exact test on every CPU kernel the machine has, measures speed, and prints MATCH or MISMATCH against the published golden digest `3e43f342…49f2`. Only with `--submit`, and after the person reads the exact JSON and types `yes`, it sends a privacy-safe result (`arc.proof-result.v1`) to a Hash Wall endpoint.

**Stacked on #137** (base branch `modern-model-smollm3`), so that `ci.yml`, golden-vectors and the SmolLM3 workflow (all with macOS legs) do not run while macOS runners are reserved for the v0.8.11 sequence. When #137 merges, retarget this PR to `main` and rebase.

Volunteer command (Mac/Linux): `scripts/proof-kit/run.sh` · Windows: `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\proof-kit\run.ps1` · `--dry-run` prints the payload · `--submit --endpoint URL` shares it after confirmation.

## CI evidence (Proof Kit workflow, Linux only)

Run [37507415675](https://github.com/FerrumVir/arc-chain/actions/runs/37507415675) (commit 90c28c5d8), both jobs green:
- **checks**: rustfmt, clippy `-D warnings` (all targets, candle), 51 modern lib tests + 6 binary tests, Python reference tests, shellcheck, `run.ps1` parse, actionlint 1.7.12, secret scan.
- **e2e-linux** (`ubuntu-latest`, AMD EPYC 9V74, 4 vCPU, a processor model not in the #137 matrix): `run.sh --dry-run` built `arc-modern`, downloaded 6.15 GB from Hugging Face in 58 s (SHA-256 checked), converted in 21 s, verified the package against the pinned manifest, and **MATCHed `3e43f342…49f2` on `cpu-scalar` (1.16 / 1.15 tok/s prefill / decode) and `cpu-simd` AVX2 (3.24 / 3.20 tok/s, 121,187 of 121,187 projections vectorised)**. The test challenge produced the same digest `fad7f448…4f6c` on both kernels. Payload 4,680 bytes, validated by the independent Python checker; stdout equals the saved file. 256 of 256 random seeds derived identical challenge prompts in Rust and Python. `--submit` against the local mock: typed `yes` → HTTP 202 pending, body identical to the saved result; typed `no` → "Not sent", the mock received nothing.

Run [37522354507](https://github.com/FerrumVir/arc-chain/actions/runs/37522354507) (current head 93e4e3682, which pins the test-challenge digest), both jobs green on an **AMD EPYC 7763** runner: golden MATCH on both kernels (1.54 / 1.54 and 3.48 / 3.45 tok/s) and the pinned test-challenge digest `fad7f448…4f6c` reproduced on a second processor model; mock submission confirmed (HTTP 202) and declined (nothing sent) again.

## Changes
- `arc-modern proof` (`crates/arc-inference/src/bin/proof_kit/`): prerequisites (≥4 GB free RAM, ≥10 GB disk for a fresh run), resumable SHA-256-checked download via the system curl, on-device conversion + pinned-manifest check, golden prompts + challenge prompt on `cpu-scalar` and `cpu-simd`, per-kernel golden digest with MATCH/MISMATCH, prefill/decode tok/s (`arc.proof-speed.v1`), coarse device profile (no hostname, user name, IP or serials), optional coarse island facts (memory class, GPU memory class, Thunderbolt 5 on Macs, download class).
- On a mismatch: first differing case and forward position from the published per-position reference, and, when another kernel matched, the first differing layer and operator from a self-checking traced forward pass (no change to `model.rs`).
- Anti-faking challenge `arc.proof-challenge.v1`: `GET <endpoint>/challenge` → seed → SHA-256 picks 4 of 256 public words into a fixed sentence → challenge digest submitted with the golden digest; a result counts once a second independent run agrees. `--dry-run` uses a fixed test challenge whose digest is now pinned from CI.
- `crates/arc-inference/src/modern/proof.rs`: derivation, digests, result builder, strict validator (exact fields, formats, classes, recomputed digests, 8 KB limit), exact wire format. GPU runs slot in (`gpu-wgpu`, `adapter`), with a TODO hook for EX13.
- Independent Python reference + tests (`scripts/arc_conformance/proof_kit_reference.py`), test vectors and word list (`docs/protocol/proof-kit/`), golden reference copied from SmolLM3 CI run 37473148757.
- `scripts/proof-kit/run.sh` / `run.ps1` (binary from `--bin`, a signed release asset checked like install.sh, or a build from the checkout), `mock_hash_wall.py` (local endpoint for tests), `pty_answer.py` (CI consent on a pseudo-terminal).
- `docs/proof-kit.md`: plain-English guide (Mac, Windows, Linux), honest scope, privacy, speed method, challenge spec, `arc.proof-result.v1` schema with the real CI payload as the example, validation rules, and what the Hash Wall endpoint must accept.
- `.github/workflows/proof-kit.yml`: Linux checks + end-to-end dry run on the real model + mock submission (confirmed and declined). macOS/Windows/Linux-arm64 only with the `proof-kit-matrix` label (do not add it until the release captain's merge sequence finishes).

## Not in this PR
- No default endpoint: the Hash Wall is not live; `--submit` needs `--endpoint`. Nothing posts to a live endpoint.
- No release ships `arc-modern` yet; adding `arc-modern-<platform>` assets to `release.yml`/`SHA256SUMS` is a separate release-process change.
- GPU path: waits for EX13's portable engine (`--gpu` is accepted and reports that).

## Testing
- [x] Proof Kit CI (Linux): checks, end-to-end dry run on the real model, mock submission confirmed and declined
- [x] Python reference tests pass locally; rustfmt clean; shellcheck clean; `run.sh --release v0.8.10` verified that release's SHA256SUMS signature with the install.sh key and correctly reported no `arc-modern` asset
- [ ] `proof-kit-matrix` (macOS, Windows, Linux arm64): pending the label, after the merge sequence

author: ntgptit
body:
## DEV-189 (EG-09 · DEV-242)

### Root cause

Plan ruling 7's start-up guard: with no transition record and the SDK on another account than `lastKnownAccount`, `_adopt` recorded a discard switch at `targetSignedIn`, so `LocalDataReset` and `pullAll` ran with no push and no question. Every path to it today has already asked (`_checkReplace` at re-auth, then a kill before `_begin`), but it is the safety net for "the session changed for no known reason", and a later path could lose unsent changes silently.

### Solution

`_adopt` (`lib/core/auth/account_coordinator_switch.dart`) reads `_sync.pendingCount()` first:
- unsent changes → pause sync, log `auth.account_mismatch_unsent` (last, signed_in, unsent) and emit `ReauthRequired(last)` (#14). The person then signs in again: another account goes through #37 (`UnsentChangesFailure` until the loss is confirmed), "Continue without this account" through #38. Nothing is reset, no record is written.
- nothing unsent → adopt as before.

### Tests

- New `test/core/auth/account_coordinator_adopt_test.dart` (the switch test file is at the guard's size limit):
  - with changes unsent, the start lands on `ReauthRequired(X)`: no reset, no pull, no push, outbox kept, sync paused, no record;
  - from there, `requestCode(U)` throws `UnsentChangesFailure(count: 2)`; with `confirmedLoss` the sign-in to U resets once and pulls U (#37);
  - with nothing unsent, U is adopted as before (reset once, pull U, no push).
- `account_coordinator_switch_test.dart` ruling-7 case now states its precondition (`readyAnonymous(world, pending: 0)`): it ran with two unsent changes before, which is exactly the case this PR changes.
- RED first: the two unsent cases failed on master (`Ready` instead of `ReauthRequired`; `StateError` instead of the failure).

### Docs

- Plan `2026-09-30-accounts-core-auth.md` ruling 7: the condition.
- Auth spec §3.3 row #2: the start-up guard's two outcomes.

### Verification

- `run_tests.sh test/core/auth test/features/account`: 264 tests, 0 failures.
- `python3 tools/docs/check.py`: PASS.
- `dod_check.sh` on `4064c6f` (master `534f0cf`): PASS — 3661 host tests, docs PASS, guard clean, generated code fresh.
- `tools/supabase/run_auth_it.sh` (required because `lib/core/auth/` changed) **could not run here**: it needs Docker, which this container cannot pull images for. No migration changed; the server is untouched by this PR.

### Risk

- A device whose last account was anonymous and that still has unsent changes would now land on `ReauthRequired` with an anonymous `last` (no email to prefill). No known path produces that state (a link keeps the uid; every switch asks first); the way out is "Continue without this account" (#38) or a sign-in with the loss confirmed. Adopting would have silently discarded those changes, which is the behaviour this PR removes.

body:
The agent guides (root `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` and the per-section files under `docs/`) still described the tree from before 3.0. They said modules shipped separately and versioned independently, that `packages/` existed, that the site wrote `SpokenBooksAudio/Data/Sounds.lua`, and that zones packs were matched on the `.toc` major version. Several paths were wrong (`scripts/release.sh`, `addon/*/README.md`). An agent following them would have bumped the wrong version or written the wrong changelog. At 38 KB the guides also cost a lot of context for what they delivered.

This rewrite brings them to 15.6 KB. Each claim kept was checked against the current tree.

## What changed

- **Root `AGENTS.md`** covers the following:
  - The real layout: modules, `SpokenContributions`, tombstones, `publishers/`, `docs/spoken/`.
  - Branches: PRs land on `develop`, which needs one approval and CI. Only the admin merges to `master`, and a push to `master` deploys the site.
  - `make test` / `test-player` / `lint`.
  - The rules every section shares: no TTS credits spent from the repo, data only comes home, frozen ids with their owning modules, forward-only migrations.
  - Lockstep versioning for Spoken and its modules.
  - The general working agreements and PR-description guidance, which used to apply only when an agent happened to read the zones file.
- **`docs/quests/CLAUDE.md`** is trimmed to what an agent needs:
  - The corpus now lives in Postgres `quest_line`.
  - The current `release.sh` targets, and where pack ids live (`publishers/quests/audio-*.md`).
  - Legacy zips come only from `quests/vX` tags.
  - Both TTS providers.
  - Lineage, icon details, transcode internals and per-pack file counts are gone; `docs/quests/README.md` already covers them.
- **`docs/zones/AGENTS.md`** is down to zones-specific facts:
  - Generated files.
  - Checks.
  - Pack changelog headings.
  - `PACK_FORMAT` as the real pack compatibility check.
- **`docs/books/AGENTS.md`**: the "droplet's Sounds.lua is ephemeral" section is gone, because the site stopped writing it on 2026-09-21. It also no longer claims the pack builds without Postgres.
- **`docs/quests/AGENTS.md`** is deleted. It only repeated the root comment rules.

This PR is stacked on #295: the root guide points at the comment-cleanup skill that #295 adds.

## Verification

Three read-only passes checked each guide's claims against the tree at 48f6ec88. I then spot-checked the facts the rewrite relies on:
- release targets
- `.toc` versions (23 at 3.0.1; packs 2.0.1 and 2.1.2)
- `changelog_for()`
- the zones and books make targets
- `PACK_FORMAT`
- the release tag patterns

Nothing was run. This PR changes only documentation.

## Notes for review

- "Open the PR against `develop`" is written as the rule for everyone. If your own work should still go straight to `master`, say so in the guide.
- Stale wording outside the guides was left alone and still needs fixing:
  - The root `Makefile` header ("two projects", "fifteen" collisions, `rsync --delete`).
  - `make/web.mk`'s header.
  - `apps/web/vitest.config.ts` naming the deleted `history.test.ts`.
  - `README.md:112` listing `packages/`.
  - `naming.py`'s docstring (`{accept|complete}` is missing `progress`).
  - `docs/zones/README.md` citing the removed `make zones-db-up`.
- Zones UI PRs #243 and #251 merged without a version bump or changelog entry. That is exactly what the versioning rule exists to catch.

author: chintanpatel24
body:
## Summary

Fixes the issue where NVIDIA NIM calls fail with:
```
NVIDIA NIM Error (404): {"status":404,"title":"Not Found","detail":"Function '9b96341b-9791-4db9-a00d-4e43aa192a39': Not found for account '...'"}
```
or HTTP 410 Gone (`meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct has reached its end of life`).

### Root Cause
1. `meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct` was hardcoded as the default model across python, go, rust, and c++, but has reached its end of life on NVIDIA NIM and returns 410/404.
2. NVIDIA NIM's `/v1/models` list returns ~80 models, but only ~11 functions are actually active and accessible for the user's account. Picking inactive models resulted in 404 Function not found.

### Key Changes
1. **Dynamic Active Endpoint Discovery:**
   - Adds concurrent probing of candidate models to filter out models returning 404/410/400.
   - Caches active, verified working endpoints.
   - Added `/admin/discover` endpoint and **"Scan & Fetch Working Endpoints"** button in the Admin UI.
2. **Auto-Healing & Resilient Request Forwarding:**
   - If an upstream request fails with 404 Function not found or 410 Gone, the proxy automatically discovers a verified working model (e.g. `meta/llama-3.2-11b-vision-instruct`), switches to it, writes it to `.env`, and retries the request seamlessly without failing Claude Code.
3. **Updated Defaults Across All Runtimes:**
   - Updated default model from deprecated `meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct` to active, verified `meta/llama-3.2-11b-vision-instruct` in Python, Go, Rust, and C++.
   - Replaced dead models in fallback lists with verified models (`meta/llama-3.2-11b-vision-instruct`, `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, `nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b`, etc.).
4. **Interactive Admin Test:**
   - `/admin/test` now sends an actual lightweight chat completion ping to verify the model is accessible and responsive.

## Resumen

Consolida la **Pérdida crediticia esperada (NIIF 9)** en **una sola herramienta** —el motor por cohortes `pce_cohortes_niif9`— y **oculta del catálogo** la versión anterior (`pce_simplificada_niif9`), para que el auditor no vea dos pruebas de lo mismo (decisión del dueño: «deseo que solo quede una prueba, la otra ocúltala»).

El frontend queda como la imagen de referencia: tarjetas de carga **Cartera — Año 1/2/3**, **Anexo inicial de la provisión (sumaria)**, **Mayor de la provisión — Año 1/2/3** (opcionales) y el soporte prospectivo; umbral de incumplimiento 730 días.

## Cambios

- **Anexo inicial = sumaria (RQ-004, requerido):** Código · Descripción · Saldo año anterior · Saldo año actual. De ahí salen la provisión inicial, la registrada y el ajuste (hoja `14_Anexo_inicial`). Sus importes se autoenlazan a la hoja de datos del cliente.
- **Mayores opcionales (RQ-005/006/007):** si no se suben, se entiende que **no hubo movimiento** (constitución, reversión y castigos en cero). Hoja `15_Movimiento_mayores`.
- **`09_Movimiento` reconstruida como reconciliación:** provisión del año anterior + constitución − reversión − castigos = provisión según el movimiento, frente a la registrada; toda por fórmulas a las hojas 14 y 15. La conciliación (08) y el resumen (01) remiten al anexo.
- **Catálogo:** `OCULTAR_PROCESADOR` en `ciclo/servicio.py` oculta `pce_simplificada_niif9` del listado, manteniéndolo **resoluble** para no romper pruebas/fichas ya creadas.

Parity fixes found by comparing the genuine `Extensions.dll` (sha256 `0f8d847b…bb11`) against this reconstruction in IDA. One commit per change.

## Behaviour
- **0x81AA00 event guard** (`FUN_102766c0`). The original refuses a dispatch with no Lua state, or with an event id outside the client's event table (`0xD3F7D0`) or without an entry there. It logs `Blocked invalid FrameScript signal event at 0x0081AA00: …` to Fatal and does **not** run the client function. Ours always ran it.
- **0x81AC90 guard log.** `format=` is printed as a pointer (std::format argument type `0xA`), as the original does, not as the format text.

## Crash report ("Ascension Debug" section)
- **Last FrameScript_SignalEvent** is now recorded by the 0x81AA00 detour, and **Last Loaded M2 Name (CM2Shared)** by the 0x81F8F0 detour (`FUN_102cb000`). Both lines were always empty before. Confirmed in a live client crash report after the change.
- The four recorders the original never writes (M2Cache, SetVertices, ShadowMap, AsyncTexture; their only references are the reader and atexit destructors) are now documented as such.

## Diagnostics (`Logs\*.txt`)
- `AscLogger::WriteStamped` reproduces `FUN_102936d0`: `[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.mmm] <line>`.
- The original's 38 timestamped lines in the ticket and poll handlers, with the original's channels and argument formats. That's GMTicketMgr 0x70B (21), PlayerTicketMgr 0x702 (15) and PlayerPollMgr list/submit (2). Each handler's events and logic are unchanged.

## Testing
- Builds clean with MSVC 2022 x86 (RelWithDebInfo, Ninja). There are no new warnings.
- Ran in the client up to character select and character create with the new build.
- Not covered: the guard's refuse path, and the ticket and poll diagnostics, have not been triggered live.

## Summary

Gap exits could be classified as losses even when the underlying move was profitable, because v3.1 based the outcome on net P/L after costs. The outcome now follows the exit type for target/stop exits and the gross price movement for gaps. body:
Closes #72.

## What was measured first
A 10,000-note vault (25 MB, ~350 words a note), generated by the existing fixture generator (new optional `bodyWords`):

| | 10k notes | 20k notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| vault index cold start | 0.28 s | 0.38 s |
| full-text index cold start | 0.59 s | 1.07 s |
| search p95 | 4-9 ms | 18 ms |
| RSS growth | ~75 MB | ~150 MB |

Everything is inside the issue's budgets (< 2 s, p95 < 50 ms) with a wide margin, and it scales linearly.

## Decision on the snapshot in `.noted/cache/`
**Not built**, deliberately: the cold start it was meant to fix is already ~0.9 s at 10k, and a persisted copy is one more thing that can go stale or corrupt (and has to stay out of Git sync). The rationale and the numbers are in `docs/guide/search.md`. If a real vault ever misses the budget, the benchmark will say so and the snapshot can be added then. Say so if you want it anyway and I'll add it on top.

- `bench/index-scale.bench.ts` + `npm run bench:index` (median of 3 runs) + `scripts/bench-compare.mjs` (budgets, and 20% regression vs. a base result with a noise floor).

- MCP search index: caps lifted from 1,500 files / 50 MB / 2 MB to the app's 20,000 / 200 MB / 20 MB (before, the oldest notes of a big vault were unsearchable for an agent), and after the first build a refresh re-reads only notes whose mtime moved. Real-FS tests for both.

body:
## Summary
Share links keep the whole design after the `#`, so link-preview bots only ever saw `og.png`, and designs couldn't be embedded anywhere (`X-Frame-Options: DENY` everywhere). This PR adds short links with a preview image and an embed page.

**Short links**
- `POST /api/shares` needs sign-in. It is same-origin only, limited by a new `SHARE_LIMITER` (10 per minute, namespace 1011/2011), capped at 64 KiB per document and 100 shares per user.
- `GET /api/shares/:id` works signed out. `DELETE /api/shares/:id` is owner only. `GET /api/me/shares` lists your shares.
- Ids are 10 random base62 characters.

**Preview pages**
- `GET /s/:id` is a small page with og/twitter tags, a canonical URL and oEmbed discovery. It forwards to `/app/?s=<id>`.
- `GET /s/:id.png` serves the preview with a one-year immutable cache, and redirects to `/og.png` when there is none.

**Preview images**
- The browser renders a 1200×630 PNG with the existing PNG export, falling back to half size and then to no image above 300 KB.
- The Worker checks the PNG signature, the chunk order and the dimensions (at most 2400 px).
- Images are stored as a D1 BLOB (migration `0010_shares.sql`). No new paid service.

**Privacy**
- Shares are included in Download my data and are deleted with the account. `docs/PRIVACY.md` is updated.

**Editor**
- Share is now a menu: Copy link, Short link with preview (signed in), Embed (copies an `<iframe>`), and Your short links (list, copy, delete).
- The long-link warning now suggests a short link.

**Embed page**
- A new read-only `/embed/` page shows the diagram and the use-case player, without CodeMirror.
- It takes `?s=` or `#code=`, plus `?theme=light|dark`, and has an "Open in Proschi" link.
- Framing is relaxed for `/embed/*` only, in `_headers`.
- `GET /api/oembed?url=` answers for `/s/<id>` and `/embed/` links.

**Docs**
- New docs page `docs/SHARING.md`; `backend/README.md` and CHANGELOG are updated.

## Deploy
Nothing to do by hand. The deploy to `main` applies the migration and creates the new limiter from `wrangler.jsonc`.

## Notes
- Migration `0010` and limiter namespace `1011`/`2011` were picked because `0009` and `1010` are taken by #111 (usage counts).
- Notion and Medium only auto-embed providers registered with Iframely or Embedly. The `<iframe>` snippet works anywhere that accepts one.
- A deleted share's image may stay in caches for up to a year; `docs/PRIVACY.md` says so.

- backend: typecheck, 169 tests
- frontend: lint, `tsc -b`, `npm run build`, `npm run build:accounts`, vitest. Two game tests timed out while the shared machine was heavily loaded; they pass with a longer timeout.
- Playwright: 144 passed, including new e2e tests for the embed page and the share menu (signed in, signed out, `?s=`).

author: queso
body:
Closes #109 together with #110. **Stacked on #110**: the base is `feat/109-rewrite-detection`, so this diff shows only the named-agent work. Merge #110 first; GitHub then retargets this to `main`.

## What changes

`agent-sdk` stations can run named agents and load plugin dirs, the same engine config `claude-headless` uses (`CONDUIT_HARNESS_<NAME>_AGENT`, `CONDUIT_HARNESS_<NAME>_PLUGIN_DIRS`, a station's `agent:`, a critic's `check.critic.agent`).

- `AgentSdkHarnessAdapterConfig` gains `agent` and `pluginDirs`; `harness-adapter.ts` lets `agent-sdk` take the two env vars. `assertUsablePluginDirs` is exported from the claude adapter and shared.
- `resolveAgentDefinition` uses `resolveClaudePluginAgent`, so the binding stamp hashes the same file as on `claude-headless` (tested). The existing load-time and dispatch-time checks and `computeAgentAwarePromptTemplateVersion` apply unchanged, maker and critic.
- The SDK gets `agent` (station over default) and `plugins` (one local entry per dir).

## Fail closed when the CLI did not load the agent

On the SDK path an unknown agent does not fail: the CLI runs its default agent and reports success (spike on #21). Two checks:

- Every `system`/`init` message must list the agent in `agents`. A miss aborts and kills the CLI.
- Every main-thread call (no `agent_id`) must carry the agent as `agent_type`. A miss denies with `continue: false`, journals a `gate-decision` hold with code `agent_not_loaded`, and bills the result the CLI emits. Subagent calls are exempt.

Both end with `HARNESS_GATE_HOLD_CODE`, so the executor holds the card without spending an attempt, as it does when the kernel cannot resolve the agent at dispatch. The executor's hold reason therefore starts "harness tool gate held station ... for a human:", followed by the adapter message naming the agent.

`claude -p --agent nosuch:agent` still exits 1 on 2.1.291; the claude adapter comment now says so and points at the SDK difference.

## Merge with #110

Merged `feat/109-rewrite-detection` in (4e06286). The two hold paths share one `stopAfterHold` timer helper; `startHold` sets `st.held` and calls it. `docs/harness-containment.md` keeps #110's hooks paragraph and adds the named-agents subsection after it; CLAUDE.md keeps both edits.

## Tests

- `harness-adapter-agent-sdk-agent.test.ts` (new): SDK options, station over default, both fail-closed signals, matching `agent_type`, subagent exemption, same hash as claude-headless, plugin-dir checks, registry wiring.
- `executor-agent-sdk-agent.test.ts` (new): `runExecutor` with the real adapter and a scripted query, maker and critic: agent reaches the SDK, span records the agent SHA-256, a CLI miss holds after one call, a definition removed before dispatch holds without calling the SDK.
- `load-harness-agent.test.ts`: flow load accepts an agent on `agent-sdk` with plugin dirs configured, rejects it without.
- Blackbox: the fake SDK reads `--agent` and `--plugin-dir`, lists agents at init and sends `agent_type`; `agent-sdk-named-agent.test.ts` covers a loaded agent (done) and a dropped one (held at attempt 0, the Write never runs).

## Live check (claude 2.1.290, haiku, merged branch, real adapter, a fixture plugin)

- `spikeplug:maker`: the gate allowed the Write, no rewrite hold, file written, usage billed ($0.022).
- `spikeplug:nosuch`: held after 584 ms on the init check, no file, no assistant message.

Not verified: an agent's frontmatter `model:` and `tools:` against the station model and `allowedTools`, agents listed in a manifest `agents` field, nested subagents.

typecheck, blackbox typecheck, `bun test src/` (4268 pass), blackbox (122 pass), mutation check and docs check pass on the merged branch.

body:
**Builds on PR #136** (the slot `local_names`), so its base is `local-names-94`: this PR shows only the #26 change. When #136 is merged into `dev` (and its branch deleted), GitHub retargets this PR to `dev`.

**Problem.** FAIRe v1.0 copied MIxS's swapped size-fraction definitions. Example: a water sample poured through a 20 µm mesh (pre-filter), then caught on a 0.22 µm filter.
- `size_frac_low` held **20** (the pre-filter, i.e. the **upper** bound), despite its name.
- `size_frac` held **0.22** (the filter, the **lower** bound).

**Fix.** Each slot keeps its meaning, values and `faire:` number, and takes the corrected MIxS name (GenomicsStandardsConsortium/mixs#566, reopened as #1414):

| Holds | v1.0 name | New name | `faire:` | Source / close mapping |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| pre-filter (20 µm) | `size_frac_low` | **`size_frac_up`** | 0000239 (unchanged) | `mixs:0000736` |
| filter (0.22 µm) | `size_frac` | **`size_frac_low`** | 0000284 (unchanged) | `mixs:0000735` |

- `size_frac_up`: title "size-fraction upper threshold"; description unchanged (it already described the pre-filter).
- `size_frac_low`: title "size-fraction lower threshold"; description = the corrected MIxS definition, "Refers to the mesh/pore size used to retain the sample. Materials smaller than the size threshold are excluded from the sample." Broad mapping to MIxS `size_frac` kept.
- Both: `modifications_made` gains `description` (MIxS's current text is still swapped); a comment records the v1.0 name and the MIxS issues; `local_names`, `classes.yaml` and `term_review_issues.csv` updated.
- Commits: two pure file renames first (so `git log --follow` tracks each slot's meaning), then the content change.

**For the v2.0.0 release notes:** the name `size_frac_low` changes meaning. Convert data: old `size_frac_low` -> `size_frac_up`; old `size_frac` -> `size_frac_low`. No alias can carry this, since `size_frac_low` is still a slot name.

**Checked:** `linkml-lint` finds no problems on a scratch build; both examples (20, 0.22) validate. Review issues: FAIR-eDNA/FAIRe-GSC-TDWG-term-review#280 (was `size_frac_low`), FAIR-eDNA/FAIRe-GSC-TDWG-term-review#279 (was `size_frac`).

Closes #26 (closed by hand with `fixed-on-dev` once on `dev`).

body:
**Description**

Moves the one-device check (does this install appear as exactly one device in RomM after pairing?) out of `PairCommand` and into `PairingService.VerifyDeviceAsync`, which returns a `DeviceCheck` (outcome and message). The console prints it as before. The gamepad pairing screen now runs it too and shows it as a "Device check" row under the paired summary, or a "Warning" row when the list could not be read or the count is not one. The check reports only; it never undoes a stored pairing.

Fixes #393

**Step 0 verdict: FIX.** On `d9a06ab` the check lived only in `src/RomMBat.Agent/Commands/PairCommand.cs:298-346` (`VerifyDeviceAsync`), and `src/RomMBat.UI/Screens/PairingViewModel.cs:254-267` stopped at `CompleteAsync`, so a pairing made from the controller never ran it.

**Decisions for veto**

- `PairingViewModel`'s internal test constructor now takes `Func<Uri, string?, RomMConnection>`: a null token means the bare pairing connection, and a token means the authenticated one for the check. One seam instead of two.
- The UI shows Paired first and fills in the check row when it returns, rather than holding the paired screen back for one more request.
- A mismatch or an unreadable list stays a warning, as the console treated it, rather than turning the stage to Refused: the token is already stored and works.
- Console messages kept their words; the two warnings now start with a capital after `Warning: `, because the message is shared with the UI row.
- Labels: `bug` (the UI skipped a check the console runs) and `semver:patch` (a fix; no migration, no re-pair).

**AI assistance disclosure**

Written entirely by Claude Code (Opus 5.5), including this description: the Step 0 ruling, code, tests, docs and the hands-on pass. The maintainer has not yet reviewed it.

**Checklist**

- [x] I've disclosed any AI assistance above
- [x] I've tested the changes locally
- [x] I've updated relevant comments
- [ ] I've assigned reviewers for this PR
- [x] I've added unit tests that cover the changes
- [x] `pwsh -File tools/pre-pr.ps1` passes: build, tests, the docs check and the guide build (trunk skipped in a worktree; CI runs it)
- [x] `cd reference && python3 verify.py` still passes

**Invariants**

- [x] No token, secret or instance URL appears in the diff
- [x] Every new user-visible string is reachable without a mouse (the check row is on the pairing screen the pad reaches)

**Tests**

`DeviceCheckTests` (new) pairs against the stub, then asserts the check's outcome: one listed match verifies; zero or two is a `Mismatch` naming the count and leaves the pairing stored; without `devices.read` it is `Skipped` and never requests `/api/devices`; a 403, or a 200 whose body is not JSON, is `Unverified`; and the connection is opened with the token pairing stored. `PairingScreenTests.A_paired_screen_runs_the_device_check_with_the_stored_token` asserts the screen reaches Paired with a `OneDevice` check, and that only the check's connection carries the token.

**Hands-on**

Build: `issue-393-device-check c768a6b`, deployed 2026-10-06T13:47:58 to the agent tree with `Publish-ToAgentTree`.

- **CLI:** `rommbat-agent pair` against the test server, approved with the approver token as `Connect-AgentTree` does (database kept, so it was a re-pair). Exit 0, and it printed `Verified: the token works and this install is one device in RomM.`
- **Gamepad UI:** `Start-RomMBatUI`, then Down ×7 to Pair again, Enter, Start. The code screen showed a code and the QR (`probe-output/handson-20261006/135001-ui-393-waiting.png`). After approving that code with the approver token, the Paired screen showed Device, Granted, and **Device check: Verified: the token works and this install is one device in RomM.** (`135019-ui-393-paired.png`). The device id matched the CLI pair's, so RomM kept one device for the tree.
- After R1.1 (`d3b5e3c`, deployed 2026-10-06T14:00:17): the CLI pair was re-run and still printed `Verified: ...`, exit 0.
- To skip typing the address on the on-screen keyboard, which this change does not touch, `ui.last_server_origin` was seeded in the tree's store.

**Docs**

Moved: `wiki/getting-started/pairing.md` (the couch flow now says the check runs and that a warning there leaves the pairing in place), `docs/architecture/identity.md` (names `PairingService.VerifyDeviceAsync` as the check that proves re-pairing keeps one device).
Read and already correct: `src/RomMBat.Agent/CLAUDE.md` (the rule this restores), the `romm-api` skill's device scopes, `docs/design/verification.md`. `wiki/reference/cli.md` is not affected: `--help` did not change.

**Compatibility**

No change to the RomM or RetroBat floor.

**Platforms certified**

None touched.

**Verified / not verified**

Verified: unit and screen tests, the full `pre-pr.ps1` suite, and the CLI and UI success paths on the deployed build against the real server. Not driven on hardware: the Mismatch, Unverified and Skipped rows on the gamepad screen. They need a server answering with a duplicate device, a refusal or a narrowed grant, and are covered by `DeviceCheckTests` only.

Not part of this change: the paired screen still shows the QR and code above the summary, as it does on main.

## What changed, and why

A planning document, no code: `docs/reflection-plan-2026-10.md` (named per `docs/AGENTS.md`'s `*-plan.md` convention), written after #36 merged and CI went green on `main`, answering "what does the codebase owe before it grows further, and what did the last three days teach about how it is worked on" — then peer-reviewed twice before being offered here (§8 of the document).

**Baseline, measured at `9c4b6e9`** (every figure regenerable from Appendix A; all reproduced independently in review): `cli.py` 1029 lines; 15 of 266 functions over 60 lines; 7 over complexity 10 (ratchet maxima: complexity 15, branches 15, statements 57, arguments 6); 5 magic values, 3 boolean positionals, 37 + 110 `E501`, 12 `PERF401`; `print` absent from every library module but `cli.py` yet unenforced; `mypy --strict` two `type-arg` errors away; `tests/` (17,366 lines) outside mypy entirely (~52 real errors once the module-mapping blocker is bypassed); 52 public symbols without docstrings; `scaffold.py` writes files with no logger; three unreferenced symbols; `ci.yml`'s 10 jobs with no top-level `permissions`, no `timeout-minutes`, no `concurrency`, every action on a floating major tag and the publisher on a branch ref; the Python version spelled eleven times across three files; the matrix stopping at 3.13 while 3.10 reaches end-of-life this month; a root-user, tag-pinned Dockerfile; seven Dependabot major bumps open since 2026-09-19 on a base two merges behind; coverage floors 7–9 points under measured; **18 of 44 spec headers say DRAFT, shipped packages among them**; the ladder runs the full suite twice and CI six times — 235 s single-process, 66 s on four xdist workers.

**Nine workstreams, six milestones, ten decisions.** W1 CI hardening and the Dependabot batch (plus the support window and the container); W2 `cli/` decomposition with pure-move proofs, `cli/__main__.py` in the first commit, the three decomposition guards made recursive and AC-DG-8's test name kept; W3 complexity by ratchet to ruff's defaults; W4 constants and lint families; W5 dead and drifting code with a `dumps_stable` that does **not** sort keys (D10 — the golden hashes depend on insertion order); W6 strict mypy, tests under mypy, docstrings by ratchet, one logger, property tests for the two readers that lack them, a separate `make audit`; W7 one-run coverage **proven with a combined run** (scoped sums reproduce 2276/2292, 744/762, 823/857, 278/298 exactly; the unscoped total is the diluted 98.4 %) and stated as superseding R-GTC-9, C-GTC-4, R-GTC-12, DEC-GTC-009/013 of `gate-tools-coverage` by name, floors set from the minimum CI leg, in-process loops for the subprocess-heavy tests; W8 subpackages behind facades, archive awareness as a feature package first (`find_spec_files` would drop archived specs silently and `detect.py:710` would count `archive/` as a package), a spec-status report, document retirement, branch protection stated, SBOM deferred with the reason; W9 a SessionStart hook that also verifies signing, verifier scans, a release skill.

**Peer review (§8).** Round 1, self-verification of every [Likely] marker: ten confirmed, two overturned (D2's mechanism; W8.2's premise), five debts added, one assumption replaced by a measurement. Round 2, an independent adversarial reviewer: 17 findings (6 HIGH), all accepted and applied — two silent reversals of recorded decisions now named (W7.2 vs `gate-tools-coverage`; the line budget vs `decompose-god-files`, now a report per D9), one byte-contract change caught (`sort_keys`), three false "unchanged" claims fixed, seven baseline errata corrected. Reviewer's verdict before corrections: "ready with corrections — not mergeable as written"; its three insisted-on corrections are in.

Pointers: README lists the plan beside the two reviews; `docs/next-steps.md` points to it as the sequencing of its own items 18 and 20–23.

author: mstarks01
body:
Closes #1415.

## What changes

litellm 1.104.0 is the first release with Opus 5.5 entries. This PR pins it and names Opus 5.5 on the strong tier of two rows:

| Row | base | strong |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `anthropic` | `claude-sonnet-5` | `claude-opus-5-5` |
| `bedrock` | `global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` | `global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5` |

`REFERENCE_MODELS`, the template in `config/model_tiers.toml`, `docs/First-Run.md`, the live workflows and the docs that name the pair move together.

## Facts the bump moved

The offline suite failed in 24 tests on the bump alone. Each failure was a pinned fact about litellm. This PR corrects each fact:

1. **Served build on Gemini.** The Gemini transformation now reads `modelVersion` from the response body. `vertex` and `gemini` are now `provider_reported`. `tests/test_identity.py` drives the installed transformation and confirms it. The fingerprints for these two rows move, and they also move because `litellm` is in `BUILD_DISTRIBUTIONS`.
2. **Unmapped models.** `get_model_info` raises `ModelNotMappedError` for an unmapped model. For a name that matches a family rule (for example `gpt-6-unreleased`), it returns a guessed entry with no price and a `key` that is not in `litellm.model_cost`. `model_info` now returns `None` for both shapes. Without this change, the conformance matrix would call a guessed model "known". `evals/harness/prices.py` reads `model_cost` directly, so a guessed entry cannot reach a price.
3. **A new remote fetch.** `LITELLM_LOCAL_AUTOROUTER_PRESETS` turns off a new fetch. The service now sets it with the other switches.
4. **Bedrock Claude 5 goes to the tool path.** The map now marks every Claude 5 on Bedrock as not native, which agrees with the AWS model cards. Opus 5.5 also refuses a forced tool, because its thinking is always on. So the Bedrock strong tier runs `offered_tool`, then `prompt`. A new test pins that ladder. The native-path and forced-tool tests now name `global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`, and a guard test checks that this model takes both paths.
5. **OpenRouter structured output.** The map now answers structured output for `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6`. The "silent capability" test uses `anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet`, which is still silent.
6. **Alias rule.** `gpt-5.6-sol` now carries a `source` URL that `gpt-5.6` does not. The alias rule ignores `source`, as it ignores the `supports_*` flags.

Two smaller corrections: the conformance docstring stated a count (2029) that was wrong before the bump, so it now says "more than half". Two offline probes passed an `int` as `Logging(start_time=...)`; 1.104.0 types it as a `datetime`.

The boto3 range in the `bedrock` extra still matches litellm 1.104.0's own requirement.

## Framework and vendor parity

No framework package changes. Every vendor row was checked by the existing registry tests (`test_vendor_neutrality.py`, `test_identity.py`, `test_conformance.py`). The `served_trust` change applies to both Gemini routes, `vertex` and `gemini`, because both use the same transformation.

## Re-baseline

The strong tier is a new model on two rows. A Baseline sealed on `claude-opus-5` does not certify a run on `claude-opus-5-5`. A new Baseline needs a paid run, and this PR does not make one.

## Evidence (offline)

- Full suite: 11668 passed, 142 skipped, exit 0 (main: 11665 collected tests passed; this PR adds three tests).
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `mypy` pass.
- `evals.harness.run replay` over `evals/emissions/*.json` gives the same output as on main. The only difference is the `clean` flag of the work tree.
- Pre-merge review: I read the diff against the five defect classes. Finding 2 above is a class 3 defect (a shape not listed) that the bump caused, and this PR fixes it.

The fix is verified by the listed offline evidence; its live quality effect remains unmeasured.

author: proggeramlug
body:
Refs #11919. node:sqlite becomes native-payload objects, and the shared native callback path gets cheaper (owner decisions 84 and 87).

**Removes:**
- NODE_SQLITE_CUSTOM_FUNCTIONS, _AGGREGATES and _ACTIVE_AGGREGATES, with their root scanner and thread-exit hooks;
- the node handle producers and dispatch-hub arms;
- the native-table receiver rows (4 receiver-less rows remain);
- HIR native-instance tracking for sqlite;
- node_stmt_session.rs, node_tag_store.rs and KIND_VALUES_NULL_DONE.

The ledgers only go down: native_handle 199/186 → 196/183, result ledger 252/228 → 236/215, unrooted-local 339 → 315.

**Changes:**
- **JS throws:** a throw from JS never unwinds through SQLite frames, and no lock is held across a C call. Before this, a UDF calling `db.exec` deadlocked.
- **Statements own their compiled `sqlite3_stmt`, as in node.** The authorizer runs once per `prepare()`, and `expandedSQL` and `columns()` read the compiled statement. A shared `live` token finalizes each statement exactly once.
- **Callback path:** one owner check per callback, a direct call into the body, and catch savepoints reused across callbacks within one native call. The payload method dispatch drops two redundant descriptor scans.
- **Birth:** payload instances are born in their final shape. A per-site memo of (ShapeId) is validated on each use.
- **Buffer API:** BLOB results are built through the B1 byte API, and the layout ratchet goes down by 2.
- **Build:** the bundled SQLite is built with `SQLITE_DEFAULT_MEMSTATUS=0`, matching node 26's `compile_options`.

**Micro-benchmarks** (instructions vs the pre-conversion base):

| Micro | Change |
|---|---|
| sq_udf | −0.18% |
| sq_ins | −37.5% |
| sq_auth | +6.4% |

sq_auth's base compiled each statement twice and ran the authorizer twice, so its output differed from node's. The remaining cost is SQLite lookaside overflow while statements stay alive until GC, plus the full collections that finalize payload cells. That is accepted under PERF_POLICY rule 4 (decision 87), with the pacing follow-up in MEMORY_PLAN item 6.

**Tests** (main 899aecd6f9 merged):
- runtime 5188/0, codegen passes;
- stdlib: the same 2 thread-exit failures as main;
- check_buffer_layout: 0 new sites;
- SQLite gap tests all equal node. Two that main fails now pass. The perry-only test equals its committed expectation.
- Sabotages are red for T4, T5, T6-all, T7, T8b, T10, T12, L1 and N1–N4.

**Programs** (output == node): tsc −0.03%, fastify −0.05%, Zod −0.03%; the others are within ±0.01%.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added synchronous `node:sqlite` support for databases, prepared statements, iterators, SQL tag stores, sessions, callbacks, and backups.
  * Added database close-and-reopen support, with clear errors for statements from an earlier open.
  * Enabled SQLite callback reentrancy and deferred database closure until callbacks finish.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Callback exceptions are rethrown as their original JavaScript values after SQLite operations return.
  * Statements are finalized when closed or released, and authorization checks occur when preparing statements.
* **Compatibility**
  * Bun SQLite operations continue to be supported.

## Complete user outcome
Identify original records blocking a TrueFlow workflow, export bounded value-free diagnostics, correct input or explicitly revise the recipe, rerun and obtain reviewed CSV/JSON output. Browser, CLI, MCP stdio and authenticated loopback HTTP share one validator.

## Parallel work reconciled — no outstanding overlap blocker
Denys explicitly requested autonomous resolution. The complete first-pair proposal at `2d7d65f09da4279a29a62651e4eaee414c181f02` (recorded in #9) was reviewed and incorporated through merge commit **5d896fd565322bc05d774f715aa53d88a4299cb2**, with both original branch heads retained as parents. No force-push, reset or loss of branch history.

Resolution: preserve published v0.4.0 machine error strings, successful shapes and tool count. Add A/B, first conflicting record and all bounded locations through structured diagnostics. The browser's concise EN/IT/ES status uses those trusted fields for the parallel proposal's actionable guidance, not regex parsing of newly changed machine messages. Its original-record, A/B, first-pair, mapped/composite-key and no-value-leak behaviors have regression coverage. Only v0.5.0 is proposed; the overlapping v0.4.1 candidate is not independently shipped. One validation engine, no duplicate registry or implementation.

## Implemented boundaries
- Empty/repeated comparison keys and require/unique recipe gates identify source, step, original logical record, first occurrence and 1-based column positions at the failing schema.
- Count all bad rows at the FIRST failing dataset/gate; list at most 100 with an explicit truncation flag. Later gates/datasets are not claimed as validated. No cell/key values, header names or paths in these diagnostics.
- Browser panel, real diagnostic JSON export, keyboard focus and edit invalidation. Data exports stay blocked until success.
- CLI opt-in --diagnostics-json: structured stdout, stable stderr, exit 1, no requested output/report files on validation failure.
- HTTP 422 optional diagnostic with closed schema; MCP isError remains true, legacy first text code plus matching structuredContent/serialized JSON.
- Private WeakMaps prevent arbitrary error metadata from becoming diagnostics.
- Fix falsy/null recipe columns bypassing validation and failed late recipe import leaving intervening output exportable.

## Actually verified locally on the resolved exact tree
**Tree 84504699396f0030d4663ff4468275bdf6b0f366** equals the uploaded tree exactly. Candidate head **5d896fd565322bc05d774f715aa53d88a4299cb2**.
- npm run validate: **399 passed, 0 failed**, Node 22.16.0.

- Direct-file navigation failed locally with ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ADMINISTRATOR. In-memory tests do not prove navigation; observe GitHub's direct-file browser job independently.
The standalone #9 head also passed GitHub run 37520130160, but that is not a substitute for checks on this combined head. Merge only after all relevant checks on the current head pass and main/parallel heads are rechecked.

## Licensing and deployment
First-party work under the owner's instructions, not an outside contribution. Personal private use free; all business/professional use paid. No new dependencies, public endpoint, paid service, secrets, outbound transfer, arbitrary path access, shell or hidden persistence. AI clients may still retain/forward input/results.

After merge, verify v0.5.0 tag/assets and Clean merged branches. #9 should only be cleaned after GitHub verifies its indirect merge and unchanged head. Other unrelated drafts remain untouched. No release is claimed before it actually exists.

**Feinschliff**
- Folgefragen-Pillen mit Hover/Fokus in Akzentfarbe (`allm-pill-accent`, `ON_ACCENT_TEXT`).
- Begrüßungsblase (inkl. Datenschutz) bleibt dauerhaft als erstes Element über dem Verlauf (`PanelGreeting`), auch nach Reload; nur bei `greetingStyle: bubble`.
- Teaser bis 3 Zeilen statt Ellipse nach 2.
- `onlineDot` nicht Standard; neue Standardtexte de/en („… und ich finde passende Angebote.", „Mitarbeitende der Einrichtung …"); Begrüßungsblase mit zwei Absätzen, max. 80 % Breite.

author: sethjjarrett-cell
body:
Fixes the verb-table bug found while building chunks.

**Preview:** https://raw.githack.com/sethjjarrett-cell/idioma/verb-tables/index.html

## The bug
- Any verb without a hand-written table was conjugated as fully regular. That produced forms like *conoco*, *dole*, *cerran*, *busce* and *leió*.
- The verb drills were never affected, because they only use the hand-listed irregulars and the three example verbs.
- What was affected: the form index behind tap-a-word, and the check that decides when a sentence is within reach.
  - Real forms such as *conozco*, *duele* and *cierran* were unknown.
  - Some bogus forms counted as known.

## The fix
`conjugate` in `verbs.js` now applies these rules to every verb in the bank:
- **Stem changes:** e→ie, o→ue, u→ue and e→i, in the stressed persons. -ir verbs also change in the preterite (*sintió*, *murió*) and in the nosotros subjunctive (*durmamos*).
- **Irregular yo forms,** with the subjunctive built on them: *conozco/conozca*, *sigo/siga*, *caigo*, *cojo*, *elijo*. The g-verbs get the same, so the subjunctive gives *tenga*, *diga*, *salga*.
- **Spelling changes that keep a sound:** *busqué*, *llegué*, *empecé*, *juegue*, *empiece*.
- **y between vowels:** *leyó*, *creyeron*, *cayó*.
- **A few specific cases:**
  - stressed í: *confío*;
  - *suponer* follows *poner*;
  - a handful of forms listed outright: *vi/vio*, *oyes*, *río*;
  - accented infinitives lose the accent in the future: *oiré*.
- **Reflexive infinitives** conjugate without their *se*: *levanto*, *despierto*.

## Effect on the word index
- About 1,000 real forms are added and 288 bogus ones removed.
- Noun plurals now compete by teaching order, like other forms. Without this, *casas* read as "you marry" (casarse) once reflexives conjugated; it's back to "houses".
- Every word whose owner changed is a genuine two-way homograph, settled by which word is taught first:
  - *juego*: I play, or game;
  - *vuelo*: I fly, or flight;
  - *cenas*: you dine, or dinners;
  - *viajes*: you travel (subjunctive), or trips.

## Tests
- New `test-verbs.mjs` (48 checks): 45 hand-checked rows, one per pattern, plus a sweep of every verb in the bank for the shapes a missed rule leaves behind.
- `test-tap.mjs` now closes the word pop-up before pressing Check. A verb's pop-up shows extra rows and can sit over the button, which made the test flaky.
- Every suite passes except `test-ui9`, which already fails on main.
- `test-audio` failed once in 35 runs. I couldn't reproduce or capture it, and it doesn't touch anything this PR changes.

author: flipperspectives-crypto
body:
Hard review of the whole repo plus fixes for the highest-impact findings. The full findings (with repro commands and their output), the plan, and the proposals are in [REVIEW.md](REVIEW.md).

Built by Lauren Flipo.

## What changed

**Security**
- `release`, `quarantine`, `/billing/create_key` and `/billing/topup` now require `X-Slime-Admin: <token>` (`SLIMEFLOW_ADMIN_TOKEN`, or a random token printed at startup). Before this change, any process or any web page could unfreeze an agent.
- CORS headers now go only on the sim endpoints. `GET /agents` used to serve stored secrets to any origin.
- Secret-shaped values are redacted before they reach history, events, or `GET /agents`.
- `user_confirmed` must be a JSON boolean. Previously `"false"` counted as confirmed.
- Billing accepts only finite amounts. A NaN topup used to give unlimited charges.

**Correctness**
- Quarantines persist across restarts (`AgentGuard(state_path=...)`, server `--state` / `--no-state`).
- Decay uses a monotonic clock, and `release()` restarts decay from now.
- Scores are rounded to 12 decimals before the unchanged `>= 0.6` comparison.
- Threshold is validated, blocked attempts are logged, and unknown kinds are tagged (with an optional `strict_kinds`).
- Secret detection now also catches sk-proj, sk-ant, AWS, GitHub, Slack, JWT, and any PEM private key.
- The HTTP server is threaded, with timeouts, body limits, and input validation.
- The billing store loads lazily (a bad file no longer breaks `import slimeflow`), skips bad rows, and writes files with mode 0600.
- The Python sim grid is scaled to 0–1 like `server.jl`. `server.jl` now fills the swarm with Harvesters and skips quarantined agents when spawning rogues. The Julia change is untested: there's no Julia or CUDA on the review machine.

**Behavior kept and pinned by tests**
- First unconfirmed delete is allowed (0.38). A second within 80 s is blocked, and the agent stays frozen until `release()`.
- Unconfirmed `code_exec` scores 0.30. Two are allowed (0.598 at 1 s apart). The third freezes the agent if the first and third are 150 s or less apart (75 s per gap when even).
- Default threshold, decay, and RISK values are unchanged.

**Docs:** README, the SDK README (the PyPI page), MONETIZE, OUTREACH_DMS and CONTRIBUTING are corrected to match the code. REVIEW.md lists each change.

**Version:** 0.3.0 in source, because the HTTP admin endpoints changed. Not built or published.

**Breaking for HTTP users:** admin calls need the token, and a string `user_confirmed` now gets a 400. `check()` no longer creates records for unknown agents.

## Tests

`cd python-sdk && ruff check . && python -m pytest -q` → 131 passed, 9 skipped (the skips are live sim tests). With `SLIMEFLOW_BILLING=0 python -m slimeflow.server --no-state` running, `tests/test_client.py` → 26 passed. Passing on Python 3.9, 3.12 and 3.13 locally. The existing CI runs the new tests as-is.

## CI change not included

The push token doesn't have GitHub's `workflow` scope, so `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is unchanged. To add the lint step and the live sim tests, apply this (web editor, or `gh auth refresh -s workflow` and push):

```diff
diff --git a/.github/workflows/ci.yml b/.github/workflows/ci.yml
index 5aa644b..3d61c66 100644
--- a/.github/workflows/ci.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/ci.yml
@@ -21,7 +21,10 @@ jobs:
       - name: Install SDK + test deps
         run: |
           python -m pip install --upgrade pip
-          pip install -e "python-sdk/[all]" pytest
+          pip install -e "python-sdk/[all]" pytest ruff
+      - name: Lint
+        working-directory: python-sdk
+        run: ruff check .
       - name: Run tests
         working-directory: python-sdk
         run: python -m pytest -q
@@ -36,6 +39,12 @@ jobs:
           assert r["quarantined"], r
           print("quarantined as expected:", r["reason"], r["anomaly"])
           PY
+      - name: Live sim tests against the Python server
+        working-directory: python-sdk
+        run: |
+          SLIMEFLOW_BILLING=0 python -m slimeflow.server --no-state &
+          for i in $(seq 1 20); do curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:8080/ping && break; sleep 0.5; done
+          python -m pytest -q tests/test_client.py -rs
 
   pypi-install:
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
```

author: itkadr-git
body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip is the open source app people use to manage AI agents for work
> - The release-freeze gate watches the newest release tag and its CI before cutting a release
> - `sort -V` in `newest_release_tag()` ranks `myr-vX.Y.Z-rc.N` above `myr-vX.Y.Z`
> - After the final tag is pushed the gate keeps watching the stale rc's green CI, so the freeze never engages on the final cut
> - The benefit is the freeze gate follows the final tag and a release cut is no longer masked by a stale rc

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

**What happened?**
After a final release tag `myr-vX.Y.Z` is pushed, the release-freeze script still selects the older `myr-vX.Y.Z-rc.N` as the newest release tag. The gate then watches the rc's green CI instead of the final's, and the freeze never engages on the final cut.

**Expected behavior**
A final tag outranks its own release candidates. Once `myr-vX.Y.Z` exists, the freeze gate tracks `myr-vX.Y.Z` and ignores the green CI of its rc.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Push tag `myr-v1.6.5-rc.4` and let its CI go green.
2. Push final tag `myr-v1.6.5`.
3. Run the release-freeze gate: it selects `myr-v1.6.5-rc.4` and never starts the freeze for `myr-v1.6.5`.

## What Changed

- `scripts/myrmidon/release/release-freeze.sh`: numeric per-field tag sort with an rc flag; a final tag outranks its release candidates.
- `scripts/myrmidon/release/release-freeze.test.mjs`: two regression tests — final outranks rc; a green rc CI does not cancel the freeze of a fresh final.
- 2 files changed, +42/-2.

## Verification

- `node --test scripts/myrmidon/release/release-freeze.test.mjs scripts/myrmidon/release/release-publish.test.mjs scripts/myrmidon/release/collect-fragments.test.mjs` — all tests pass (92 pass, 0 fail in the devbuild image on the pre-rebase base; 81 pass, 0 fail on the rebased head locally, same three files).
- The patch applies cleanly on current main; the branch contains exactly the two files above.

## Risks

- Low risk: the change is confined to tag-selection logic of the release-freeze script and is covered by new regression tests.

## Model Used

None — human-authored fix relayed from an internal review follow-up.

body:
## Summary

- **`~/.himmel/eval-runs.jsonl`**: an append-only ledger, one row per eval run.
  - It is registered in `scripts/observability/ledgers.json`.
  - The schema is documented in the `scripts/eval/lib/eval_runs.py` header and in `scripts/eval/README.md`.
  - Each row carries:
    - the min envelope: `v`, `ts`, `host`, `source`, `kind`;
    - `eval`, `run_id`, `gitsha`, `confighash` (which excludes the git sha), `config`, `model`/`lane` and `n`;
    - `metrics`, plus `reps`, `ci`, `ci_level` and `ci_method`;
    - per-case `cases`, `artifact`, `status` (`ok`/`partial`/`inconclusive`) and `meta`.
  - Those fields serve HIMMEL-4648 (reps, bootstrap CIs, calibration), HIMMEL-4650 (paired per-query compare) and HIMMEL-4652 (Prometheus exporter) without a migration.
- **One shared writer** in `scripts/eval/lib/eval_runs.py`: Python stdlib, with a CLI for the bash evals.
  - It validates each row, refusing non-finite numbers, and writes it with a single `O_APPEND` write whose length is checked.
  - lane-quality, qmd-quality, guard-corpus `diff` and scrape-bench each call it once per run.
  - A ledger error only warns; it never changes an eval's result.
- **`scripts/eval/eval-compare <eval> [--baseline <run-id> | --best-of N]`** prints the delta per metric, using thresholds from the `scripts/eval/eval-compare.json` config table.
  - It exits 1 when a metric falls past its noise band: the CI bound when present, else the threshold from the table.
  - It exits 3 when there is nothing to compare: no candidate, no ok baseline, a candidate that is not ok, no gated metric on both sides, or a malformed line that may be the newest run.

The qmd-quality backfill was skipped on purpose. The four stored outputs carry no git sha, so a backfilled row would get the current HEAD, which is the wrong provenance.

Tests write only to a temp ledger (they export `HIMMEL_EVAL_RUNS_LEDGER`) and make no model calls or bank draws. Each eval's test runs a fixture and checks that a valid row is appended.

/pr-check ran 3 rounds; every finding has a terminal verdict. Lower-severity findings are deferred to v1.0.2c:
- HIMMEL-4658: qmd corpus identity in the hashed config.
- HIMMEL-4659: repo-relative hook identity in guard-corpus, and refusing a self-baseline in eval-compare.

## Test plan

- `scripts/eval/test-eval-runs.sh`: unchanged fixture exits 0, seeded regression exits 1, plus the validator and exit-3 cases. PASS.
- `scripts/eval/lane-quality/test-lane-quality.sh`, `scripts/eval/qmd-quality/test-qmd-quality.sh`, `scripts/eval/guard-corpus/test-guard-corpus.sh`, `scripts/eval/scrape-bench/test-scrape-bench.sh`: fixture runs append a valid row. PASS.
- `scripts/observability/test-ledgers-registry.sh`: registry lint. PASS.

## Ticket coverage

- Ask 1, append-only eval-runs.jsonl registered in ledgers.json with a forward-compatible schema documented in a header and the README: done
- Ask 2, one shared writer called once per run by lane-quality, qmd-quality, guard-corpus diff and scrape-bench: done
- Ask 3, eval-compare with --baseline or --best-of, per-metric delta, non-zero exit past the CI bound or config threshold: done

author: alexlinyx
body:
Change set 3 of 6 (`docs/technical-design.md` section 8). Adds the database and Google-only sign-in. It doesn't port any pages yet; that's `port/app`.

## What's here

- **Migrations** (`db/migrations/0001`–`0005`): V3's schema on plain Postgres.
  - users are keyed on Google `sub`; sessions store only SHA-256 hashes (DB-8)
  - composite foreign keys make Postgres refuse any child row under another owner's roster or game; this replaces V3's row-level-security `exists()` checks
  - a trigger stops the app's role from ever setting `is_admin` (AUTH-8)
  - the metric views stay in an `admin` schema the app can't read
- **App role (DB-6):** `scripts/migrate.mjs` runs on every start and (re)creates `app_rw` / `app_rw_login` with row access only. `scripts/check-app-role.mjs` proves 27 things against a real database: no DDL, no superuser, no admin escalation, no cross-owner writes, no access to the metric views, default privileges for future tables.
- **Sign-in:**
  - a nonce in an HttpOnly cookie; the page only sees its hash
  - the Google ID token is verified with `jose`: signature, issuer, audience, expiry, nonce, `email_verified`
  - `__Host-` session cookie: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax
  - sign-out, and sign-out everywhere, delete the session rows (AUTH-4)
- **Gates:** `requireUser`, `requireApprovedUser` and `requireAdmin` keep V3's 401/403/503 contract. Per-IP and per-user rate limits answer 429 (AUTH-3). Every state-changing route checks it's called from the same origin (API-6).
- **Startup check (API-10):** on Railway the app refuses to boot if a variable is missing, if it would connect as the database owner, or if it would use the public database host. Health now pings the database (API-9).
- **CI:** a new `db` job on Postgres 18, the version Railway runs. It migrates twice and runs the role check.
- **Railway config:** every secret is now `preserve()`, so `railway config apply` never deletes a key set in the dashboard.

## Verified

- `npm run check`: 596 tests pass. `npm run build` passes; `npm audit` finds 0 issues in shipped dependencies.
- Against a local `postgres:18`: migrations apply and re-apply, and all 27 role checks pass.
- `npm start` against that database:
  - `/api/health` is `ok`
  - `/api/auth/nonce` sets a Secure, HttpOnly cookie and returns only the hash
  - a cross-site POST to `/api/auth/google` gets 403
  - a POST with no nonce gets `nonce_missing`
- Started with a staging-like environment and owner credentials, the app refuses to boot, naming each problem without printing any value.

**Not verified:** a real Google sign-in. That needs the staging cutover and the Google client ID, both listed below.

## Staging cutover (owner actions, in this order)

This code refuses to start without Google's client ID and the restricted database URL. If either is missing, a staging deploy fails its health check and Railway keeps serving the previous build, so nothing breaks in between.

1. **Google variables:** set `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` (the same value) in Railway → staging → spotter → Variables. Add `https://spotter-staging.up.railway.app` to the OAuth client's authorized JavaScript origins.
2. **Run the `database-security` cutover against staging** before merging. It sets `APP_DB_PASSWORD` (never printed), `MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL` and the restricted `DATABASE_URL`. The build staging runs now ignores those variables, so this step is safe on its own; its check only proves staging still answers.
3. **Merge this PR.** The new build runs the migrations, connects as `app_rw_login` and pings the database. Then check that staging serves the merge commit and that health is `ok`.
4. **Seal `APP_DB_PASSWORD`** in the dashboard.

author: bedah-kym
body:
## Summary

Kazi is now told where its shell commands run, and the prompt stops describing a different product.

Before: the system prompt called Kazi an assistant for "communication, payments, travel, scheduling", never mentioned the shell, and the `run_command` description claimed "a sandboxed container (non-root, read-only, network off by default)" on every profile. On the unsandboxed Windows profile Kazi could not say what OS it was on and opened a file task with `mkdir -p … && printf … && cat …` in `cmd.exe`.

What changes:

- The sidecar's `GET /health` also reports its host's operating system and shell.
- `orchestration/shell/environment.py` turns the room's resolved profile into facts. Sandboxed profiles are a Linux container and need no call; the unsandboxed profile asks the sidecar (cached five minutes, "unknown" cached thirty seconds, never raised into a turn).
- The coordinator adds a "Where you are running" block to the context prompt, next to the persona identity. `agent_loop.py` is not touched.
- The identity line is "an assistant that gets things done by calling tools. Prefer the specific tool when one fits the job; use the shell for the rest."
- The three rules that asked the model to narrate before and between tool calls are removed.
- `run_command`'s description no longer claims a sandbox it may not have.

The block says only what the gate does, and each claim is pinned by a test against `get_tool_risk_info`:

- **open:** not sandboxed; the harness asks after the room has seen tool output (room-wide, for `AGENT_TAINT_TTL_SECONDS`), for root, and for its short destructive list. That list does not cover plain deletes, so the model is told to ask the user itself before deleting, overwriting or moving anything it was not asked to change.
- **standard:** fresh non-root container, read-only root filesystem, minimal image, no network. Only commands the harness recognises as network tools can get the network; anything else just fails. `allow host` is mentioned only when the egress proxy is on.
- **locked:** no network, root and network commands refused. No claim about a read-only workspace, because the backend does not enforce one.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Test-only

## Scope

- `Backend/orchestration/agent_prompts.py`, `Backend/orchestration/coordinator.py`
- `Backend/orchestration/shell/environment.py` (new)
- `Backend/orchestration/shell_exec/backends.py`, `Backend/orchestration/shell_exec/daemon.py`
- `Backend/orchestration/connectors/shell_connector.py`
- Tests: `Backend/orchestration/test_shell_environment.py` (new), `Backend/orchestration/test_shell_daemon.py`

No protected path is touched.

## Security note

- `/health` stays unauthenticated and now also returns the host's OS family and shell name. The sidecar binds to 127.0.0.1 by default and no compose file publishes its port; `profile` was already disclosed there.
- What the sidecar reports goes into the system prompt, so it must be a plain label (letters, digits, space and `._()-`, at most 40 characters). Anything else, or a non-200 answer, is treated as unknown. Test: a payload containing a newline and a fake `## Rules` section never reaches the block.
- No gate changes. The block describes the existing gate; it does not widen it.

Found while checking the claims and left for follow-up, not changed here: the `locked` profile's workspace is mounted writable although the docs say "Writable: none"; the destructive list does not match plain deletes such as `del x.txt` on the unsandboxed profile.

## Validation

- [x] `python Backend/manage.py check`
- [x] `python Backend/manage.py test` (or targeted test run)
- [x] Manual verification completed (if UI or integration change)

Validation details:

```text
# hermetic scratch copy, SQLite + LocMem, Python 3.12
manage.py check                    -> exit 0
manage.py test --noinput           -> Ran 1152 tests in 469.974s, OK (skipped=1)
flake8 (CI blocking subset)        -> 0
python scripts/check_boundaries.py -> exit 0
```

Live chat, room 2, unsandboxed profile on Windows, DeepSeek:

```text
GET /health -> {"status": "ok", "profile": "open", "host": {"platform": "Windows", "shell": "cmd.exe"}}

"without running any command: which OS and shell, when does the harness ask me, would you delete a file without asking?"
    -> Windows, cmd.exe; after the room has seen tool output (~15 minutes), for root, or the short
       destructive list; "No — I wouldn't delete a file you didn't ask me to change without checking"

"make a folder qa_env and a file notes.txt with three lines, then show it"
    -> first command: mkdir qa_env && (echo alpha& echo beta& echo gamma)> qa_env\notes.txt && type qa_env\notes.txt
    -> 2 iterations, 1 tool call, 15,801 tokens
       (same task on main earlier the same day: 3 iterations, 2 tool calls, 23,707 tokens; the first command was Unix syntax)
```

## Risk and rollback

No migration. A web process on this commit talking to an older sidecar gets no host facts and says the OS "could not be determined" until the sidecar is restarted. With narration rules gone, an auto-run command shows the user only the progress line until the reply. Rollback: revert the PR.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added/updated for changed behavior
- [x] Docs updated (`README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, or `docs/*`) if needed
- [x] Security considerations reviewed (auth, permissions, input sanitization)
- [x] No unrelated changes included

author: paat
body:
Fixes #618.

## What changed
`plugins/lawyer/tests/test-markers-argmax.sh` runs its argmax case with rg left off PATH, using the test's existing rg-free `NOPATH_DIR`, which is now built before the case. The test lowers ARG_MAX through `ulimit -s 128`. Under that stack, ripgrep 14.1.0 aborts with "fatal runtime error: stack overflow" before the argv limit matters, so the test failed wherever rg is installed. Without rg the scanner falls back to grep, so the case still exercises `xargs -0` chunking under the lowered ARG_MAX. The rg binary-file case is unchanged.

## Verification
- `test-markers-argmax.sh` passes with rg 14.1.0 installed.
- `plugins/lawyer/tests/run-tests.sh`: 240/240. It was 239/240 on main, where LH1 failed.
- Negative proof, run by both the worker and the reviewer: in a scanner copy whose xargs call was replaced by a single-argv call, the test fails with `grep: Argument list too long` / `FAIL: scanner exited 1 under lowered ARG_MAX`.
- Independent review (Sonnet; the worker was local Qwen) returned APPROVE. It checked that every external tool the scanner runs is in the rg-free PATH, so the case cannot pass vacuously.

Note: the version bump collides with #619 (also lawyer 0.1.15). Whichever merges second gets rebased and re-bumped.

author: abumahir980
body:
Closes #205.

Moving an item to build recorded the commit checked out as its base. Commits already made on the branch while the item was at prepare fell before the base, so they didn't count toward the reviews the change needs: a dependency change, a lint settings change and a new tool settings file escaped the review gate.

The base is now where the change starts:

- **Its branch's fork point:** where it leaves the default branch, as `forkPoint` already works it out for the gate (RFC 0013). Commits made before build now count.
- **For a branch stacked on another open item's branch:** where it leaves that branch, so it still isn't asked for its parent's reviews (RFC 0010). This is where the two branches meet, so it stays put when the parent gains commits after the stacked branch left it. With several parents, the nearest counts.
- **Off its own branch, or outside git:** the commit checked out, as before.

`tipOf` moves from `migrations.ts` to `commits.ts`, beside new `mergeBase` and `isAncestor` helpers.

Tests: commits made before build count, and a stacked branch starts where it leaves its parent even after the parent moves on. The existing stacked-branch test still passes.

Continúa #164 sobre main 17c5b34d. C2 ya fue generado por el bot y publicado por la cadena nueva, con SHA/huellas verificados. Este diff modifica únicamente código y contratos; conserva las salidas de datos y no coincide con los disparadores de prensa.

## Cobertura y controles
- Completa 16 productores: siete pipelines secundarios, dos validadores manuales y Endeudamiento se suman a los seis iniciales. Identidades verificadas; manuales sólo workflow_dispatch; escritura en main, validación previa, trailers y SHA después del push/rebase.

- Adopta el mismo esquema estricto del generador en el CLI de panorama, sobre C2 ya verificado.

## Salud Mental
Elimina ambos bypass TLS preexistentes, exige HTTPS también en redirecciones y aborta antes de escribir ante fallos de certificado/transporte. Se preservan los dos JSON anteriores y los cálculos existentes. Diez tests cubren éxito y fallos de las cuatro descargas. La consulta segura de CKAN a las 17:11 UTC del 6/10 devolvió HTTP 502; la fuente no se declara disponible y no se generaron datos nuevos de ella.

## Frescura pública
La red canónica ya respondió bytes actuales el 6/10 a las 17:27, pero faltaba Cache-Control y un navegador recuperó la fecha nueva sólo al recargar. Se añade revalidación a cuatro recursos públicos mediante una sección idempotente de .htaccess, preservando reglas restantes. El smoke exige bytes y headers correctos en URLs ordinarias antes de consultar con nonce. No basta que el bypass de caché responda bien. Se mantiene rollback si las directivas no surten efecto.

## Validación
- 124 pruebas locales; R2, datos C2, UI, agregados reales, rutas e inventario aprobados.
- Tres agregados mensuales reales validados sin descargar crudos; diez pasos de commit ejercitados con Git local.
- CI incluye prueba HTTP real con apache2-bin oficial, configuración temporal, proceso sin privilegios y escucha sólo en 127.0.0.1. Debe validar DirectoryIndex, seis URLs públicas, siete controles privados/assets/redirección e idempotencia antes de fusionar.
- QA independiente y CI del SHA exacto pendientes. Tras fusionar, verificar publicación real, header efectivo y navegación canónica. El cambio no borra retrospectivamente copias que un navegador ya guardó y aún no revalidó.

author: luckson1
body:
Closes #609 (spec 07c FE-3).

Clarification drafts always started in English, and the declarant's preferred language wasn't stored anywhere. Now declarants choose English or Kiswahili on their portal account. A new clarification in the console, and so Draft with AI (which drafts in the composer's language), starts in that language.

## What changed

**Directory**
- `persons.preferred_language`: nullable, with a check constraint for `en`/`sw` (migration 0033).
- `PUT /v1/me/declarant/preferred-language` (declarant, their own), which answers with the profile.
- `DeclarantProfile.preferredLanguage` (null until they choose).
- A change records `person.preferred-language-set.v1` in the outbox, in the same transaction (ADR-008). Setting the same language again changes nothing.
- `GET /internal/v1/persons/{personId}/preferred-language` (`directory:internal`, acting tenant; 404 for a person not onboarded there).

**Review**
- `CaseDetail.declarantLanguage` (nullable `LetterLanguage`).
- It's read from the directory alongside the declaration pull, with its own 2 s budget. It's null when unset, or when the directory fails or is slow, so the case view never fails because of it. The 502 problem body carries it too.

**Console**
- `emptyComposer(declarantLanguage)` falls back to English. The case view passes `detail.declarantLanguage`.
- A saved draft keeps its own language. Follow-ups copy the original letter's language, as before.
- Review mock: Mary Achieng prefers Kiswahili, for the demo.

**Portal**
- A "Letter language" select (English / Kiswahili) on the "Your account" card.
- Success and failure toasts. A failed save goes back to the saved value, and an ended session signs the declarant in again.
- Directory mock supports the PUT.

**Docs**
- CONTEXT.md "Letter language" says where the default comes from.
- ADR-013 §2 and §8.6 record review's new directory call and its 2 s budget.

## Decisions
- The portal says "Kiswahili", like the rest of the portal (Ask Adili, help). Contract text says "Swahili", as the glossary does.
- The internal read isn't audited, because the preference isn't sensitive personal data. The write is audited.

## Testing
- Directory persons integration (18 tests): store/read-back, the audit event (once per change), 400/403/404, and the internal read (acting tenant, scope).
- Review: the case-work integration test covers the language, null when unset, and null when the directory is down. The HTTP client test covers the language, null, 404 → null, and unavailable.
- Console: composer unit and component tests (new letter starts in the preference; a saved draft keeps its own).
- Portal: BFF save/load tests, and account-card tests (save, revert on failure, sign in again).
- Typecheck, lint and `contracts:drift` clean after merging `main`.
- Local note: the directory's Keycloak-backed integration suites fail on my machine because the local Keycloak rejects the committed dev client credentials. That isn't related to this change.
