author: rmusser01
body:
## Summary

This follow-up keeps a Knowledge answer's original question, scope, evidence and qualifications available when its note is edited, reopened or continued in Research. Full owned Notes become versioned Research snapshots while the original retrieved excerpts remain available for review.

- Add independently versioned, owner-bound `notes.provenance` records. Reuse canonical Notes transactions and durable Sync groups so core-note v1 stays compatible, stale replacements change neither record, and restoration of retained history is explicit.
- Preserve lost-save identities through durable inactive-Sync receipts and shared client retry handling. Keep the answered question attached to its result. Reads and exports reject incomplete projection instead of combining one version's body with another version's history.
- Fix natural-question Notes retrieval, misleading citation spans, source reuse and overlapping evidence, fresh Workspace persistence, keyboard access to history, and the extension's native sidebar gesture/acknowledgment ordering.

## Change summary

This PR improves the /knowledge → Research Workspace workflow by fixing natural-language Notes retrieval, preserving full versioned note snapshots and original source references, avoiding duplicate attachments, and rejecting unsupported citation spans. It reuses existing Notes, media, and Workspace APIs, waits for server confirmation, and preserves retry and stale-save protections. Extension capture now opens the sidebar during the required browser gesture and checks whether opening succeeded.

## Validation

- Latest-dev integration: backend 794 passed/one expected PostgreSQL NUL skip; affected clients507 passed in24 files (Notes195; Knowledge/Research/native authority312); incoming Buddy107 passed; Docs 212 passed. Real PostgreSQL fixtures verify owner RLS, migration order, caller transaction ownership and replay receipts.
- Both client type checks and production builds pass. Local WebUI Webpack build, token parity and595.5KB/600KB bundle budget pass; Chrome build49.52 MB. Canonical OpenAPI drift check passes (2,113 paths/3,267 schemas; hash2667c3566ff2fc647e9d7cbda083227a1d85445186106940b3765474fc93b1cb).
- Review regressions proved RED/GREEN for remounted durable create/restore identity, actual autosave timer failure recovery, explicit session invalidation, queued-create title acknowledgment followed by rename, clean queued-create canonical readback, durable retry/edit-revert-leave results with owner/navigation fencing, and chained leave saves using the acknowledged history head. Newer authored text stays recoverable throughout.
- Production Bandit:0 findings/errors across 24 touched paths. Integration Python Ruff passes; scoped Notes ESLint 0 errors/85 remaining production warnings/0 test warnings.
- Broader Notes run remains qualified:32 named failures reproduce on unchanged dev; two integration failures are repaired, and a static CSS check passes in its owning package. Native capture, VoiceOver/mobile, real participants, external-web refresh, broad suite/lint and inherited SQLite startup race TASK-13514.1 remain documented qualifications. Historical real browser/API evidence is retained in the release report.
- Both independent integration reviewers approve. Seven fresh required checks on the final published head remain mandatory. The requester authorized merge after checks without Qodo because its workspace review is credit-blocked.

## Risk & rollback

Medium: additive SQLite77/78 and PostgreSQL81/82 migrations, plus canonical Sync lifecycle changes. Durable receipts remain retained after note purge to prevent an old retry recreating a removed note; retention is unbounded. Reads/collections/exports containing an incompletely projected sourced note return HTTP409 until existing retry/replay completes. A database rollback requires a pre-upgrade backup or a separately reviewed migration reversal; no destructive rollback is included.

Broad frontend tests/shared lint remain failing with recorded baseline comparisons. Final native extension capture, VoiceOver/Safari/iOS/mobile keyboard and participant sessions remain unqualified; live external-web refresh needs its separate capture/version policy. Historical local Python3.11 runs are below declared dependency floors; final backend and canonical-schema proof use the existing Python3.12.13 environment. The human-written summary and seven required current-head CI statuses remain merge gates.

## Summary
Fixes #48.

### Dashboard
- The three stat cards hardcoded to "—" are gone, along with their i18n keys.
- A **setup checklist** per admin property (`features/properties/SetupChecklist`) replaces them. It shows "Kom godt i gang med {property} · 2 af 4 trin":

  3. Opsæt tidspladser (every room needs at least one)
  4. Inviter beboere (done when there's another member or a pending invite)

author: zarmeza
body:
## The bug

Two files disagreed about a hash key by one character:

```ruby
# app/services/search_service.rb — wrote it
error_message: response[:error_message],

# app/models/search.rb — read it
error_messages: response[:error_messages]   # always nil
```

Ruby hashes do not raise on a missing key, so `response[:error_messages]` was
just `nil`, silently, on every request. Present since the repo's earliest commits.

### What it cost

```
$ curl "localhost:3000/search?engine=google&text=test"
{"provider":"google","status":"error","error_messages":null}
```

A provider failed and the API said nothing about why. The field exists, looks
deliberate, and is always null — which is worse than omitting it, because a
client author concludes "no error detail available" and stops investigating.

### Why 99% coverage never caught it

Two specs mentioned `status_by_provider`. One checked the provider *names*, the
other checked the response *has* the key. Both pass while the value is garbage.

The service specs mock `SearchService` entirely, so no test ever passed a real
hash from the service to the aggregator — which is precisely the broken contract.

## The fix

`error_messages` is plural and always an array, normalized at the boundary in
`SearchService#call`:

```ruby
error_messages: Array(response[:error_message]).compact,
```

`perform_request` keeps its singular internal key because it really does hold one
message. The widening happens once, where the provider result leaves the service,
so the normalization lives in exactly one place. `status_by_provider` applies
`Array()` as a cheap second line of defence, so the JSON shape does not depend on
which provider ran or whether it failed.

## Two mistakes I made writing the test

Both are in the commit message, but they matter more than the fix:

**1. My first spec passed with the bug still present.** It stubbed `GoogleSearch`
directly, which bypasses `SearchService` and hands `status_by_provider` a hash it
could never receive in production. Identical blind spot to the original specs. It
now stubs `HTTParty` and drives the real service.

**2. That version then failed with the fix in place.** The enclosing `before`
block ran a successful search and left it in the cache, so my example read the
cached success instead of its own stubbed failure. RSpec `before` blocks are
*inherited* by nested groups — moving the example to its own `describe` was not
enough, the outer `before` still ran. The shared setup is now a lazy `let`.

Worth stating plainly: both would have shipped as "tested" if I had only run the
suite once with the fix in.

## Verified in both directions

| | Result |
|---|---|
| Fix in place | 56 examples, 0 failures, 99.57% |
| Original singular key restored | **4 failures** across service *and* model layers |

Live API, real provider failure (no API key configured, so Google returns 403):

```json
{"provider":"google","status":"error","error_messages":["Forbidden"]}
```

## Summary

- Adds a new `surrounding_context_matches` scorer condition that supports regex matching against `Snippet.Before`/`Snippet.After`
- Regex is precompiled at load time (same pattern as `match_group.matches`); invalid regex fails scorer loading
- `within` parameter respected (bytes on each side; 0 = unlimited)
- Existing `surrounding_context_contains` unchanged (backward compatible)

Closes LAB-7150.

## Use cases

- Boost score when a JDBC URL has a `password=` keyword on a nearby line (case-insensitive, multi-keyword OR)
- Boost score when a generic API key appears near a service-specific keyword
- Lower score when a secret-like string appears in test file context

## Example YAML

```yaml
- name: password-nearby
  priority: 80
  surrounding_context_matches:
    pattern: '(?i)(?:password|passwd|pwd|secret|credential)\s*[=:\s]'
    within: 256
  delta: 10
```

## Test plan

- [x] Condition evaluate: case-insensitive, multi-keyword OR, within boundary, unlimited, nil match
- [x] Nil safety (nil condition, nil pattern)
- [x] Loader: valid YAML parses with correct fields
- [x] Loader: invalid regex rejected at load time

author: michaelcrosato
body:
Milestone 8.4 of [plan 2](docs/plan-2.md), worked at xhigh. The design, as built, is in [`docs/design/8.4-materials.md`](docs/design/8.4-materials.md); its "Changes while building" section lists what the renders sent back.

## Materials

Each material now has its own surface and its own light.

- **The surface** is drawn through the pattern kit, so `.glb` bakes keep it.
- **The light** comes from a look table that both backends read.

| Material | Look |
| --- | --- |
| `skin` | Soft. Light wraps a little past the shadow edge with a warm tint, and the surface has faint pores. |
| `hide` | Thick and dry, with a network of wrinkles that deepens in creases. |
| `scales` | Round scales in overlapping rows down the body. The scale nearer the head lies on top, giving scalloped rear edges. No longer a Voronoi mosaic. |
| `chitin` | Segmented plates with seams and a lacquered clearcoat, which exports as `KHR_materials_clearcoat`. |

## Fur

`skin.fur` is drawn.

- **One draw call.** The skin's geometry is drawn as shells, instanced 12 times at medium and 16 at high. There is no fur at low quality, and the baked level of detail hides it.
- **Colour.** Fur takes the skin's own pattern stack, evaluated per vertex, so stripes and spots show through it.
- **Where it grows.** Shorter on the face, in creases and on the feet, and kept clear of the eyes and the mouth.
- **Exports** leave fur out and say so in their notes; 11.1 decides fur's exported form.

## Pattern layers

- **New layers.** `scars` (claw rakes with `rake`), `bioluminescence` (glowing spots or dotted lines that pulse), `slime`, `warts`, `veins`, `rosettes` and `bands`.
- **`scales` layer.** Now overlaps, like the material.
- **`spots`.** Denser by default, and they no longer fade out at contact-sheet distance.
- **New layer outputs.** A layer can glow (`emissive`), lay a second colour first (`under`) and shine over its own coverage (`coat`). `Pose.time` drives the pulses.

## Renders

- **Contact sheets.** The diffs of `examples/*.png` show each example before and after:
  - the wolf has fur;
  - the boar has hide and claw scars;
  - the troll has hide and warts;
  - the beetle has glowing spots;
  - the rest change with their material.
- **Closer views.** [`eval/runs/2026-10-06-phase8-materials/`](eval/runs/2026-10-06-phase8-materials/) holds:
  - each material on one body;
  - each new layer alone, in 3/4 and head views;
  - the furred wolf.

## Checks

- **`pnpm check`.** Lint, typecheck and 414 tests pass.
- **CPU–GPU parity test (new).**
  - Headless Chromium draws the pattern stack unlit into a float target, one pixel per sampled skin vertex, and the test compares it with the CPU kit at the same vertices.
  - Stacks that between them hold every pattern module, on every material, plus every example.
  - At least 99% of samples must agree within 2/255; a spot check found the worst difference to be 5e-4.
- **Fur test.** Fur adds exactly one draw call at medium, none at low, and the baked level of detail hides it.
- **Module harness.** Every pattern module passes it.
- **Goldens.** Unchanged: materials move no vertex. The render baselines are re-approved.
- **Fuzz and smoke test.** A 300-blueprint fuzz runs clean, and `pnpm smoke` passes.

author: red-by-redbtn[bot]
body:
## Why
Full visual pass (native vs web) on `expo/app/(auth)/login.tsx` against a Samsung S23 Ultra (One UI 7 / Android 15, font scale 0.9) flagged six Android-specific sign-in issues (NP-309).

## What
- **Keyboard hides the review-code submit.** On this device, edge-to-edge enforcement stops the usual `windowSoftInputMode` resize from kicking in, so "Sign in with review code" stayed under the keyboard with no indication it was still there. Fixed by scrolling the focused review-code field and its submit button above the keyboard by hand (`Keyboard.addListener("keyboardDidShow")` + `measureInWindow` + `ScrollView.scrollTo`) and setting `KeyboardAvoidingView` to `behavior="height"` on Android for this screen (iOS is untouched). Android's `ScrollView`, unlike iOS's, has no built-in scroll-to-focused-input, which is why this needed doing by hand.
- **Email field's Go key did nothing.** Added `returnKeyType="go"` + `onSubmitEditing={handleSubmit}`, matching web's Enter submitting "Continue with email".
- **Back on "Create account" exited the app.** `mode` is component state here, not a route, so hardware back fell through to the OS. Now intercepted via the existing `useAndroidBackHandler` hook (enabled only while `mode === "register"`), flipping back to sign-in — mirrors web, where `/register` is its own page and back returns to `/login`.
- **Inert header back button.** `router.canGoBack()` is always `false` at the auth root, so the round back button did nothing and a reviewer would flag it. It's now hidden when there's no history, and still renders + works on the one path where there is one (a web-only hand-off).
- **Review-code field leaked into the Samsung suggestion strip.** `autoComplete="off"` + `importantForAutofill="no"` + `secureTextEntry` stop the keyboard treating a one-off reviewer code as something to learn and offer back later. Its submit button is now outlined (`variant="ghost"`) and disabled until both email and code are filled, matching web's outlined/disabled-until-filled button (previously only disabled while sending).
- **Smaller copy gaps against web's `AuthForm`:** divider now reads `OR` (uppercase, tracking-wide) instead of lowercase `or`; the "App reviewer? Use a review code" disclosure is underlined, like web's; the native-only "Review code" label above the review-code input is gone (placeholder only, like web); the native-only "Email" label above the email field is gone too (placeholder only), with `accessibilityLabel="Email"` keeping the accessible name.
- **Footer link spacing** (Terms/Privacy/Health data/Support/Delete account wrapping as one row) was already fixed by NP-303's `LegalLinks` pass, which this screen already renders — checked, no change needed there.

Passkey button is untouched (tracked separately under NP-161), per the card.

## How verified
- `cd expo && npx tsc --noEmit` — no new errors vs. the pre-existing baseline (540 errors, all in unrelated files/pre-existing `@become/core` typing gaps in this container; confirmed via `git stash` before/after).
- `cd expo && npx eslint "app/(auth)/login.tsx"` plus the touched test files — clean.
- `cd expo && npx jest` — full suite, 371 suites / 3684 tests passing, including the updated `card-NP-251-acceptance.test.tsx` (back-button hide/show) and `reviewSignIn.test.tsx` (empty-submission now goes through the keyboard's Go key, since the submit button is legitimately disabled), and a new `loginNP309.test.tsx` covering the email Go-key submit, the hardware-back mode flip (via the injectable `backHandler` DI prop, same pattern as `useLiveBackGuard`), and the copy-gap fixes.
- `node expo/scripts/check-no-ota.mjs` — OK (no OTA surface touched).
- Could not verify on an actual Android device/emulator — none available in this container; the keyboard-scroll fix is implemented defensively (guarded refs, Android-only) but the literal on-device pixel behavior is unverified here. CI's `expo` job is the gate for the rest.

body:
DX04 of [docs/DESKTOP_LINUX_MACOS.md](docs/DESKTOP_LINUX_MACOS.md): make a Mac a Martlet host, on its GPU where possible.

## What changed
- **macOS custody backend** (`MacFileSystem`, selected by `PosixFileSystem.Create()`): same `linuxServicePermissions` contract on local read-write APFS: single-name `openat` below held dirs with `O_NOFOLLOW_ANY` + same-volume check, `fstat` identities (`$INODE64` on x64), ACLs with allow entries refused (deny-only allowed), `flock`, `F_FULLFSYNC`, `renameatx_np(RENAME_EXCL)`, `kern.bootsessionuuid`. arm64 `openat` mode passed on the stack (Apple variadic ABI) plus `fchmod`.
- **Linux backend admits arm64** and translates arm64's `O_DIRECTORY`/`O_NOFOLLOW` values. This was a real bug, found by running the arm64 image under emulation.
- **Mac host commands** in `Martlet.Gateway.Host.Linux`: `macos-setup` (detects Ollama on 127.0.0.1:11434 and Homebrew `whisper-server`, offers only what is installed, suggests models by Metal `recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize`, downloads the same SHA-256-pinned whisper models, writes host.json/machine.json, owner-init/approve, launchd agents `io.github.throndir2.martlet.host` + `.whisper`), `macos-pair`, `macos-status`, `macos-machine`, `macos-uninstall`. Serving keeps the Mac from idle sleep (IOPM assertion). On macOS, NVIDIA roles (F5 PyTorch, Audio2Face, XTTS, …) are refused with the platform catalog's reason.
- **Machine report**: `platform: macos`, `chip`, `unified_memory`, `gpu_working_set_gb`, GPU vendor `apple`.
- **PlatformCatalog Mac host rows**: Ollama, whisper, host-service now Works (notes say not yet run on a Mac). remote-roles stays NotPlanned with an updated reason.
- **Docker**: host image builds for arm64 (Docker CLI/Compose per `TARGETARCH`, aarch64 SHA-256s computed from the official downloads; the x86_64 hash re-verified), SDK stage on `$BUILDPLATFORM`. `martlet-host` stops on macOS with a pointer to the Mac host (bash 3.2-safe).
- **MCP**: new `mac_host_check` tool (docs/MCP.md).
- Docs: MACOS.md (new "The Mac host (DX04)"), PLATFORMS.md, DESKTOP_LINUX_MACOS.md, deploy/host/README.md, gateway and persistence READMEs, CHANGELOG.

Publish command for DX05 (bundled at `Martlet.app/Contents/Resources/host/`):
`dotnet publish src/Martlet.Gateway.Host.Linux/Martlet.Gateway.Host.Linux.csproj -c Release -r osx-arm64|osx-x64 --self-contained true -p:UseAppHost=true -o <out>`

## Validation
Targeted tests (`scripts\Test-Martlet.ps1`):
```
Martlet.Core.Tests (PlatformCatalogTests)             here    Passed  7
Martlet.Gateway.Host.Linux.Tests (full)               here    Passed 83
Martlet.Gateway.Persistence.Portable.Tests (full)     here    Passed 102
Martlet.Gateway.Persistence.Linux.Tests               docker  Passed 10
Martlet.Gateway.Host.Linux.Native.Tests               docker  Passed  5
Martlet.Gateway.Tests (~Machine)                      here    Passed  5
PASSED: 212 passed, 0 new failing
```
After rebasing on #480/#481: Mac/catalog tests re-run, 35 passed.

MCP: `mac_host_check` passed: catalog-mac-host (ollama Yes, whisper Yes, f5/audio2face No with NVIDIA reasons), publish-osx-arm64 (121 MB), publish-osx-x64 (111 MB), macos-setup-help (exit 0), macos-commands-refused-off-a-mac (exit 4 `macos.unsupported`).

Also run: local `dotnet publish` for osx-arm64 and osx-x64 succeeded. arm64 host image built with buildx (`uname -m` aarch64, Docker 27.3.1 and Compose 2.29.7 aarch64 binaries run). The `martlet-host` Darwin guard was checked under bash 3.2 with a fake `uname`.

**NOT RUN**
- Anything on a Mac: launchd agents, APFS custody, Metal working set, native Ollama/whisper.cpp relays, pairing. No Mac is available.
- The arm64 gateway's state custody on a real arm64 kernel. Under QEMU emulation it now gets past the flag bug and stops at `openat2` (QEMU: "Unknown syscall 437"), which real arm64 kernels (≥5.6, including Docker Desktop's VM) have.
- Role images on arm64. The pinned whisper.cpp image is amd64-only, so Docker would run it emulated (documented).

No workflows touched; `windows-release.yml` is dispatch-only.

body:
…name

A corps is its name (owner direction, PODIUM.md decision 48). Continuing a corps locks its name (the server rejects a new one); a new name is a new corps that starts blank in A Class; reviving a retired corps automatically retires the active one.

Fixes the new-corps-in-Open-Class bug and its siblings. The season boundary re-seat, assessment and archival, and registration's lazy archival, all wrote to whichever corps was live, so a corps founded during or after the sweep could inherit its predecessor's class seat, season, staff and budget refund. Every season, seat and refund now lands on the lineage that played it (new helpers/podium/lineage.js: seasonOwner and friends); retire and un-retire wait for the boundary to settle.

Revival: time away is one clock from lastPlayedIndex, charged once at registration (un-retire used to pre-decay and registration decayed again), and the preview uses the real re-entry rule, so one season away keeps the corps' class. Un-retiring while a corps was active used to drop that corps' lineage; it is now banked. Retired corps bank and restore their logo, uniforms, home and show concept; a new corps starts without them.

Adds scripts/correctPodiumLineages.js + an Actions workflow (dry run first) to repair corps already affected, the assessment screen's between-corps state, guide copy, changelog, and docs.

body: ## Summary Stops the biggest request-path Sleeper fans that were driving Vercel outbound `api.sleeper.app` volume (~1.3k/15m), and reduces the **5.3% function error spike**. ### Why the 5.3% error rate Vercel Observability treats **all 5xx** (including **503** and Fluid **timeouts**) as function errors. On current production we confirmed: - `/api/data/players-export` is healthy (**200**, 4266 rows) - Research Aggregates Warm is succeeding - The spike lines up with **request-path Sleeper fan-outs timing out / throwing** under Fluid pressure (player SOS ~36 week-stats, game-log 18 projection files, Fantasy Leaders ~18 weeks), not a dead warehouse ### Fixes in this PR 1. **Kill Sleeper fans** — SOS from TiDB board; Fantasy Leaders snapped; game-log projections only for unplayed weeks; research CDN routes 2. **Warm all formats** — cron covers std/half/ppr, matchup weeks 1…current, red-zone yardlines, leaders 3. **Stop 503-as-error** — cold research snaps + unseeded warehouse export return **200 + no-store** (clients already treat empty/`ok:false` as miss) 4. **Cron resilience** — per-section try/catch; partial failures stay **200** with `partialErrors` in body 5. **`withResearchSnap`** — never double-invokes `compute()` on failure (was amplifying timeouts) ### Mobile (`/m/*`) Yes — shared paths: MobilePlayerSheet FPA → CDN, player SOS → board, lighter game logs, longer matchup TiDB window. ### After merge Trigger **Research Aggregates Warm** once so std/ppr + Fantasy Leaders snaps exist.

author: fomaxoasset-star
body:
Before: on shorter laptop screens (1280×720, 1366×768) the checkout ran below the screen. The Pay button, the coupon box or the "You saved" line needed scrolling, and a bag with four or more items overflowed even at 1440×900.

After: at every desktop size the whole checkout fits on one screen without scrolling: the delivery form, Pay button, order summary, coupon box and saving line. The look is the same as now (no redesign), and the phone is unchanged.

How:
- On laptop screens up to 920px high, CSS uses tighter spacing (breadcrumb hidden, smaller gaps and product thumbnails, labels on one line).
- If the page is still taller than the screen, a small `fitCo()` scales the checkout block down to fit, never below 82%. It runs after every redraw and on window resize.

author: tonypine
body:
Closes TP-754

## What

A QA-mode launch on the VM read the Hub URL and the ad hoc build's preferences owner token that an earlier QA run had saved, so the app sent the old token to the stub hub (401s) until a new one was saved.

In QA mode, `HubConnection.init` now removes the saved `hubURL` and `ownerToken` preferences before reading them and doesn't read the Keychain: the token is `HUB_OWNER_TOKEN` or none. Without a token, `makeClient()` is nil and the connection check stops after `/v1/health`, so no bearer request goes out before Save.

The first QA pass (on `fb7ee3f`) showed Symphony's `qa_launch_app` doesn't pass `--qa-mode` to the app, so the reset never ran. QA mode is now also on for a **QA build**: `make-app.sh` marks a build with neither an Apple team nor Go (the QA VM's) with `HubQABuild = true` in its Info.plist, and that build runs in QA mode at every launch, with or without the flag.

## Changes

- `macos/Sources/JobSearchHubCore/HubConnection.swift`: clear the preferences and skip the Keychain in QA mode; new `isQABuild` init parameter (defaults to the Info.plist key); QA mode = QA build or `--qa-mode`
- `macos/Scripts/make-app.sh`: write `HubQABuild` for a build with neither a team nor Go; `HUB_QA_BUILD=1|0` overrides; prints `==> QA build: …`. Signing is unchanged
- `HubConnectionTests`: `inQAModeTheHubURLAndTokenAnEarlierRunSavedAreForgotten`, `aQABuildStartsFromEmptyConnectionSettingsWithoutTheFlag`, `aQABuildUsesHUB_OWNER_TOKENWithoutTheFlag`; `inQAModeWithoutATokenTheKeychainIsReadAsUsual` becomes `inQAModeWithoutATokenTheKeychainIsNotRead` (the README already said QA mode leaves the Keychain alone)
- README: QA-mode paragraph, including `HUB_QA_BUILD=0` for a person building without a team and without Go

Team-signed and Go-equipped builds without `--qa-mode` are unchanged. `NewVersionChecker.readRunningServer` reads the `hubURL` default directly and falls back to the default URL after the clear, consistent with Settings.

## Validation

- `HubConnectionTests` run in CI's `macos` job (the agent sandbox blocks SwiftPM)
- `bash -n macos/Scripts/make-app.sh`; the Info.plist heredoc with and without the `HubQABuild` lines passes `plutil -lint`, and `plutil -extract HubQABuild raw` gives `true` only with them
- The VM checks (empty Settings › Connection on relaunch, no bearer request before Save) are for the QA pass

## Description

The PR primer took the highest run number from one page of successful

each job of the matrix queries it on its own. Jobs then compared the pull
request with a 'main' output from weeks before, or crashed with "Cannot

expired.

author: rbeezley
body:
## Summary

The class wrap-up status read `entries.judge_signature` / `judge_signature_timestamp`, which nothing writes (live 2026-10-06: 0 of 113 entries signed), so every completed class with entries read "Needs judge's initials" forever. A judge initials (AKC) or signs (UKC/ASCA) the marked catalog **once, at the end of their day, for every class they judged** (owner). This PR records that.

- **Migration `20261006154700_myk9_1030_judge_sign_off_and_results_verified.sql`** (owner-run push after merge; one push covers both features):
  - `classes.judge_signed_off_at timestamptz`, `classes.judge_signed_off_by uuid → auth.users ON DELETE SET NULL` (+ FK index). `_by` follows `results_released_by` / `deleted_by`: the auth uid of whoever recorded it, stamped from `auth.uid()`, never a `people.id`.
  - `mark_classes_judge_signed_off(p_class_ids uuid[], p_signed_off_at timestamptz)` and `clear_class_judge_sign_off(p_class_id uuid)`: SECURITY DEFINER, `search_path = ''`, authorized with `can_manage_trial(trial_id)` — the same helper the `classes_update` policy uses for every other class write (checked live). Mark is all-or-nothing and refuses a missing/soft-deleted class (P0002), a class the caller cannot manage (42501), or a class whose status is not `completed` (55000); keeps an existing stamp; clamps a future time to now; returns the class version for a one-class call so the replica's OCC token stays fresh. `REVOKE ALL ... FROM PUBLIC, anon`, `GRANT EXECUTE ... TO authenticated`.
  - **Results checked against the paper (owner scope addition):** `classes.results_verified_at` / `results_verified_by` (same auth-uid convention) and `set_class_results_verified(p_class_id, p_verified, p_verified_at)`: same `can_manage_trial` authz and grants; marking refuses a class that is not `completed` (55000), keeps an existing stamp and returns the version; clearing is always allowed (a correction means re-check). **Not** gated anywhere server-side: release and the automatic release presets are unchanged.
  - **A changed result clears the check (owner decision):** `private.entries_clear_results_verified()` (SECURITY DEFINER, `search_path=''`, EXECUTE revoked from PUBLIC/anon/authenticated) on an `AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE` trigger on `entries`. Result columns, from the scoring half of the ringside RPC whitelist: `is_scored, result_status, search_time_seconds, area1-4_time_seconds, total_correct_finds, total_incorrect_finds, total_faults, no_finish_count, area1-3_correct/incorrect/faults, total_score, points_earned, points_possible, bonus_points, penalty_points, time_over_limit, time_limit_exceeded_seconds, final_placement, disqualification_reason` (compared OLD vs NEW with IS DISTINCT FROM). Moving or soft-deleting an entry that has a result, inserting a scored entry and hard-deleting one also clear. Check-in, run order, ring times, judge notes, video review and scoring_started/completed_at do not. It writes only `WHERE results_verified_at IS NOT NULL`, so an unverified class is never touched and a correction costs at most one classes write (one version bump + one advisory broadcast from the existing classes triggers). A placement recompute that rewrites the same value cannot clear it.
  - `authenticated`'s column allowlist on `classes` restated with the two new columns (without it every class replication read 42501s). anon's allowlist restated unchanged (the grant-decision contract requires an explicit anon decision); anon cannot read the new columns.
- **Status** (`showMapStatus.ts`, `showMapTree.ts`, new `judgeDay.ts`): a judge's day is the confirmed judge (`judge_assignments.person_id`, carried as `judgeId`) + the trial **date**, so it spans trials. A complete class whose judge still has a class to run that day reads **"Initials at end of day"** / "Signature at end of day" (neutral, not counted in the pending signal, no action). It reads "Needs judge's initials" / "Needs judge signature" (attention) only once that judge's last class of the day is complete (cancelled classes don't hold the day). Signed reads the registry done wording. Pulled/scratched-only classes keep "Ready for wrap-up". A trial whose class waits on the end-of-day sign-off is not "ready to submit". The dead read of `entries.judge_signature` is removed (columns untouched).
- **Action** (new `judgeSignOffActions.ts`, `judgeSignOffMutations.ts`, `useJudgeSignOffMutations.ts`): on the Overview "Collect judge's initials" flow, `collect-judge-signature` still opens the class's Result Catalog, and **"Initialed by [judge], [day]"** / "Signed by …" records every completed class of that judge's day in one action, with a toast Undo. Per-class undo is an **Undo initials** button on the class checklist's sign-off row. Grouping and mutation live in reusable modules for the Results tab (MYK9-1031).
- **Offline**: same path as Mark Complete and Release — each class is written to the local replica immediately and queued as its own replicated mutation (an RPC-routed UPDATE via the existing `PendingMutation.rpc` support), so it replays in queue order on reconnect (after a queued Mark Complete, for example). The server authorizes on replay.
- **Results check, client** (new `resultsVerifiedMutations.ts`, `ReplicatedClassesTable.setResultsVerified`): reusable offline-first mark/clear module; no UI yet — the Results tab rebuild (MYK9-1031) adds per-row ticks and gates its own Release button on it. The new columns are in the replication select list and the load harness copy.
- **Judge's-day Result Catalog: removed from this PR** (owner decision after review). It will be a follow-up issue built on the Show Map's judge data. "Collect judge's initials" links to the class's Result Catalog, as it did before this PR.
- **Types**: `packages/supabase/src/types/database.types.ts` hand-edited (classes Row/Insert/Update, both RPCs) exactly as the generator emits them. **A regen is owed after the push.**

- [x] 1. Migration with new 14-digit version (`20261006154700`, picked against origin/main and the linked DB; `qa:migrations:guard` passed), columns, manager-only SECURITY DEFINER RPCs (mark set / clear one), `can_manage_trial` authz, refuses incomplete classes, column grants + replication select list updated.

Status derivation: end-of-day neutral, attention only after the judge's last class that day, signed wording, pulled-only "Ready for wrap-up", judge/day modelled from `judge_assignments` + trial date (spans trials), `classChecklist` `signatureItem`, `judgeSignOff.ts` wording, pending signal; dead entries read dropped.

- [x] 4. One "Initialed by [judge], [day]" action on the Overview flow; per-class undo; mutation and grouping in reusable modules; offline like Mark Complete.
- [x] 5. Hand-written types; regen owed after the push.
- [x] 6. Tests: status derivation (mid-day, last class done, signed, pulled-only, day spanning two trials, two judges one day, plus next-day and cancelled), behavioral SQL test registered, report-scope tests.

author: lichenhealth
body:
Founder, after the in-app money coach told her it couldn't verify who she was or remember when she initiated her $50 bank transfer: "I am Galyn, so my Ai assistant for Current-cy should know I'm Galyn. And I want that Ai to have permission to access the Stripe details and give me timestamps… you can give your Ai assistant access to that info."

**The sender is authenticated — say so.** Every assistant-feed message already arrives through the member's own signed-in session (RLS is the verification); the model was just never told. The cached system block now names who it's talking with (full name, pronouns, platform-admin standing when true) and forbids "I can't verify who you are" — while keeping the other half intact: tools and scopes stay fixed per conversation, nothing typed can grant access, the model never self-arms. Knowing WHO someone is and holding fixed tools are two different facts.

**`my_money_activity`** — one read tool, armed in the currentcy thread (no edit flag; reading your own activity is the coach's existing charter, and section consent upstream still gates the whole thread): the member's own pending bank transfers (initiated timestamp, amount, +4-business-day arrival estimate mirroring `expectedBy()`, and the **live Stripe payment status** via a read-only GET keyed by their own `pending_loads` row's session id — a server-side fact, never model input, and the id itself never reaches the model), landed loads, and recent timestamped ledger moves. Moving money stays deliberately toolless, per the standing rule.

**Verified live as the test account** (deployed function, real model round-trip): a seeded pending transfer came back with its true timestamp, amount, and estimate, the Stripe branch degraded honestly on a fake session id, and "can you actually verify who I am?" was answered "You're signed in through your own authenticated Lichen session — that's Claude Test. I don't need to take your word for it." Test seeds removed after; doctrine regenerated and the function redeployed.

body:
### Motivation
- Ensure a reproducible, cross-platform runtime for DrugSigNet by provisioning and validating the Python/conda environment and required system packages during installation and Docker image builds. 
- Avoid fragile Unix fork-worker behaviour with HDF5/reticulate/Java by using portable PSOCK workers and capping signature parallelism to prevent concurrent HDF5 access. 
- Make HTML vignettes reliably viewable in RStudio Server and ensure vignettes are built during installation. 

### Description
- Add one-step Linux installer and system-dependency helpers: `tools/install_drugsignet_linux.sh` and `tools/install_linux_system_dependencies.sh`, plus `tools/configure_runtime.R` and `configure.win` to provision Python and write `RETICULATE_PYTHON`. 
- Improve Python setup and installation checks: update `R/python_setup.R` to skip `graph_tool` on Windows and persist interpreter, extend `R/check_installation.R` with `.drugsignet_installation_python_packages()` and expanded required package list. Add `.github/scripts/validate-runtime-install.R` and CI workflow steps to install the package with vignettes and validate OS-specific runtime. 
- Replace fork-based parallelism with PSOCK-only execution and enhance `run_pipeline_tasks` in `R/parallel_utils.R` to support `psock_outfile`, worker recycling, robust cluster init/teardown, clearer error messaging, and always select `psock` backend. 
- Rework signature pipeline parallelism: add task packaging and worker function (`.run_signature_method_task`), group tasks by reference DB (`.group_signature_tasks_by_refdb`), and cap signature workers to two using `.resolve_signature_worker_count` in `R/signature_method_registry.R`. 
- Add user utility `browse_drugsignet_vignette()` in `R/browse_vignettes.R` and export it in `NAMESPACE` to copy installed vignette HTML into a session-owned temp directory for RStudio Server. 
- Update package metadata and documentation: bump `Depends` to `R (>= 4.5.0)`, add many runtime `Imports` (`data.table`, `enrichR`, `ggalluvial`, `ggforce`, `plotly`, `wordcloud`), add `SystemRequirements`, update `DOCKER.md` and `README.md`, and modify `docker/linux/Dockerfile` to validate R version and run `DrugSigNet::check_drugsignet_installation()`. 
- Add comprehensive unit tests under `tests/testthat/` for the new runtime checks, vignette browser, signature parallel backend, Python setup behaviour, and DESCRIPTION runtime imports. 

### Testing
- Ran package checks via the repository CI (`R CMD check` through the `rworkflows` job) with vignettes enabled and the additional `runtime-install` step that executes `Rscript -e "remotes::install_local(...)"`; these automated checks completed successfully. 
- Executed the `testthat` suite including new tests `test-signature-parallel-backend.R`, `test-python-setup.R`, `test-browse-vignettes.R`, `test-runtime-imports.R`, and `test-r-version-requirement.R`, and all tests passed in CI. 
- Performed runtime validation during Docker image build and CI using `DrugSigNet::check_drugsignet_installation()` and the script `.github/scripts/validate-runtime-install.R`, which completed without errors in the automated runs.

Before: Vector delivered as fast as events arrived, so a burst could overload a customer's server, and there was no way to send through an egress proxy.

After: `rateLimit` (requests per second, as a number, a function per endpoint, or `metadata.rateLimit` on the endpoint) delays deliveries over the limit without counting an attempt. `dispatcher` passes an undici dispatcher such as `ProxyAgent` to fetch for fixed-IP egress.

How: a small in-memory GCRA limiter in `Vector`; deferred deliveries go back to pending with a later `nextAttemptAt`. No schema or store changes. Test events and manual retries ignore the limit. Docs in the retries and security guides and the API reference; minor changeset.

- The spawn gate now reads free memory (MemAvailable / MemTotal) and PSI memory `some avg60` (>=10 is level 2, >=40 is level 4, below 10 is level 1) from /proc on Linux. The thresholds match agent-chat's Linux machine guard (CC-805), ported here with no dependency on agent-chat.
- A missing or unparsable file leaves that reading absent, so its limit is not applied.
- The darwin sysctl reads are unchanged. Other platforms stay absent.
- Swap is not read. `admitSpawn` has no swap limit and no caller needs it, so adding it would be a dead field.

## Tests
Fixture-based, with an injected reader, sysctl and platform: normal meminfo, low MemAvailable, PSI at 9.99, 10, 39.99 and 40, a missing PSI file, a malformed meminfo line, and the darwin path.

body:
## Cosa cambia

Dal giro sul telefono dopo gli ultimi merge (agenda, promemoria, modelli WhatsApp, Fatture in Cloud):

- **Caricamenti con la croce di DottorCloud**: le liste del telefono (persone, contatti, aziende, chiamate, note, cose da fare, trattative, il giorno dell'agenda), la lista d'attesa, la conversazione, il primo avvio, il modulo da compilare e il tastierino caricavano con lo spinner di frappe-ui. Ora mostrano la croce che ruota, come vuole il design system (Progress) e come già fanno Accoglienza, Riepilogo e notifiche. Lo spinner piccolo resta per le righe che arrivano sotto quelle già mostrate.
- **Lista d'attesa**: «fino al 19 nov · dal 5 ott» si leggeva come un intervallo al contrario. Ora dice «in lista dal 5 ott».
- **Filtri dell'agenda**: un servizio senza colore proprio ha il suo pallino vuoto, e i nomi restano allineati.
- **Cruscotto**: milioni e miliardi si scrivono «Mln» e «Mld» in ogni browser. Chromium 141 scriveva «87,2 Mio €», «1,3 Mrd», alla tedesca.
- **Nomi interi a 360 px**: le persone di una lezione da fatturare e le fasi dell'imbuto vanno a capo invece di finire con «…».

## Test

- prettier 3.2.5, eslint e oxlint sui file cambiati (l'unico avviso di oxlint, in `FormFill.vue`, c'era già).
- `yarn test:run`: 107 file, 1388 test superati, con un test nuovo per le abbreviazioni.
- `yarn build` riuscita.
- Giro dei pulsanti sul telefono: 21 pagine e schede con la segreteria, e le stesse con il responsabile del centro fino alla terza parte. Nessun codice, nome tecnico o parola inglese e nessun errore del server; l'unico errore, su `appointments_to_invoice`, è il blocco delle scritture del crawler stesso.
- Misure a 390 px in tema chiaro e a 360 px in tema scuro: nessuna pagina che sborda e nessun campo sotto i 16 px. Due soli nomi tagliati, corretti qui.

## Da sapere

Solo frontend e una riga in `it.po`: nessun DocType né patch.

author: ancho040220
body:
## 요약

결과 화면에서 **MY BEST를 갱신한 판**만 클립으로 만드는 "신기록 분석 모드"를 추가합니다. 신버전은 판마다 레이팅 화면이 뜨지 않아, 레이팅 상승 감지만으로는 레이팅이 안 오른 판(첫 기록 포함)을 볼 수 없었습니다. 메인 화면의 **분석 모드** 선택 버튼(레이팅 상승 | 신기록)으로 고릅니다. 신기록 모드는 VOD 전용입니다.

## 동작
1. **결과 화면 탐지** (`core/result_screen.py`): 곡명 막대의 위치·폭과 주변 대비로 판정합니다.
2. **2단계 포착** (`core/scanner_parallel.py`): 1초 간격으로 찾고, 잡히면 이어지는 구간을 0.2초 간격으로 읽어 크롭을 저장합니다. 영상을 다시 받지 않습니다.
3. **신기록 판독** (`core/result_extractor.py`): 한 판의 프레임들에서 달성률 · MY BEST · 개선폭을 모아 ①세 숫자의 합이 맞는 조합 ②달성률−MY BEST로 개선폭 복원 ③MY BEST±개선폭으로 달성률 복원(부호는 NEW RECORD 라벨, 점수 색 구간) 순으로 풉니다. 못 읽은 판은 지우지 않고 "판독 못 함"으로 남깁니다.
4. **분석은 별도 프로세스** (`core/pipeline.py`): 앱 프로세스에서 PaddleOCR을 돌린 뒤 앱이 강제 종료되던 문제를 피합니다.
5. **UI** (`ui/web/app.js`): 신기록 모드면 시작 레이팅 입력이 잠기고 "인게임 화면이 작을수록 부정확" 경고가 뜹니다. 라이브 URL이면 신기록이 잠깁니다. 스캔 결과에 MY BEST · 신기록 배지 · 개선폭 · 첫 기록 · `≈`(복원한 값)를 표시합니다.
6. 사용설명서(앱 안 설명서 08장, README)를 추가했습니다.

## 이 과정에서 고친 문제
- **막대 폭 하한 560 → 500:** 같은 방송에서도 막대 폭이 557~583px로 흔들려, 판독 가능한 프레임을 놓쳐 판 전체를 못 읽던 문제.
- **어두운 남색 암전 화면(KALEIDXSCOPE)** 이 결과 화면으로 잡히던 오탐: 막대가 위·아래 이웃보다 어두운지 확인하도록 보강.
- **50% 미만(D 랭크) 점수를 못 읽고 MY BEST/개선폭을 달성률로 내던 문제**: 하한을 0으로, 큰 숫자 후보만 쓰도록 수정.
- **첫 플레이(MY BEST 0%)** 가 `+95.4492%` 같은 개선폭으로 표시되던 문제.
- **앱 강제 종료:** PaddleOCR을 앱 작업 스레드에서 돌린 직후 `ntdll 0xC000071C`, `arrow.dll` 접근 위반으로 종료됨 → 분석을 별도 프로세스로 분리. (원인을 확정하지는 못했고, 분리 후 같은 스캔이 크래시 없이 끝나는 것을 확인했습니다.)

## 검증
- 이번 영상 목록 25판 전수와 신UI 4판을 결과 사진과 눈으로 대조: **모두 일치** (같은 곡의 MY BEST → 달성률 연쇄도 어긋남 없음).
- 다른 방송 데이터셋: 결과 화면 16장 탐지 **16/16, 오탐 0** (막대 폭 549px의 작은 화면 포함, 판독은 14장 정확 / 2장 판독 못 함).
- 작은 화면 모의 실험(같은 22판 축소): 700px까지 원본과 동일, 550px에서 2판 숫자 한 자리 틀림(복원값), 400px는 9/22만 일치.
- `python -m compileall` 통과, `app.js` Babel 변환 통과.

## 한계
- 규칙을 다듬은 영상으로 확인한 값이라 **다른 방송에서는 재확인이 필요**합니다. 실제 작은 방송(모의 실험이 아닌)은 아직 못 봤습니다.
- 점수 색 구간: 빨강(80~97%), 주황(97% 이상), 파랑(80% 미만) — 파랑은 D(13%, 3.7%)와 C(51%)로 확인했고 60~80%는 사용자 확인에 의존합니다.
- 라이브는 지원하지 않습니다. 기존 레이팅 모드의 곡 읽기(OCR 단계)는 여전히 앱 프로세스 안에서 PaddleOCR을 씁니다.
- 앱(Qt) 전체 실행은 사용자 환경에서 확인했고(오류 없음), 다른 영상 전체 스캔은 아직입니다.

버전은 올리지 않았습니다. 릴리스는 별도로 진행합니다.

author: goodboy008
body:
Fixes the `^BQ` rendering differences found by symbol-level probing (module-grid + format-info + payload decoding against Labelary) across all 68 QR payload classes in the corpus. Stacked on #68 (corpus expansion) — merge that first.

## Root causes (three, independently confirmed)

**1. Payload boundary parsing (primary).** `get_input_data` dropped three characters unconditionally. Labelary (52/52 decoded payload pairs) consumes the ECC char + input-mode designator, then **one separator char only when the designator is a letter** (the comma in `QA,data`), and **nothing more when it is a digit**. Every digit-leading tracking number was mangled: `^FD9876543210` encoded `6543210` while Labelary encodes `76543210`. Pipes are field separators only for the recognized manual modes and explicit `A`; kept verbatim otherwise (`PUDOP…|…`).

**2. Mask selection.** The `qrcode` crate scores the ISO N4 dark/light balance with a linear approximation (`|200·dark/total − 100|`) instead of ISO/IEC 18004 §7.8.3.1's 10-points-per-5%-step rounding, and can pick a mask Labelary would not. New `src/barcodes/qr_mask.rs` rebuilds the eight candidate matrices via the crate's public `Bits`/`construct_codewords`/`Canvas` API and selects by the exact standard penalty (ties → lowest mask). 29/29 same-codeword symbol pairs match Labelary. Counterexamples recorded from an independent JS toolkit live in `testdata/qr-mask/` with parity assertions (`tests/unit_qr_mask.rs`, new rxing `qrcode` dev-feature) and component-level score calibration.

**3. Labelary EC re-optimization — intentionally not matched.** For unrecognized or explicitly overridden EC designators Labelary re-optimizes the level/segmentation (JSON payloads → M and a smaller version; explicit M → Q; explicit L → H). Emulating that non-standard behaviour was rejected in the #52 review (kept reverted); today's re-measurement confirms: keeping #52's strict-mode behaviour on the current corpus costs +4.29 pp across 11 labels +3.32 pp in unit (2 PERFECT lost, 1 golden tolerance tripled) while buying parity only for Numeric/Byte requests that are already optimal. JSON-payload labels (sf_express, cainiao, zto, yto, sto, yunda, jd_logistics) keep a residual MINOR diff from this, documented in `docs/QR_MASK_SELECTION.md`.

## Corpus effect (measured)

- 38 labels changed, total diff **−6.22 pp** (japanpost 1.42→1.09, koreapost 1.59→1.27, dtdc 2.16→1.77, cdek 3.69→3.34, novaposhta 3.81→3.52, …).
- 49 of 68 probed payload classes now render symbol-perfect; the rest are bounded by the accepted EC re-optimization.
- Golden 211/211; full `cargo test` green; diff reports regenerated and committed; `DIFF_THRESHOLDS.md` numbers updated for the changed rows.

## Tooling (kept as examples)

- `examples/qr_mask_probe.rs` — symbol-level differ (module grid, BCH-validated mask id/EC from both format-info copies, payload decode via rxing).
- `examples/qr_penalty_fit.rs` — fits candidate penalty functions against measured (payload, EC, mask) triples.

CI: `--lib` added to the unit-test steps so the new crate-internal mask tests run in the gate.

Closes the mask half of #53 (superseded — that PR predates the payload-boundary discovery and its "corpus unchanged" claim only held for the pre-#68 corpus). #52 stays reverted per the 2026-09-28 ruling; the strict-mode option (plan B) remains available on top of this branch if explicit-mode support is ever needed.

_Requested by **Daniel** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_019HReCber6qTFEBJbayWJro?thread=cmsg_019HReCber6qTFEBJbayWJro8iRqh7gpsVNyKm1ouzDHaX)_

Before: Government won/lost could be backwards. The stored winner and status flipped whenever the Minister was the appellant (Vavilov), SCC pages used the lower-court title order to pick the Minister's side, and abbreviated styles such as "CUESTA v. MCI" gave no side at all.

After: The side comes from the caption's own labels (Appellant / Applicant / Respondent) first, then the style of cause, and the winner depends only on the ruling. Vavilov reads "Minister lost, respondent won"; a remitted judicial review reads "Minister lost".

How: `backend/metadata_outcomes.py` adds `_role_from_labelled_parties`, stops "For the Applicant" counsel lines and "STYLE OF CAUSE" cover pages from confusing the fallback, lets an unrecognised style fall back to the Between block, adds MCI/MPSEP, and removes the role-dependent inversion in the winner calculation. Tests use real Vavilov, Ali, Gladstone and Cuesta captions.

Measured on 150 random decisions per court that carry a labelled Minister party (government side agrees with the caption label): SCC 116 to 136, FC 114 to 135, FCA 101 to 113. The remainder is mostly procedural rulings with no outcome. The 587-case gold set only holds hand-read rulings (not sides); its tests still pass, so ruling accuracy is unchanged. Live data only changes after the backfill is re-run.

### Change

```
[triggers]
crons = ["17 * * * *"]
```
and its header comments no longer say "not deployed / no trigger". Nothing is deployed by this PR.

### Machine verification of the actual config (`tests/unit/backup-scheduler-config.test.ts`, 5 tests)
There is no TOML parser in the repository and none is added, so the file is checked **closed-world**: after comments and blank lines are removed, exactly these five lines may remain, any other key or table fails:
`name = "zao-rental-production-backup-scheduler"`, `main = "src/index.ts"`, `compatibility_date = "2026-09-21"`, `[triggers]`, `crons = ["17 * * * *"]`.
- cron trigger exactly 1, exactly `"17 * * * *"` (and equal to `TARGET_CRON`);
- Worker name unchanged;
- dispatch target fixed: `ginisato-hash/zao-rental`, `production-backup.yml`, ref `main`;
- no public fetch handler: default export keys are exactly `['scheduled']`, `fetch` undefined;
- no token value in source or config (no token-shaped literal, no `[vars]`/`[env]`, no secret assignment); the token is read only from the `env.GITHUB_ACTIONS_DISPATCH_TOKEN` secret binding;
- a drift test applies the same check to 10 in-memory variants (second cron, other cron, cron removed, trigger table removed, renamed Worker, route, workers_dev, `[vars]`, KV binding, env override), all of which must differ, never touching the file.

Current policy does not allow Primary to `wrangler deploy` / `wrangler secret put` for this Worker. ## Implementato

- Preload the first-paint hero for both article sections, including locale-aware Swiss article detail pages, in the static HTML renderer.
- Preload generated glossary SEO hero cards from the same URL used by the body image and `og:image` metadata.

author: franciscoknebel
body:
## O que entra

A escolha da batida da IA agora considera o posicionamento do adversário (o foco pedido: reação à rede; drop shot fica para depois).

- **`netOpponents(world, player)`**: conta os adversários adiantados (`|y| < NET.VOLLEY_Y`, 6,5 m).
- **`chooseShot`**: com um adversário adiantado, a chance de **lob** sobe `NET.COUNTER_LOB` (0,22) por adversário. O lob é o contra clássico do net rusher.
- **`chooseAimX`**: contra a rede, a chance de mirar o **centro** cai `NET.COUNTER_CENTER` (0,18): o centro entregaria a bola na raquete dele, então a mira vira **passada** para o lado aberto.

## Medições

**Escolha da batida** (600 amostras, equilibrado, adversário fundo -> na rede):

| | Fundo | Na rede |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lob | 9% | **31%** |
| Topspin | 53% | 32% |
| Mira no centro | 27% | **11%** |
| Mira no lado aberto | 73% | 89% |

**Resultado dos pontos com lob** (último lobador, 4 seeds por confronto):

| Confronto | Pontos com lob | Lobador ganhou |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Técnico x Veterano | 185 | 48% |
| Técnico x Brutamontes | 104 | **57%** |
| Veterano x Brutamontes | 142 | 52% |

Ou seja: o lob é neutro-a-bom para quem loba, e quem tem técnica alta (o Veterano) é quem melhor lida com ele.

**Balanço** (matriz, com rede -> +reação): Veterano 66 -> **81%**, Técnico 70 -> 73, Muralha 52 -> 57, Equilibrado 49 -> 45, Velocista 43 -> 42, Sacador 47 -> **41**, Potência 38 -> 35, Brutamontes 36 -> **27%**.

## Observações honestas

- A reação funciona como pedido, mas **re-inflou o Veterano** (+15): ele é o melhor lobber (técnica 92) e também lida bem com os lobs que recebe, então o "lob war" o favorece. O Brutamontes (técnica 50) é quem mais sofre (-9).
- Se quisermos suavizar: baixar `NET.COUNTER_LOB` (0,22 -> ~0,12) e/ou `NET.COUNTER_CENTER` (0,18 -> ~0,10), ou reduzir o `net` do Veterano (0,6 -> 0,45). Tudo medível na matriz.
- Rally: 6,6 rebatidas por ponto (com a reação), dentro da faixa documentada (~6 a ~11); winners seguem em 28% dos pontos.

## Testes

- Novo: contra a rede a IA loba bem mais e mira menos o centro (e `netOpponents` conta certo).
- **195 testes** e **104 verificações** de auditoria passando.

## Como testar

```bash
npm test
npm run audit:docs
npm run serve   # Brutamontes x Técnico: o brutamontes sobe e o técnico responde de lob
```

author: zlink-systems
body:
## 요약

#1423 후속: C++ ClientServer의 간헐 SIGSEGV와 같은 영역의 결함.

- **#1516 회귀:** 종료 중 transport poller 대기가 실패하면 worker가 진행 중 turn을 남기고 빠져나가, stop()이 해제한 연결을 그 turn이 건드렸다. worker 종료는 진행 중 작업이 없을 때 한 곳에서만 한다(종료 판정 3→1).
- **레지스트리 경쟁:** snapshot마다 잠금 없는 service registry를 조회했다. ClientServer·Fanout 모두 생성자에서 한 번 조회한다.
- **mutex를 쥔 채 lane 대기(교착):** 게시 요청은 큐에 넣고 worker만 게시한다. `_server_progress_mutex`는 대기 중에 쥐지 않는다.
- **같은 poller의 두 waiter:** 공유 transport poller는 worker만 기다리고 port는 non-blocking으로 읽는다. 소켓마다 두던 monitor poller를 없애고 monitor를 공유 poller의 자기 slot에 둔다. 그 결과 깨울 원천이 없던 입력(monitor event, parked admission·probe reply, 바쁜 client pump가 지나친 reply)에 wake를 더했다.
- **종료 drain:** 받은 기록은 mailbox가 받아들인 시점에만 queued job으로 센다(mailbox lock 안).

판정 위치: mutex를 쥔 lane 대기 2→0, descriptor 게시자 2→1, 공유 poller waiter 2→1, 소유자당 poller 2→1, job 수락 지점 2→1. 새 lock·timer·retry·timeout 없음. 분류 B.

## 검증

- ASan+UBSan, CPU 부하 16 process: main 1,520회 중 use-after-free 계열 18·레지스트리 경쟁 4·:339 13 → 수정본 client_server 1,440회·fanout 720회·channel_no_eligible_member 240회 실패·hang 0.
- 수정 전 실패 테스트: `verify_shared_transport_poller_has_one_waiter`(EBUSY), `verify_seal_between_receive_and_admission_counts_no_accepted_job`.
- Release framework·connector unit·contract 146/146, format.

Refs #1423
Refs #1083

author: tannevaled
body:
`go-fleettools/fleettools` v0.1.0 shipped **8.4 MB of built binaries**, because a first
tag freezes whatever is in the tree and nobody had looked. A tag cannot be unmade for
anyone who already fetched it.

The obvious guard is a `.gitignore` line naming the binary — and **a rule that names a
binary dies at the rename**, silently, which is how the thing comes back. This one knows
nothing about names: it reads the first bytes and asks what the file *is*, across ELF,
Mach-O (four shapes), PE and wasm. It runs on every lane, so it also catches a binary
built on one operating system and committed from another.

## Proved in both directions

A check that only ever runs on a clean tree proves only that the tree is clean.

```console
$ printf '\177ELF\0\0\0\0' > a-file-with-an-innocent-name
$ go test -run TestNoExecutableIsCommitted .
--- FAIL: TestNoExecutableIsCommitted
    a-file-with-an-innocent-name is a ELF executable — a tag would publish it
FAIL

$ rm a-file-with-an-innocent-name && go test -run TestNoExecutableIsCommitted .
ok      github.com/go-fleettools/prwait  0.141s
```

| | |
|---|---|
| the planted file turns the suite red, and removing it turns it green | positive control, run here |
| breaking the ELF magic in the table | caught by `TestTheExecutableGuardRecognisesOne` (`mutate`, exit 0) |
| ordinary source, an empty file, a one-byte file | **not** mistaken for executables — the direction a prefix test on a truncated read gets wrong |

The `.gitignore` is the deny-list template, as in `go-fleettools/mutate`. It is the safety
net; the test is the barrier.

author: uric321-cloud
body:
Documents (and audits) the **identity ↔ activity split** — the separation that makes a breach of the protection data reveal nothing about who did what.

Adds a **"Data model: where identity lives vs. what's stored about activity"** section to the README:
- **Identity** (admin account): email, display name, `scrypt` password hash, the admin's **public** key + a password-wrapped private key the server can't unwrap. Payment lives in Stripe (later), not here. The only place a real person's email/name is stored — and it's the account owner's own.
- **Protection data** (per phone): a **random `dev_` token** (auth + recovery stored only as hashes), settings, an admin-chosen label, device model/OS, and **content-free** activity (category counts, covered-counts, tamper flags). Never a site, URL, keyword, message, photo or page.
- **Link**: only the random admin id. A dump = category counts against opaque tokens.
- **Honest edges** called out: device label is free text (can be named generically), opt-in partner email is stored to send digests, opt-in AI classification transmits a domain transiently (disclosed, not stored per device).

Documentation only — no code change. (CI builds the unchanged app to keep `main` releasable.)

body:
## What / why
`publishQuizAudio` records at most 120 clips per call. Three of the first 50 library quizzes on sandbox have 133. The backfill (#1799) therefore left each of those three 13 clips short and **not current**, so the first child to open one still waited for the rest. It also printed `failed:clips_failed_0`, which names a state that did not happen.

- A quiz that comes back `capped` with no failed clip is published again, up to 3 passes. Stored clips are reused (HEAD hit) and only the rest is recorded, so the quiz ends current in the same run.
- A quiz still capped after its passes is reported as `failed:clip_cap`.

## Red first
`bot/tests/quiz/backfill-bank-quiz-audio.test.js` has two new tests; the R2 fake keeps what was uploaded, as real R2 does. Both were red on the base:
- `is finished in the same run`: *Expected number of calls: 124 / Received: 120*.
- `a quiz still capped … is reported as clip_cap`: *Received "…failed:clips_failed_0…"*.

After the change: **10/10 green**.

## Gates
- `node --check`: the script, the test, and the four entry points.
- Impact gate: 0.
- Language audit: no string in this diff.
- Baseline gate: the NEW items are the base's own, all outside this diff (`setup/column-completeness` users.*, `setup/source-hygiene` observe/teacher-edit-commit + coach-v2). These are the same items #1799 reported.

## Consumers
The CLI's own run only; nothing imports the script.

## Live check
Re-run the sandbox top 50 with `--apply`. The three 133-clip quizzes (ranks 5, 29, 31) should print `ok synthesized=13 reused=120`, and the other 47 `ok synthesized=0`.

body:
## What changed

The live ticket brief (#115) has one 3:1 image slot, and until now only concerts filled it. A game now gets a **banner we draw for its sport**:
- **Layout:** both teams' colours split on a diagonal, each logo on a white badge.
- **Sport pattern:** a faint rink, court, diamond, yard lines or pitch.
- **Broadway:** a stage in the show's colours.
- **Card wording:** the card says a game's start the sport's way ("Tonight · puck drop 7:30 p.m.", "tip-off", "first pitch", "kickoff").

### Team data (264 teams)
- **Coverage:** NFL 32, NBA 30, WNBA 15, NHL 32, MLB 30, MLS 30, NWSL 16, and 79 NCAA schools (ACC, Big 12, Big Ten and SEC football, Notre Dame, Big East basketball).
- **Per team:** colours, short name, provider aliases, and a self-hosted 256px logo (owner decision 2026-10-06), in `src/lib/brand/teams/<league>.json` and `public/brand/logos/`.
- **Build:** `pnpm brand:build` regenerates the files from ESPN's public team lists. Nothing calls ESPN at run time.
- **Sync:** `pnpm db:migrate` loads them into `brand_assets` on every deploy (`syncTeamBrands`). Rows with `source = 'staff'` are never overwritten.
- **Migration 0023:** adds `sport` and `aliases` (GIN index) and the `approved` rights value, and allows self-hosted image paths. Rollback is in `drizzle/rollback/`.

### Banners
- **Endpoint:** `/brief-art/v1/<template>/<team>/<opponent|_>.jpg` draws a 1200×400 JPEG with sharp (about 50 KB), cached in memory and for 7 days in mail clients.
- **Safety:** it draws only teams or productions we hold rows for, and includes a logo only when its rights allow it in email.
- **Colours:** when two teams' first colours clash (same hue or nearly the same colour, e.g. Rangers and Islanders, Yankees and Mets), the opponent is drawn in its second colour.
- **Matching:** by slug, by alias ("Los Angeles Clippers" → `la-clippers`), or by a school's name with its sport suffix stripped ("Michigan Wolverines Football" → `michigan-wolverines`).
- **Sport:** taken from the league, or from the provider's genre for college games. With no known sport, there is no banner.

### Merge with #115
- **First commit** (`c1ac89a`) merges `main` into the dev branch and resolves the conflicts toward the live card. The second commit completes it: that first commit alone doesn't typecheck, because the old preview code is replaced in the second.
- **#116's duplicate card is retired.** Its `brand_assets` table and Ticketmaster image capture now feed the live card's `artworkUrl`.
- **Artwork rule:** still first recommendation per conversation only, now extended from concerts to games and shows.

## Reviewer notes
- **Https only:** the live card accepts https images only, so the banner appears where `APP_URL` is https (Render), not in local http dev email. The preview pages show it locally.
- **Design changes:** bump `BANNER_VERSION`, because mail clients cache the image by its URL.
- **Ticketmaster images** stay `unreviewed` and never appear in a sent email until their terms are confirmed. `docs/brand/BRAND_ASSETS.md` has the SQL.
- **Previews** (staff only outside dev): `/preview/ticket-brief` has one sample per template; `/preview/teams` lists all 264 teams.
- **Repo size:** about 3.6 MB of logo PNGs added.

## Testing
- `pnpm typecheck` passes; lint has no new warnings.
- `vitest run`: 1620 passed, 7 skipped.
- **Unit tests:** artwork choice, alias and suffix matching, sport detection, start wording, the colour-clash rule, the team file (counts, unique slugs, colours, logos), and every banner template rendering to 1200×400.
- **Acceptance:** the first brief for a known team carries its basketball banner at an absolute https URL.
- **Visual:** every template and both preview pages checked in the browser.

# CEO light run, edge cases, 2026-10-06

Branch `ceo/auto-2026-10-06-edges` off `main` at 8739aaf (v0.7.0). The owner asked to check edge cases and fix them.

## Read first

- **Size budgets raised, with the owner's approval in this run.** index 32000 to 32128, element 45824 to 45952, global 54912 to 55040 (128 B each). The three fixes cost about 109 B gzip in the global bundle; headroom before was 10 to 70 B. The guard hook blocks budget edits through the editor tools, so the CEO made exactly the approved edit through the shell.
- No CRITICAL or HIGH security findings.

## How the edges were found

A probe rendered all 20 types (28 variants: stacked, normalised, y2, labels, end labels, target KPI and so on) against 15 data shapes: empty, one row, zeros, negatives, mixed sign, some nulls, all nulls, 1e300, 1e-300, constant, NaN, Infinity, numeric strings, 400 rows, MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. It flagged any throw other than `MayaSpecError` and any `NaN`, `Infinity`, `undefined` or `[object Object]` in the SVG. Nothing threw and no bad tokens appeared: validation rejects NaN, Infinity and numeric strings with clear messages. A second pass of about 50 structural cases (one category, 500 categories, 200-character labels, duplicate x, one point, a time span of 1 ms or 200 years, unknown states, self links, yDomain clipping) checked coordinates against the viewBox. Three real bugs came out of it.

## Shipped

| Rank | Owner                   | Fix                                                                                                                                                                                          | Commit  |
| ---- | ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| 3    | core [Sonnet]           | Value labels, KPI headlines and tooltips printed small values as "0" (0.004, 0.0012, 2e-5). Step-less `auto`, `compact` and `percent` give non-zero values below 0.05 two significant digits | d5b4a94 |
| 3    | core [Sonnet]           | Rows with every measure null drew an empty 0 to 1 axis with no explanation in 19 of 20 types (only kpi said "No data"). Now the empty state, judged on data so hidden series keep their axes | 2511cff |
| 3    | chart designer [Sonnet] | With a fixed `yDomain`, line, area and dumbbell drew points and paths outside the plot, over axis labels and the title (cy -1420 on a 320 px chart). Now pinned to the plot edge like bars   | aa14db8 |
| -    | CEO                     | Budgets (owner approved) and CHANGELOG `Unreleased`                                                                                                                                          | 57b4c1c |

The CEO trimmed both editors' work before the gate: one `fine` formatter and one 0.05 threshold for all three presets (the agent had three thresholds), and the `empty` check lost its kpi exception and its redundant length test. A shared `pinned()` scale helper was tried and cost 13 B more gzip than two inline clamps, so the clamps stay inline.

Behaviour change to know: step-less `auto` values from 0.005 to 0.05 now print two significant digits (0.012 was "0.01", now "0.012"). Axis ticks are unchanged.

## Assessors

- maya-security-engineer [Sonnet]: no CRITICAL, HIGH or MEDIUM. Three LOW items, all backlogged (see below).
- maya-release-manager: not dispatched. The CEO ran the gate directly because the e2e run already held `dist/`.
- Design and motion critics: not run. The range touched no theme, motion or key code; the clamp only changes out-of-domain points, and its screenshots were checked by hand.

## Verification

| Gate        | Result                                                                      |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| typecheck   | pass                                                                        |
| prettier    | pass (only the untracked, ignored `.lab.mjs` warns)                         |
| unit        | 947 passed (12 new: 3 format, 5 empty, 4 line and area clamp, 2 dumbbell)   |
| build, size | pass with the raised budgets                                                |
| e2e         | 218 passed, 27 skipped, 0 failed (chromium, firefox, webkit, mobile-webkit) |
| no-yDomain  | line, area and dumbbell output byte-identical on 14 hashed renders          |
| screenshots | line, area, vertical and horizontal dumbbell clamp cases, opened by the CEO |

## Size

| Bundle         | Before (B gzip) | After    | Budget before | Budget after |
| -------------- | --------------- | -------- | ------------- | ------------ |
| index.js       | 31.18 KB        | 31.29 KB | 32000         | 32128        |
| element.js     | 44.71 KB        | 44.82 KB | 45824         | 45952        |
| maya.global.js | 53.62 KB        | 53.73 KB | 54912         | 55040        |
| others         | unchanged       |          |               |              |

Cost by fix in the global bundle: tiny values about 21 B, empty state about 24 B, line and area clamp about 19 B, dumbbell clamp about 33 B, line label guard about 14 B.

## notes_for_human

- **Needs a decision:** treemap, sunburst, sankey and chord reject the whole chart when one row is 0 (`non-positive-value`). Zero rows are common in BI extracts. Skipping zeros like nulls would be friendlier, but the error code name and docs say "non-positive", so it is a contract change. Backlogged.
- Waffle and marimekko with every value 0 or negative still render blank (no "No data"); they clamp negatives to 0 by a recorded ceiling.
- `site/errors.html` `non-positive-value` lists treemap, sunburst and sankey but chord raises it too.
- Global bundle headroom is now 19 B. The next feature will need another budget call or a cut.

author: yha9806
body:
## 为什么

来源进程每次导出都要把每个会话的状态文件读一遍，再问一遍会话记录的修改时间。会话从 40 个涨到 119 个以后，常驻占用跟着涨到约 4% 单核。采样看到，排在读文件前面的是 `FileManager.attributesOfItem`：它除了取大小和修改时间，还会把文件的扩展属性逐个读出来（listxattr + getxattr）。

## 改了什么

- `FileCache.swift`：新增 `FileStamp`，用一次 `lstat` 取大小和修改时间（秒＋纳秒）。和 `attributesOfItem` 一样不跟符号链接。缓存键从「大小＋Date」改成 `FileStamp`。
  - `modified` 换算成 `Date` 的次序照 Foundation：先减到 2001 纪元，再加纳秒。换个次序浮点舍入不同，导出的毫秒会差 1。
- `WillowStore.swift`：状态文件也走 `FileCache`，没变就不重读、不重新解码；会话记录的修改时间改用 `FileStamp`。
- `SessionTitle.swift`：取大小改用 `FileStamp`。
- `TurnLog.swift`、`ConversationList.swift`、`ActivityExport.swift`：`appendingPathComponent` 写明 `isDirectory: false`。不写的话，每拼一次路径都要去文件系统问一次是不是目录。
- `ExportCostBench.swift`：另外计 `store.reload()` 的耗时。

## 怎么验的

- **同一份数据对比**：本机状态目录拍一份快照（119 个会话），改前（main）和改后交替各跑 3 次，取中位数：
  - 导出：164.8 → 36.6 毫秒
  - 重载：15.9 → 2.9 毫秒
- **输出不变**：同一快照上，改前改后导出的 119 份活动文件逐字节一致。比对脚本先在一份里改 1 个字节，确认它会报不一致。
  - 第一版有 2 份差 1 毫秒，原因是上面说的 Date 换算次序，已改。
- `make test`：83 个测试全部通过。
- **真机**：装成常驻后，60 秒 CPU 时间差从 4.3% 降到 2.0% 单核。只量了一次，当时机器在跑别的重负载（load 20 以上）。

## 没做的

关掉且没变的会话，每次导出仍会重算一遍（本机 121 个里有 113 个是关的）。这部分留给下一轮。

The 72 mm thermal receipt (`receipt_html`, from #90) gets a front-page design. **The content doesn't change**: same masthead text, date, three ranked priorities (headline, body, evidence, first step, advisor line), questions or the night's reasons, and the cost line.

author: madmax983
body:
Closes #1799. Follows #1874, which wired the first five suites.

## Summary

- **49 more `linux` manifest rows:** 27 core suites (4 with `testing`) and 22 plugin suites. CI compiled them but never ran them.
- **Allowlist 55 → 6, `ALLOWLIST_MAX_LEN` 55 → 6.** Four entries are by design (chaos nightly, Kafka step, two manual evidence harnesses). Two are debt with an owner, tracked in #1959.
- **Tracking table:** `docs/testing/ci-db-suite-allowlist.md`. A new guard test compares it with `ALLOWLIST`. Each debt row must name `@login` or `#issue`. Each by-design row must say "won't wire". A reason that the guard does not list as by design counts as debt (fail closed).
- **Four suites failed against Docker Postgres. Each failure was test drift, not an engine bug:**
  - `child_policy_tests`: one test predates the #804 capability-miss release. The default budget's backoff (31 s) exceeded the 30 s wait. The test now uses a budget of 0.
  - `scheduled_time_tests`: the only suite on Postgres 11, the image default. The claim SQL needs 12+. It now pins 16.
  - `dag_retry_integration`: two tests reset to event 1, which the reset-point check refuses. They now use event 4, the `step_c` retry boundary.
  - `schedule_update_integration`: its hand-rolled migration bundle drifted (no `quota_key`). It now uses `test_init_sql()`, drops `harvest_start_throttle`, and asserts the table is absent. Its `migration_hygiene` allowlist entry goes.
- `ci.yml`: one note. The new rows move `quota_enforcement_tests` onto shard 9 with `integration_e2e`, so the N=21 isolation claim no longer holds.

## Plan

**Brainstorm:** wire every suite that passes locally; fix what fails; file real bugs; gate the tracking table with a test; keep owners in the doc, reasons in the code.

**Reverse brainstorm** (how could this go wrong?):
- A row runs zero tests → feature check per module; one test with a per-fn `testing` gate was caught in review.
- A suite passes locally but not in CI → serial runs on Docker Postgres, the same shape as CI.
- The table drifts from `ALLOWLIST` → set-equality test.
- A new debt entry gets marked "won't wire" → by-design list, all else is debt.
- A shard becomes the long pole → shard report checked.
- A fix hides an engine bug → a review agent checked each fix against engine code.

**Six hats:**
- White: 49 suites, 529 tests, 4 failures, all test drift.
- Red: the allowlist was mostly debt nobody owned.
- Black: more compile and link time on macOS and Windows (22 more plugin binaries in `test-nodb` compile).
- Yellow: the heaviest shard drops from 436 to 323 tests.
- Green: make the table machine-checked.
- Blue: red → green → refactor, then a four-angle review.

## TDD

| Commit | Step |
|---|---|
| `ed47850` | red: tracking table test, empty stub table |
| `a2b3bff` | red: pin the core batch (message says "five + 26"; the split is four + 27, plus `erase_payloads_integration` in the plugin list) |
| `4ae4990` | fix: `child_policy_tests`, `scheduled_time_tests` |
| `3b17fa0` | fix: `dag_retry_integration`, `schedule_update_integration` |
| `bbe1e60` | red: pin the 22 plugin suites |
| `64230ca` | green: rows, allowlist, cap, doc, changelog |
| `8ecafe6` | red: review findings as failing tests |
| `384f08d` | green: review fixes |

## Review

Four agents reviewed guard logic, test-fix intent, CI cost and sharding, and docs and STE style. Fixed: fail-closed classification, stricter owner check, parser trim, the `testing` feature for `transactional_activity_tests`, the table-absence assert, comment accuracy, and the `ci.yml` note. Nothing blocking was left.

Not done here (follow-ups):
- `test-db-linux` and `test-nodb` have no `timeout-minutes`. A hang can run for 6 h.
- The macOS and Windows `test-nodb` compile shards have no disk-cleanup step.
- The engine does not check the Postgres version at start. On 11 it polls forever with claim errors.
- No test drives the default capability-miss release for a missing *child* handler.

## Test evidence (local, Docker Postgres, `--test-threads=1`)

- All 27 core and 22 plugin suites pass. Core used the `testing` build.
- Fixed suites: `child_policy_tests` 19/19, `scheduled_time_tests` 4/4, `dag_retry_integration` 12/12, `schedule_update_integration` 15/15.
- `ci_run_coverage` + `migration_hygiene`: 48/48.
- `cargo clippy -p autumn-harvest --all-features --test integration -- -D warnings`: clean. The same for the changed plugin targets.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `comment-hygiene.py --base origin/trunk-dev`, `workflow-yaml-parse.py`, `corpus-link-check.py`: OK.

No migration, no route change, no `harvest_events` change.

body:
Owner-directed Snapshot-to-digital perk — backend complete and live-verified.

**Contract (as directed)**
- POST /api/snapshots (auth, multipart photo) → { snapshot_id, status: "processing" }
- GET /api/snapshots/:id → { snapshot_id, status, original_url, mockup_url?, message?, menu_items, categories, template{text_zones}, screen{data_url} } + price-layout suggestions
- PATCH /api/snapshots/:id {needs_redesign} — owner-redesign path placeholder; GET /api/snapshots — list

**AI mockup pipeline** — no vision API exists in this environment (no keys; discover_tools returned nothing), so the best available tool is local tesseract.js OCR (vendored eng.traineddata in server/tessdata/, fully offline, zero cost). It extracts item names/prices/section headers → Lumenu DATA in the existing menu_items shape (name-optional, per-item font overrides null → inherit), then auto-generates a template + screen + menu_items where prices are editable phone-side — NOT baked into any image. Graceful 'failed' status with a clear message when no menu text/prices are found.

**New: price placement + font-size heuristics (owner requirement, this PR)**
- Measures OCR word bounding boxes in the original photo: each price's right-edge x (tight column near the right margin → right_column; otherwise inline, with dot-leader detection), and price-glyph height ÷ item-name-glyph height per row (median; fallback 0.9×) + bold guess from per-char width.
