author: lambersond
body:
## Summary

Module 0.9.0 ([lambersond/fvtt-sending-stone#11](https://github.com/lambersond/fvtt-sending-stone/pull/11)) sends the character's favorites: what the player starred in Foundry, as the Favorites panels in dnd5e and Tidy 5e show them. This PR shows them in the app on the four tabs they're most used from: Actions, Inventory, Spells and Effects.

## Where they show

- **Phones, tablets and smaller laptops:** a Favorites strip at the top of those four tabs.
  - Its heading hides or shows it, and this browser remembers that for each character.
  - Where the strip is at least 592 px wide, it splits into two lists side by side. That covers a tablet or a 1280–1366 px laptop.
- **Where the sheet is at least 936 px wide:** a 360 px column to the left of the tab, like Tidy's sidebar, which scrolls on its own. That's about a 1440 px laptop and up, with the chat beside the sheet.
- Character, Features and Biography don't show favorites.

## How each one shows

Each favorite looks and works the same as the row for it elsewhere on the sheet.
- **Item:** shown as its action if it is one, so its attack and damage roll. Right-click or long-press offers advantage or critical damage. Otherwise it shows as its spell, item, feature or class; a class shows its hit dice.
- **Activity,** such as a staff's Cast Fireball: shown as an action of its own, labeled with its item's name.
- **Effect:** says whether it's off or unavailable.
- **Skill or tool:** a check to roll.
- **Spell slots:** shown with pips.
- **Old-style resources:** shown with their uses.
- **Notes the Actions tab gives in a group heading** show on the row instead, such as a quantity (×3) or the item a spell is cast from (From Wand of Magic Missiles).
- **Stars:** a ★ marks each favorite wherever else the sheet lists it, including skills on Character and items inside containers.
- **Roll tray:** it now also shows on Inventory, Spells and Effects when a favorite there can roll.

Favorites are read-only for now. Starring from the app comes with the write-back work.

## Changes

- **Schema and types** (`schemas/sending-stone.ts`, `types/sending-stone.ts`):
  - `favorites` is a union with one shape per favorite type.
  - Malformed favorites and types the app doesn't know are dropped.
  - Sheets from older modules read as having no favorites.
- **`utils/favorites.ts`:** matches each favorite to what it refers to elsewhere on the sheet, and builds the keys the stars use.
- **`favorites.tsx`:** the strip, the column and their rows.
- **`favorite-mark.tsx`:** the star, passed down through React context.
- **`action-entry.tsx`:** the Actions tab's row, chips and damage menu, moved out of `actions-tab.tsx` so a favorite uses the same row. `useDamageRolls` works like `useD20Rolls`.
- **The tabs:**
  - The item, spell, feature and effect rows are now exported.
  - Each of the four tabs takes a `favorites` slot, shown first.
- **`Scroller`:** gets `min-w-0`, so it can sit beside the column.

## Testing

- **Unit tests:** 715 pass, and lint, typecheck and the build are clean. New tests cover `utils/favorites`, the panel, where the pane places favorites, the stars on each tab, the schema and the table view.
- **New browser test:** 52 checks. It runs the module's real code in a stand-in Foundry against the production build.
  - **Sizes:** phone (in dark mode), tablet, and laptops 1366, 1440 and 1920 px wide.
  - **Rolling from favorites:** Fireball's 8d6, Arcana, and Thieves' Tools by long-press with advantage.
  - **Hiding the strip:** remembered across tabs and after a reload.
  - **Stars and the column:** stars appear on every tab, and the column scrolls on its own.
  - **Live updates:** changing favorites in Foundry updates the app without a reload.
- **Earlier browser tests:** all pass with the same counts as before: organize 43, step3 36, step2 57, step1 34, sheet 59, gm 61, conditions 22, late-setup 4, layout 12.
- **Not tried in real Foundry.**

## Release

This needs module 0.9.0; tag it v0.9.0 if that isn't done yet. With an older module, sheets have no favorites and the app looks as it does today.

author: justinmchase
body:
Adds to the planned chapters:

**Fundamental patterns:** errors as modeled data bound to aggregates; workflows with progress trees; queries that are always paged and limited, with opt-in sorting and filtering and whole-collection iteration only in suitable modes; timers and deadlines; tenancy; standard problem responses; hard vs soft deletion; mocking.

**Cross-cutting concerns:** extensions to the runtime for correlation, audit, and tracing, independent of program code.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Documentation-only planning for future spec chapters; no runtime, API, or implementation changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Expands the **Planned chapters** section of the Coleslaw spec README with two new outlines that describe future normative chapters, not implemented behavior.
> 
> **Fundamental patterns** groups first-class language constructs for common application concerns: modeled **errors** on aggregates, runtime-driven **workflows** with progress trees, bounded **queries** (pagination, limits, opt-in sort/filter), **timers**, language-enforced **tenancy**, RFC 9457-style **problems**, standard **Discarded** / **Removed** deletion semantics, and **mocking** for tests.
> 
> **Cross-cutting concerns** adds **extensions** (correlation, audit, tracing at runtime) and **decorators** (declaration metadata read by extensions, e.g. `[Auditable]`), so cross-cutting behavior stays out of application code.

body:
*Educational only — not financial advice.*

## What failed
At 15:55 ET on 2026-10-06, `flatten_mcf` cancelled MCF's orders and then closed the positions straight away. The broker had not yet settled the cancels, so the stop and target legs still held the shares, and every close came back with `40310000 insufficient qty available`. The cancels then went through, which left 10 positions open after the close with no stops. They were closed by hand after hours at about 16:06.

## Fix (order handling only, no setup or strategy change)
- `AlpacaBroker.close_mcf_position`: cancels this system's open orders on the symbol, waits until no MCF orders remain and `qty_available` covers the position, then closes. If the close is rejected, it cancels again and retries. It touches only `mcf-` orders, because the account is shared.
- `flatten_mcf`:
  - covers every symbol MCF traded today, taken from the broker's order history and not only from local state
  - makes 3 passes, then does a final broker check
  - `health.flatten_failed` lists anything still open, so it shows on the live status
- The time stop uses the same safe close. Trade management is still off by default.
- `Publisher` skips paths that do not exist. The end-of-day journal push failed on a missing `universe.csv`.
- Research work-in-progress files from the overnight rule-18 rework swarm, under `research/rework/` (no code paths).

## Tests
`tests/test_flatten.py` uses a broker fake whose cancels settle late, which is today's failure:
- a close that waits succeeds
- a slow cancel recovers through the retry loop
- the runner's flatten leaves no positions and an empty `flatten_failed`

author: florentindubois
body:
## Problem and change

Sōzu 2.2.1 starts its replacement without `--upgrade-protocol` and exports a flat snapshot. The current candidate rejects that invocation before importing the running proxy. This change accepts the legacy shape on Linux, restores a paused command hub, replies with the legacy boolean acknowledgement and waits for the old main's actual exit through a pidfd before using shared sockets. Explicit protocol-v2 handoffs retain their strict contract; outgoing upgrades never fall back to v1.

The full `sozu upgrade` command also collects every worker result and exits nonzero if any active worker fails, identifying those workers and stating that the main has already upgraded. Already draining or stopped workers are skipped.

## Preconditions and remaining release gates

- The first transition requires idle administration and Linux `pidfd_open` support. A PID-1 parent is refused.
- `NOTIFY_SOCKET` causes refusal before acknowledgement. A successful handoff under the shipped systemd units remains unqualified; those deployments require an accepted controlled restart procedure or a separately verified supervision handoff.
- The 2.2.1 snapshot omits administrative tasks and userspace channel buffers. Quiescence cannot establish v2's lossless guarantee, including for partially read asynchronous worker events. The legacy sender's success audit is not proof of activation.
- A slow parent leaves the replacement paused, without forced termination. A CLI timeout therefore requires inspecting process state before recovery.

The operator procedure, lifecycle documentation, test guide, release checklist and changelog describe these constraints. This PR does not declare 2.3.0 release-ready or change package versions.

## Validation

Validated locally on Linux with Rust 1.93.1 and nightly rustfmt, against base `24b833c5018948d025f7d16fb25b7ff5e5e5f691`:

```sh
mise exec -- cargo +1.93.1 build --all-features --locked -j4
mise exec -- cargo +1.93.1 clippy --all-targets --all-features --locked -j4 -- -D warnings
mise exec -- cargo +nightly fmt --all -- --check
mise exec -- cargo +1.93.1 test --workspace --locked -j4 -- --test-threads=8 --skip tests::fuzz_tests::
mise exec -- cargo +1.93.1 test -p sozu-e2e test_upgrade --locked -j4
mise exec -- cargo +1.93.1 test -p sozu --test upgrade_cli_result --locked
```

- Workspace: 2,870 passed, zero failures; 28 existing/dedicated ignores and four fuzz wrappers filtered as in CI. Upgrade E2E: 7 passed. CLI process tests: 2 passed.
- The complete interversion matrix ran with both `SOZU_MATRIX_LEGACY` and `SOZU_MATRIX_OPTION3` set and `--include-ignored --test-threads=1`: 5 passed. It covers HTTP/HTTPS/TCP/UDP traffic, certificate and routing-state preservation, replacement executable identity, draining workers, pre-ack failures, notify refusal and outgoing v2-to-legacy rejection.
- Dedicated existing process tests for descriptor inheritance, draining workers, transfer rejection and PID-file failures: 6 passed.
- The same final positive interversion test fails against the unmodified base candidate and passes with this implementation. The CLI regression was also observed failing before its fix.

The legacy binary is the published x86_64 GNU/Linux ring artifact for 2.2.1, embedded revision `cd02310` (tag `cd023104fab02084f948a93364315944748d74cd`), checked against the release archive checksums. Binary SHA-256: `20e58da65e95cc3058eee50a112cd99a090e9e0441333961d2eccc5b6d2dfe71`. HTTPS checks use the repository's test certificate with `curl --insecure`; they prove TLS transport and preserved certificate material, not CA trust policy.

author: dhensby
body:
Expert puzzles played like Hard ones. This is step **A** of the difficulty review: tighten how Expert puzzles are picked, without adding techniques. Step **B**, teaching the grader chain techniques (Skyscraper, 2-String Kite, XY-Chain, W-Wing) so Expert can go past wings, comes in later PRs.

## Why

Expert was picked by its hardest technique alone. Puzzles that need a fish or a wing usually coast on easier techniques until most of the grid is full, then need it once near the end. Over 300 generated puzzles per tier:

| Median | Medium | Hard | Expert before | Expert now |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cells filled with singles before anything harder | 15 | 12 | 22 | 11 |
| Empty cells when the tier's technique is first needed | 41 | 43 | 28 | 43 |
| Hardest step: X-Wing / XYZ-Wing / Swordfish | – | – | 2% / 12% / 0% | 9% / 16% / 1% |

Before, Expert's easy opening was *longer* than Hard's, and two in three Experts needed their wing exactly once, with most of the grid already filled. A snag that late is easy to spot or to guess past. The puzzle that prompted this (`?p=BTW--fxsfGKIYSUNmiAhJZN0AYAY`) filled 27 cells with singles, then needed one XY-Wing with 27 cells left.

## What changes

- The generator now also requires everything easier than Expert to run out with **at least 40 cells still empty**. Medium already has a similar extra rule (it must need locked candidates).
- The label doesn't change: `rate` still calls any puzzle that needs a fish or wing Expert, so shared links and history keep their tiers.
- Cost: about 115 attempts per Expert instead of 19. That's a median of 85 ms (p90 191 ms) in Chromium on a Mac, and it runs in the worker ahead of time. The default cap of 1,000 attempts runs out about once in several thousand puzzles. When it does, the fallback is a classic Expert, still labelled honestly.
- `GENERATOR_VERSION` goes up to 2, and the Expert golden puzzle is updated.
- The README, the Help dialog and some code comments now describe the new rule and timings.
- Expert's property tests use 4 seeds instead of 25. Under coverage each attempt costs tens of milliseconds; 25 seeds would have needed about 4,300 attempts and broken the hook's 60 s timeout. With 4 seeds, the file's run under coverage goes from 19.5 s to 24.5 s locally.

## Testing

- `npm run coverage`: all 2,204 tests pass, and the core stays at 100% coverage.
- `npm run test:e2e`: 160 passed.
- Checked in the browser: New game → Expert dealt an XY-Wing puzzle that needs it with 43 cells empty.

  - New `mailSweepsPerTenant.test.ts` uses two tenants under the runtime role and covers four cases:

    - the reindex sweep indexes both tenants, each row carrying its own tenant id and Emails database id;
    - with tenant B missing its mail databases, tenant zero is still indexed and the run rejects with the missing-modules message;

body:
## Summary

P10 SP3 routes props from the selected scene-graph node's category via `--routing scene-graph`; `--routing oracle` remains the default. Graph routing uses graph table nodes for retry/remaining-work control and never falls back to simulator category/bin state for a destination. Per-round `decision` is separate from simulator-truth `evaluation`; correct-bin totals remain offline truth-labelled scores. The failure analyzer now catches a graph category error even when an object lands in its selected bin.

This branch also incorporates the project-status documentation commit from PR #32, so README/ROADMAP/CLAUDE status stays consistent. The pending live-viewer work remains separate in draft PR #33.

## Evidence

GraspGen/fused props pick-all, paired seeds 0–9, all cohorts 10/10 completed, zero crashes and zero objects knocked off:

| Routing / identity | Correct bin | Any bin | Wrong bin | Category accuracy | Mean location agreement |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Oracle routing | 36/40 | 36/40 | 0 | n/a | n/a |
| Graph routing / perceived identity | 29/40 | 34/40 | 5 | 34/40 | 99.6% |
| Graph routing / oracle identity | 33/40 | 34/40 | 1 | 38/40 | 100.0% |

Raw per-seed `benchmark.py` summaries and reproduction commands are tracked in `docs/benchmarks/2026-10-06-sp3/`. The perceived-route score is seven objects below the fresh oracle baseline; this is an implementation/validation gate, not a claim of performance parity. GraspGen inference is stochastic, so paired seed differences are observed, not proof of a single cause. Six perceived category errors occurred; five became wrong-bin placements. The true-name graph run's two category misses were both the Fondant box.

## Neizrakstīts

Nav — katrs nodaļas teikums ir izrakstīts vismaz vienā Solījumā. Kā atsevišķs Solījums nav izrakstīta „-ot” daļa „samazinot birokrātiju ārstiem un gaidīšanas laiku pacientiem” — mērķis (§1), sk. 2. punktu zemāk.

## Redaktoram izlemt (ekstraktora ieteikumi)

1. **Kvotu sistēmas reforma — Pārbaudāms?** (`as-kvotu-sistemas-reforma`)
   (a) „Reformēsim kvotu sistēmu”
   (b) §2: konkrēts objekts (kvotu sistēma), bet reformas saturs nav nosaukts.
   (c) Ieteikums: Pārbaudāms; „izpildīts” = normatīvajos aktos būtiski mainīti valsts apmaksāto pakalpojumu apjomu (kvotu) plānošanas un piešķiršanas principi. Alternatīva: Nepārbaudāms (virziens bez satura).
   (d) Vidēja.

2. **„samazinot … gaidīšanas laiku pacientiem” — atsevišķs Solījums?** (`as-kvotu-sistemas-reforma`, `as-vienota-pieraksta-ieviesana`)
   (a) „Reformēsim kvotu sistēmu, ieviesīsim vienotu pierakstu, samazinot birokrātiju ārstiem un gaidīšanas laiku pacientiem.”
   (b) §1: „-ot” daļa apraksta mērķi (analoģija ar „mazinot nodokļu slogu”), tāpēc nav dalīta; citāti — tikai darbības daļas.
   (c) Ieteikums: nedalīt. Alternatīva: atsevišķs Pārbaudāms Solījums „Gaidīšanas laika samazināšana pacientiem” (rādītājs — NVD gaidīšanas rindu dati), citējot visu teikumu.
   (d) Vidēja.

3. **Veselības aprūpe izglītības iestādēs — atsevišķs Solījums?** (`as-veselibas-aprupe-izglitibas-iestades`, `as-bernu-savlaiciga-diagnostika-un-arstesana`)
   (a) „Bērniem nodrošināsim savlaicīgu diagnostiku un ārstēšanu, paplašinot pakalpojumu pieejamību un stiprinot veselības aprūpi izglītības iestādēs.”
   (b) §1 robežgadījums: „stiprinot” ir vispārīgs darbības vārds, bet objekts (veselības aprūpe izglītības iestādēs) ir atsevišķa joma ar savu iznākumu; „paplašinot pakalpojumu pieejamību” — veids, nav dalīts.
   (c) Ieteikums: 2 Solījumi (abi Nepārbaudāmi). Alternatīva: viens Solījums ar visu teikumu.
   (d) Vidēja.

4. **Zāļu cenas — viens Solījums un Pārbaudāms?** (`as-zalu-cenu-optimizacija`)
   (a) „Optimizēsim zāļu cenas ar caurredzamiem iepirkumiem un apjoma līgumiem, valsts lomu kompensējamo medikamentu piegādē.”
   (b) §1: instrumenti zem viena darbības vārda; §2: „optimizēsim” bez mēra, bet instrumenti konkrēti.
   (c) Ieteikums: viens Pārbaudāms Solījums; „izpildīts” = ieviesti apjoma līgumi un valsts iesaistīta kompensējamo medikamentu piegādē, daļa — „daļēji izpildīts”. Alternatīva: dalīt — „valsts loma kompensējamo medikamentu piegādē” atsevišķi (strukturāla tirgus izmaiņa, statuss var atšķirties), citējot visu teikumu abos; vai viss Nepārbaudāms.
   (d) Vidēja.

5. **Mediķu piesaiste novados — Pārbaudāms?** (`as-mediku-piesaiste-novados`)
   (a) „Novados piesaistīsim mediķus ar mērķstipendijām, mājokļu atbalstu un prakšu programmām.”
   (b) §2: mediķu skaita mēra nav, bet nosaukti trīs konkrēti instrumenti. Daļa šādu atbalsta formu var jau pastāvēt (arī pašvaldībās) — nav pārbaudīts.
   (c) Ieteikums: Pārbaudāms; „izpildīts” = valsts līmenī ieviestas visas trīs atbalsta formas mediķiem novados, daļa — „daļēji izpildīts”. Alternatīva: Nepārbaudāms.
   (d) Vidēja.

6. **Līdzmaksājumi — kuri?** (`as-lidzmaksajumu-samazinasana`)
   (a) „Pakāpeniski samazināsim līdzmaksājumus bērniem, senioriem un hronisku slimību pacientiem.”
   (b) Avots nenosaka, vai kompensējamo zāļu līdzmaksājumi (teikums seko zāļu cenu teikumam) vai arī pacienta iemaksas par pakalpojumiem; „seniori” nav definēti.
   (c) Ieteikums: Pārbaudāms; vērtēt abus līdzmaksājumu veidus, „izpildīts” = samazinājums visām trim grupām; definīcijas — pirms vērtēšanas. Alternatīva: tikai zāļu līdzmaksājumi.
   (d) Augsta (par pārbaudāmību); zema (par tvērumu).

7. **Veselības apdrošināšanas modelis un NVD fonds — divi Solījumi?** (`as-valsts-veselibas-apdrosinasanas-modelis`, `as-nvd-parveide-par-fondu`)

   (c) Ieteikums: 2 Solījumi. Alternatīva: viens (fonds kā apdrošināšanas modeļa daļa).
   (d) Augsta.

8. **„Sakārtosim veselības aprūpes pārvaldību” — Solījums vai ievads?** (`as-veselibas-aprupes-parvaldibas-sakartosana`)
   (a) „Sakārtosim veselības aprūpes pārvaldību.”
   (b) §1/§2: atsevišķs teikums ar darbības vārdu; nākamais teikums satur divus atsevišķus Solījumus, tāpēc nav apvienojams kā konkretizācija (atšķirībā no „Stabilizēsim nodokļu politiku”).
   (c) Ieteikums: atsevišķs Nepārbaudāms Solījums. Alternatīva: neizrakstīt kā nodaļas ievadu.

9. **Atbildīgā iestāde — integrācija un ilgstošā aprūpe** (`as-veselibas-un-socialas-aprupes-integracija`, `as-paliativas-un-ilgstosas-aprupes-pieejamiba`)

author: arjundevjha
body:
💡 What:
Optimized `cubic_formula` solver in `Math/Algebra/Polynomials/cubic_formula.py`:
- Precomputed `SQRT_3 = 3.0 ** 0.5` at module scope to eliminate redundant 100-iteration `nth_root(3, 2)` Newton-Raphson loops on every function call.
- Replaced `nth_root(inner_term_2, 2)` calls with direct hardware IEEE 754 float exponentiation `** 0.5`.
- Precomputed reciprocal multipliers (`inv_3a = 1.0 / (3.0 * a)` and `inv_6a = 0.5 * inv_3a`).
- Precomputed complex cube roots (`cb1 = cubed_value_1 ** (1.0 / 3.0)` and `cb2 = cubed_value_2 ** (1.0 / 3.0)`) once instead of evaluating them 3 times each across root calculations.

🎯 Why:
Every execution of `cubic_formula` previously invoked `nth_root(3, 2)` and `nth_root(inner_term_2, 2)`, each running up to 100 Newton-Raphson loop iterations. In addition, complex cube roots and reciprocal fractions were repeatedly recomputed across root expressions.

📊 Impact:
Execution time for `cubic_formula` dropped from ~72 ms to ~35 ms for 10,000 invocations — a **~2x speedup** (~50% reduction in execution time).

🔬 Measurement:
Verified with `pytest` (all 921 tests passing) and measured execution timing over 10,000 calls using `time.perf_counter()`.

author: ehelbig1
body:
Backlog item `croner` 2 → 4. The outcome is a hold, with tests so the next attempt shows the same differences at once.

## What I measured

A throwaway harness linked croner 2.2.0, 3.0.1 and 4.0.1 side by side and compared the next 40 run times from eight start points around the daylight-saving changes, for the 25 schedules on the fleet (read-only) and 104 synthetic expressions in five time zones.

| Behaviour | 2.2.0 (now) | 3.0.1 | 4.0.1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Daily job in the hour **before** the spring gap (`0 1 * * *`, New York) | once | **twice** (01:00 EST and 03:00 EDT) | **twice** |
| Sub-daily job in the repeated autumn hour (`*/30 * * * *`) | pauses for the hour | pauses | runs through it |
| `1W` when the 1st is a Saturday | previous month's Friday, or skips | next Monday | next Monday |
| Six- and seven-field expressions | refused | accepted | accepted |
| `5/5` step shorthand | accepted | accepted | refused |

The first row decides it. The job's time exists and has already fired; the newer versions fire it again at the end of the gap. The same happens in London (jobs at 00:00–00:59) and Berlin (01:00–01:59).

## Decision: hold at 2.2

A schedule that fires twice starts its workflow twice, and nothing downstream would call that an error. What 2.2 gets wrong is smaller: five polling schedules on the fleet pause for one hour on 2026-11-01. No fleet schedule is in the 1 AM New York hour today, but one could be added any day.

## What changes in the code

- `talos-scheduler`: the next-run arithmetic moves into `next_trigger_after` / `next_n_triggers_after`, which take the instant as an argument. The public functions call them with the current time and are otherwise unchanged. Until now the clock was read inside, so the existing tests could only assert "it returned something".
- Seven new tests pin the scheduler's answers across both changes and the syntax it accepts. Built against croner 4.0.1 as a check, exactly the three that should fail do (the duplicate, the autumn hour, the accepted syntax).
- One test is marked "recorded, not endorsed": the autumn pause is 2.2's behaviour, pinned so a change is noticed, not because it is right.

Verified: 37 scheduler unit tests pass; clippy `-D warnings` on the crate and `make lint` pass.

## For you to decide

Reporting the duplicate upstream would be worth doing, but it posts under your name, so I have not. The one-line reproduction is in `docs/engineering-log/packages/2026-10-06-croner-held.md`.

author: andrea-williams
body:
Issue #5260 

### The Bug
When a reporter is filling out the activities forms in a report, the methodology used is saved as a string representation of the name in `methodology_data` json. However, when a report is being cloned to make a supplementary report version, the methodology data is saved as the integer representation of the methodology ID.

This was a problem in `EmissionCategoryMappingService.is_pulp_and_paper_woody_biomass()` because the logic in it relied on the methodology appearing as a string, not an ID.

If the reporter happened to click the 'Save' button to navigate through all the forms, the form data would be rendered and re-saved, which would fix the issue. However, if the reporter instead used the tasklist to navigate past the activity pages, `is_pulp_and_paper_woody_biomass()` was always returning False because `methodology_data['methodology']` was being saved as an integer.

```
        if activity and activity.slug == 'pulp_and_paper':
            if methodology_data['methodology'] in ['Solids-HHV', 'Solids-CC']:
                return True
            elif methodology_data['methodology'] in [
                'Alternative Parameter Measurement Methodology',
                'Replacement Methodology',
            ]:
                if methodology_data.get('isWoodyBiomass', False):
                    return True
        return False
```

This bug is only a problem for pulp and paper operations creating a supplementary report version (for any reporting year).

### The Fix

See changes made to `report_supplementary_cloning.py` - the methodology now always gets saved as a string, not an integer ID. It also now passes all report_methodology json data to `apply_emission_categories()`.

Added a new unit test to check the regression for applying emission categories, and updated an existing test to assert that methodology data is also copied correctly when cloning a report.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Submit an original annual report (any reporting year) with registration purpose "OBPS Regulated", where one of the activities is Pulp and paper production, at least one of the selected products is for Pulp and paper, and where the methodology used is "Solids-HHV" or "Solids-CC".
2. Create a supplementary report for your report. When you get to Step 2 - "Report Information", use the tasklist to navigate directly to the "Allocation of emissions" page (skipping the activities forms). 
3. Scroll down the page to the "CO2 emissions from excluded woody biomass" section - the total allocated should be 100%, without any errors. If you're instead seeing a message saying that the category is over-allocated, something's going horribly wrong.

author: guintherkovalski
body:
## AI masks with SAM 3: Object (clicks) and Describe (text)

Closes part of **LR-MASK-OBJECTS** (M12) and the "AI masks" gap in `docs/parity.md`: real segmentation for the Masking panel, from Meta's **SAM 3** (Segment Anything with Concepts), run **in LightCraft itself, in pure Rust**. On macOS it runs on the GPU through Metal; elsewhere on the CPU for now.

### What users get
- **Object** tile: click the thing to select it; each click refines it, **⌥-click** leaves a part out (green / red dots on the photo).
- **Describe** tile: type what to select — `sky`, `the red car`, or `car, road` — every instance the model finds joins the mask.
- **+ / −** right under the selected mask (and the Add / Subtract / Intersect menus) combine selections, e.g. Describe `car` → + → Describe `road`; − → Describe `people`.
- **Detail pass**: about a second after the last click (or after a description), the area around the selection is segmented again, zoomed in, from a sharper source — in the background — for 5–10× finer edges on small objects.
- **Edge** slider per selection: −100 crisper … +100 feathered (resolution independent).
- **Hover a mask** in the Masks list to see it in red on the photo. The always-on overlay is now off by default (O / the eye still turn it on).

### How it's built
- **`crates/segment` (new, L3)** — a port of the Hugging Face `transformers` SAM 3 implementation (Apache-2.0, attributed in `NOTICE`) to [candle](https://github.com/huggingface/candle): the 32-layer ViT with 2-D RoPE and windowed attention, both feature pyramids, the SAM 2-style prompt encoder + two-way mask decoder (clicks), and the CLIP text encoder + DETR encoder/decoder + pixel decoder (text). The CLIP BPE tokenizer is a small pure-Rust implementation.
  - **candle is pinned at 0.9.2**: 0.10+ makes `candle-core` depend on `tokenizers` with the Oniguruma **C** library. The dependency tree has no `cc`/`cmake`/`-sys` crates.
  - **No `unsafe`**: weights are read with positional reads instead of a memory map (only the tensors a path needs), so `unsafe` stays in `lightcraft-sysmem`.
  - Compiles for `wasm32` (as every library crate must) with the model gated to native targets.
- **`develop`**: `MaskShape::Object { hint, exclude, seg, detail, edge }` (the existing shape, extended) and a new `MaskShape::Prompt { text, seg, detail, edge }`. `SegMask` stores the model's 288² mask logits (quantized to `i8`, deflated, base64; ~10–30 KB), optionally over a sub-rectangle (detail patches).
- **`pipeline`**: samples stored logits bilinearly at any output size → sigmoid, so **renders, exports and the web build never need the model**, and edges stay smooth at full resolution.
- **`engine`**: cargo feature **`sam`** (on in the desktop app, off for web/CLI). The photo is rendered as developed, uncropped and without masks at 1008 px (the frame mask coordinates live in) and encoded once per photo on a worker thread; detail passes run on a worker thread and apply when done (if the selection hasn't changed). Commands: `mask.add` / `mask.addComponent` (`object`, `prompt`), `mask.objectPoint`, `mask.refineDetail`, `segment.prepare`.
- **App**: a small stderr logger (`LIGHTCRAFT_LOG=info`); failed commands are logged; AI-mask errors are shown as they are, for 6 s (e.g. a photo whose file was moved, or a missing model).

### The model (not bundled)
The weights are Meta's `facebook/sam3` checkpoint (SAM License, gated on Hugging Face). Users install them once:

```sh
HF_TOKEN=hf_... tools/install-sam3.sh      # macOS / Linux  (tools/install-sam3.ps1 on Windows)
tools/install-sam3.sh --check
```

It downloads into the folder LightCraft reads (`~/Library/Application Support/LightCraft/models/sam3/`, or `LIGHTCRAFT_SAM3_DIR`), resumes interrupted downloads and checks the official SHA-256. Without it, Object / Describe explain what's missing. Whether to bundle or recommend these weights is a maintainer decision — see `docs/ai-masks.md`.

### Accuracy and speed
`crates/segment/tests/reference.rs` compares every stage against the Python reference (`tools/sam3_reference.py`, made with `transformers`): on Metal the backbone matches to **7e-5** relative error, click masks to **~3e-5**, text features / query scores / boxes to **≤1e-4**, best-instance masks to **≤4e-5**; the tokenizer matches Hugging Face's on accents and punctuation. (Skipped without `LIGHTCRAFT_SAM3_DIR` / `LIGHTCRAFT_SAM3_REF`.)

Apple M4 Pro (warm): image encode **3.1 s** (once per photo, background), each click **~35 ms**, each description **~0.6 s**, detail pass **~5 s** (background). First use after launch adds ~6 s (GPU kernel compilation). f16 was tried and rejected (overflow, ~7 % faster).

### Tests
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 7 steps pass (fmt, clippy, test, parity, layers, assets, wasm).
- New: stored segmentations at any size and through a crop, detail patches over the coarse mask, Edge hardening/feathering, damaged data selects nothing, tokenizer, preprocessing, `SegMask` round trips, detail-region framing, engine errors without the model, hover overlay.

### Known limitations / follow-ups
- A click that lands while a detail pass is running waits for it (up to ~5 s); the first click on a photo waits for its analysis if it isn't done yet.
- Windows/Linux run on the CPU (untested, much slower); no brush/box object mode yet.
- Subject / Sky / People could use the same model with fixed prompts.

Fixes #280. Contributes to #278 without closing that broader task.

Combine component rates before applying the joint scenario's sampling weight. For independent faults, the resulting rate is `weight * p_cond * product(component_rates)`, not `p_cond * product(weight * component_rates)`.

The correction makes total rates and constant-consequence FMEA expectations invariant to how many injection-time samples are used. Phase opportunities, time exposure, fault injection metadata, start times and the component-independence assumption are unchanged. This fixes the constructor calculation underneath #55's bulk weight forwarding.

## Compatibility

Independent joint rates change when the scenario weight is neither zero nor one. Nonnegative weights with the max/selected-component bases and ordinary single-fault rates retain their previous values. The model-free constructor follows the same once-per-scenario convention. Existing phase, metadata-order and exposure tests contained the old repeated-weight expectation; only those rate expectations are updated. Their other assertions remain intact.

## Validation

Six new methods cover one/two/three faults, zero/nonunit weights, conditional probabilities, all baserate options, model-free construction, multiple time-sampling resolutions, even/all/quadrature methods, phase opportunities/exposure, JointFaultSample, source nonmutation, and real fault-simulation histories/FMEA outputs. A two-fault constant-loss example keeps the analytically expected loss of 1.8 with one, two or four samples.

- The final new regressions fail against unchanged dev and pass with this patch.
- New/related tests and scenario doctests: **53 tests and 433 subtests passed on both Python 3.12.11 and 3.14.7**.
- All three fixes in this batch together: **17 tests and 230 subtests passed on both runtimes**.
- Scoped Ruff checks, new-test formatting and `git diff --check` passed.

```sh
PYTHONPATH=src:. MPLBACKEND=Agg python -m pytest -o addopts= --noconftest -q --doctest-modules \
  tests/test_joint_scenario_quadrature.py tests/test_joint_fault_weights.py \

  tests/test_simulation_exposure.py tests/test_fault_weight_arrays.py \
  tests/test_zero_fault_start_times.py tests/test_scenario_defaults.py \
  tests/test_scenario.py src/fmdtools/sim/scenario.py
```

Reference for the scenario-weight contract: https://nasa.github.io/fmdtools/docs-source/fmdtools.sim.html#fmdtools.sim.sample.FaultSample.add_joint_fault_scenario

Tested on macOS CPU. The full repository/notebook suites were not run. No dependency, workflow or public-signature changes.

Exact tested head `f7684c11d370f980d0b22d79fb95c282664adae2`, based on dev `0aa579a6c77ef61e230512c7116e87b5b1186d8f`.

The complete tests-directory run exposed 18 subtest failures in two additional existing files that still expected squared sampling weights. Those exact expectations now use one quadrature allocation and include an independent analytical total-phase-rate invariant across sampling methods; no assertions were removed. The new checks fail against the old implementation.

Local validation on Python 3.14.7: **784 passed, 2 warnings, 4240 subtests passed in 18.36s**. The focused new regression cases fail against unchanged dev. All 14 patches in this maintenance group apply together without conflicts and pass **850 tests and 4,522 subtests** in the full `tests/` directory, with two pre-existing warnings. The unchanged baseline passes 777 tests and 4,034 subtests. This combined candidate is a compatibility check only, not a bundled PR.

The tests used the real package and examples. A temporary external pytest configuration and `--noconftest` select the intended tests instead of the repository hook's default doctest/notebook list. author: victor-ab
body:
Models with float64 thresholds (LightGBM, scikit-learn) loaded with `precision="single"` can send a float32 input down a different branch than the source model does.

## Cause

The importer narrows each threshold with `threshold_type(node.threshold())`, which rounds to nearest. For inclusive operators (`<=`, `>`), `decision_forest_builder::add_node` then stores `nextafter(t32, +inf)` and inference evaluates `x < stored`.

When rounding goes up (`t32 > t`), the float32 input `x == t32` satisfies `x <= t` in nvForest, but the source model sees `double(x) > t` and goes the other way. Exclusive operators (`<`, `>=`) have the mirror problem when rounding goes down.

Only one float32 value per split is affected, `x == t32`, but across a large model that adds up. It is more likely with rounded data such as prices or percentages: there the midpoint thresholds are themselves rounded values, which then show up as inputs.

## Fix

Round in the direction that preserves each comparison:

- inclusive operators: the largest float32 `<= t`
- exclusive operators: the smallest float32 `>= t`

For every float32 `x`, `x <= t` gives the same result as `x <= floor32(t)`, and `x < t` the same as `x < ceil32(t)`. Single precision then routes each float32 input exactly as a float64 comparison would.

- **scikit-learn** casts inputs to float32 itself, so single precision now matches it for any input.
- **LightGBM** compares inputs in float64. float64 inputs can still differ near a threshold, because nvForest casts inputs to float32 in single precision; `precision="double"` avoids that.

The change is a small helper, `detail::cast_threshold`, next to `safe_cast_floating_point` in `decision_forest_builder.hpp`. `treelite_importer` calls it at load time. Nothing changes for:

- inference kernels and speed
- double precision
- models whose thresholds are already float32, such as XGBoost

Thresholds beyond the float range map to `±FLT_MAX` or `±inf` on the side that keeps the comparison; LightGBM stores infinite thresholds as `±1e300`. NaN thresholds are left unchanged.

Why the importer and not `add_node`: `add_node` only receives the already-narrowed value.

Suggested labels: `bug`, `non-breaking`. The API doesn't change. Single-precision predictions change only for inputs that were misrouted, and they now match the source model.

## Tests

- **`TreeliteImporter.CastThreshold` (C++)** tests the conversion directly: ties, round-down cases, out-of-range values, values below the smallest denormal, NaN, and widening.
- **`TreeliteImporter.SinglePrecisionDoubleThresholds` (C++)** builds a float64-threshold model with one tree per operator (`<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`).
  - It loads the model in single precision with each layout.
  - It checks the float32 neighbors of thresholds that round up, round down, and overflow (`±1e300`) against float64 comparisons.
- **`test_sklearn_single_precision_float64_threshold` and `test_lightgbm_single_precision_float64_threshold` (Python, CPU and GPU)** train a one-split model on synthetic data with each framework.
  - Each checks nvForest against its framework's own predictions.
  - Each asserts that the trained threshold really rounds up, so it can't silently stop covering the bug.
  - LightGBM isn't in the test dependencies, so in CI only the scikit-learn test runs. The LightGBM test is skipped unless LightGBM is installed, as `test_lightgbm` is.

Validated on an NVIDIA B300 with a CUDA 12.9 conda build of this branch:

- **C++:** all `ctest` tests pass. With the importer change reverted, `SinglePrecisionDoubleThresholds` fails for `<=`/`>` at the round-up threshold and for `<`/`>=` at the round-down and `-1e300` thresholds.
- **Python:** both new tests pass on CPU and GPU, and all four cases fail against the nvforest-cu13 26.08 wheels.
- **Full suite:** the rest of `python/nvforest/tests` passes, apart from `test_lightgbm_train_with_gpu_device_param`. That test fails only because the CPU-only LightGBM wheel I installed reports "No OpenCL device found".

## Reproducer

```python
import numpy as np
import nvforest
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestRegressor

eps = float(np.finfo(np.float32).eps)
X_train = np.array([[1.0], [1.0 + 3 * eps]], dtype=np.float32)
model = RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=1, max_depth=1, bootstrap=False).fit(X_train, [0.0, 1.0])

# The split threshold is halfway between the training values, 1 + 1.5 * eps
# (float64). Its nearest float32 is 1 + 2 * eps, which lies above the threshold.
X = np.array([[1.0 + 2 * eps]], dtype=np.float32)
print(model.predict(X))  # [1.]
fm = nvforest.load_from_sklearn(model, precision="single", device="cpu")
print(fm.predict(X))     # [0.] on 26.08, [1.] with this change
```

The same happens on GPU, and with LightGBM: a one-split model trained on the same data predicts 0.55, and nvForest 26.08 gives 0.45.

body:
### 🎯 ¿Qué hace este PR?

El calendario del selector de fecha de la web cambiaba de alto al pasar de mes, porque mostraba tantas filas como semanas tenía cada mes (4, 5 o 6). Al cambiar de alto se movía en la pantalla, sobre todo cuando se abría hacia arriba del campo, y las flechas se corrían.

Ahora muestra siempre 6 semanas y completa los lugares sobrantes con días del mes siguiente, en gris. El calendario conserva su tamaño y su lugar. Además, el panel ya no tiene el tope del 60% del alto de pantalla, que estaba pensado para listas largas, así que el calendario se ve entero sin scroll cuando hay lugar.

Es un único componente, así que el cambio llega a todos los formularios de la web, en computadora y en celular. La app nativa usa el selector del sistema operativo y no tiene este problema.

body:
運営者の「女優検索と、トップの下のほう（予約）が少し重い・表示が遅い」への対応です。

## 測ったこと（スマホ相当: CPU 4倍遅く・4G 相当の回線・画像は本物と同じくらいの大きさ）
- トップの重さのほとんどは画像。パッケージ画像は1枚約100KBで、予約受付中だけで50本＝約5MB。トップを下まで見ると約9.3MB読んでいた
- 女優検索は、文字を入れるたび・条件を変えるたびに、約1万人の「読み」をそろえ直して並べ替えていた（1回 0.1〜0.25秒）

## 変えたこと
1. **予約受付中は、発売日が近い12本だけを先に見せ、残りは「もっと見る（あと○本）」**（運営者が選んだ形）
   - 残りもHTMLには全部入れる（予約の一覧ページが無いため。検索エンジンと、JavaScript が使えない人には全部見える）
   - たたんだ作品は、JavaScript が使えるとき（`html.js`）だけ隠れ、開くまで画像を読まない
   - 「VR作品を隠す」「単体作品のみ」のときは、隠れない先頭の12本を数え直す（`vr-filter.js` の `foldLayout`）。一部だけ見えている日付は「3本（全8本）」
   - トップを下まで見たときの画像: **約9.3MB → 約4.6MB**
2. **女優検索**: 照らし合わせ用の文字を1人1回だけ作り、並べ替えた一覧を並び順ごとに覚えておく
   - 1文字入れたとき 約0.1秒 → 約0.01〜0.05秒、全部消したとき 約0.25秒 → 約0.04秒、並び順を変えたとき 約0.22秒 → 約0.06秒（CPU 4倍遅い状態）
   - 本物の索引（約1万人）で、88通りの条件・並び順の結果が、前とまったく同じことを確かめた

## 確認
- `bash scripts/check.sh` 合格（たたみ方・覚えておく仕組みのテストを追加）
- 手元の代わりのビルドで、全ページの検査 309 件すべて合格（予約受付中のたたみ方・`html.js` の印の検査を追加）
- ブラウザで「もっと見る」の動き（スマホ・パソコン・VRを隠すとき・JavaScript が使えないとき）を確認

author: thelabdude
body:
## Summary

bb_worker memory-maps its 16 GiB local CAS and file pool, and that page cache counts against the worker container's 1300Mi limit. On the busiest production pool the worker sat at its limit and read 2.7× more from disk than it wrote, tripping `NodeMemoryMajorPagesFaults`. Meanwhile runners peaked at 28.3 of their 48 GiB.

This moves memory from the runner to the worker in every example `RbeWorker`, without raising any pod's total request:

- Pools with a 48Gi runner: runner 40Gi, worker 9Gi
- Testcontainers pools (concurrency 2): worker 4Gi, runner request 13Gi (limit stays 32Gi)
- README: new "Worker and runner memory" section on sizing and on spotting an undersized worker cache

## Related issue

None.

## Scope

- [ ] `hermetiq` chart
- [ ] `buildbarn` chart
- [ ] `bb-worker-operator` chart
- [x] Custom values or examples
- [x] Documentation or repository tooling

## Testing

```text
kubectl kustomize custom-values/rbeworkers (+ each optional component)   # all render
pod memory requests: 49.27 -> 49 GiB (48Gi-runner pools), 17.27 -> 17 GiB (testcontainers)
```

## Upgrade and compatibility impact

- Applying this rolls every running worker pool.
- The runner limit drops to 40Gi (1.4× the measured 14-day peak). Pools with heavier workloads should check runner memory first.
- Overlays that override only the runner's memory now also request the 9Gi worker.

## Contributor checklist

- [x] The change is focused, documented, and does not include secrets or customer data.
- [ ] Changed charts pass `helm lint` and `helm template` with defaults and relevant override scenarios.
- [ ] New or changed chart behavior has automated coverage where practical.

- [ ] Security-sensitive changes use least-privilege RBAC and preserve the charts' pod/container hardening defaults.

author: johanneslichtenberger
body:
## Intent

We have to make a production ready low latency version of sirix! Commit permission given for this production work; the merge into main waits for an explicit approval. We don't need to support old database formats, we have no users.

We should tackle all follow ups regarding the found bugs, too.

This follow-up:

The diff-replay design review (2026-10-04, report: data/sirix-diff-replay-design-review/report.md) found that R16 (a field moved under an object created later in the same change) still makes revision copy throw on main in every Dewey/recompute mode, and that the key-sorted replay allocator cannot be patched to cover that class. Its recommendation: separate the public diff from replication; make revision replay consume a typed target-state delta keyed by persistent node identity, applied through a transaction-local import that separates record creation from link installation; keep the public diff API, its JSON shape and hashed early stop; validate in shadow mode against full snapshot reconstruction first. Asked whether to implement it now, later, or not at all, the captain answered: "Diff-replay design now".

## What Changed

- Replace presentation-diff revision replay with page-derived identity deltas and staged imports, preserving node keys, topology, Dewey IDs, allocation frontiers, and node history, including moves under later-created parents.
- Reconcile path summaries and derived indexes across import epochs; fix structural hash/count maintenance, sparse trie growth, array index membership, and async diff publication while preserving the public diff API and JSON format.
- Add snapshot-oracle regression coverage, deterministic work budgets, replay and latency evidence, and protocol documentation.

## Paired latency evidence

Historical measurements compare candidate `c10f64aae7bdd8de505eb8a213a8045a73c2b501` with baseline `af9f20e5a8d917066c143773ca18c08f0118ca2f`. They predate the review repairs and CI cleanup; no new benchmark campaign is claimed for the current head. The primary campaign used 12 alternating AB/BA fork pairs pinned to CPUs 0–11 (`taskset -c 0-11`) and a fixed-seed, 5,000-draw paired fork-block bootstrap. Ratios are candidate/baseline pooled medians.

| Operation | Baseline ms | Measured candidate ms | Ratio | 95% paired interval |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Bulk append + commit | 47.0312 | 50.5795 | 1.0754 | 1.0072–1.1282 |
| Public compact diff | 31.9049 | 32.3471 | 1.0139 | 0.9833–1.0504 |
| Public materialized diff | 30.5226 | 31.1780 | 1.0215 | 0.9901–1.0535 |
| Replay input construction | 30.2546 | 2.9293 | 0.0968 | 0.0936–0.1035 |
| Revision copy | 93.6554 | 34.1586 | 0.3647 | 0.3339–0.3836 |
| Unchanged public diff | 0.2686 | 0.2540 | 0.9460 | 0.8754–1.0357 |

No primary lower bound exceeds the specified 1.05 confirmed-regression threshold. This is **not evidence of unchanged source latency**: source append's point estimate is 7.5% higher, and its interval allows a 12.8% slowdown. Both public-diff intervals also extend above 5%.

Extended six-pair results retain wider uncertainty: the 32,768-element unchanged-prefix copy measured 116.4249 → 133.2245 ms (ratio interval 0.8872–1.3757), and compact diff measured 31.4344 → 39.0062 ms (1.0443–1.6144). Sparse results are candidate-only because the baseline did not complete; they support no comparative speedup claim. The move fixture does not establish wide-subtree move latency. Import retains epoch-sized state; these results establish neither a fixed resident-memory bound nor production tail latency.

[Full latency report, environment, raw-data pointers and limitations](https://github.com/sirixdb/sirix/blob/df1f5fed6f179e305d5bcc6d2816b7a16dc09290/build/replay/latency/report.md).

## Known CodeFactor notes

The first CI repair (`df1f5fed6`) corrected both auxiliary Java package-directory mismatches and simplified twelve flagged methods through behavior-preserving extractions. Its local validation passed formatting, Error Prone compilation, the relocated benchmark compiler task, 1,366 core tests (including 229 core/projection work-budget cases), and 32 query checks, with 11 existing skips. The follow-up repair (`43c7ef596`) further simplified four methods that remained above the provider threshold. Its final-source formatting, Error Prone compilation, 1,401 core tests (including the same 229 core/projection budget cases), and 32 query checks passed, with 16 existing skips. These are focused local selections; full-suite acceptance depends on the hosted checks for the current head. No work-budget bound or assertion was weakened.

The following five original complexity findings remain under the authorized small-fix scope. Addressing them would require broader restructuring of coordinated import stages, projection-order planning, test fixtures/oracles, or the historical measurement driver.

| Source | Method | Reported complexity |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `JsonNodeTrxImpl` | `importRevisionLocked` | 39 |

author: kavigupta
body:
When a family fails the FNR limit on a population, the search asks that population for more prefixes. If its source can't draw (no source, or one that fails its yield test), `grow_population` used to retire the population, table and all, and the search went on without it. Now the population stays as it is: the search still holds families to it, and moves on to its other levers (more suffixes) as before.

## Why

A round's boundary harvest is the strings its pass couldn't place. It's what makes later families decide the states the round got stuck on. Retiring it drops that constraint exactly when a family has just failed on it.

Whether a source can draw says little about whether its population matters. A `BoundarySource`'s yield is how often a random probe gets stuck. A state that's almost never decided, but that few probes pass through, gives a low yield. Its harvest then fails the yield test and is retired, even though those are the states blocking the round.

Seen on `t_mp_1001` (instrumented, seed 5). In each refused round, one rare state was undecided 83–99% of the time under the round's family. It made up 30–40% of that round's harvest. The next family failed the FNR on that harvest, the source failed its yield test, the harvest was retired, and the next family left the state undecided again. This went on until a harvest happened to be met without being grown.

That target is outside the learner's preconditions (class-preserving fraction 0.002). What happened there isn't evidence of an in-scope failure, and the merit of this change rests on the argument above. It also brings the Python in line with the termination proof's model, where every kept harvest stays a population.

## Risk

Retirement also ended searches that can't be met: on a target where no family decides a kept population, the search now keeps going instead of dropping the population. On admitted targets the class-preserving precondition says such a family exists. CI's L* suites are the check that nothing admitted stalls.

author: unxmaal
body:
Closes #506.

Before schema 24, `backfill_candidates` linked every screen, measure and adopt verdict to the spec `screen.candidate_for` resolves from the weights on the migrating machine's disk. On golden v10 and v18, which carry no weights, the code adoption therefore landed on `org-a/coder-7b-GGUF`. The run's receipt had recorded `llamacpp:coder-7b-Q4_K_M`.

**Change.** A new helper, `memory_store._candidate_from_receipt`, picks a spec for each verdict that cites a run, in this order:
1. **The disk spec, confirmed by the receipt.** The disk spec's receipt key ran in that run, and the receipt's specs map agrees or has no entry. When the map names a different spec for that key, the receipt's spec wins. This also corrected the golden tts verdicts from `tts:` to `mlx:`.
2. **The one spec that can belong to this proposal.** Otherwise, it takes the single spec in the run that is not a reference, a typed default, a gateway alias, or a spec owned by another proposal.
3. **The disk spec, as a recorded guess.** A verdict with no run, or an ambiguous one, falls back to the disk spec. Each guess is listed in `meta.candidate_guesses`.

No schema change.

**Red/green.** The golden test now asserts the code adoption's spec in every era. It failed on v10 and v18 (`'org-a/coder-7b-GGUF' != 'llamacpp:coder-7b-Q4_K_M'`) and passes after the fix. For eras below 24 it also asserts that the by-hand svg verdict, which no run backs, is recorded as a guess, and that the coder verdict is not.

**Checks.** `make check` passes, both normally and with empty homes. A dry run of the Studio's real schema-17 backup passes every invariant with 0 guesses.

author: ghostjima
body:
## What changes

The stages of a case become explicit states with allowed transitions, each taken by its role, and every transition is recorded in the case's journal with who, when and why. The assistant's handover changes the register once a person confirms it.

**`packages/grid`**

- A transition table (`workflow.ts`): the operator asks for facts (registered or drafting to waiting for facts), starts drafting, records facts received, and hands the draft over to legal review (from any stage before review); the legal reviewer, a new role, approves a reply for signature or returns it for rework; the signatory sends a reply or returns it for rework; the supervisor closes an answered case and, as before, extends the deadline. "Returned for rework" is the transition back to drafting from legal review or from signature; it needs a reason from a list (facts missing, wrong ground, wrong or missing deadline, missing client option, wording, another reason with a comment of at least 10 characters).
- `checkTransition` and `applyTransition` refuse with codes (`transition-not-allowed`, `stage-not-for-role`, `reason-required`, `comment-required`, `comment-too-long`, `reply-needs-outcome`, `refusal-needs-ground`). Inline stage edits follow the same table; a return is refused from a cell (`reason-required`) since it needs a reason.
- The journal (`caseJournal`): for a generated row, the history is worked out from the row as generated, seeded by the row (facts asked for first in most cases, the first action within two working days of registration, returns for rework now and then, the extension, the send and the close on the register's days); changes made in the page are added after it. Transitions, extensions, undone edits and the colleague's moves are journaled. The register's generated columns and the golden digest do not change.
- Roles: `reviewer` joins `operator`, `signatory` and `supervisor`, with two reviewers and one supervisor in the language pools.

**`apps/desk`**

- The open case shows the work on it: the stage, the transitions the page's role may take (each a button that says what it does), and the journal. A return opens a dialog with the reason and a comment; after a transition the focus goes to the panel's heading. The header marks a case returned for rework. `?role=` opens the desk as a role; the queue's role switch has the reviewer.
- The assistant's handover: the run hands over in its own log; the case moves to legal review, with the draft kept on the case for the reviewer, once a person confirms it: in the run when the step asked (recorded at once), or with Confirm the handover under the finished step. The journal entry names the assistant and the person. The run's log stays; the step is no longer undone from the run; a case past drafting shows no Run.

Decisions taken conservatively, for the owner to confirm:

- Legal review may receive a reply undecided (the assistant's draft leaves the decision to the reviewer); a decision, and a refusal's ground, are needed to go to signature and to be sent. Before, a decision was needed to enter legal review.
- The supervisor no longer moves stages beyond closing an answered case; extensions, reassignment and export stay theirs.
- The handover is the operator's, on their own cases; under another role the step says so and the case does not move.
- The signatory's "send" stays a single transition here ("Sign and send"); the signature and the dispatch come in the next pull requests.
- What a person does in the page is dated on the day the data is taken (6 October 2026), at the time of day in Moscow, so the journal agrees with the register's deadlines.
- The simulated colleague moves a case on only by a transition of the table; where a case cannot move on (closed, or undecided before signature) it writes a note.

Stacked on #18.

## How it was checked

- Grid: the table (every stage reachable, one transition per pair, each role's own); the refusals; `applyTransition` writes the stage and the entry and changes nothing on a refusal; the journal of every generated row ends at its stage by transitions of the table, in time order, never after the day the data is taken, with its operator and signatory, the reply sent on the register's day, the first action within two working days, a minority returned, extensions journaled; edits, undo, the colleague and a reload of a row; the page's "now".
- Desk: the handover is recorded only once a person confirmed it, as the operator, with a draft; the words have the same keys in both languages.
- e2e (new `workflow.spec.ts`): the reviewer returns a reply with a reason (refusals, keyboard, focus on the heading, journal with who, when and why); approval by keyboard; roles acting only on their own; the assistant's handover confirmed under the step and confirmed in the run; another role sees why it is not recorded; axe on the work with its journal and on the return dialog with its refusal, in Russian and English, light and dark; no sideways scroll at 375 px. Existing tests follow the new rules (the inline edit test runs as the reviewer; a case past drafting has no Run).
- The full CI list, locally on commit a3f8e00: cargo fmt, clippy on the four feature sets, cargo test (release, default, no default, all features), MSRV 1.85 native and wasm32, wasm-pack build, frozen install, build, typecheck, unit tests (353 passed: rules 10, runner 95, grid 150, desk 78, scripts 20), check-text, e2e (136 passed, axe 21 states x 4), Lighthouse desktop and mobile (100, 100, 100) and the badges script on those outputs.

author: jonmmease
body:
## Why

Chart labels sometimes need more than one line: long category names, axis titles, legend entries, tooltips. Labels were single lines: `\` was an error, and the port had left out upstream's line breaking.

## What

- **Explicit breaks:** `\` and `#linebreak()` (with `justify`) end lines, as in Typst. Lines stack with Typst's leading, and the label takes the first line's baseline. Paragraph breaks and line breaks in equations stay errors, and newlines in data still become spaces.
- **Wrapping:** `LabelOptions::width` is `Auto` (lines end only at explicit breaks), `Max(w)` (wrap at `w`; as wide as the widest line) or `Fixed(w)` (exactly `w` wide). Lines break greedily with upstream's `linebreak_simple`, and equations break after relations and operators, as upstream's do. Break opportunities come from `unicode-linebreak` rather than ICU4X; D27 in `UPSTREAM.md` lists the three ways they differ.
- **Alignment:** `LabelOptions::align` (start, left, center, right or end) aligns lines within the width, through upstream's `AlignElem`, now ported.
- **Line limits:** `max_lines` drops lines past the limit. With `ellipsis`, the last line ends in "…" where text is cut, shortened at grapheme boundaries to fit. `LabelFlags::truncated` reports the cut.
- **Line metrics:** `LabelMetrics::lines` gives each line's left, right, top, baseline and bottom, in place of the first line's baseline, ascent and descent. Left and right span what the line draws, where alignment put it. A line is as tall as its own content, so a line with tall math moves the lines after it.
- **Hanging signs:** with `hanging_signs`, a `+`, `−`, `-`, `±` or `∓` that starts a line hangs out of it by its full width, as Typst hangs punctuation at a line's end, so numbers align by their digits whatever their sign, in every alignment.
- **Oracles:** the reference generator takes a case's width and alignment. 39 new frame cases compare explicit breaks, wrapping and alignment with upstream Typst's layout.
- **Example:** `examples/multiline.rs` renders the new options with each label's box outlined, and the README shows its image:

![Multi-line labels: widths, alignment, line limits and hanging signs](https://github.com/jonmmease/avenger/blob/4bf231aee47bb97d0918954fb4321a1189fe3181/docs/images/typst-multiline-labels.png?raw=true)

```diff
-# Usability interviews
+# Front interviews: two non-developers
+## Research goals            persona, problem, product: the assumptions in docs/product.md
+## Why this method, and what it cannot show    (course sources; two people, 20 and 25 min, friends)
 ## Setup                     Where, How long, Recording, Privacy (unchanged), mock data
-## Script / ## Tasks         T1-T4, 4-minute caps, fixed moderator lines
+## The session               6 blocks: start easy, background, the story ("Tell me about the

+                             your experience?"), try the board ("Is this right?"), close
-## What to record, per task  success, time, first click, errors, SEQ; reaction words
+## After each session        notes in their words; feedback weighed: core problem or preference
 ## What stays out            unchanged, except Results now hold paraphrased findings and
                              whether the problem statement matched
-## Severity / ## Reporting   0-4 scale, per-task values
 ## Results                   per-session table (P1, P2 columns), feedback, themes, insights,
                              job stories, verdicts, refined problem statement
```

The same change, carried to the docs that described the old test:

```diff
 README.md            Usability interviews: P2 a developer  ->  Front interviews, neither a developer
 docs/product.md      risk row, go/no-go, Validated by: four tasks, severity 3 or 4
                      ->  story + problem statement + board; core problems fixed
 docs/qa/test-plan.md     level name; release needs no open core problem
 docs/qa/test-map.md      what the interviews prove: persona and problem match, board looks right

```

## Evidence

- **Before:** `grep -rnE 'T1|T4|SEQ|first click|reaction word|developer|timed' README.md docs/` hit the old protocol's tasks, SEQ, first clicks and reaction words, plus "P2, a developer" in `README.md`, `docs/product.md` and `docs/qa/test-map.md`.

- The Privacy bullet and the first and last paragraphs of "What stays out of this repository" are byte-identical to `dev` (checked by script).
- Every quoted course line matches the cohort's method reference; every scripted line matches the interview guide.
- No en or em dash in the diff.
- `npm run gate`: typecheck, lint and format check pass; 39 test files and 489 tests pass; coverage 97.72% statements, 90.95% branches.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Docs only; a revert restores the usability test plan.

**Blast Radius:** docs

No code, config or test changes. The ship criterion in `docs/product.md` and `docs/qa/test-plan.md` moves from "no severity 3 or 4 problem in creating a task" to "every core problem fixed", and the rollback trigger from "a severity 4 report" to "a report that someone cannot create a task", since the severity scale left with the test.

Follow-up to barracuda's #1560 review (12 of 13 web points OK; this was the partial one): the source filter only narrowed by source *type*, although the server already accepts `supplierId`.

body:
## AI masks with SAM 3: Object (clicks) and Describe (text)

Closes part of **LR-MASK-OBJECTS** (M12) and the "AI masks" gap in `docs/parity.md`: real segmentation for the Masking panel, from Meta's **SAM 3** (Segment Anything with Concepts), run **in LightCraft itself, in pure Rust**. On macOS it runs on the GPU through Metal; elsewhere on the CPU for now.

### What users get
- **Object** tile: click the thing to select it; each click refines it, **⌥-click** leaves a part out (green / red dots on the photo).
- **Describe** tile: type what to select — `sky`, `the red car`, or `car, road` — every instance the model finds joins the mask.
- **+ / −** right under the selected mask (and the Add / Subtract / Intersect menus) combine selections, e.g. Describe `car` → + → Describe `road`; − → Describe `people`.
- **Detail pass**: about a second after the last click (or after a description), the area around the selection is segmented again, zoomed in, from a sharper source — in the background — for 5–10× finer edges on small objects.
- **Edge** slider per selection: −100 crisper … +100 feathered (resolution independent).
- **Hover a mask** in the Masks list to see it in red on the photo. The always-on overlay is now off by default (O / the eye still turn it on).

### How it's built
- **`crates/segment` (new, L3)** — a port of the Hugging Face `transformers` SAM 3 implementation (Apache-2.0, attributed in `NOTICE`) to [candle](https://github.com/huggingface/candle): the 32-layer ViT with 2-D RoPE and windowed attention, both feature pyramids, the SAM 2-style prompt encoder + two-way mask decoder (clicks), and the CLIP text encoder + DETR encoder/decoder + pixel decoder (text). The CLIP BPE tokenizer is a small pure-Rust implementation.
  - **candle is pinned at 0.9.2**: 0.10+ makes `candle-core` depend on `tokenizers` with the Oniguruma **C** library. The dependency tree has no `cc`/`cmake`/`-sys` crates.
  - **No `unsafe`**: weights are read with positional reads instead of a memory map (only the tensors a path needs), so `unsafe` stays in `lightcraft-sysmem`.
  - Compiles for `wasm32` (as every library crate must) with the model gated to native targets.
- **`develop`**: `MaskShape::Object { hint, exclude, seg, detail, edge }` (the existing shape, extended) and a new `MaskShape::Prompt { text, seg, detail, edge }`. `SegMask` stores the model's 288² mask logits (quantized to `i8`, deflated, base64; ~10–30 KB), optionally over a sub-rectangle (detail patches).
- **`pipeline`**: samples stored logits bilinearly at any output size → sigmoid, so **renders, exports and the web build never need the model**, and edges stay smooth at full resolution.
- **`engine`**: cargo feature **`sam`** (on in the desktop app, off for web/CLI). The photo is rendered as developed, uncropped and without masks at 1008 px (the frame mask coordinates live in) and encoded once per photo on a worker thread; detail passes run on a worker thread and apply when done (if the selection hasn't changed). Commands: `mask.add` / `mask.addComponent` (`object`, `prompt`), `mask.objectPoint`, `mask.refineDetail`, `segment.prepare`.
- **App**: a small stderr logger (`LIGHTCRAFT_LOG=info`); failed commands are logged; AI-mask errors are shown as they are, for 6 s (e.g. a photo whose file was moved, or a missing model).

### The model (not bundled)
The weights are Meta's `facebook/sam3` checkpoint (SAM License, gated on Hugging Face). Users install them once:

```sh
HF_TOKEN=hf_... tools/install-sam3.sh      # macOS / Linux  (tools/install-sam3.ps1 on Windows)
tools/install-sam3.sh --check
```

It downloads into the folder LightCraft reads (`~/Library/Application Support/LightCraft/models/sam3/`, or `LIGHTCRAFT_SAM3_DIR`), resumes interrupted downloads and checks the official SHA-256. Without it, Object / Describe explain what's missing. Whether to bundle or recommend these weights is a maintainer decision — see `docs/ai-masks.md`.

### Accuracy and speed
`crates/segment/tests/reference.rs` compares every stage against the Python reference (`tools/sam3_reference.py`, made with `transformers`): on Metal the backbone matches to **7e-5** relative error, click masks to **~3e-5**, text features / query scores / boxes to **≤1e-4**, best-instance masks to **≤4e-5**; the tokenizer matches Hugging Face's on accents and punctuation. (Skipped without `LIGHTCRAFT_SAM3_DIR` / `LIGHTCRAFT_SAM3_REF`.)

Apple M4 Pro (warm): image encode **3.1 s** (once per photo, background), each click **~35 ms**, each description **~0.6 s**, detail pass **~5 s** (background). First use after launch adds ~6 s (GPU kernel compilation). f16 was tried and rejected (overflow, ~7 % faster).

### Tests
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 7 steps pass (fmt, clippy, test, parity, layers, assets, wasm).
- New: stored segmentations at any size and through a crop, detail patches over the coarse mask, Edge hardening/feathering, damaged data selects nothing, tokenizer, preprocessing, `SegMask` round trips, detail-region framing, engine errors without the model, hover overlay.

### Known limitations / follow-ups
- A click that lands while a detail pass is running waits for it (up to ~5 s); the first click on a photo waits for its analysis if it isn't done yet.
- Windows/Linux run on the CPU (untested, much slower); no brush/box object mode yet.
- Subject / Sky / People could use the same model with fixed prompts.

| `<title>` over 60 chars on /faq, guides | Listing pages appended the long home title (" — ksefuj.to — walidator KSeF FA(3)"); guide titles were 67-80 chars | listing pages use " — ksefuj.to"; guide titles rewritten to <=49; two blog titles that were 61 trimmed |
| Guides not to STYLE.md | verbose, repeated facts | PL/EN/UK guides rewritten, `updated: 2026-10-07`, `pnpm check:style` clean |

Guides contained none of the old claims (106gc, certificate types, ZAW-FA, exempt stages), so none were touched or added; facts, sources and links are preserved.

Already present: BlogPosting on posts, FAQPage on /faq (built from MDX). Added: `BreadcrumbList` on blog posts and guides, `mainEntityOfPage` on BlogPosting, `seo.ogImage` override for `image`. Guides switched from `HowTo` (no step markup, invalid without `step`) to `Article`.

body: Refs #865 Stacked on #866 (base `feat/prompt-brief`): merge #866 first; this PR then retargets to `main`. ## Summary `pixel install` registers only `run-hook task-event` for Claude and Codex, and #866 delivers retrieval context through its `prompt-submit` event, so the other hook handlers have no registration path left. This deletes them: the guard (rewrite, deny and advisory arms, the AGY pre-invocation path), `composed-guard`, `post-tool-use`, `metrics`, `session-start`, `post-compaction` and the legacy `prompt-submit`, with their modules, ~5,300 lines of tests, the plugin hook script and the OpenCode plugin asset. - **Upgrade safety:** a user who upgraded the binary but never re-ran `pixel install` still has `pixel run-hook guard …` registered, and a `PreToolUse` hook that exits 2 blocks the host's tool call. Every retired verb therefore stays accepted, with its old flags (`--provider`, `--backup`, `--delegate-rtk`, `--event`), as a hidden silent no-op: exit 0, no output, stdin drained within the existing cap. The install and uninstall recognisers that retire old registrations (`has_pixel_guard`, `remove_pre_tool_use_guard`, the per-host removers) are kept with their tests. - **Not touched:** `search-like-rg`, `execution-brief` and `squash-branch` (its alias `rewrite` is unrelated to the guard rewrite), `call_guard.rs` (the repeated-call guard inside `search-content` and `find-code`), `task-event` and the task gates. - **`pixel config policy` now controls nothing.** No hook reads it. The key stays and its wording says so; `task_context` and `task_boundary` are inert too. Removing the keys is a follow-up. - **Doctor:** all seven checks I audited stay, because each reports a leftover of a retired artifact or checks the `task-event` registration. The one removal is the yellow branch of `install.claude-hooks` that warned when a Pixel plugin and the global hooks were both enabled; the plugin ships skills only now. ```diff crates/pixel/src/ -├── guard.rs guard/contract_tests.rs # 12,306 lines -├── prompt_submit.rs post_compaction.rs pixel_question.rs ├── call_guard.rs # kept: search-content repeat guard +├── prompt_continuation.rs # is_trivial_continuation, used by the brief ``` ## Evidence - **Before:** retired verbs parsed and ran handlers; no standard install registered any of them. - **After** (real debug binary at `03b4041e`, `bash` loop over `pixel run-hook ` with a PreToolUse payload on stdin): `guard --provider claude|codex --delegate-rtk|devin`, `composed-guard --backup …`, `post-tool-use`, `metrics`, `session-start`, `post-compaction`, `prompt-submit --provider claude|codex` and the `hook` alias: all exit 0, 0 stdout bytes, 0 stderr bytes. `task-event --event prompt-submit` still answers `{}`. The CLI test is `hook_stdin_cap_cli::retired_hook_verbs_should_accept_their_old_flags_and_answer_nothing` (every verb, both spellings, empty, small and over-cap payloads). - **Ran locally on this exact head** (`git diff --shortstat feat/prompt-brief...HEAD`: 46 files, +736 / −22,584): `cargo fmt --all -- --check` ok; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `TMPDIR=/tmp cargo test -p pixel-cli --bin pixel` 674 passed; `-p pixel-install` 493 passed; `-p pixel-cli --test cli` 294 passed, 1 ignored (includes `docs_drift`); `scripts/gen-plugin-assets.sh --check` in sync; `prepare.sh --check` well formed. - **One caveat:** two earlier runs of the full `--test cli` suite at machine load 110–135 failed 5–7 tests (`prompt_brief_cli` ×4, `task_cli` ×1–3); the same tests pass alone (33 of 33) and the full suite passes at load 25. Those are the 750 ms brief window and process-spawn timing under load, not this PR, but CI should be watched for it. - **Not run:** `scripts/pixel-smoke-test.sh` and `scripts/system_audit.py` (they now assert the retired verbs exit 0 silently; no installed binary here), an installed-hook check on a machine with an old registration, and the Node OpenCode test (deleted with the asset). ## Merge Danger **Door:** one-way for the deleted behaviour: anyone who hand-wired `pixel run-hook guard` under `policy enforce` for a non-Codex, non-Claude provider loses the rewrite, approval and denial. A revert restores it. Nothing stored changes, and `pixel install` writes the same files as before. **Blast radius:** medium. The only live hook, `task-event`, is untouched. The risk is an old registration breaking a host, and the no-op verbs and the kept removers exist for that; they are tested but not exercised against a real old install. ## Docs touched `ARCHITECTURE.md` (hook table now `task-event` only plus the retired-verbs paragraph; `## Crates` and Command surface rows; the policy and `[PIXEL:TASK_CONTEXT]` paragraphs removed), `docs/threat-model.md`, `docs/manual-setup.md`, `docs/assurance-case.md`, `docs/system-audit.md`, `docs/review-gate-design.md`, `changelog.d/865-retire-hooks.removed.md`. Stale mentions left for a follow-up: `CONTRIBUTING.md:456`, `website/content/docs.md:83`, the `docker-setup-smoke` skill's `policy enforce`, `docs/motion/scripts/record-demo.sh` (pins a recording). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Changes** * Claude and Codex now receive a bounded evidence brief with each code prompt through `pixel install`; ordinary searches remain native. * The optional Pixel impact skill and OpenCode integration have been removed. Pi’s `/pixel-impact` command and `pixel impact` remain available. * Installation now registers only the task-event hook. Retired hook commands remain accepted but exit silently. * Retrieval-policy settings are retained for compatibility but no longer affect native tools.

body:
자율 개선 에이전트가 생성한 PR입니다. (run 2026-10-07-075834-Momento-improve, base 1ef81d6)

## 2026-10-07
- 선택: 보존 정책 저장 실패를 서버의 영문 문장·pgx 원문 대신 한국어로 안내한다 (가치 2 / 위험 1 / 작업량 S)
- 결과: 성공
- 요약: `RetentionAdmin` 의 Alert 이 `{save.error.message}`(AdminPage.tsx:2957) 로 서버 문장을 그대로 띄워, 다섯 칸이 전부 `type="number"` 자유 입력인데도 범위를 벗어난 값에 **화면에 없는 영문 컬럼명**이 올라왔다 — `raw_event_months must be between 1 and 120`(advanced_analytics.go:82). 500 으로 떨어지면 `err.Error()`(advanced_analytics.go:117)가 그대로 실려 pgx 원문이 브라우저까지 흘렀다. v0.34.54~57 선례대로 `adminErrors.ts` 에 `describeRetentionError` 를 **새로** 두고(기존 `refusal` 과 문장 상수 `UNREADABLE_PAYLOAD`·`LOST_REQUEST`·`PASS_TO_ADMIN` 만 재사용, 네 `describe*` 와 합치지 않음) 2957 Alert **한 줄만** `RetentionErrorAlert` 로 바꿨다(프로덕션 2파일 + 테스트 1파일). `INVALID_RETENTION` 은 코드 하나에 원인이 다섯이므로 `PASSWORD_PROBLEM`(adminErrors.ts:37) 선례대로 서버 문장에서 컬럼명을 읽어 가르고, 각 안내가 그 칸의 화면 라벨을 「」 로 부르며 허용 범위를 한국어 단위로 말한다(`「Raw Event (개월)」 은 1개월에서 120개월 사이로 적으세요.` 꼴). 다섯 중 어느 것도 맞지 않으면(서버가 검사를 늘린 경우) 영문을 본문에 올리지 않고 중립 문구 + `detail` 로 되돌린다. **`RETENTION_SAVE_FAILED` 문구는 중립**이다 — INSERT 가 `ON CONFLICT(site_id) DO UPDATE`(advanced_analytics.go:115) 라 '이미 등록된 정책' 은 거짓이고 같은 500 을 DB 장애도 쓰며, 이 환경에 Postgres 가 없어 재현하지 못했으므로 원인을 단정하지 않았다. 서버(`advanced_analytics.go`)·`validateRetention` 의 범위·나머지 Alert 다섯 곳(2413·2510·3112·1372·2761)·입력 차단은 손대지 않았다. 검증: `cd web && npm ci && npm run lint && npm test && npm run build` 전부 통과(테스트 223 → 234, +11), `go vet ./internal/httpapi/` 통과. 순수 함수 테스트에 더해 **실제 프로덕션 배선**을 확인했다 — `npm run build` 의 dist 를 `/api/v1/me`·`/api/v1/sites`·`/api/v1/sites/{id}/retention` 을 흉내 낸 임시 서버에 올리고 headless Chrome(google-chrome, puppeteer-core 는 /tmp)으로 `/admin?section=retention` 의 칸을 실제로 채우고 「보존 정책 저장」 을 눌러 Alert DOM 을 읽었다. 에러 객체는 손으로 만든 대역이 아니라 `api()` 가 HTTP 응답에서 만든 진짜 `APIError` 다. 11건 전부 기대대로: 다섯 거절이 각각 자기 라벨을 가리키고 본문에 영문 컬럼명·`must be between` 0개, 두 500 모두 본문에 `SQLSTATE`·`violates` 없고 원문은 detail caption 에, `UNKNOWN_SITE`·`INVALID_PAYLOAD` 한국어, 모르는 코드는 서버 메시지 그대로. 과제서가 코드로만 확인했던 것 하나를 브라우저로 마쳤다 — 「Aggregation (개월)」 을 비우면 `aggregation_months:null` 이 실려 가고 서버가 통과시킨다(`put={…,"aggregation_months":null,…}`). 임시 하네스는 /tmp 에만 두고 `web/dist` 는 커밋 전에 지워 `git status` 로 3파일만 담긴 것을 확인했다. `npx prettier --check` 는 게이트로 쓰지 않았다.
- 실패 재현: 순수 함수 — 먼저 `SyntaxError: The requested module '../src/pages/adminErrors.ts' does not provide an export named 'describeRetentionError'`, 그 다음 **지금 Alert 과 똑같이 동작하는 항등 스텁**(`error.message` 를 그대로 돌려주는 구현)으로 새 11건 중 7건 실패 — `not ok 36 - 보존 정책 안내에 영문 컬럼명과 must be between 이 남지 않는다` / `error: 'raw_event_months: 영문 컬럼명 "raw_event_months" 이 안내 본문에 섞였다: raw_event_months must be between 1 and 120'`, `not ok 39 - 보존 정책 저장 500 의 pgx 원문은 Alert 본문이 아니라 detail 로만 남는다` / `error: 'RETENTION_SAVE_FAILED: Postgres 표지 "SQLSTATE" 가 Alert 본문에 섞였다'` (기존 33건은 스텁에서도 **전부 통과** — 새 테스트가 보존 정책 결함만 짚는다는 증거). 프로덕션 배선 — 고치기 전 main 그대로의 dist 로 같은 브라우저 하네스를 돌리자 11건 중 **9건 실패**: `body="raw_event_months must be between 1 and 120"`, `body="ERROR: insert or update on table \"retention_policies\" violates foreign key constraint … (SQLSTATE 23503)"` → `본문에 샌 Postgres 표지: SQLSTATE, violates`, `body="site not found"` → `RESULT: 기대와 다름 (9건)`(exit 1). 고친 뒤 같은 하네스가 `RESULT: 전부 기대대로`(11/11).
- 보류 아이디어: 「JSON Schema」 칸에 입력 중 JSON 구문 helperText 검증을 붙인다 — 다섯 줄 자유 입력이라 onBlur/디바운스 설계가 본체 (가치 2 / 위험 1 / S); 보존 정책 다섯 칸에 입력 중 범위 helperText 검증을 붙여 왕복을 줄인다 — 이번 회차가 문구만 했고 과제서가 입력 차단을 금지했다, CIDR 회차와 같은 구조로 순수 모듈 `retentionRule.ts` 를 두면 Alert 과 helperText 가 같은 범위를 쓴다 (가치 2 / 위험 1 / S, 신규); 남은 create/update 오류 Alert 네 곳(2510 rekey·3112 dimensions·1372 설치 코드·2761 삭제)을 한 조각씩 — 묶지 말 것 (가치 2 / 위험 1 / M); 설정 저장(AdminPage.tsx:2413) 실패를 한국어로 안내한다 — 한 Alert 이 9개 그룹을 덮어 M (가치 2 / 위험 2 / M); 표 검색이 숨긴 열의 값까지 뒤진다 — 열두 회차 연속 미선정, docs 검색 절로 의도를 먼저 가릴 것 (가치 2 / 위험 2 / S)
