body:
## Issue
- Closes #195

## Dev Tracking
One of three performance fixes, each in its own PR: Docling converter reuse (this PR), job-stats rescans, and embeddings batching.

## Description
### Problem
Docling's `DocumentConverter` was rebuilt **for every worker thread of every micro-batch**. Each rebuild reloads the layout, TableFormer and OCR models.

**Why that happened:**
- Micro-batching is on by default: batches of 100 docs, up to 10 running at once. A new operator instance is created per node per batch.
- `operator_utils.py` cached converters per thread (`threading.local()`). The reason was to avoid docling-parse segfaults when two threads use one converter.
- But `text_extraction.py` / `extract_operator.py` create a **new** `ThreadPoolExecutor` in every `transform()` call. So every batch's threads started with an empty cache and built their own converter.
- Docling initialises pipelines under a module-global lock (`_PIPELINE_CACHE_LOCK`), so these model loads also ran one after another.

**Scale:** with the default `min(2*cpu, 16)` text workers and 10 concurrent batches:
- up to **160 converters in memory at the same time** (out-of-memory risk);
- about **1,600 model initialisations for 10k PDFs** on a 16-core host, all serialised behind that lock.

**Related problems fixed here:**
- **GPU path:** built its converter once per adapter instance, which means once per micro-batch.
- **Docling entity extraction:** built a new `DocumentExtractor`, which loads the VLM, **per document**.
- **Cache key bug:** the key used only the option **type names** (`type(opt).__name__`). Different OCR, table or accelerator settings of the same option class therefore collided and could share a converter, which is a correctness bug.

### Solution
A new module, `src/docpipe/integrations/docling/converter_pool.py`, holds a bounded pool shared by the whole process:
- **Exclusive use:** a converter is checked out only for the duration of one `convert()` call and returned in a `finally`. No converter is ever used by two threads at once, so the segfault protection is kept.
- **Reuse:** converters survive across worker threads, micro-batches and operator instances. Text, GPU and Docling entity extraction all use the same pool.
- **Bounded:** `DOCPIPE_DOCLING_CONVERTER_POOL_SIZE`.
  - The default `min(2*cpu, 16)` equals the default number of text workers, so a single batch at default settings never waits.
  - Concurrent micro-batches share converters instead of multiplying them: at most 16 instead of up to 160.
  - When the pool is full, callers wait instead of building more. An INFO log says so once and names the environment variable.
- **Fair between configurations:** when the pool is full, an idle converter of a different configuration is only evicted if one of these holds:
  - the requester has none yet;
  - the other configuration holds at least two more converters than the requester;
  - the converter has been idle for at least 30 s.
  
  This avoids constant evict-and-rebuild when text and entity extraction run side by side.
- **Memory:** idle converters are freed after `DOCPIPE_DOCLING_CONVERTER_IDLE_TTL_SECONDS` (default 600 s; 0 keeps them until the process exits) by a daemon reaper thread. A long-running API server therefore gives model memory back between jobs. An `atexit` hook shuts the pool down.
- **Process safety:** after a fork (`ProcessPoolExecutor`, `use_processes`) the child resets to a fresh pool via `os.register_at_fork`.
- **Correct cache key:** a SHA-256 over the actual option **values**.
  - Pydantic models are walked field by field and keep each nested model's concrete type.
  - Enums, classes and paths are included; secrets are hashed, never stored.
  - Unknown objects fall back to type plus repr, which can only cause a cache miss, never a false match.
  - Verified with real docling options:
    - Identical settings built separately share a key.
    - These all get different keys: OCR on vs off; EasyOCR / RapidOCR / Tesseract / TesseractCLI; a different OCR language; cuda vs mps.

The explicit `converter=` argument of `extract_content` still works and bypasses the pool.

### Thread budget (documented, defaults unchanged)
Up to pool size × Docling `num_threads` inference threads can run at once (default 4 per converter), for example 16 × 4 = 64 on a 16-core host. The README explains how to lower either value (`DOCPIPE_DOCLING_CONVERTER_POOL_SIZE`, `DOCLING_NUM_THREADS` / `OMP_NUM_THREADS`) if the CPU is oversubscribed.

## Basic Checklist
- [x] Code follows project standards (keyword-only arguments, `get_logger()`, %-style logging, no unicode in logging)
- [x] Tests added/updated for new functionality
- [x] Documentation updated (see Documentation Update Checklist below)
- [x] No breaking changes (or documented in Breaking Changes section)
- [x] All commits carry a `Signed-off-by` trailer
- [ ] All commits are GPG-verified

## Breaking Changes
None for flows, configuration or output.
- **Behaviour:** idle converters now stay in memory for up to 10 minutes after a job, configurable. Before, they were freed when a batch's threads ended.
- **Internal:** the private helpers `_get_or_create_converter`, `_thread_local_converters` and `DoclingAdapter._build_gpu_converter` / `_gpu_converter` were removed. Nothing in `src` used them any more; the tests were updated.

## Dependencies
None.

## Testing Details
**Benchmark** (not committed). It drives the real `DoclingAdapter.transform` path with a new adapter per batch: 10 batches × 100 docs, `max_workers=16`. A stub converter stands in for Docling: its constructor sleeps 2 s under a global lock, like Docling's pipeline lock, and `convert()` sleeps 20 ms.

| Scenario | Constructions | Peak live converters | Wall time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before, batches one after another | 160 | 16 | 320.4 s |
| **After**, batches one after another | **16** | 16 | **33.4 s** |
| Before, 10 concurrent batches | 160 | 45 | 320.2 s |
| **After**, 10 concurrent batches | **16** | **16** | **32.1 s** |
| After, 10 concurrent batches, pool size 8 | 8 | 8 | 16.1 s |

No scenario used a converter from two threads at once. With real Docling the models load on the first `convert()` of each converter, so the saving shows up there.

**Tests:**
- New: `tests/unit/integrations/docling/test_converter_pool.py` and `tests/unit/operators/extract/test_docling_converter_pool_reuse.py` (end to end through `DoclingAdapter.transform`).
- They check:
  - Constructions across 5 batches × 8 workers, sequential and concurrent: at most 8 in total.
  - Reuse by later batches and new adapter instances.
  - Exclusive use, checked with instrumented stubs.
  - Key equality and inequality.
  - The cap under 12 to 40 threads.
  - Waiting, eviction, fair share, TTL, environment parsing and the fork hook.
  - Pool reuse in the GPU path and for Docling entity extraction.
- The pool tests passed 5 runs in a row.

```bash
pytest tests/unit/integrations/docling tests/unit/util/test_operator_utils.py tests/unit/operators/extract -q -o addopts=""
# Only failures: the 11 extract tests that need Docling model downloads, which are blocked (403) in the
# test environment. They fail identically on unchanged main; no new failures.

pytest tests/unit -q -o addopts=""
# 8176 passed, 20 skipped, 24 failed. The 24 are exactly the model-download failures on unchanged main.
```
Not tested against real Docling models: model downloads are blocked in the test environment, so all tests use stubs. A smoke test with real models before merging is recommended.

**Side fix:** `test_docling_entity_adapter.py` now only replaces `docling` with a mock when docling is not installed. Before, the mock leaked into later tests ("'docling' is not a package").

## Documentation Update Checklist
- [x] Operator documentation in docs/operators/: `docs/operators/extract/extract_operator_readme.md

Closes #97

Text inputs, selects, and textareas inherited the 13–14px size of the label around them, which makes iOS Safari zoom the page when one is focused. They now set their own size (`1rem`) in both the web and admin stylesheets.

**Done when**

Every text input, select, and textarea on the web and admin apps computes to at least 16px. New browser tests in each app's `accessibility.spec.ts` measure this on the main form pages. The web tests fail without the fix (controls measured 14px); I did not run that check for the admin tests.

**Checks**

- Format, typecheck, lint, and unit tests pass for web and admin.
- Admin: fresh build, browser suite passes.
- Web: dev and production browser suites pass locally on macOS.

**Known CI failure: Linux visual baselines**

The larger controls change 14 screenshots (events, schools, teams, login, signup, event-new, account; desktop and mobile). The macOS baselines are regenerated in this pull request. The Linux baselines are not, so the visual regression tests will fail in CI until they are regenerated from this run's failure artifacts and committed here.

*Written for Samuel (plain English), and for the next Claude session reviewing this PR.*

## M14 follow-up V3a: Import in one place (from your verdict on #90)

**What changes for you**
- **A new Import page** (`/import`), the one place to add things. It has three parts:
  - **Add books:** EPUB or PDF files, dropped anywhere on the page or picked with **Choose files**. Each file's result is listed, as before.
  - **Add your audiobook to a book:** choose one of your books that has a file, press **Choose**, then add its read-along package (a folder, or a .zip of it) exactly as on the book's own page. The list holds only books with a file, since a package is checked against the book's file.
  - **How books are heard:** the line you approved: "To hear a book, add its file first. Then an EPUB can be read aloud paragraph by paragraph by an AI voice (paid the first time each paragraph plays, then free), or any book, EPUB or PDF, can get your own audiobook, which plays straight through for free."
- **Home's Import button now opens the Import page.** It used to open the file picker, which lived inside Home's drop strip. The strip is gone, and a file dropped on Home is no longer added.
- **An empty Home links to Import:** a new user sees "Good to see you, (their first name). Your library is empty. Add your books on the Import page.", with the link. An empty Library says the same.
- **The Library's views** (All, Want to Read, Finished, Books, Audiobooks, PDFs) **no longer have a drop box.**
- **The book page keeps its own "Your audiobook" section**, as planned.
- **Not in this PR:** Import in the sidebar and a fifth phone tab (V3b), and whole-book AI narration (V5).

**This branch sits on #97** (V1 and V2). Until #97 merges, this PR also shows V1's and V2's commits. V3a is the commit "M14 follow-up V3a: Import in one place ...", then "M14 follow-up V3a, review fixes ..." (below), with ledger commits between and after.

## How it works (for the reviewer)
- **`app/(app)/import/page.tsx`** (+ `page.module.css`): a server page. The audiobook list is the user's books that are not removed and have a file (`books.fileKey` not null), by title. A plain form (`GET /import?book=<id>#audio-h`) chooses the book; the page then shows `AudiobookUpload`, the book page's own component, for that book. The drop-anywhere `ImportRoot` and the `ImportZone` hint moved here from Home.
- **`app/(app)/page.tsx`:** `ImportLink`, a link styled like the old button, replaces `ImportButton`; no `ImportRoot` or `ImportZone`.
- **`components/upload/HomeImport.tsx`:** `ImportLink` added. `ImportButton` and the hint's phone-only hiding were removed: nothing used them any more.
- **`app/(app)/library/Dropzone.tsx`** deleted, and its CSS.
- **Found and fixed while testing:** with books in the library, the book list's longest title ("The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde, by Robert Louis Stevenson") made the page 553 px wide in a 390 px phone screen. The page's column now fits the screen (`grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr)`, and `min-width: 0` on the list).
- **Tests:** `uploads.spec.ts` and `reader.spec.ts` add books on `/import`; `home.spec.ts` checks Home's Import opens `/import`, with no drop strip; `shell.spec.ts` finds Import as a link; `/import` joins `e2e/pages.ts` (photographed and checked for accessibility in four looks). A new test in `uploads.spec.ts`:
  - the Library has no drop box;
  - the audiobook list holds exactly the books the library export lists with a file;
  - a read-along package (.zip) made from Frankenstein's file is added to Frankenstein from the Import page (the book's import list shows it), then removed;
  - with the book chosen, the page passes the accessibility check and fits the screen in all four looks (desktop and phone, light and dark).

## Review fixes (second commit)
A review of this draft (two reviewers, then a skeptic for each finding) confirmed seven problems that the tests had passed. Each is fixed, and each fix has a check that fails without it:

| What was wrong | Fix | Check |
|---|---|---|
| **Home's Import went blank under the mouse:** the word and icon took the links' hover colour, which is the button's own hover background | `HomeImport.module.css`: the hover keeps the text colour (`color: var(--on-accent)`), as Home's other button-links do | `home.spec.ts`: hovers Import, waits for the colour change to end, and checks the text colour differs from the background |
| **On `/import`, adding a book while your audiobook was uploading** made the audiobook part call that running upload one that "did not finish" (adding a book refreshes the page, and the server lists the running upload as unfinished) | `AudiobookUpload.tsx`: no "did not finish" rows while this page is sending; and the upload it has just finished is never shown as unfinished while the page catches up | `readalong.spec.ts` (Cancel part): during a held upload, the book is put in a collection (which refreshes the page; the collection button's pressed state shows the refresh arrived), then "did not finish" must not appear |
| **No test checked that a page updates itself after an upload** (the moved tests reload the page) | none needed in the app | `uploads.spec.ts`: right after the first three books are added, the Import page offers Frankenstein for your audiobook, with no reload |
| **The approved line on how books are heard was checked by its first sentence only** | none needed in the app | `uploads.spec.ts`: the whole paragraph must match, word for word |
| **"Your audiobook" was a second top-level heading inside "Add your audiobook to a book"** (a screen reader's list of headings showed them side by side) | `AudiobookUpload` takes a heading level: 3 on the Import page, 2 (unchanged) on the book page | `uploads.spec.ts`: on `/import`, "Your audiobook" is a level-3 heading |
| **A read-along .zip dropped on the audiobook part was sent to the book uploader** (a drop anywhere on the page adds books) and refused as a broken EPUB | `useBookUpload.ts`: a `.zip` is not sent as a book; its row says: "A .zip is not a book. If it is your own audiobook, choose its book under “Add your audiobook to a book”, then choose the .zip there." Other files go to the server as before. The hidden status line counts only files the server read. | `uploads.spec.ts`: a .zip dropped on the "Your audiobook" part makes no upload request, and the message appears |
| **The Import page's serif text stayed at the desktop reading size (20 px) on phones** | `page.module.css`: 18 px below 48 rem, the switch point the other pages use | `uploads.spec.ts`: 18 px in the phone looks, 20 px on desktop |

## Evidence
On the laptop (a Mac; sound on the built-in speakers, not Bluetooth). CI's result will be added below.

**After the review fixes** (commit adebd11):
- **`npm run check`:** exit 0, `Tests 462 passed | 2 skipped (464)`.
- **Whole browser suite from a fresh database** (`rm -rf .data/e2e .data/e2e-files e2e/.auth && npx playwright test --ignore-snapshots`): `291 passed (7.7m)`. This includes the new checks above in Chromium, and the read-along one in WebKit too.
- **Screenshot looked at:** `import-audiobook-desktop-light` (a book chosen, its package added): "Your audiobook" looks as before (h2 and h3 share one style).
- **Mutation checks for the fixes** (the fix undone on purpose, the app rebuilt, the test run on a database copy; each after a control run of the same test on the unbroken build, all `1 passed`):

| Broken on purpose | Caught at |
|---|---|
| The hover's text colour removed (`HomeImport.module.css`) | `home.spec.ts:115`: `Expected: not "rgb(42, 82, 77)"`: under the mouse, the text was the colour of the button |
| "Did not finish" rows shown while the page sends (`AudiobookUpload.tsx`: the `progress ? [] :` guard removed) | `readalong.spec.ts:350`: the section said "An upload from 7 Oct 2026 did not finish and cannot be continued" while it showed "Sending the audio (15 MB)" |
| A .zip sent as a book agai

author: copilot
body:
Bots rarely started strafe jumps. With `bot_strafejumps_debug` on, the log was flooded with one generic message: `input/state conflict (attacking, force power, special move, etc)`. `BotSFJ_HasInputConflict` ORed together about 40 conditions. It ran both when starting a jump and on every frame of an active one, so any match blocked the start or aborted mid-air.

### Root causes
- **Vertical movement input:** the check rejected any vertical component (`fabsf(bi->dir[2]) > 0.001f`). Navigation builds its move direction as a 3D vector to the waypoint (`ai_main.c` ~23153), so that component is almost never zero. The direction is only flattened after the SFJ controller owns input, and it could never get ownership. The result was a deadlock for navigation-started jumps.
- **Speed check:** `fabsf(ps->speed - ps->basespeed) > 0.5f` compared speed after movement physics had scaled it. Backpedalling, saber swings, spinning moves and the saber's move-speed scale all reduce `ps->speed`. Staff users and bots backing up were therefore permanently in conflict.
- **Navigation inputs:** navigation's own jump/crouch/walk inputs and jump timers (`jumpTime`, `jumpHoldTime`, `jumpPrep`) aborted active jumps.

### Changes
- **`ai_strafejump.h`**
  - Adds `bot_sfj_conflict_t` (`NONE` / `SOFT` / `HARD`).
  - Adds `BotSFJ_PhaseInProgress`, true for takeoff, air, landing and rejump.
  - Adds `BotSFJ_ConflictBlocks`: hard conflicts always block; soft conflicts block only outside the in-progress phases.
- **`BotSFJ_GetInputConflict`** (replaces `BotSFJ_HasInputConflict`)
  - Returns a classification plus a specific reason string, checking hard conditions first.
  - **Hard:** dead, abnormal movement type or vehicle, water, unsupported movement style, grip/drain/lightning/speed/rage, force-jump charge or flip, knockdown or roll, special or rebound jump anim, saber lock, forced movement, kick moves owning movement, holding position (`beStill`, waiting, camping), and a queued force power, ski or use.
  - **Soft:** queued attack/jump/crouch/walk, `weaponTime`, saber specials, saber defense, navigation jump timers, and jump still held.
  - The vertical-input check is removed.
  - The speed check now only rejects `basespeed <= 0` or dragging a body. Force speed and rage are still checked directly.
- **`BotSFJ_SelectIntent` / `BotSFJ_ApplyInput`**
  - Both call sites go through `BotSFJ_ConflictBlocks(conflict, bs->sfjPhase)`.
  - While a strafe jump is active, `ApplyInput` checks eligibility against a copy of the input with navigation's jump/crouch/walk inputs and vertical direction stripped.
  - The controller's output now also removes `ACTION_WALK`.
  - Enemy-proximity hand-off is unchanged.
- **Debug output:** reasons are now specific, e.g. `[SFJ] bot 0: input/state conflict: weaponTime active` and `final input: visible enemy in saber range`.
- **Tests:** `tests/bot_ai_tuning.cpp` gains `strafejump_soft_conflicts_only_block_initiation`. It covers every phase and checks that ownership survives a soft conflict in the active phases but not a hard one.

### Reviewer notes
- Ignoring a soft conflict mid-jump keeps the input's `ACTION_ATTACK` bits, so a bot can swing while strafing. The existing enemy stop-distance and saber-range guards still hand control back to combat.
- **Not changed:** the 0.2s mid-air hazard look-ahead (`BotSFJ_HazardAhead`). Strafe-jumping into a wall is probably related, but this needs confirmation from the new per-reason debug output first.
- The Gemini suggestions in the issue were not applied. They target files and signatures that don't exist here, and two of them (the airborne arc bypass and the backtracking fix) already exist in the code.

author: manuelmicheli
body:
Before: on event day every arrival was checked in by finding the person in the list and pressing a button. The people expected on site had nothing to show at the entrance.

After: everyone on the crew has a personal pass. From the run of show on the website the agency opens it or sends it on WhatsApp. The person opens the link without an account and sees the QR, a 6-character code, the day, call time and venue. In the app, the event day screen has a "Scansiona i pass" button. The camera reads the QR and checks the person in on the spot, even without signal. The code can also be typed by hand. The app says when a pass is for another day, already used, or unknown.

How:
- **Database**: migration `crew_passes`.
  - `event_crew.pass_token` is random (32 hex characters), unique, and has no insert or update grant, so nobody can choose or change it.
  - The security definer function `crew_pass(token)` is open to anon and returns only the matching pass.
  - SQL test `crew_passes.test.sql`.
- **Core** (`event-day.ts`, with tests):
  - `passUrl`, `passCode`, `readPass` (link, token or short code) and `findPass` (a short code must match exactly one pass).
  - `passFitsNow`: a pass is valid on its day and until 6 in the morning after.
  - `withSentCheckins`.
- **Web**:
  - Public page `/pass/[token]` with the QR drawn on the server (`qrcode`); `/pass` added to the public paths in the proxy.
  - "Apri il pass" and "Invia su WhatsApp" links on each crew row in the run of show.
  - The e2e test opens Sara's pass from a session without login and checks a wrong pass.
- **App**:
  - New screen `scansiona/[id]` using `expo-camera` (camera permission only; RECORD_AUDIO is blocked).
  - It reads the crew from the copy of the event day saved on the phone.
  - The camera callback goes through a ref, because the web camera keeps the first callback it was given.
- **Fix to the offline event day (#16)**: a check-in sent while online fell back to "atteso" until the next reload. Check-ins the server has accepted now stay visible until a server load includes them, and they are also written into the copy saved on the phone.

Checked:
- typecheck, lint and tests for core, mobile, web and db; all SQL tests pass, including the new one; the web build passes.
- Visual QA of the app with Playwright on 20 screens, light and dark. It used Chromium's fake camera and a fake QR reader, and covered: permission, camera, valid pass, other day, already used, unknown pass, a QR that is not a pass, a code typed offline and sending when the network came back. The arrivals list showed the right people as arrived after the scans.
- The pass page in 4 states (waiting, arrived, cancelled, not found), at 390 and 320 px, light and dark.
- 0 problems found (text outside buttons, contrast, touch targets).

body:
Bead: ah-4q5p, filed by Forge: the semantics.rs unit() fixture lists no men, so rules that read a unit's items break 150 tests or grow workarounds.

## What this changes

The fixture half of the bead was already on main. ah-xi43 (#817) made unit() list 1 human [HUMN], and with_men, with_people and with_race keep the headcount and the item list in step. This PR adds a test that pins that, so it cannot be quietly undone.

What was still left is the production guard the bead names. capacity_after_orders (orders/semantics.rs), unit_movement_from_items and mobility_with_ruleset (movement/mode.rs) each ignored the item list when it listed fewer men than unit.men. On a real report that cannot happen:
- classify_unit sets men to exactly the man-tagged items.
- A unit it cannot classify holds an unknown tag, and capacities_from_items already returns None for that.

The guard's only users were the carrying / carrying_with test fixtures. They stripped a unit's men and set an estimated headcount just to force the printed-line fallback. This PR:
- Rewrites those fixtures so their allowance is made of real men. Per data/HUMN and data/LEAD a man walks 15 (capacity 5 plus his own 10). Per data/HORS a horse moves 70 (20 plus its own 50).
- Removes the three guards.
- Deletes the one test that pinned the fixture-only fallback.
- Adds RED-first tests showing the item list now decides: one in semantics.rs and two in mode.rs.

No player-visible behaviour changes (ux:none).

## Validation (the plan's)

- cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --no-fail-fast: 3678 passed, 0 failed.
- cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast: 3826 passed, 0 failed.
- grep for listed_men / men < unit.men in the two files: no matches.

author: dmerrick
body:
## What

- **`web/watch.html`**: one page whose whole body is the live player, `?platform=twitch|youtube` (`&channel=` for the Debug build's staging channel). Twitch's player renders only inside a page whose hostname it was told (`parent`), and an app has none, so the page is the way in. `parent` is the page's own host, so the same file serves every alias, stage and a per-PR preview. YouTube reads `/api/live` for the video id, as the board's live tile does.
- **Watch tab** in the app: a SwiftUI `WebView` (iOS 26) on that page, Twitch or YouTube by a kept segmented picker, and the channel's chat under the player for a signed-in login. The chat body moves out of the Chat tab into a `ChatPane` both tabs show.
- **No browsing:** a navigation decider allows only our host in the main frame, so a tap in the player that would leave for twitch.tv or youtube.com goes nowhere. The app never browses the web, which keeps the store's *unrestricted web access* answer at no. An "Open in Twitch / YouTube" toolbar link leaves the app instead.
- The page is made on appearance and dropped on leaving (no stream decoding behind another tab); the audio session is `.playback` while the tab shows, so the silent switch doesn't mute it.

## Why a web view

Neither platform publishes a native way to play a live stream, and pulling their HLS is against both sets of terms. The raw mediamtx feed tempomat plays sits behind the console on the LAN. So the embed is the only route to watching on the platforms, and the work is in what surrounds it.

## Not in this PR

- Playback needs one tap: `WebPage.Configuration` has no autoplay-without-a-gesture knob. The tap starts it *with* sound, so it is the one tap the unmute would otherwise cost. A `WKWebView` wrapper is the upgrade if it grates (marked `ponytail:` in `Watch.swift`).
- Store declarations: both players show ads, so `advertising = false` and the review notes' *no ads* line stop being true once this ships. Not touched here.
- Liveness (the tab saying *offline* rather than the player's own offline screen), iPad side-by-side, PiP verification on a device, and folding the board's live tile onto this page: filed in the vault.

## Verified

`task ios:build` green on the simulator (iOS 26). The page itself is served only once this deploys, so the Debug build's Watch tab (pointed at stage) 404s until stage carries it; the per-PR preview is the place to try it before then.

author: alpibrupa
body:
## What

Design section 48 (docs only, nothing built): **signed, tamper-evident delivery receipts**: a proof that an event was delivered, that a third party can check without trusting the service.

A Merkle log (RFC 9162) over the delivery outcomes with signed checkpoints; salted payload hashes, so erasing an event becomes crypto-shredding of its salt and the proof of delivery survives; an optional counter-signature by the receiver (Ed25519); a `hooks-verify` tool and an independent Python verifier as the oracle. The section critiques the idea as first proposed (what it does and does not prove: a receipt says the service sent bytes and what status came back, not that the receiver acted on them) and says what is claimed and what is not.

It needs two lex-sys additions, both filed and still open: a shared seeded DRBG in `std` (lex-sys#289) and constant-time Ed25519 scalar arithmetic (lex-sys#290). Slices 1 and 2 depend on them; nothing here starts until they exist.

Section 48 sits between 47 (privacy and audit) and 50.

author: brianmills2718
body:
## Purpose

Run the first comparative workflow pilot proposed by the adaptive-framing work.

Test question:

> What is the smallest useful representation of a frame for Inquiry Graph?

## Workflow

Two lanes were kept distinct by role/source:

1. **reuse/discovery** — search internal and mature prior art for existing framing decompositions;
2. **empirical frame/question pressure** — derive actual representation needs from three real Inquiry Graphs.

This is a one-session workflow pilot, not an independent randomized multi-agent experiment.

## Main result

The reuse lane found an existing Epistemic Warrant participant-relative framing:

`frame(model hypothesis, goal/criterion, boundary+access, resources, active query)`

that had not surfaced in the earlier sequential discussion.

The empirical lane found only three cross-case invariant needs:

- frame content;
- applies-to / inquiry scope;
- active query.

Method-specific coordinates remain optional.

## Implementation

Adds a projection-only `FrameProfile` and three real profiles.

No core `Frame` node kind is added.

Framing/reframing acts remain moves/relations; frame-relative questions/candidates remain graph consequences rather than duplicated profile fields.

## Comparative finding

The parallel process materially reduced the residual abstraction: instead of inventing a broad universal frame record, it reused existing coordinates and kept only three invariant roles.

The fit review records this as positive but weak process evidence and sets reviewer agreement + a second materially different workflow case as the next promotion gates.

author: arkanfzi
body:
**Masalahnya.** `POST /api/contact` adalah satu-satunya rute publik yang menulis DB **dan** memicu pengiriman SMTP. Tanpa rem, satu skrip bisa membanjiri `contact_messages` dan kuota SMTP milik bersama.

**Kenapa bukan per-IP (terukur, bukan dugaan).** Pada request log produksi 2026-10-06: 12 POST ke rute itu datang dari 11 `httpRequest.remoteIp`, dan IP terbanyak (`136.124.34.25`, 7 POST) adalah pool egress Cloud Run tempat frontend keluar — semua pengunjung yang masuk lewat rewrite Next berbagi satu alamat. Bucket per-IP di sana tetap satu bucket bersama, dan `X-Forwarded-For` boleh diisi sendiri oleh pengirimnya. Jadi bucketnya eksplisit global per proses.

**Yang berubah.**
- `go-backend/main.go`: token bucket (`kontakBurst=10`, refill 1 token per menit, mutex-guarded). Dicek **setelah** validasi isian, jadi muatan cacat tetap pulang dengan 400 tanpa menghabiskan token. Yang ditolak menjawab 429 + `Retry-After: 60` + kalimat alasan, yang sudah ditampilkan apa adanya oleh `Contact.tsx` lewat `readApiError`.
- `go-backend/main_test.go`: burst tepat, pulih pada 30/60/90/120 detik, tidak menumpuk lebih dari burst setelah sehari menganggur, jam mundur (koreksi NTP) tidak mengunci rute, dan concurrency pada satu titik waktu harus persis `kontakBurst`.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: satu langkah baru di job `api`, dijalankan pertama supaya embernya pasti penuh — 20 POST sah harus jadi tepat 10x201 + 10x429, `Retry-After=60`, jumlah baris naik tepat sebesar yang diterima, sampel dibersihkan, lalu backend dinyalakan ulang agar langkah sesudahnya (termasuk `DB mati menjawab 500`) tidak kebagisan 429.

**Dibuktikan di luar CI.** Dijalankan end-to-end di jaringan kontainer sendiri (Postgres 15 + binary statis, host `127.0.0.1:18080`): 20 POST menghasilkan `diterima=10 ditolak=10`, `Retry-After=60`, baris `0 -> 10`; empat muatan cacat saat ember kosong tetap 400; setelah 65 detik tepat 1 POST masuk lalu 429 lagi.

**Batasan yang jujur.** Bucket hidup di satu proses; Cloud Run dapat punya lebih dari satu replika, jadi angka ini rem, bukan kuota global. Di produksi yang berubah: flood dari satu skrip tertahan, penggunaan normal tidak pernah merasa ada batas.

Deploy: satu, karena `go-backend/main.go` berubah.

author: rahulrtg
body:
## Resultaat

Publiek bellen/videobellen bestaat alleen nog als het RTG-relais **aantoonbaar** relayt; anders staat het server-side dicht (fail-closed).

- **`server/kern/rtc/`**: een echte TURN-client (RFC 5389/5766) en relayproef: twee allocaties met een vers kortlevend credential, permissies, 64 KiB in beide richtingen (SHA-256 vergeleken), over udp/tcp/tls en over élk geconfigureerd adres.
- **Relaystand wordt afgeleid, nooit opgeslagen** (`relaystand.js`): geen setter, geen route of vlag die "geverifieerd" kan zetten; bewijs draagt 10 minuten en is gebonden aan configuratievingerafdruk + draaiende release. Kill switch `RTG_RTC_UIT=1` wint van alles.
- **`/api/ice` gaf vóór deze PR aan iedereen, zonder sessie, een geldig coturn-credential van een uur** (in feite een open relais met een omweg). Nu: alleen voor een geauthenticeerde actor (Bearer, gezinsPoort, gezinssessie, klas), kortlevend (`TURN_CREDENTIAL_TTL`, standaard 3600 s), ondoorzichtig actorlabel, plafond per actor, `no-store`, op de lijst eenmalige geheimen. Alle 14 belschermen sturen hun sessie mee; theater/clips gebruikten Google-STUN en gebruiken nu de eigen uitgifte.
- **Monotone policy**: `connection.voice`/`connection.video` dragen `provider: rtc-relay` (kill switch > autorisatie > kwalificatie > provider), ook voor het kantoor. Eén RTC-poort vóór alle routers dekt alle 19 WebRTC-signaalroutes; ophangen blijft open. Een toets zakt als er een signaalroute bij komt die niet gedekt is.
- **Publieke productie weigert een vaste `TURN_USER`/`TURN_PASS`** (permanente frontendcredential).
- **Releasepoort**: `scripts/golive.js` beproeft het echte relais in het kandidaatimage met de productieconfig; `live-kandidaat.js` weigert promotie zonder geslaagde `turnRelay` over elk `turns:`-adres.
- **Infra**: `scripts/turn/maak-config.js` (coturn-config met `use-auth-secret`, `denied-peer-ip` over alle private/loopback/link-local/CGNAT/multicast-bereiken, beperkt poortbereik, quota) en `docker-compose.turn.yml` (coturn 4.7.0 vastgepind op digest). `docs/turn-server.md` herschreven.
- **Smoke na uitrol**: `npm run turnproef` (geforceerd relay-gesprek tegen het live relais + negatieve controle).

## Architectuurgrens

- [x] Productie, simulatie en spel blijven aantoonbaar gescheiden
- [x] Nieuwe schrijfacties gebruiken bestaande authenticatie en autorisatie (resolveSession, gezinsPoort, sessieVan, leraarQ/ouderQ)
- [x] AI bereidt voor; onomkeerbare of hoog-risicobesluiten blijven menselijk
- [x] Ontbrekende koppelingen worden niet met demo-uitkomsten gemaskeerd: zonder bewezen relais is RTC dicht, met de reden in `/api/rtc/stand`

## Risico en herstel

- **Grootste risico**: na uitrol staat publiek bellen dicht tot de TURN-host bestaat en de proef slaagt. Dat is de bedoeling, geen regressie.
- **Bewuste uitzondering**: het SOS-meekijkkanaal van een ontmoeting (`/api/ontmoeten/signaal`, `/api/office/ontmoeting/signaal`) valt buiten de RTC-poort; een veiligheidskanaal gaat niet dicht omdat een kwaliteitsafhankelijkheid wegvalt. Ter beslissing aan de eigenaar.
- **Observatiesignaal**: `GET /api/rtc/stand` → `geverifieerd`.
- **Rollback**: app naar het vorige image (`npm run deploy:terug`); TURN-host `docker compose -f docker-compose.turn.yml down` zet RTC fail-closed dicht; noodgeval `RTG_RTC_UIT=1`.

## Bewijs

- [x] Gerichte tests: `test/rtc-relay.test.js` (13, tegen een echte coturn), `test/rtc-relay.e2e.js` (2, echte Chromium, `iceTransportPolicy: 'relay'`, audio+video+64 KiB heen en terug, relay-paar aan beide kanten; gemanipuleerd/verlopen/vreemd geheim/andere gebruikersnaam verbinden niet), plus bijgewerkte `schild`, `foundation`, `productie-communicatie` en `live-kandidaat`. Mutaties nagetrokken: policy zonder provider-check, uitgifte zonder bewijs, anonieme uitgifte, open poort, geldigheidsplafond en open-relaisdetectie laten elk de juiste toets zakken.
- [x] `npm run check`: Alles in orde (75 punten)
- [ ] `npm run ast-scan`
- [ ] `npm test`: niet volledig lokaal gedraaid; CI is de scheidsrechter
- [ ] `npm run build`
- [ ] `npm run ci:lokaal`: deels gedraaid (normverval, wetten, overleving, gezag, envelop, isolatiepoort en gluurronde staan). De rolronde vond `/api/ice` als rolgedeeld loket; dat is nu bij naam vastgelegd en de rolronde staat op 0 gaten. Daarna afgebroken; `npm run registerklopt`: alle registers kloppen.
- [ ] Schermen op relevante formaten gecontroleerd: n.v.t. (alleen het ophalen van ICE-servers is gewijzigd)

CI installeert `coturn` in de scherf-, incremental- en schermenjobs; zonder het pakket zakken de RTC-toetsen in CI (lokaal overslaan met de reden).

## Go-live

Buiten deze repository, door iemand met toegang tot de infrastructuur:
1. Een VPS met een openbaar IPv4-adres, een DNS A-record `turn.<productiedomein>` daarnaar, en een publiek vertrouwd TLS-certificaat voor die naam.
2. Firewall: 3478/udp+tcp, 5349/tcp en 49160-49999/udp; al het andere dicht.
3. Een `TURN_SECRET` uit de secretstore; `maak-config.js` draaien en `docker compose -f docker-compose.turn.yml up -d` starten.
4. `TURN_URL=turns:turn.<domein>:5349?transport=tcp` en `TURN_SECRET` in de app-secret zetten.
5. Golive in het kandidaatimage moet `turnRelay.ok` geven, daarna de bestaande promotie van exact die digest, en daarna `npm run turnproef` tegen productie.
6. Het externe `connectionRealtime`-bewijs (twee netwerk-AS'en, getekend door de meetrunner) blijft vereist; het runneranker `deploy/evidence-runner-v1.pub` bestaat nog niet.

body: ## What was wrong Submitting a join request did two things: it stored a `pending` row, and it posted a portal notice (`Join request from …`) to every admin. That notice is what shows on the resident dashboard under Personal notices, on Notices, and in the Notices unread badge. Delete already removed the `join_requests` row, and the admin card “Join requests waiting” already counted only `status = 'pending'`. The notice was never removed, so after Delete the request was gone from Join requests but still appeared as a pending request on the dashboard and under Notices. Decline, Mark reviewed, and Approve left the same notice in place. A declined, reviewed, or approved request therefore still looked pending anywhere notices are listed. ## What changed - Notices, the dashboard notice list, and the unread badge keep a join-request notice only while a matching request is still `pending`. An already-deleted request (no row left) drops off those surfaces without another delete. Declined, reviewed, and approved requests are excluded too. - Delete, Decline, Mark reviewed, and Approve now remove the matching notice. A new request stores its id on the notice so one delete does not clear a different pending request. - Other account notices are unchanged. The Join requests admin list still shows declined and approved rows so they can be approved later; they are not part of the waiting count. ## Tests `npm test` (51 passing) and `npm run check` both pass. New cases cover delete, decline, review, approve, an already-removed request, the unread badge, and the dashboard and Notices pages.

body:
## Problema
O "Conectar" da Shopee abria a tela de erro da Shopee: `The domain of redirect is not consistent with the Redirect URL Domain declared in console`.

O endereço de volta era montado a partir de `req.url`. Esse endereço é o domínio pelo qual o sistema foi aberto, ou até o host interno do deploy na Vercel, e pode não ser o `painel-liard-xi.vercel.app` cadastrado no app da Shopee.

## Correção
- **`lib/origem.ts`**, com testes:
  - `origemDaRequisicao` usa o `x-forwarded-host`, que é o domínio que o navegador realmente pediu, e valida o formato do host;
  - `dominioPrincipalSeDiferente` lê a `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL`.
- **`/api/shopee/conectar` e `/api/mercadolivre/conectar`:** quando a `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` está definida e o domínio atual é outro, redirecionam primeiro para o domínio principal. Assim os cookies do `estado` e a volta ficam no mesmo domínio cadastrado.
- **Os dois callbacks** redirecionam para a tela pelo mesmo domínio.

## Configuração na Vercel
- Criar `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` = `https://painel-liard-xi.vercel.app` (Config, Production).
- Ela também corrige os links dos e-mails de cadastro e de recuperação de senha, que passam a apontar sempre para o domínio principal.

body:
## 무엇을 바꿨나

감사 결과 확정과 승인 전이를 **이벤트 v2**로 남기고, 소비자가 DB가 아니라 이벤트 출처로만 받게 했다. 전송은 아웃박스 폴링이다(Kafka는 로드맵 마지막 단계에서 전송만 교체한다).

- **계약**: `contracts/events/finguard-event-v2.schema.json`. 하나의 닫힌 봉투에 감사 결과 3종(확정·미확인·해소)과 승인 전이 6종(요청·승인·거절·만료·묶기·사용)을 담는다. 타입별 필수·금지 필드는 `AuditCompletion`과 같다. 고객 식별자는 어느 깊이에도 없다. fixture는 유효 11·무효 20.
- **아웃박스(V12)**: 변경과 같은 트랜잭션에서 한 행씩 쓴다. 이벤트 기록이 실패하면 변경도 롤백된다. 원천 하나에 행 하나(unique)이고, 이벤트 문자열을 그대로 저장하고 SHA-256을 함께 둔다. 행은 바꾸거나 지울 수 없다(트리거). 피드 번호만 한 번 매긴다.
- **승인 단일 쓰기 경로**: 승인 요청 저장은 `ApprovalEventWriter` 하나로만 한다. 이 경로를 거치지 않은 저장과, DB에서 분리된 요청은 엔티티 검사에서 실패한다.
- **시퀀서 + 피드**: bigserial id는 커밋 순서가 아니어서, id로 읽는 소비자는 늦게 커밋된 이벤트를 건너뛴다. 단일 시퀀서가 커밋된 행에만 피드 번호를 매긴다(같은 advisory 잠금, 캐시 없는 시퀀스). `GET /feed/v1/events`는 원문과 해시를 페이지로 내보내고 피드 세대를 함께 준다.
- **피드 전용 Credential**: 피드는 `/internal/*`가 아니라 `/feed/*`에 둔다. 내부 인증 필터는 요청 URI로 경로를 다시 가르지 않는다(과거 우회 이력). 대신 각 Credential을 서로 다른 서블릿 패턴에 붙인다. 두 값이 같으면 Core가 기동하지 않는다.
- **소비자 실행기 + 승인 알림함(V13)**: 소비자는 불투명 체크포인트를 쓰는 `EventSource`에만 의존한다. 한 트랜잭션에서 체크포인트를 잠그고, 해시와 봉투를 확인하고, 이벤트 id로 중복을 거르고, 처리하고, 체크포인트를 저장한다. 믿을 수 없는 이벤트는 건너뛰지 않고 멈춘다. 승인 요청은 승인자 알림함으로, 결정과 만료는 요청 직원에게 간다. 알림 API와 화면(상단 알림 버튼)을 추가했다.
- **경보 워커(새 모듈 `backend:alert-worker`)**: 피드만 HTTP로 읽고 자기 DB(`finguard_alerts`)에 상태를 둔다. K4 규칙(차단 급증·위험 표시 급증·결과 미확인)을 그대로 옮겼다. 체크포인트는 비교 후 갱신한다. 같은 위치에서 무결성 실패가 이어지면 사건을 남기고 멈춘다(health DOWN). 피드가 잠깐 안 되면 최대 30초까지 간격을 늘려 다시 시도한다.
- **배선**: 선택 overlay `infrastructure/docker-compose.events.yml`을 추가했다. 기본 compose는 그대로다. 두 비밀값은 compose secret이고, 컨테이너 안에서 Spring configtree로 읽는다. 워커 역할과 DB를 만드는 초기화 스크립트는 멱등이다. 워커 역할은 Core·`postgres`·`template1` DB에 접속할 수 없다.

## 사용법

```bash
# .env에 추가(예시 파일에는 아직 없다)
EVENT_FEED_CREDENTIAL=...      # 피드 전용, 내부 Credential과 달라야 함
ALERT_WORKER_DB_PASSWORD=...
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.events.yml up -d
# 기존 볼륨이면 지우지 말고 한 번:
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.events.yml exec -T postgres sh /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/20-alert-worker.sh
```

## SPEC에서 바뀐 점

- 피드 경로는 SPEC의 `/internal/v1/events`가 아니라 `/feed/v1/events`다(위 이유).
- DB 격리는 **단방향**이다. 워커는 Core DB에 접속할 수 없다. 반대 방향은 막지 못한다 — 이 compose의 Core는 PostgreSQL superuser로 접속한다(기존 구성). 백로그.

## 검증

- core-api, alert-worker, gateway, 계약 테스트 전부 통과. 프런트엔드 vitest 91, 빌드 통과. 단위마다 Codex 리뷰를 받고 반영했다.
- 안전장치를 일부러 고장 내 확인했다.
  - 격리 스크립트의 CONNECT 회수를 지우면 격리 테스트가 실패한다.
    - 처음에는 이 확인이 통과해 버렸다. 원인은 Gradle이 모듈 밖 스크립트 변경을 몰라 이전 결과를 재사용한 것이었다. 스크립트를 테스트 입력으로 선언해 고쳤다.
  - 초기화 스크립트를 서브셸 없이 되돌리면 "비밀번호 없는 새 DB 기동" 테스트가 실패한다. Postgres가 실행 권한 없는 초기화 스크립트를 source해서 `exit 0`이 기동을 끝내던 실제 버그다.
- **실측(finguard-s5) PASS**: 정상·차단 버스트·APPROVAL·승인 후 다시 실행을 섞었다. 경보 워커를 세 번 강제 종료하고 Core를 한 번 재시작했다.
  - 이벤트 19건. 아웃박스 = 피드 = 워커 처리 기록(id·해시 집합 일치, 해시 불일치 0). 유실·중복 0.
  - 워커 카운터와 경보가 아웃박스 이벤트로 다시 계산한 값과 같다. 강제 종료 뒤에도 같은 이벤트가 두 번 반영되지 않았다.
  - 무결성 사건 0. 승인 알림은 승인자에게 요청 1번, 요청 직원에게 승인 1번.
  - 한계: 이벤트 수가 적고, 강제 종료는 호출 묶음 사이에 넣어 "커밋 도중"이 보장되지 않는다. 커밋 도중 실패와 워커 동시 실행은 단위 테스트로 확인했다.

## 남은 것

- 양방향 DB 격리(Core를 superuser가 아닌 역할로).
- 결과 기록 API에서 빈 정책 버전을 거부(지금은 이벤트에서만 뺀다).
- `.env.example`에 새 변수 2개 추가.
- App 테스트의 순서 기반 fetch mock을 경로 기반으로.
- 아웃박스 보존·정리. 이벤트를 더 많이, 커밋 도중에 강제 종료하는 실측.
- 다음 단계: 5(응답 속 민감정보 MASK). Kafka는 마지막.

author: ynakagawa
body:
Please always provide the [GitHub issue(s)](../issues) your PR is for, as well as test URLs where your change can be observed (before and after):

Fix #N/A — no tracking issue; this comes from the 3M "what would it take to add our components?" request against the **MDS for AEM Pilot** Figma file.

Test URLs:
- Before: https://main--3m--ynaka-adobe.aem.page/blocks/mds-components
- After: https://ynaka-adobe-special-giggle--3m--ynaka-adobe.aem.page/blocks/mds-components

Same page, same content, both URLs live. `main` has none of these blocks, so it renders the raw authored tables — the diff between the two tabs *is* the change.

---

## What this is

3M asked what the lift would be to bring their design-system components into AEM. Rather than answer with a number alone, this builds the net-new ones so the answer is demonstrable.

I inventoried the pilot Figma file into **28 component instances**, which deduplicate to **18 unique components**. Eight of those are variants of blocks this repo already has and are not in scope here. The remaining ten are what this PR covers: **nine net-new blocks, plus an additive extension to the existing `accordion`**.

| Block | MDS ID | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `stackable` | rMDS-206 | Alternating media/text rows; side flips automatically |
| `column-link-list` | rMDS-203 | Multi-column links; PDF/external affordance derived from the href |
| `image-features` | rMDS-217 | Auto-numbered feature steps beside an image |
| `compare-table` | rMDS-218 | Spec comparison; reflows to one card per column under 600px |
| `resource-list` | TBD-Resource Block | Document library, authored rows **or** query-index driven |
| `anchor-nav` | — | Scroll-spy section nav; `tabs` variant also covers the MDS tab bar |
| `page-nav` | — | Page title + sticky section navigation |
| `breadcrumb` | — | Trail derived from the URL, author rows override |
| `product-selector` | — | Finder entry; selections build query params onto the CTA |
| `accordion` *(existing)* | — | Adds `single` / `open` variants and deep-linkable item IDs |

Two MDS instances collapsed into existing blocks here: the media/text rows and the link list each appeared both inside a page template and again as a standalone component frame.

### A note on `accordion`

I originally wrote this as a net-new block. It isn't — `main` already had one from #36, and rebasing surfaced the collision. Rather than replace it, I rewrote my version to keep **main's exact DOM structure and class names** (`accordion-item`, `accordion-item-label`, `accordion-item-body`) and layer three additive features on top:

- `single` variant — only one item open at a time
- `open` variant — first item starts expanded
- deep-linkable IDs (`#faq-<slug>`), trimmed on a word boundary so URLs stay readable

**`blocks/accordion/accordion.css` is byte-identical to `main`.** Existing FAQ content keeps rendering exactly as it does today; the authoring contract (cell 1 = label, cell 2 = body) is unchanged.

## Authoring contract

Every block follows the repo convention — JSDoc header documenting cell order, `export default function decorate(block)`, build-then-`replaceChildren`, variants via block class, mobile-first CSS at 600/900/1200. All cells are optional: a row missing an image, a CTA or a body still renders rather than throwing. That matters because authors will not fill every field.

No new dependencies. No build step. Styling uses the existing `:root` tokens (`--accent`, `--ink`, `--muted`, `--line`, `--maxw`) rather than introducing a parallel palette.

## Accessibility

- `accordion` stays on native `<details>`, so it is keyboard operable and findable by in-browser search even before JS runs
- `compare-table` boolean cells carry visually-hidden text, so the tick/cross icons are not the only signal
- `page-nav` menus close on Escape and restore focus to the trigger
- `resource-list` announces "Showing 3 of 6" through a live region and moves focus to newly revealed rows on "Show more"
- `anchor-nav` reflects current section via `aria-current`

## Validation

Rebased onto `main`, then ran the full CI command locally:

```
npm run lint  →  exit 0
              ✖ 7 problems (0 errors, 7 warnings)
```

Zero errors. The seven warnings are pre-existing, in `tools/target` and `tools/sidekick`, and are untouched here. `lint:css` is clean. CI `build` and `aem-psi-check` both pass on the rebased branch.

Beyond lint, I ran the page in a browser against a local dev server and probed the DOM directly. All 10 blocks reach `data-block-status="loaded"`; computed styles confirm the responsive rules apply at mobile, tablet and desktop widths; all images resolve with no broken requests.

That probing caught two bugs lint could not:

1. **`anchor-nav`** was collecting `h2`s from *inside* other blocks, so the product-selector's CTA heading became a tab. Now prefers headings that aren't nested in a `.block`, falling back to all if none are structural.
2. **`accordion`** truncated deep-link IDs mid-word (`...reaches-full-stre`). Added word-boundary trimming.

## Imagery

The live site has no uploaded media, so the media-bearing blocks had nothing to render. I added four abstract SVG placeholders built from the brand tokens — under 1 KB each, 16 KB total. They are stand-ins for the preview, not proposed design assets; real authoring would upload through DA.

## Notes for review

- `drafts/mds-components.plain.html` is the local harness and is excluded from delivery via `.hlxignore`. The previewable copy lives in DA at `/blocks/mds-components`, alongside the existing `/blocks/columns` demo. It is previewed, not published.
- **Not included:** the 8 variants of existing blocks (cards, carousel, contact-cta, hero, header, footer). The first six are additive and low-risk; the header and footer changes touch components live on every page, so I'd rather scope those separately than bundle regression risk into this PR.
- Roughly 11 `rMDS` IDs referenced in the pilot aren't present in that file and are presumably in a parent MDS library I don't have access to. They are unestimated scope.
- The pilot has no mobile artboards, so responsive behaviour here is my interpretation, not a spec. Worth confirming with 3M.

author: crenshawdev
body:
Fixes #184.
Fixes #200.
Fixes #201.

Three findings against the MCP session server from an outside review of main, two in the code and one in the tests.

#184: the worker could say it had drained before the last answer left. Closing or abandoning admission looked at the queue alone, and the finished decision's slot was freed before its answer was sent, so a client could see the drain published and never get the answer behind it. The worker now tracks an answer in flight under the same mutex as the queue, and close, abandon and normal completion share one drain decision: queue empty and nothing in flight. The shutdown text in design 0012 and Figure 1 now say the order plainly, wait up to ten seconds, abandon only at the bound, and make the one checkpoint attempt either way.

#200: not a production bug, a blind test. The capture handler already attached instruction evidence before preparation, but no test could tell, because the only place to look was the finished domain command. Preparation now goes through `prepare_capture`, which takes a plain function pointer, so nothing can hand preparation a different caller on the way in, and the tests observe the caller and the write request at that boundary without running discovery, git or the policy step.

#201: when a body lookup found the bytes purged, the answer took the reason from the hash-global status, so two projects purging the same text at the same time could hand one project the other's tombstone reason. The read now goes back to the project's own view and takes the reason from that view's tombstone only. A view that doesn't confirm the purge answers `failed` with `ledger-unavailable`, which is the honest answer when the ledger moved under the read. The decision is a pure function with a test for each arm, and a SQLite test records the same 4,097-byte text under two projects, purges both with different reasons, and checks that each stale read gets its own.

The docs moved with it. Design 0001 states the per-project tombstone, designs 0003, 0012 and 0014 cite the code where it now lives, and the roadmap takes the three issues out of Build 3's open work with the counts dated.

Verified: 3,325 tests pass across the workspace at the second to last commit, the last one adds a single test, after which the `baley` crate's 2,362 pass and clippy with `-D warnings`, fmt and cargo-deny are clean. `Cargo.lock` is unchanged, all 39 Mermaid blocks in the touched docs parse, and every citation in `docs/` into the changed source files lands. There are 6 new tests, and each was run against a break of what it guards and failed: a drain decision that reads the queue alone, a purge answer that takes the global reason, evidence attached after preparation, a preparation handed no request.

A second model wrote it and I reviewed it twice. The first review found fifteen citations pointing at the wrong lines, a closure in `serve` that could swap the caller with no test failing, the `ledger-unavailable` arm untested, and a shutdown sentence that had abandonment happening on a completed drain. The second found the observation helper dropping the request it was handed, so a preparation given no request failed nothing. All of it is fixed on the branch.

Not verified: the assembled server, the transport flush before exit, and real concurrent SQLite purge scheduling, the test replays saved observations. The built binary wasn't run by hand.

Left for later: the roadmap's issue table and milestone counts are reconciled by the last of today's fix pull requests to merge.

author: kinabalu
body:
## Problem

The calculator couldn't show a number as a fraction or a Roman numeral, and it couldn't adjust a color, mix two colors or check contrast. These were the "bigger features" left over from the Raycast parity review.

## Behavior

**Fractions** (`NumberForms`)
- `0.25 as fraction` → 1/4. `1/3 + 1/6 as fraction` → 1/2. `2.75 as fraction` → 11/4, tagged `2 3/4`. `as mixed number` swaps the two.
- The answer is the closest fraction with a denominator up to 10,000, found from continued fractions and semiconvergents. So `0.333333` → 1/3 and `pi` → 355/113, tagged "Approximate" when the fraction isn't exact.

**Roman numerals**
- `2026 in roman` → MMXXVI (1–3999). `XIV in decimal`, `roman XIV` and `roman numeral MMXXVI` go the other way, and swap works between the two directions.
- Only standard forms are read, so `IIII`, `VX` and `IC` give no answer. A bare `XIV` stays a search.

**Color adjustments** (`ColorAdjustments`)
- `#f00 lighten 10%`, `darken`, `saturate`, `desaturate`, and `lighten(#f00, 10%)` take absolute HSL steps, as Sass does: `#ff3333`. **HSL rather than OKLCH** so the results match the Sass and Less values people compare against. The tradeoff is recorded in the design doc.
- `complement of #3a7bd5` adds 180° to the HSL hue. `#3a7bd5 at 50% alpha` and `with 50% opacity` replace the alpha.
- `mix(#f00, #00f)` and `color-mix(in srgb, #f00 25%, #00f)` follow CSS Color 5: OKLab by default, `srgb` and `srgb-linear` on request, premultiplied alpha, and percentages that are filled in or scaled to 100.
- `contrast #fff #3a7bd5` gives the WCAG 2 ratio of the first color as text on the second, with an AA/AAA verdict. The ratio is floored to two decimals, so it never reads as passing when it doesn't.
- Results answer in the input's format, or the one after `in`. Named colors work because the operation word marks the query as a color. The swatch shows the resulting color, and there's no swap.
- `rgbToHSL` now treats channel spreads under 1e-6 as gray, so OKLab mixes of grays don't show a stray hue.

## Validation

- `swift test --package-path Core`: all 216 tests pass. The new `NumberFormsTests` and `ColorAdjustmentsTests` cover:
  - exact and approximate fractions, the denominator bound, mixed numbers and German decimal commas
  - every Roman numeral from 1 to 3999 round-tripped, plus non-standard forms rejected
  - Sass lighten/darken/saturate values
  - CSS color-mix values (`color-mix(in oklab, red, blue)` = `rgb(140 83 162)`)
  - WCAG pairs: 21:1, white on navy 16:1, `#767676` passes AA at 4.54, `#777` fails at 4.47
  - translucent text, and plain words that stay searches
  - each new query giving exactly one card through `CalculationAnswer.answers`
- `Scripts/test.sh --base origin/main`: SwiftLint and the 189 hosted tests pass. The classifier found no UI changes; the card layout is unchanged and only the existing swatch is reused.

## Limitations

- Adjustments accept only the formats ColorCalculator already reads after `in` (hex through oklch), not the NSColor/UIColor targets coming in the Raycast-gaps PR.
- `mix(...) in srgb` isn't read; the interpolation space goes inside `color-mix(in srgb, …)`.
- Contrast uses WCAG 2, not APCA.

body:
Closes #33

> Branch empilhada sobre a #46 (lista de escolas): mergear depois dela.

## O que muda

- **Admin › Escolas › editar**: ao salvar com "Escola ativa" alterada, uma confirmação diz o efeito com o número de pessoas, contado pela API (`GET /api/users?schoolId=…&isActive=true`):
  - **Desativar**: "6 pessoas perdem o acesso na hora: não conseguem entrar até a escola ser reativada. Nada é apagado."
  - **Reativar**: quantas pessoas com conta ativa voltam a entrar.
  - Se a contagem falhar, a confirmação aparece sem o número. Cancelar mantém o formulário aberto com o que foi digitado.
- **Confirmações reversíveis**: o diálogo de confirmação dizia "Esta ação não pode ser desfeita." em toda ação de perigo, inclusive nas reversíveis. A nova opção `reversible` tira essa frase de desativar ou reativar escola e usuário, remover da escola e desvincular turma ou responsável. Exclusões continuam com o aviso.

## Como testar

Admin › Escolas › Jardim das Flores › Editar › desmarque "Escola ativa" › Salvar: a confirmação diz "6 pessoas perdem o acesso…", sem a frase de ação definitiva. Cancelar volta ao formulário (conferido no Chrome headless).

author: abelkf
body:
## Description

Reorganize the guides by integration path. This PR sits on top of #26.

- **Getting Started** now asks the reader to choose a path and compares the paths in a table.
- **Accept Payments in the Browser**: one page per method covers collect with Elements and create the payment. These are Accept Card Payments, Accept Bank Account Payments (manual and verified), Accept Apple Pay and Accept Google Pay. The 3DS and Recollect a CVC guides move here.
- **Accept Payments Server-to-server**: Save Cards (the `collect.publicsquare.com` flow that was inside Collect Cards) and Inline Card Payments and Payouts (the two guides from #26 in one page).
- **eCommerce Plugins** and **Marketplaces** are separate groups.
- **Manage Payments**: Authorize and Capture, Verify Cards, Cancel Payments, Refunds (now with cancel), Send Payouts (card, ACH and cancel) and Transactions and Settlements.
- **Go Live**: Production Checklist and Testing.
- Pages that had a Payment Intents section and a Legacy section now use tabs. Payment Intents is the default. The tabs share `groupId="api-style"`, so the choice carries over between pages. `?api=legacy` selects Legacy in a link.
- Each of the 16 removed URLs has a redirect from `@docusaurus/plugin-client-redirects` to the page that holds its content. The plugin was already a dependency.

The merged pages reuse the existing text and code samples. Some samples already had errors before this PR, and this PR does not fix them. Examples are the Google Pay `allowedCardNetworks=[...]` syntax and trailing commas in some response JSON.

author: tristanmatthias
body:
**The bug:** `work run` trapped TERM as an interrupt and asked the Sprite to stop the run. An agent harness TERMs a lane's background processes when its turn ends, so every lane that left killed its own run (exit 143) and met a dead or restarted run on its return — which read all evening as "the Sprite stood still". The Sprite never did.

**Proof, live on a Sprite before the fix:** TERM to the follower → "work: interrupted — stopping the run", the run `Terminated`, "ended 143" after 4 stamps. HUP to the follower, nobody attached for nine minutes → all 60 ten-second stamps present, no gap, ended 0.

**The fix (tools/work):** TERM and HUP detach (143 / 129) and say how to follow and how to end the run. Ctrl-C and `work stop` are the two that end one. BUSY (76) says the run is live with nobody following it and names `work attach` first. `work test` starts its run through `run`, so it is covered.

**Tests (tools/work_test.sh):** one case per signal — TERM: exit 143, the "run goes on" line, no stop sent; HUP: 129, same; INT: 130, exactly one stop. The TERM case was seen failing on the old tool first.

CLAUDE.md's sentence is made true: Ctrl-C or `work stop` ends a run; a drop, a hangup or the client being killed never does.

Reviewed by the lead by reading (about 20 lines of tool).

body:
## Summary

Adds a focused Windows CI gate for the portable backend-runtime fix behind #566.

The actual packaging fix is already on `main`: Windows desktop builds stage a verified embedded Python runtime instead of copying the developer venv, reject `pyvenv.cfg` / `.pth` / `.egg-link` metadata, scan for build-machine path leaks, and run a relocation/import smoke test before packaging.

What was missing was continuous execution of the dedicated regression test. This PR runs:

```
node --test desktop-shell/tauri-skeleton/scripts/build-backend-runtime.test.cjs
```

on `windows-latest` for every normal CI invocation.

That locks in the exact failure mode reported in #566 without adding installer/runtime behavior or user-facing setup.

Refs #566.

author: santiagodevrel
body:
Players could lose progress when code verification, receipt submission or optional browser features failed. Registration and payment retries now retain the intended operation, score inputs accept two-digit values, and PIN writes cannot overwrite a newer credential.

- Preserve OTP entry, the intended account and onboarding destination through reloads, lost responses and blocked storage. Invalid verification preserves an existing session.
- Keep receipt request identity in memory, prevent slot removal during upload and cancel payment navigation after leaving the screen.
- Restore an expired payment session in another tab without discarding the receipt or changing its request identity.
- Keep narrow 1X2 labels readable at enlarged text sizes and add accessible manual-question labels.
- Fence PIN writes by authenticated owner, verified phone, request UUID and credential revision. Migration 167 adds metadata while preserving existing credentials and allows safe rolling deployment.
- Catch optional welcome-download and service-worker-registration failures. Add recovery browser checks to CI against the production build.
- Keep phone, PIN, receipt and prediction controls disabled until handlers and saved drafts are ready. Normalize match-time spaces to prevent actual WebKit hydration failures.
- Preserve score replacement on native WebKit clicks, refresh server completion counts only after confirmed saves, and postpone invitation prompts while a player is typing or has unsaved work.
- Prevent late upload replies from navigating after leaving the payment screen; provide an explicit link after confirmation. Keep the native slot selector readable in dark mode.

Validation: local production build, typecheck and lint passed (11 existing image warnings); 1,879 unit tests passed, one skipped. Recovery/translation/update checks cover Chrome and WebKit, including delayed JavaScript. Receipt verification covers actual local Storage bytes, database confirmation, API and UI; prediction checks cover 92 draft/save fault scenarios and 14 real database-to-UI cases across Chrome and WebKit. The final receipt suite passes all seven cases in each engine, including delayed confirmation after navigating away and session recovery with the original file and request UUID. Recovery checks pass 96 cases; public accessibility checks pass 24 cases. Complete isolated migration replay, nine SQL regression suites and real independent-owner/contended PIN transactions passed. Registration, onboarding and fresh-context PIN login are checked with local accounts at 320/768/1280 px and 200% enlargement; affected layout edges include 639/640/641 px.

Apply `167_phone_password_write_revisions.sql` before the application release. No rollout flags, peppers or existing credentials need changing. No dependencies were added. Carrier SMS delivery, real transfers and physical Safari/iOS/Android devices were not exercised; passing these checks does not establish a universal failure-free guarantee.


Delivery: merged as `1e3d675893b526386dde39c00ffa401b358bc96c` and deployed to https://lapollacolombiana.com (`dpl_CH1ed4eHssTL1Fv78PEUgvtRfxrU`). Migration 167 is recorded and verified with server-only execution permissions. Production checks confirm delayed-JavaScript login recovery at three widths, the authenticated payment picker becoming ready, the active service worker, uncached authentication APIs, and no exposed sensitive file routes. Both task-created preview deployments were removed and their URLs now return 404.

author: nekodas-neko
body:
Closes #2337

A user with no ring and no HR source saw three defaults presented as readings. I re-checked all three against `main` before starting and none had been fixed.

1. **End-of-day review** printed "Body Battery 50 (down 0)" when `/api/body-battery` returned `hasData: false`.
2. **Zone quota** showed "0 / 108 min" on every zone, though nothing could have recorded zone minutes.
3. **`progress-summary`** returned `thisWeekHours: 0` while `lastNightHours` was null, so the goals card drew 0 h against the sleep goal.

## Engine (first commit)

- **`hasHrSource(profile)`** in `packages/shared/src/health/hr-profile.ts` is the only definition. It is true when any plausible HR reading landed in the profile's 90-day observed window, from ring, strap or Health Connect. Every zone route already resolves that profile, so the check adds no query. If the observed read fails, the result is `null`, never `false`: `resolveHrProfile` now records the failure as `observedUnread`, so a database fault can't tell anyone they have no source.
- **`ZoneQuota.hasHrSource?: boolean | null`** is set by `computeZoneQuota(targets, days, { hasHrSource })`. When the option is left out, the quota has no such key, so its output is byte-identical to before. `quotaHasNoHrSource()` returns true only for a known `false`. A missing flag (older cached payloads) or `null` (failed read) keeps the old behaviour.
- `cardio-week` carries the flag on both quotas. `cardio-trends` and `zone-minutes` carry it at the top level.
- **Recommenders that read the quota:**
  - `recommendSession` (TimePickerSheet) no longer says "a walk would put a dent in your Z2 minutes".
  - `recommendRunType` returns null.
  - `recommendWalkPattern` falls back to the easy steps walk, the same fallback it already uses when there is no Zone 2 target.
  - A fitting prescribed run still wins.
- **`progress-summary`**: `thisWeekHours` is now `number | null`. It is null when no night this week passes `recordsSleep`.

## Surface (second commit, plus a fix found while testing)

- **End-of-day review:** a new `measuredBattery()` helper (`components/nutrition/end-of-day/measured-battery.ts`) gates all three uses of the battery: the insight line, the day-summary chip, and the tiredness slider prefill. Before this, the prefill took "Good" from the default 50 and set the slider to 2; it now starts at the neutral 3. This is the same `noData` refusal `body-battery-card.tsx` already makes.
- **Zone quota card:** shows the empty-state copy the Time in Zone card already uses ("…wear the ring or strap during a workout.") in place of the zone rows. The Today / This week toggle is dropped too, because both views are empty. No new design.
- **Trends zone chart:** shows the same empty state when `hasHrSource === false` and every stack is zero. Real history from a source that has since been removed still draws.
- **Goals card:** already hid a null row. Testing turned up a trap: with a sleep goal, no recorded night and no scheduled program, "This Week" had no rows, so the card returned null and took its toggle with it. The view is persisted, so the card then stayed gone. Now, when one view is empty and the other is not, the card stays and shows "Nothing recorded this week yet."

## Not changed, with reasons

- **Time in Zone card:** it already renders absence when the window has zero seconds. It now receives `hasHrSource` but needs no change.
- **LazyDayCreditCard:** it already hides at 0 minutes.
- **TodaysCardioCard:** a no-HR user's logged activities have `avgHr == null`, so their logged minutes already count. "0 / 30" there means nothing was logged, which is true.
- **No local-store path computes any of these values on device.** They are server-derived reads, so there was no offline path to change.
- **#2198** (`type: tuning`, same milestone) is untouched. It needs the owner's sign-off.

The tests pin this:

- Each recommender returns `toEqual` the old answer for `true`, `null` and a missing flag.
- `measuredBattery` passes a measured battery through as the same object.
- The weekly sleep sum is unchanged for any week with a recorded night.

- `pnpm check:rules`: **Ran 81 of 81 Custom Rules steps**, all passed.
- `pnpm typecheck` is clean. `pnpm typecheck:tests` is at baseline (82 files, none above).
- `pnpm test`: 11,422 passed and 10 failed. All 10 are known local flakes, and each passed when re-run on its own (or with a longer timeout for the tree walks): catalogue-equipment-guard, e2e-ui-touched, check-comment-blindness, push-mutations-web-parity, repository-ownership-scoping, no-cloud-calls, exercise-role-labels and rv103-rv104. The two claude-ro role tests fail locally because of drift in the shared dev DB.

## Why
Since #734 every push to `master` ends with a red **Secret Scanning** run, and pull requests get no Secret Scanning check at all.

`.github/workflows/secret-scan.yml` has three `uses:` keys in the TruffleHog step (`@v3.97.2`, `@v3.97.1`, `@v3.97.9`). A strict YAML parser rejects it (`duplicated mapping key`), so GitHub refuses to start the workflow: 0 jobs, 0 seconds, conclusion `failure`.

It happened because overlapping Dependabot PRs (#734, #739, #747) edited the same line; the conflict resolutions on #734 and #739 kept both versions.

## What
Keep one `uses:` line, pinned to `v3.97.9` (the newest of the three). Nothing else changes.

## Checked
- All five workflow files parse with js-yaml (strict mode).
- `git diff`: 2 deletions, 0 additions.
- This PR should be the first one to show a Secret Scanning check since #734, which is the proof that the workflow starts again.

No secret scanning runs on pushes or pull requests.

💡 What: Updated `ScrollReveal` component to use a shared, module-level `IntersectionObserver` cached by threshold, and a `WeakMap` for per-element callbacks, instead of creating a new observer instance for every element.

🎯 Why: The previous implementation created a new `IntersectionObserver` instance for every observed element (e.g., every section or card using `ScrollReveal`). This caused O(n) memory overhead and excessive listener instantiation, leading to potential scrolling jank on pages with many elements.

📊 Impact: Reduces memory footprint by scaling observer instances to O(1) per threshold instead of O(n) per element. Also removes unnecessary main thread overhead during initialization. 

🔬 Measurement: Verify that animations still trigger flawlessly when elements scroll into view, run `npm run test:e2e` to ensure no visual regressions, and observe reduced memory snapshot size using Chrome DevTools for pages with long scrollable lists.

author: sam-goodwin
body:
One implementation of ignore-file filtering, `Util/Ignore.ts`, replaces three: the `.dockerignore` matcher embedded in `Docker/BuildHash`, the read-everything-then-filter walk in Workers assets, and the lossy gitignore→glob converter behind `Command.Build` memos.

```ts
const rules = parseIgnoreRules(content, "dockerignore"); // or "gitignore"
rules.ignores("node_modules/pkg/index.js"); // true
rules.prunes("node_modules");               // true: nothing below can be re-included

const entries = yield* walkIgnoring({
  list: yield* listFileSystemDirectory(root),
  rules,
  force: ["Dockerfile"], // always kept, parents never pruned
});
```

The two dialects differ where the real tools differ:

```sh
# rules: foo, *.log, logs + !logs/keep.log
                     .gitignore   .dockerignore
a/foo                ignored      kept         # bare names: any depth vs root only
a/b.log              ignored      kept
logs/keep.log        ignored      kept         # re-include below an excluded dir
```

### User-visible fixes

`.assetsignore`'d folders are no longer read, so an unreadable one no longer fails the deploy:

```ts
// .assetsignore: private/
yield* Cloudflare.Worker("Site", { assets: { directory: "./dist" } });
```

```diff
- EACCES: permission denied, open './dist/private/cache'
+ ✓ Site  created
```

Memos read each ancestor `.gitignore` relative to its own directory and honor `!` negations:

```ts
// repo/.gitignore: /app/generated/   *.log   !keep.log
yield* Command.Build("App", { command: "bun run build", cwd: "./app" });
```

```diff
  edit app/generated/types.ts
- [App] update   (rebuilds: the anchored rule never matched from app/)
+ [App] noop
```

Docker build hashes are unchanged. A golden test covers this, so existing images are not rebuilt.

Builds on #1945, which should merge first. The duplicate gitignore→glob converters in `frontend-frameworks` remain. That package doesn't depend on alchemy or `node-utils`.
